## E. Post-MVP refinements to already-shipped features

These aren't bugs — the features work — but there's known
follow-up polish the original ship didn't include.

### Extend brag #270's operator-doc sentinel-grep to OS / Postgres / Node.js version recommendations — DEFERRED 2026-05-17 (Part 122 cp28)

cp28's Sally-operator walkthrough surfaced DD-cp28-Sally-Op-1
(HIGH): `docs/RUN-A-MORPHIT-NODE.md` §3 told operators to choose
**Debian 12 or Ubuntu 22.04 LTS**, but `ops/ansible/playbook.yml:47-54`
hard-fails unless `ansible_distribution == "Ubuntu"` AND
`ansible_distribution_version == "24.04"`; `scripts/vps-bootstrap.sh:21`
prompts on mismatch; `README.md` L7+L42 + `OPERATIONS.md` throughout
all say Ubuntu 24.04.  An operator following the grandma-friendly
runbook literally would pick an unsupported OS and hit deployment
failure as their first interaction with the project.

Brag list entry #270 ("Operator-doc audit pinned by regression
smokes — every CLI command, every environment variable, every API
field path, every install location named in the operator docs is
sentinel-grep checked against the real code") names exactly the
discipline that should have caught this — but the actual sentinel
surface in `apps/web/scripts/persona-walkthrough-smoke.ts` only
covers CLI commands + env var names + path locations.  Recommended
OS versions, Postgres versions, Node.js versions, and similar
"system-prerequisite" claims are NOT currently covered.

Action items for the post-launch sweep:
1. Add a new sentinel class to persona-walkthrough-smoke.ts that
   parses operator-facing docs (`RUN-A-MORPHIT-NODE.md`,
   `OPERATIONS.md`, `README.md`, `RELEASE-NOTES-v1.0.0-beta.1.md`)
   for phrases of the form `Ubuntu N.NN`, `Debian N`,
   `Postgres N` / `PostgreSQL N`, `Node.js N`/`node N`.
2. For each match, verify the recommended version against the
   matching source-of-truth:
   - OS recommendations → `ops/ansible/playbook.yml` distribution
     assertion + `scripts/vps-bootstrap.sh` os-release grep
   - Postgres recommendations → schema-applies-cleanly CI matrix
   - Node.js recommendations → root `package.json:engines.node`
3. Sentinel failure if any doc recommends a version the CI
   matrix / playbook assertion does not accept.

This finding's class is exactly the cp28 Pattern Lesson 14:
"The grandma-friendly entry-point doc is the most operator-hostile
drift surface."  Extending the sentinel-grep closes the class.

Estimated work: ~2 hours.  Not pre-launch blocking (cp28 fixed
the specific Sally-Op-1 instance; the sentinel extension prevents
recurrence).  Filed for the first post-launch hardening sprint.

### Add CI gate that regenerates every derived artifact in a fresh checkout and diffs against committed — DEFERRED 2026-05-17 (Part 122 cp28)

cp28's Sally-operator walkthrough surfaced DD-cp28-Sally-Op-3
(MEDIUM): `scripts/build-llms-full.mjs:38` generator header was
**stale by 4 checkpoints** (cp3/cp21/cp24/cp27), but the on-disk
`apps/web/static/llms-full.txt` had been **hand-edited** to the
correct 7-asset form during an earlier checkpoint.  This created
a silent ticking bomb: the next `npm run build` would have
regenerated llms-full.txt with the stale 3-asset header, silently
wiping the manual fix.

cp28 Pattern Lesson 13 banked this as the highest-leverage bug
class in the repo: **generator-vs-artifact drift hidden behind
hand-fixes.**  The artifacts at risk include (at minimum):

- `apps/web/static/llms-full.txt` (built by `scripts/build-llms-full.mjs`)
- `apps/web/static/sitemap.xml` (built by `scripts/build-sitemap.mjs`)
- `apps/web/static/morphit-mediakit.zip` (built by `scripts/build-mediakit.sh`)
- `apps/web/static/verify.json` (built by `scripts/build-verify-json.mjs`)
- `apps/web/static/llms.txt` (status: needs verification — does it have a builder, or is it hand-maintained?)

Recommended CI gate:
1. In a fresh checkout (no committed-artifact bias), run every
   `scripts/build-*.{mjs,sh}` builder.
2. Diff the output against the committed version of each derived
   artifact.
3. Any non-empty diff fails the CI run with a clear error message:
   "Generated artifact X is out-of-sync with its generator Y.
   Either re-run `Y` and commit, OR fix the generator if it's
   stale."

Estimated work: ~3 hours (mostly figuring out which artifacts have
nondeterministic outputs like timestamps and either making the
builders deterministic or normalizing diffs).  Not pre-launch
blocking (cp28 fixed the specific Sally-Op-3 instance, and the
mediakit-builder fix is the only known hand-edit hidden behind a
stale builder); the CI gate prevents recurrence.

### Replace brag-list-by-number citations with phrase-anchored citations — DEFERRED 2026-05-17 (Part 122 cp26 DD)

cp26's deep-deep surfaced a class of pre-existing drift: cross-doc
citations like `(brag #208)` in `docs/audit/2026-05-stride-matrix.md`,
`MORPHIT-BRAG-LIST.md item #208` in `docs/adr/0022-desktop-qr-pairing.md`,
and `brag list entry #237` in `docs/i18n-untranslated-2026-05.txt`
are STRUCTURALLY FRAGILE.  Every time the brag list is renumbered
(insertions in the middle, slim passes that drop entries), every
citation by number drifts silently.  cp26 added 5 entries in
section 2 and renumbered items 30+ by +5; the DD found 7+ external
citations affected, and confirmed they had ALREADY been stale
through earlier brag-list edits (Part 120 slim, etc.).

The cp26 DD fixed the citations to current positions, but this
is whack-a-mole.  Real fix: replace ALL `brag #N` citations with
phrase-anchored citations of the form `(brag list entry on
Desktop QR-pairing)` or with stable hash-anchor links if the
brag list ever gets per-entry anchors.

Affected files at this snapshot:
- `docs/audit/2026-05-stride-matrix.md` (6 `brag #` citations,
  including 2 to entries since dropped during Part 120 slim)
- `docs/adr/0022-desktop-qr-pairing.md` (1 `item #` citation)
- `docs/i18n-untranslated-2026-05.txt` (1 `entry #` citation)
- `apps/web/scripts/wiring-completeness-smoke.ts` (1 comment
  citing `brag list #65`)

Future-proofing pattern: when a doc needs to cite a specific
brag claim, embed the claim phrase verbatim (so grep can find
the cross-reference even after renumbering) and optionally add
the current number as a navigation aid: `(brag list:
"Desktop QR-pairing" — currently #218)`.  The number is hint,
the phrase is the contract.

### Native translations for cp26 privacy keys in 6 locales — DEFERRED 2026-05-17 (Part 122 cp26)

Cp26 shipped 67 new i18n keys for the transparent-chain privacy
framework (amount-jitter generic copy, address-reuse warning,
PayJoin labels, per-asset privacy guide content, shared sections
like fresh-address advice + opt-in tech + universal practices +
what-not-to-do).  Native translations done for `en` + `es` +
`fr` + `de`.  Remaining 6 locales — `it`, `pl`, `ru`, `fa`,
`zh-CN`, `zh-HK` — ship cp26 keys as English fallback to
maintain locale parity at the file-shape level.

Locale parity is `2,630 keys × 10 = 26,300 strings` end-to-end
green; the file-shape invariant smoke passes.  But users in the
6 EN-fallback locales see English copy on the privacy guide
pages, the jitter toggle, the reuse warning, and the PayJoin
field until a future translation pass.

This is intentional per Ken's plowing discipline: ship the
privacy framework now, file the REVISIT, don't block on
translation completeness.  An independent translation
checkpoint can replace these en-fallbacks with native copy
without touching anything else.

Files affected per locale: `apps/web/src/lib/i18n/locales/{it,pl,ru,fa,zh-CN,zh-HK}.json`
under the keys `chat.address.amount_jitter_*`,
`chat.address.reuse_warning_*`, `chat.address.payjoin_*`,
`privacy.*`.  Diff-friendly: every key has a stable English
default; native pass replaces values one-by-one.

To verify which keys still need native translation:
```bash
# Compare a key against en.json; if identical, it's en-fallback
jq -r '.privacy.guides.btc.intro' apps/web/src/lib/i18n/locales/it.json
jq -r '.privacy.guides.btc.intro' apps/web/src/lib/i18n/locales/en.json
```

### Price feed integration — DEFERRED 2026-04-24

Current redundancy is adequate:
- **BLURT/USD:** Klingex + Coingecko (2 sources, fallback chain).
- **BTC/USD, XMR/USD:** Coingecko (industry default; price
  consensus across reputable sources is tight enough that adding
  more doesn't materially improve accuracy).

Evaluated in `docs/PRICE-SOURCES-RESEARCH.md` and deferred:

- **CoinMarketCap for BLURT:** feasible but the research flagged
  the CMC BLURT feed as possibly stuck (`$0 volume` snapshot).
  Adding a flaky third source is a liability not an asset —
  redundancy means more *reliable* sources, not higher count.
  Revisit only if an operator independently verifies the CMC
  feed stays healthy over a 7-day monitoring window (that
  verification is tracked in §A as a separate operator task).
- **Tribaldex / Hive-Engine:** REJECTED. Reports `SWAP.BLURT`
  (wrapped sidechain token with depeg risk against real BLURT);
  would require a three-hop derivation that breaks during bridge
  stress — exactly when accurate pricing matters most.
- **Blockchair, Blockchain.com:** not applicable for BLURT
  (unsupported). Useful as BTC/XMR block explorers for the
  attestation workstream (ADR-0011 sub-phase 4b), not for
  price feeds.
- **More BTC/XMR USD sources:** don't materially add value
  for price accuracy. The real BTC/XMR resilience work lives
  in fee *attestation*, not in price feeds — that's tracked
  separately under ADR-0011.

Revisit this decision if: (a) Klingex's API changes or goes
down, (b) Coingecko imposes rate limits or outages we can't
absorb with local caching, or (c) an operator verifies a new
source is consistently healthy.

### Chat inbox polish — SHIPPED 2026-04-24 (Phases A + B)

The `/chat` inbox landed earlier with basic list-conversations
functionality. For active traders juggling multiple DM threads
this was under-featured (no unread indicator, no count, no
sort). Shipped two layered improvements in one session arc.

**Phase A — client-side unread state (SHIPPED 2026-04-24):**

- `apps/web/src/lib/chat/readState.ts` — localStorage-backed
  per-peer last-visited tracker with Svelte store reactivity.
  API: `markConversationRead`, `getLastVisited`, `isUnread`,
  `clearReadState`, `mergeRemoteReadState`, and a reactive
  `readState` store. Bounded at MAX_PEERS = 500, oldest-dropped.
  Invalid account names + malformed timestamps silently
  filtered at both read and write boundaries.
- `apps/web/src/lib/chat/readState.test.ts` — 22 unit tests
  covering mark/retrieve round-trip, isUnread logic, monotonic
  merge semantics, MAX_PEERS cap, graceful fallback on corrupt
  storage, store reactivity.
- `/chat/+page.svelte` — rewritten with unread-first sort, per-
  conversation unread dot + bolded name + emerald timestamp,
  unread-count pill in header, "Mark all as read" button,
  aria-labels distinguishing read/unread states.
- 5 new `chat.inbox` i18n keys × 10 locales at clean parity
  (unread_count, unread_aria, mark_all_read,
  conversation_aria_{read,unread}).

**Phase B — on-chain read receipts (SHIPPED 2026-04-24):**

Cross-device sync via new `morphit_chat_read_v1` custom_json
op. Architecture matches existing chat ops: posting-key signed,
indexer-materialized, public metadata, stateless API.

- `apps/indexer/src/db/schema-v14.sql` — `chat_read_state`
  table keyed on (reader_account, peer_account), with
  last_read_at + source trace columns. Migration registered
  in `migrations.ts` as v14.
- `apps/indexer/src/indexer/handlers/chatRead.ts` — handler
  for `morphit_chat_read_v1`. Atomic monotonic-advance via
  `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE WHERE
  chat_read_state.last_read_at < EXCLUDED.last_read_at`,
  so out-of-order acks from a stale device cannot regress
  read state. 60s clock-skew tolerance past block time;
  floor at 2020-01-01.
- `apps/indexer/src/api/chatReadState.ts` — read endpoint
  `GET /v1/chat-read-state/:account` returning every
  (peer, last_read_at) row for the account. Mounted with
  the standard `listRatePerMin` rate limiter. No auth
  (same rationale as `/v1/conversations` — data is already
  on-chain).
- `packages/indexer-client/src/index.ts` — `ChatReadStateEntry`
  + `ChatReadStateResponse` types exported alongside
  `ConversationsResponse`. Doc-comment on the latter updated
  to reference on-chain read receipts.
- `apps/web/src/lib/blurt/ops/chatRead.ts` — op builder
  `broadcastChatRead(live, peer, lastReadAt?)`. Uses
  `BroadcastError('no_account')` for user-facing condition;
  plain `Error` for structural-invariant violations
  (invalid peer name, self-chat) since those shouldn't
  happen from real UI flows and the `BroadcastError` code
  union is fixed (`'no_account' | 'locked'`).
- `apps/web/src/lib/net/config.ts` — `OP_IDS.chatRead`
  added to mirror indexer dispatcher.
- `apps/web/src/lib/indexer/client.ts` — `getChatReadState`
  client helper.
- `apps/web/src/routes/chat/+page.svelte` — inbox `onMount`
  now `Promise.all`s conversations fetch + read-state fetch,
  calls `mergeRemoteReadState` on success, silently falls
  through to Phase A local-only behavior on read-state fetch
  failure.
- `apps/web/src/routes/chat/[peer=account]/+page.svelte` —
  conversation open triggers both `markConversationRead(peer)`
  (synchronous local) and `broadcastChatRead(live, peer)`
  (async, via dynamic import, skipped if session locked).
  Ack timestamp is `Date.now()` at open time; slight
  over-ack edge case documented in-file.
- `mergeRemoteReadState` in `readState.ts` — monotonic
  merge semantics: incoming server entry only wins if
  strictly newer than local; local wins otherwise. This
  mirrors the indexer handler's SQL guard, so the two
  layers cannot regress each other.

**Cross-device contract:**
- Writes go on-chain via `morphit_chat_read_v1` AND to local
  storage (shadow write for instant UI feedback).
- Reads merge local + server state with "max wins" per peer.
- On-chain state is authoritative for durability; local state
  is authoritative for "right now" UX (no roundtrip wait).
- Phase A local-only still works for users who never ack
  on-chain (e.g. reading while session locked); they just
  don't get cross-device sync.

**Deferred / explicitly out of scope for this session:**
- Server-push live unread deltas (users open inbox and
  see real-time unread changes without refresh) — Phase C,
  needs SSE or WebSocket infrastructure which isn't built.
- Last-message preview snippet — blocked by E2EE: a decrypted
  preview would require decrypting on inbox load for every
  conversation, which is expensive and partly defeats the
  "inbox is cheap to visit" design principle. Re-consider
  if the chat per-conversation endpoint is extended with a
  "give me just the latest ciphertext and its direction"
  signal later.
- Requests tab for stranger-initiated conversations —
  blocked on Finding H (chat anti-spam) implementation.
- Archive / pin / mute — not requested; add if demanded.

### Inline character counter on ProtectedTextarea — SHIPPED 2026-04-24

User request: "if there's a max number of characters that a user
can type into the order description or notes fields about the
order, then put a tiny little counter in the bottom right corner
of the textarea area, so that the user can easily see how many
more characters he is allowed to type." Follow-up: "be consistent
with your choice app-wide."

Before this work, counter UX was inconsistent across the app:
two order-terms textareas had NO counter, feedback forms and
chat composer had label-row counters with a 256-numerator /
1024-maxlength asymmetry that wasn't obviously documented.

**Solution: counter built into `ProtectedTextarea` as opt-in.**
Three new props — `showCounter: boolean`, `counterMode:
'codepoint' | 'utf16'`, `counterLimit?: number`. Defaults off
so prior call sites aren't affected if anyone consumes the
component elsewhere.

**Tiered visibility** (chosen for UX calmness):
- 0–74% of limit: counter hidden entirely (opacity 0). Users
  well below the cap never see a number they don't care about.
- 75–89%: faint (opacity 0.55, neutral slate color). First hint.
- 90–99%: amber, full opacity, semibold. Clear "getting close."
- ≥100%: red, full opacity, semibold. Clear "stop."

Transitions are 180ms ease-out on opacity + color. Respects
`prefers-reduced-motion`.

**Positioning:** absolute bottom-right, inset 1rem from right
edge so it clears the native textarea resize grip on browsers
that render one. `pointer-events: none` so it never blocks
text selection, clicks, or the resize grip itself. `user-
select: none` so triple-click-to-select-all doesn't grab the
counter text. `tabular-nums` so digit-width stability keeps
the counter from jittering as numbers change.

**Accessibility:** `aria-live="polite"` only activates when
tier is amber or red. A polite live region that announces
every keystroke is noise for screen reader users; keeping
quiet until the user is close to or past the limit is both
less annoying and more useful.

**Two counting modes** reflect the two validator shapes in the
codebase:
- `'utf16'` (default, matches native `maxlength` semantics) —
  used for order terms where the indexer validates `.length`
  directly against 2048.
- `'codepoint'` — used for chat and feedback where emoji are
  1-per-character by the indexer's validators. The `maxlength`
  stays at the UTF-16 defense ceiling (1024), `counterLimit`
  is the codepoint soft cap (256). So a user pasting 256
  emoji hits the counter's red tier but the browser doesn't
  hard-block them; further typing is refused only if they'd
  exceed 1024 UTF-16 units.

**Five call sites, all now using the same component:**
- `apps/web/src/routes/post/+page.svelte` — order terms, utf16
  mode, limit 2048. Counter added (was missing entirely).
- `apps/web/src/routes/post/edit/[permlink]/+page.svelte` —
  order terms edit, same config. Counter added.
- `apps/web/src/lib/components/LeaveFeedbackForm.svelte` —
  comment, codepoint mode, limit 256 / maxlength 1024.
  Migrated from label-row counter. Removed orphaned
  `commentCodepointCount` derived.
- `apps/web/src/lib/components/RespondToFeedbackForm.svelte` —
  response comment, same config. Migrated. Removed orphaned
  `codepointCount` derived.
- `apps/web/src/lib/components/ChatComposer.svelte` — message,
  same config. Migrated. `codepointCount` + `overCap` kept
  because they still gate `canSend` — the Send button stays
  disabled over-cap, that's independent of how the count is
  displayed.

**Tier thresholds verified against all call-site limits via
manual simulation:** terms counter kicks in at 1536 chars
(75% of 2048), faint→amber at 1844 (90%), amber→red at 2048
(100%). Feedback counter faint at 192 codepoints, amber at 231,
red at 256. No off-by-one at boundaries.

**What this does NOT change:**
- The seed-phrase paste textarea in `onboarding/import/+page.svelte`
  deliberately has no counter — a count there implies the seed
  should be a specific length, which is true but not useful UX;
  the validator catches bad seeds by content, not length.
- The old label-row `commentCodepointCount` pattern is gone
  from the three migrated forms. Any future form that needs a
  character counter should use `showCounter` + `counterMode` +
  `counterLimit` rather than adding prose above the field.

Frontend typecheck: 0 errors after all migrations.

### Operator-account balance monitoring — SHIPPED 2026-04-24

User request: "if the @morphit-relay and/or @morphit-fees
account get drained to a critical level, always notify the
instance admin ahead of time so that he can get some more funds
in there."

Gap found in the existing code: `lowBalanceScanner.ts`
monitors USER accounts to auto-refill them with BLURT dust, but
nothing monitored the operator's own service accounts. A
drained @morphit-relay means welcome bonuses, loyalty
delegations, and dust refills silently stop — operators only
noticed when users complained.

**New module: `apps/indexer/src/indexer/operatorAccountBalanceScanner.ts`**
(~260 lines, 310-line vitest suite at
`apps/indexer/test/indexer/operatorAccountBalanceScanner.test.ts`).

**Four alert kinds** in a discriminated union routable by sinks:
- `LOW_BALANCE` — balance crossed below threshold, fired once
  per downward cross. Payload includes account, role label
  (`'relay'` / `'fees'`), current balance, configured threshold.
- `RECOVERED` — balance returned above threshold. Fired once
  per recovery so operators know "crisis resolved" and can stop
  worrying.
- `SUSTAINED_RPC_FAILURE` — N consecutive RPC failures to the
  Blurt node (configurable N, default 3). Prevents silent
  failure where "can't check balance" gets confused with
  "balance is fine."
- `SHAPE_ERROR` — balance string unparseable. Rare; indicates
  chain upgrade weirdness or corrupted response.

**Hysteresis by design.** Scanner state (per-account
below/above) is in-memory. Downward cross fires LOW_BALANCE
once; subsequent scans while still below are silent (no spam).
Upward cross fires RECOVERED once and re-arms the downward
trigger. Losing state on process restart fires at most one
extra alert if already below — acceptable.

**Injectable AlertSink** matching the `WitnessFeePoller`
pattern. Default routes through the structured logger (module
`operator-balance`) so operators on systemd/journald see JSON
log entries with `level: "error"` on `LOW_BALANCE`. Operators
wanting richer integration (Discord webhook, email, SMS,
Matrix, etc.) swap in a custom sink at Poller construction
time.

**Opt-in by default.** Four new env vars:
- `MORPHIT_INDEXER_OPERATOR_BALANCE_INTERVAL_MS` (default
  900000 = 15 min). Operational urgency is higher than the
  6-hour user-dust scanner but not so urgent that we hammer
  the Blurt node.
- `MORPHIT_INDEXER_OPERATOR_BALANCE_RELAY_THRESHOLD_BLURT`
  (default 0 = disabled).
- `MORPHIT_INDEXER_OPERATOR_BALANCE_FEES_THRESHOLD_BLURT`
  (default 0 = disabled).
- `MORPHIT_INDEXER_OPERATOR_BALANCE_FAILURE_ALERT_THRESHOLD`
  (default 3 consecutive RPC failures before sustained alert).

The zero-default matters: operators upgrading without reading
release notes get no surprise alerts. To opt in, they set
non-zero thresholds. Typical values: relay ~100 BLURT
(enough runway to notice + top up), fees ~10 BLURT (fees
normally accumulate — reaching 10 means something's wrong,
either a misconfigured auto-sweep or an account compromise).

**Wired into the Poller tick loop** next to
`witnessFeePoller.maybePoll()` and
`lowBalanceScanner.maybeScan()`. Self-throttling via
`intervalMs`; errors swallowed and logged rather than
propagated.

**Exposed via `/v1/health?verbose=1`** under a new
`diagnostics.operator_balances` array. Each entry:
`{account, role, threshold_blurt, below_threshold,
last_observed_blurt}`. Empty array when no monitoring
configured. Operators can poll this to confirm the scanner is
actually observing the accounts without waiting for an alert.

**Test coverage (11 cases, typecheck-clean, manual simulation
passes for hysteresis transitions):**
- opt-out: both thresholds 0 → no RPC call, no alerts
- above threshold first scan → no alert
- below threshold first scan → LOW_BALANCE alert
- hysteresis: second scan still below → no duplicate alert
- recovery: above after below → RECOVERED, then re-arms
- RPC failures: SUSTAINED after threshold, success resets
- SHAPE_ERROR on unparseable balance
- missing account in response → silent, error counted
- partial config (only relay, not fees) → only relay checked
- maybeScan respects intervalMs throttle

**Gaps honestly flagged:**
- Tests are unit-level against a mocked BlurtClient. End-to-end
  verification against a real Blurt testnet with a funded +
  drained account is a human-review gate.
- The default structured-log sink is fine for JSON-aware ops,
  but operators without a log aggregator will want to override
  with a Discord/email/webhook sink. Writing the "how to
  configure a Discord alert sink" operator doc is a natural
  follow-up but not blocker for shipping.
- @morphit-fees dropping is abnormal (fees accumulate, don't
  drain). The only way it triggers LOW_BALANCE is misconfigured
  auto-sweep or account compromise. Flagging either is the
  correct outcome, but operators should read the alert as
  "investigate why" not "top up."

### Relay origin allowlist — SHIPPED 2026-04-24

User request: "I certainly don't want to pay the new user blurt
account registration fees that take place on other instances,
so please make sure of that." Paired with a second ask — giving
community operators their own low-balance alerts, which the
operator-account balance scanner above already delivers (it's
generic; each community operator enables it for their own
accounts via env vars).

**The "other instances billing my relay" gap.** Before this
session, the relay's CORS middleware withheld
`Access-Control-Allow-*` headers from unallowed origins, which
browsers honor by blocking the fetch. BUT `curl` / Postman /
server-to-server clients ignore CORS entirely. A hostile or
misconfigured frontend using a non-browser signup client could
POST directly to `/v1/account/create` and spend the relay's
BLURT regardless of origin. Three concrete threat scenarios:

- **Community mirror misconfiguration.** Operator B forks
  Morphit, forgets to update `MORPHIT_RELAY_ORIGIN` in their
  frontend build, their users' signups bill operator A's relay.
- **Hostile frontend.** Someone deliberately points their
  frontend at a victim operator's relay to drain funds.
- **Curl spam.** Bots ignoring CORS POST directly.

**Fix: server-side origin enforcement on fund-spending
endpoints.**

New middleware: `apps/relay/src/middleware/origin_enforcement.ts`
(`enforceOriginAllowlist`). Wired in
`apps/relay/src/main.ts` scoped to `/v1/account/create` ONLY
(not the entire app) so:
- Availability and health endpoints stay permissive (operators
  debugging via curl still work; liveness probes still work)
- Only the endpoint that spends BLURT is gated

**Policy decisions (documented in the module header):**
- Origin present + in allowlist → proceed
- Origin present + NOT in allowlist → 403 `origin_not_allowed`
- Origin missing → 403 `origin_required`
- OPTIONS preflight → passthrough (CORS middleware upstream
  handles it)

The "missing Origin → reject" rule is the less-obvious one but
correct: modern browsers always send Origin on cross-origin
POSTs, and since frontend + relay run on different origins in
every non-trivial deployment, a legitimate browser-driven
signup always has Origin set. Missing means non-browser client,
ancient browser, or privacy extension stripping headers — all
three are cases where rejecting is the safe call for a fund-
spending endpoint.

**Reuses existing config.** The allowlist config env var
`MORPHIT_RELAY_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` was already defined for the CORS
middleware; the new middleware reads the same list, so
operators only configure one place. The config already errors
at startup if the list is empty, which gives the secure-default
behavior of rejecting all signups until the operator explicitly
configures allowed origins.

**Test coverage** — `apps/relay/test/origin_enforcement.test.ts`,
7 cases:
- Allowed origin proceeds
- Disallowed origin → 403 `origin_not_allowed`
- Missing origin → 403 `origin_required`
- Empty allowlist rejects all
- Exact-match discipline (scheme + host + port must match,
  no subdomain or wildcard semantics)
- Multiple allowed origins all work
- OPTIONS preflight passes through

Relay typecheck: 0 errors. Existing create.test.ts unaffected
(it builds its own minimal Hono app without the main.ts
middleware chain).

**Documentation in OPERATIONS.md:**
- §16 "Operator-account balance alerts" — how each community
  operator enables the scanner for their own @morphit-relay /
  @morphit-fees accounts. Covers threshold choice, alert kinds,
  `/v1/health?verbose=1` verification, and two paths for
  routing alerts elsewhere (log-tail sidecar vs fork-and-
  replace-sink).
- §17 "Relay origin allowlist" — threat model, config syntax,
  exact-match rules, behavior for legitimate + illegitimate
  requests, limits of the defense (origin is forgeable by
  non-browser clients — this gates misconfiguration + casual
  abuse, not sophisticated attack).

**Limits, honestly.** Origin can be forged by non-browser
clients. This middleware:
- Fully closes the "browser on another frontend accidentally
  bills my relay" case (common, documented, fixed).
- Partially closes the curl / script abuse case (raises friction
  from "paste URL" to "write header-forging script").
- Does NOT replace rate limits. The existing per-IP hourly +
  daily limiters in `apps/relay/src/middleware/ratelimit.ts` do
  the bot-defense job. Origin enforcement is orthogonal to
  rate limits.

For cryptographic assurance of "this request came from my
frontend," you'd need a shared-secret token embedded at build
time and validated by the relay. That's a larger design change
tracked as future work, not blocking this ship.

### Follow-up (same session, 2026-04-24): observability + colocation clarity

User asked whether colocated deployments (frontend + relay +
indexer on one host) could default-allow "localhost" as an
origin. Short answer: no — the Origin header reflects the
PAGE'S URL (what the browser sees), not the backend's loopback
address. In a same-server deployment the browser still sends
the public hostname as Origin. Clarified this in OPERATIONS.md
§17 with a new subsection "What goes in the allowlist?"
covering three common topologies (colocated, split-subdomain,
multi-mirror).

Also corrected an inaccuracy in the middleware's own comment:
I had written "browsers always send Origin on CROSS-origin
POSTs" but the fuller truth per the Fetch spec is browsers
send Origin on same-origin POST/PUT/DELETE too (just not
same-origin GETs). The "missing Origin → reject" rule is
still correct for this endpoint because it's POST-only, but
the docstring now says so for the right reason.

Observability improvements to help operators debug "my users
can't sign up":

- `rejected_disallowed_origin` logged at WARN with payload
  `{origin, allowed_origins, path, hint}`. The hint string
  tells the operator exactly what to change
  (`MORPHIT_RELAY_ALLOWED_ORIGINS`). One `journalctl` grep
  surfaces the fix.
- `rejected_missing_origin` logged at INFO — almost always
  non-browser clients (curl, bots), not operator-actionable
  on its own.
- Both deduplicated per-(code, origin) within a 5-minute
  window so a sustained curl-storm can't flood the journal.
  Lazy pruning of the dedup map keeps memory bounded.

Logger module `relay-origin` so operators can filter:
```
sudo journalctl -u morphit-relay.service | grep '\[relay-origin\]'
```

OPERATIONS.md §17 gained a new "Reading the logs" subsection
documenting both log lines.

Relay typecheck still clean, no test regressions (the existing
7-case origin test doesn't observe logs, which are additive).

---

## F. Security audit findings (in-progress — shipping-turn catalog)

Recorded from the code-audit-and-attack-vector review
started Apr 2026. Each finding has a file:line anchor,
severity, and fix shape so the next session can pick up
without re-reading the code. Severity uses the
straightforward scale: LOW = defense-in-depth, no
exploit today; MEDIUM = real bypass but blast radius
bounded; HIGH = real bypass with unbounded damage;
CRITICAL = key material or funds at risk with a
reachable path. No HIGH/CRITICAL findings so far.

### Finding A — `fiat_currency` content validation missing — SHIPPED

- **Severity:** LOW (defense-in-depth; no exploit today)
- **Status:** SHIPPED (this session). Added `/^[A-Z]+$/`
  check at intake in both `order.ts` and `orderReplace.ts`.
  The two validators stay parallel.
- **Location:** `apps/indexer/src/indexer/handlers/order.ts:91`
- **Description:** `fiat_currency` was validated only on length
  (1..8 chars), not on content. An attacker could submit e.g.
  `"USD\n"` or `'USD\"'`. All current render sites auto-escape
  (Svelte `{value}` interpolation + `xmlEscape()` in the RSS
  feed), so there was no exploitable path today.
- **Fix:** add a `/^[A-Z]+$/` regex at intake, matching what the
  orderbook query filter already requires at
  `apps/indexer/src/api/orderbook.ts:33`.
- **Blast radius:** zero today; this is a safety belt against
  a future renderer that forgets to escape.

### Finding B — indexer rate-limit bypass via forged `x-real-ip` — SHIPPED

- **Severity:** MEDIUM (real bypass, but bounded)
- **Status:** SHIPPED. `clientIp()` in
  `apps/indexer/src/api/middleware/ratelimit.ts` now
  reads the socket peer from Hono's Node adapter and
  honors forwarded-address headers ONLY when the peer
  is a loopback address. A direct-connection attacker
  cannot forge the header to get a fresh bucket —
  their socket address is used instead, and all their
  requests share one bucket regardless of what headers
  they send. OPERATIONS.md §14 documents the
  deployment-topology requirement (apps must be behind
  loopback proxy) that this fix depends on, along with
  a verification procedure operators should run during
  setup.
- **Location:** `apps/indexer/src/api/middleware/ratelimit.ts:49-56`
- **Description:** Trusts `x-real-ip` and `x-forwarded-for`
  headers unconditionally. Comment says "nginx is the only
  thing reaching it," but there's no runtime check that the
  peer is actually loopback. Forged headers per request give
  every request a fresh bucket → full rate-limit bypass on
  public GET endpoints (orderbook, FAQ lookups, etc.).
- **Fix:** prefer the raw socket peer address as ground truth;
  honor `x-real-ip` / `x-forwarded-for` only when the peer is
  `127.0.0.1` / `::1`. Threads through Hono's Node adapter —
  not a one-line change but not invasive either.
- **Blast radius:** scraping abuse, skewed usage stats, no
  direct financial impact. Degrades the indexer's ability to
  shed load under a targeted request flood.

### Finding C — false alarm (recorded for explicit traceability)

- **Severity:** NONE
- **Location:** `apps/indexer/src/indexer/handlers/feedback.ts:126`,
  `apps/indexer/src/indexer/dispatcher.ts:534`
- **Description:** SQL template-string interpolation
  (`SAVEPOINT ${name}`) jumped out on first scan. Verified
  safe: interpolated values are hardcoded constants
  (`welcome_bonus_sp`) or bounded integers
  (`op_${trxInBlock}_${opInTrx}`), never user input.
- **Action:** none, but if a future refactor derives savepoint
  names from anything user-controllable, this pattern must be
  reviewed.

### Finding D — drainer trusts every queue recipient — SHIPPED

- **Severity:** LOW (defense-in-depth)
- **Status:** SHIPPED (this session). Added a
  `ACCOUNT_NAME_RE` constant + guard at the top of
  `processRow` that rejects any row whose recipient
  doesn't match `/^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{2,15}$/`. The throw
  flows into `recordFailure`, incrementing the row's
  error_count so repeated invalid rows escalate to
  operator attention rather than silently retry.
- **Location:** `apps/relay/src/queue/drainer.ts:147` (`processRow`)
- **Description:** The drainer broadcasts a BLURT transfer to
  whatever `row.recipient` says, without re-validating it
  against the Blurt account-name regex. All current writers to
  `relay_pending_transfers` validate upstream (feedback handler →
  `ACCOUNT_NAME_RE`, loyalty → `ctx.signer` from chain, low-
  balance scanner → `accounts.name` via SELECT), so no
  exploitable path today.
- **Fix:** one-line guard in `processRow` that rejects rows
  whose `recipient` doesn't match `/^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{2,15}$/`.
- **Blast radius:** if an attacker ever gets direct write
  access to the database (operator misstep, a future SQLi found
  later, a manual psql session), this guard narrows the attack
  surface from "any string → receives BLURT" to "valid-shaped
  Blurt accounts only."

### Finding E — relay `/v1/account/create` rate-limit bypass (costs BLURT) — SHIPPED

- **Severity:** MEDIUM (real bypass, worse than B because
  every call costs BLURT)
- **Status:** SHIPPED. `clientIp()` in
  `apps/relay/src/middleware/ip.ts` now uses the same
  socket-peer-first pattern as Finding B's fix. The
  relay's account-creation endpoint can no longer be
  abused by a direct-connection attacker forging
  `X-Forwarded-For` per request. Mitigation is
  belt-and-braces with `HealthService.canAcceptCreation()`
  which already capped damage at the relay's BLURT
  balance — now the limiter itself also works
  correctly. Same operator setup requirement as Finding
  B (see OPERATIONS.md §14).
- **Location:** `apps/relay/src/middleware/ip.ts:12-22`
- **Description:** Same forward-address-forgery class as
  Finding B, but on the account-creation endpoint. Per-hour
  AND per-day limiters both key on the same forgeable IP —
  forging `X-Forwarded-For` per request bypasses both tiers.
  Every bypass-assisted create drains real BLURT from
  `@morphit-relay`.
- **Mitigation in place:** `HealthService.canAcceptCreation()`
  refuses new creates when the relay's BLURT balance is low,
  capping total damage at "relay runs dry" — so this is a
  denial-of-service against account creation, not unlimited
  theft. But a drained relay = no new Morphit accounts until
  an operator refills.
- **Fix:** same shape as B. Honor forwarded-address headers
  only when the socket peer is loopback.
- **Blast radius:** relay's BLURT balance. Bounded by
  `canAcceptCreation()`'s floor, bounded by chain-level
  per-block-producer account creation caps.

### Finding F — password argument can't be zeroed in JS — CLOSED 2026-04-24

- **Severity:** LOW (JS language limitation, not a bug)
- **Status:** CLOSED as accepted residual risk. Documented in
  `docs/SECURITY.md` under "Known minor threat-model items"
  with full attacker-model rationale. Option (A) taken: accept
  the JS ceiling, match the industry standard, write it down
  so future auditors don't flag it as missed coverage.
- **Location:** `apps/web/src/lib/crypto/keystore.ts:145`
  (`decryptIdentity`) and every caller that supplies the
  password as a `string`
- **Description:** Derived symmetric keys and plaintext are
  correctly scrubbed with `sodium.memzero()` after use. The
  **password itself** can't be — JS strings are immutable,
  so whatever is assigned to the `password` parameter stays
  in V8's string table until GC decides to reclaim it. GC
  timing is non-deterministic; a process memory dump taken
  mid-session could recover recent passwords.
- **Rationale for Option (A):** the attacker model this
  defense would address is "live browser-process memory read
  access." At that privilege level the attacker can already
  read the decrypted posting key from LiveIdentity, chat
  plaintext during render, session cookies, etc. — closing
  the password-string window alone is one door in a house
  where every other door is also open. Full Uint8Array
  refactor (Option B) touches every login / unlock / password-
  change form and adds maintenance burden for maintainers
  without raising the effective security bar against the
  threat it targets. Option (A) is what every web-crypto app
  does today; we formalize it rather than silently inheriting
  the industry default.
- **Blast radius:** requires process memory read access,
  which is already game-over for any web-crypto design.

### Finding G — featureBid handler doesn't gate on fee_status — SHIPPED

- **Severity:** LOW (UX wart, not correctness or loss)
- **Status:** SHIPPED (this session). Added `fee_status`
  to the order probe SELECT and a new rejection reason
  `referenced_order_fee_not_verified`. When the bidder's
  own order hasn't verified its listing fee, the bid is
  rejected early so the per-op savepoint rolls the
  user's BLURT transfer back — no wasted funds.
- **Location:** `apps/indexer/src/indexer/handlers/featureBid.ts:135`
- **Description:** The handler checks `order.status === 'live'`
  but not `fee_status === 'verified'`. A user can bid on
  their own order before its listing fee verifies. The
  user's BLURT transfer for the feature bid goes through
  correctly, but the slot doesn't surface on the
  `/v1/orderbook/featured` endpoint (which DOES require
  `fee_status='verified'`) until the listing fee also
  verifies.
- **Discovered:** during the `/my/orders` call-site audit
  this session — the frontend filter was also wrong
  (`fee_status === 'waived'` branch is dead because
  waived orders have `fee_status='verified'`). Fixed the
  frontend; handler-level guard still pending.
- **Fix:** add the fee_status predicate to the SQL at
  `featureBid.ts:124` and a new rejection reason
  (`referenced_order_fee_not_verified`). One-line change.
- **Blast radius:** user wastes BLURT on a slot that
  activates later than expected. Auto-resolves on its own
  the moment the listing fee verifies — just confusing UX.
- **Also fixed this session (unrelated but same root cause):**
  the dead `'waived'` branch in
  `apps/indexer/src/api/featuredOrderbook.ts:106` and in
  `apps/web/src/routes/my/orders/+page.svelte` — both now
  correctly use just `fee_status === 'verified'`.

### Finding H — chat handler accepts messages with no counterparty check — SHIPPED 2026-04-24 (all layers end-to-end)

- **Severity:** MEDIUM (spam / harassment vector)
- **Status:** FULLY SHIPPED. All three layers (block list,
  stranger-fee admission, rate limits) are live at the
  indexer, surfaced in the frontend UI (block button +
  ConfirmModal, pay-to-message modal, admission probe,
  Requests tab, Dismiss affordance, inbox hide/block
  filter, moved-to-Messages toast). See the follow-up
  REVISIT entries below this one for the implementation
  detail; this original entry is preserved for the
  design reasoning.
- **Location:** `apps/indexer/src/indexer/handlers/chat.ts:45-90`
- **Description:** Anyone can send an encrypted message to
  anyone else via `morphit_chat_v1` — there's no
  counterparty verification (no order permlink in payload,
  no check that sender and recipient are parties to any
  shared trade). Combined with free account creation via
  ADR-0010's welcome waiver, a sybil attacker can create
  throwaway accounts and flood any user's chat inbox.
- **Contextual note:** This is not accidental — the Phase 5
  chat scaffolding landed before ADR-0014 resolved the
  counterparty-scoping question. It's a deferred design
  decision, not a missed validation.

- **DECIDED fix: (b) + (c) combined.** Belt-and-suspenders
  defense layering UX-level mitigation with economic deterrence.
  Rejected (a) "require order_permlink" as too restrictive —
  it kills legitimate first-contact cases (new trader asks
  about terms before placing order; operators coordinating;
  user warns someone about a scammer). The belt-and-suspenders
  choice over pure (b) or pure (c) reflects the user's call
  that chat abuse is a real enough threat to pay some first-
  contact friction to prevent.

- **Implementation shape for future session:**

  **Indexer work:**
  1. New op `morphit_block_v1` — posted by a recipient to
     permanently block a sender. Handler writes to a new
     `blocks(blocker, blocked, since_block)` table with a
     composite PK.
  2. New op `morphit_stranger_fee_v1` — posted by a sender
     paying the small BLURT stranger-fee for first contact
     with a specific recipient. Handler validates the BLURT
     transfer landed on `@morphit-fees`, records the payment
     in `stranger_fees(sender, recipient, paid_at, trx_id)`
     so the same sender→recipient pair is fee-free forever
     after.
  3. Amend chat handler `apps/indexer/src/indexer/handlers/chat.ts`:
     at intake, check three gates in order — (i) reject if
     a block row exists for (recipient blocks sender); (ii)
     rate-limit per recipient (reject if ≥20 unique new
     senders have messaged this recipient in the last 24h
     without a reply, or ≥50 messages from a single sender
     without a recipient reply); (iii) reject with
     `stranger_fee_required` if sender has no prior exchange
     with recipient AND no `stranger_fees` row exists for
     the pair. New rejection reason codes thread through the
     dispatcher.

  **Client work:**
  1. New `/chat` inbox "Requests" tab for messages from
     strangers who've paid the fee. Users opt in to reading
     by tapping the requests counter.
  2. Block button on each message header; confirmation
     dialog; broadcasts `morphit_block_v1` signed with
     posting key.
  3. First-contact flow: when user tries to send to a peer
     they've never exchanged with, show a one-time modal
     "This is your first message to @alice. Morphit charges
     a small ~1¢ fee (in BLURT) to prevent spam. Pay & send?"
     On confirm, client broadcasts the stranger-fee op and
     the chat message in sequence; indexer accepts after
     the fee op lands.
  4. Settings page gains "Blocked accounts" list with
     unblock affordance.

  **Stranger-fee amount:** recommend $0.01 USD equivalent
  in BLURT, denominated and converted at message-send time
  using the existing price-feed path. Low enough that any
  legitimate first-contact user will pay without thinking;
  high enough that 1000 sybil messages costs $10 real money.

  **i18n:** ~12 new keys × 10 locales (stranger_fee modal
  body + confirm, block action label + success, requests tab
  label + empty state, 3 new rejection-reason messages).

- **Blast radius:** inbox spam, harassment targeting,
  possible phishing vector inside the chat UI. No data
  leak — messages are ECIES-encrypted and only the recipient
  can decrypt.
- **Cross-ref:** this decision closes the remaining open
  chat-scoping design question from ADR-0014 (the chat-side
  half of "verified-chat badge" decided earlier in this
  session stack). The ADR-0014 note should be updated to
  reflect that chat-counterparty scoping is now resolved
  via the rate-limit + block + stranger-fee triad rather
  than via order_permlink coupling.

### Finding I — feeAttest sybil attack on BTC/XMR attestation — SHIPPED 2026-04-24 (indexer gate + display end-to-end; attest UI deferred)

- **Severity:** MEDIUM (economic bypass of listing fee)
- **Status:** Indexer gate SHIPPED — eligibility helper,
  handler rejections, `/v1/attestor-eligibility` endpoint,
  config phase switch, schema v17 partial-index widening.
  Display layer SHIPPED — all six fee_status values
  rendered with proper copy + color across order-detail
  and my/orders, orderbook + RSS + featured endpoints
  include attestation-verified orders, feature-bid handler
  accepts them, fee-status-filter-lint regression guard.
  **Only the frontend attest UI itself is deferred** —
  that's genuinely a new feature session (no attest
  surface exists yet). See follow-up REVISIT entries for
  implementation detail; this original entry preserves
  the design reasoning.
- **Location:** `apps/indexer/src/indexer/handlers/feeAttest.ts:138-148`
- **Description:** ADR-0011 §3 requires ≥2 distinct
  attestors with ≥1 non-poster to promote a `pending_external`
  order to `verified_by_attestation`. Given that
  `@morphit-relay` creates accounts for free (welcome
  waiver), a grifter can: (1) post a BTC/XMR order, (2)
  create a throwaway account, (3) have both the throwaway
  AND their primary attest the (never-actually-paid)
  fee, (4) get `fee_status=verified_by_attestation`. No
  on-chain BTC/XMR payment required.
- **Cost to attacker:** ~0 (free accounts + cents in chain
  fees). **Damage per incident:** small ($0.125 USD
  listing fee avoided), but systematic abuse erodes the
  fee pool that funds operators.

- **DECIDED fix: (a) + (b) combined with staging.** Each
  attestor must satisfy:
  - **(a) Loyalty threshold:** at least the first loyalty
    milestone — 100 BLURT cumulative listing fees paid on
    Morphit — before their attestations count toward quorum.
  - **(b) Age threshold:** account on Blurt chain for ≥30
    days before first attestation counts.

  **Staged rollout** to avoid blocking legitimate early
  users during the chicken-and-egg window:

  1. **Launch phase (OR gate):** an attestor qualifies if
     they meet **either** (a) OR (b). Lower bar, still
     blocks freshly-farmed sock accounts (must pay $20 in
     BLURT fees OR wait 30 days).
  2. **Steady-state phase (AND gate):** attestor must meet
     **both** (a) AND (b). Attacker needs BOTH to wait 30
     days AND pay $20+ per sock — negative-ROI economics.

  **Phase transition trigger:** whichever is first of
  90 days from ADR-0011 activation OR 500 accounts on the
  chain that already meet both gates. The 500-accounts
  alternative prevents indefinite-launch-phase drift if
  real traffic grows faster than the calendar (the point of
  the calendar trigger is to guarantee migration eventually
  happens; the account-count trigger lets us migrate sooner
  if the ecosystem has enough eligible attestors). The
  operator flips the gate via a config parameter; no
  redeploy required.

  **Rejected (c) scaling quorum with transaction value:**
  the real threat is small-fraud-at-scale (sybil × $0.125
  fee × 1000 orders/day), which (c) doesn't address — an
  attacker bypassing $0.125 fees stays at 2-attestor
  quorum where the sybil attack is cheapest.

- **Implementation shape for future session:**

  **Indexer work:**
  1. New helper `apps/indexer/src/indexer/attestorEligibility.ts`
     with `isEligibleAttestor(account, phase, db)` that
     checks loyalty + age thresholds against the current
     phase's rule (OR vs AND). Returns `{eligible: boolean, reason: string}`.
  2. Config-driven phase: new indexer config key
     `MORPHIT_ATTESTATION_PHASE = 'launch' | 'steady'`
     with default `'launch'`. Operator flips via env var at
     the phase-transition trigger.
  3. Amend `apps/indexer/src/indexer/handlers/feeAttest.ts`:
     at intake, call `isEligibleAttestor()` for the attesting
     account. On rejection, store a new rejection reason
     (`attestor_not_eligible` with a sub-code indicating
     which gate failed) so frontends can explain.
  4. New endpoint `GET /v1/attestor-eligibility/:account`
     returning `{eligible, reason, missing_loyalty: N,
     days_until_eligible: N}` so users can self-check
     before attempting to attest.

  **Client work:**
  1. The fee-attestation UI on order-detail pages calls the
     eligibility endpoint before showing the attest button.
     Non-eligible users see a helpful explanation
     ("Attesting requires 100 BLURT paid OR 30 days on
     chain — you have 47 BLURT paid and 18 days on chain.
     52 days to auto-qualify by age.").
  2. The same explanation appears on `/faq` as a new entry
     linked from `how_to_leave_feedback`-adjacent content.

  **i18n:** ~6 new keys × 10 locales (eligibility-check
  explanation, missing-loyalty hint, missing-age hint, time-
  remaining-until-age hint, 2 rejection-reason messages).

  **Migration data:** the loyalty-milestones and
  account-age data the eligibility check needs already
  exist in the indexer (loyalty tracked via ADR-0011,
  account age from Blurt chain data available through the
  existing accounts table). No new data collection.

  **SECURITY.md:** add a paragraph to the ADR-0011
  threat-model section documenting the sybil defense.

- **Blast radius:** economic. Doesn't affect trade safety
  — buyer and seller still coordinate independently, and
  the buyer has no incentive to trust an unverified order's
  self-claimed price anyway.
- **Rationale for staging:** pure (a)+(b) AND from day one
  would block legitimate early users (who haven't reached
  100 BLURT fees paid AND 30-day age) from attesting during
  the first 90 days, creating a chicken-and-egg where BTC/XMR
  orders can't get attested at all. Staging solves this:
  launch with OR (still blocks farmed socks), tighten to
  AND once the ecosystem has enough naturally-qualified
  attestors. Operator retains manual control of the phase
  flip via config.

### Finding J — release.valid rejection reason discarded — SHIPPED

- **Severity:** LOW (operational visibility gap)
- **Status:** SHIPPED (this session). Schema migration v10
  adds `invalid_reason TEXT` column (nullable for
  back-compat). `release.ts` handler now stores the
  reason instead of discarding it via `void invalidReason`.
  Historical rows keep NULL; new rejections preserve the
  specific classification (signer_not_official_account /
  signer_no_single_posting_key / pubkey_mismatch).
- **Location:** `apps/indexer/src/indexer/handlers/release.ts:148-153`
- **Description:** When a release op is marked
  `valid=false` (wrong signer, or posting pubkey
  mismatch — the two key-compromise signals the audit
  trail is explicitly designed to preserve), the specific
  reason is computed in `invalidReason` but **discarded**
  via `void invalidReason;`. The DB row records `valid=false`
  but not WHY. Operators investigating a potential key
  compromise lose the crucial distinction between
  "someone signed with a stolen key but the right account"
  (pubkey_mismatch — immediate rotation needed) and
  "someone impersonated our account entirely"
  (signer_not_official_account — phishing / no real
  compromise).
- **Fix:** add a `invalid_reason TEXT` column to the
  `releases` table (migration v10) and store the value.
- **Blast radius:** post-incident forensics gap. No active
  exploit.

### Finding K — display_name has no content restriction — SHIPPED

- **Severity:** LOW (impersonation-lite)
- **Status:** All three options shipped.
  - **(a)** Control chars + bidi overrides + zero-width
    characters rejected by `FORBIDDEN_DISPLAY_NAME_CHARS`
    (indexer) and `FORBIDDEN_CODEPOINTS` (client). Was
    already in place; audit note was stale.
  - **(b)** Leading `@` (U+0040) and leading fullwidth
    `＠` (U+FF20) now rejected by both sides. Indexer
    returns `display_name_leading_at`; client returns
    `profile.display_name.errors.leading_at`. Script 47.
  - **(c)** Confusable-script impersonation now rejected.
    New modules `apps/web/src/lib/crypto/confusables.ts` and
    mirror `apps/indexer/src/indexer/confusables.ts`
    implement a ~250-entry hand-curated skeleton table
    (Cyrillic / Greek / fullwidth / small-caps / accented
    Latin / em-dash et al) + a case-insensitive
    reserved-name-impersonation check. Any display_name
    whose skeleton matches a reserved operator handle's
    skeleton is rejected unless byte-identical to the
    canonical form. Indexer returns
    `display_name_impersonates_reserved`; client returns
    `profile.display_name.errors.impersonation`. 30+ tests
    in `confusables.test.ts` covering all substitution
    classes plus negative cases. Script 48. Sync-
    responsibility comment on both sides of the duplicated
    table.
- **Location:** `apps/indexer/src/indexer/handlers/profile.ts`,
  `apps/web/src/lib/crypto/profile.ts`, plus the two
  `confusables.ts` modules.
- **Blast radius:** closed. A future attacker would need to
  find a Unicode character we didn't cover; this is
  defense-in-depth atop the always-rendered identicon,
  not the sole defense.
- **Known limitation (acceptable):** Case-insensitive
  matching on skeletons means a user legitimately wanting
  `MORPHIT` or `Morphit` as their display_name gets a
  false-positive rejection. Tiny false-positive rate,
  large anti-phishing gain — acceptable trade.

### Finding L — unbounded JSONB payload size — SHIPPED

- **Severity:** LOW (DoS amplifier, bounded by chain)
- **Status:** SHIPPED. New shared helper at
  `apps/indexer/src/indexer/payloadSize.ts` exports
  `checkJsonbSize(value)` with a 4KB cap
  (`MAX_JSONB_BYTES = 4096`). 8× the largest legitimate
  payload we emit, half the chain-level ~8KB op limit.
  Byte-length measurement via `TextEncoder` — matches
  what JSONB actually stores (not code-point count).
- **Applied to 5 handlers, 6 JSONB fields total:**
  - `order.ts` + `orderReplace.ts` — `price_model`
    (rejection reason `price_model_too_large`)
  - `chat.ts` — `header`
    (rejection reason `header_too_large`)
  - `profile.ts` — `json_metadata`
    (rejection reason `json_metadata_too_large`)
  - `release.ts` — `hash_manifest` AND `endpoints`
    (rejection reasons `hash_manifest_too_large` /
    `endpoints_too_large`)
- **Key design detail:** the helper returns the
  pre-serialized string on success, and every handler
  passes `v.<field>_serialized` straight to
  `client.query()` instead of re-stringifying. The
  stored JSONB value is byte-identical to what passed
  the size check — no TOCTOU gap where a mutation
  between check and store could slip through.
- **Regression tests shipped for 4 of 5 handlers**
  (order, orderReplace, profile, release). Each test
  constructs a payload past the 4KB cap via
  `'x'.repeat(4100)` padding and asserts both the
  specific `_too_large` rejection reason AND that
  `mock.queries.length === 0` — proving the rejection
  happens at validation time, before the DB write. For
  release.ts this also proves the cap runs before
  chain-side signature-verification RPC reads. Order
  handler gets an additional positive-path test
  ("accepts right under 4KB cap") to catch future
  off-by-one regressions. Chat handler is NOT covered
  because it has no dedicated unit-test file — only
  integration coverage; adding unit scaffolding for
  chat is a separate followup.
- **Location:** `order.ts`, `orderReplace.ts`, `chat.ts` (header),
  `profile.ts` (json_metadata), `release.ts` (hash_manifest,
  endpoints)
- **Description:** Every handler that accepts a JSON
  object passes it through to a JSONB column with no size
  cap. The Blurt chain's custom_json op has a de-facto ~8KB
  limit that gates at intake, but: (a) that limit has
  changed in the past and could change again, (b) if an
  indexer replay ingests a batch of 1000 blocks with
  max-size payloads, the DB could grow unexpectedly, (c)
  JSONB serialization cost is O(size).
- **Fix:** validate serialized-length of each object
  before storing. Cap at e.g. 4KB per object, reject
  larger with `payload_too_large`.
- **Blast radius:** storage inflation + serialization CPU.
  Bounded by chain-level op limits in practice.

### Finding M — CSP `connect-src` allows wildcard `https:` — DECISION LOCKED 2026-04-24

- **Severity:** LOW (defense-in-depth gap, known deferral)
- **Status:** Current plan ratified. Continue waiting for
  `morphit_release_v1` endpoint registry. Hard-coded allowlist
  explicitly **rejected** as the wrong tradeoff today:
  operational maintenance cost (every new community RPC or
  mirror needs a Morphit release) vs. defense-in-depth against
  a threat we're already preventing through Svelte's auto-escape,
  strict input validation, bounded field lengths, and schema
  validation (Findings A, K, L collectively).
- **Location:** `apps/web/svelte.config.js:34`
- **Description:** `connect-src: ['self', 'https:']` lets
  the app's fetch calls reach **any** HTTPS endpoint on
  the internet. Intended to cover community Blurt RPC
  node rotation (`rpc.blurt.blog`, `rpc.blurt.one`, user-
  added mirrors), but acts as a bypass if an XSS payload
  ever lands — an attacker could exfiltrate data to any
  host they control. All other directives are tight
  (`default-src 'self'`, `script-src 'self'`,
  `style-src 'self'`, `object-src 'none'`,
  `frame-ancestors 'none'`).
- **Scheduled proper fix:** switch to an explicit allowlist
  sourced from the community endpoint registry once
  `morphit_release_v1` is populated with enough current
  endpoints that the allowlist is representative. The
  allowlist becomes data-driven from chain state rather
  than hardcoded — self-maintaining as new operators
  publish their endpoints.

- **Revisit trigger (added 2026-04-24):** if **ANY** of these
  conditions hit, re-evaluate whether to ship a hardcoded
  interim allowlist:
  1. **Calendar:** 6 months from this decision (2026-10-24).
     If `morphit_release_v1` still isn't populated, the
     deferral is no longer a "scheduled fix" — it's drift.
     Ship the hardcoded allowlist as an interim.
  2. **Incident:** any reported XSS attempt on a production
     Morphit instance, successful or not. Revisit immediately.
  3. **Operator escalation:** a security audit (external or
     internal), a privacy review for a partner integration, or
     an operator deployment requiring tighter CSP (e.g., a
     hosted Tor hidden service with stricter policy). Revisit
     on request.
  4. **Registry threshold:** `morphit_release_v1` populates
     with ≥5 distinct endpoint entries. At that point the
     registry is representative enough to power a production
     allowlist; ship it.

  **Action:** a calendar reminder should be noted in the
  project's maintenance tracker with the 2026-10-24 date.
  If the project doesn't have a maintenance tracker yet, the
  entry in this document IS the reminder — a future session
  doing a general REVISIT walkthrough will see it.

- **Blast radius:** only matters if an XSS payload ever
  lands. All input-rendering sites auto-escape (Svelte
  `{value}` interpolation, `xmlEscape()` in RSS, sanitized
  SVG rendering via `sanitizeSvg`); XSS is unlikely but
  defense-in-depth matters for a keys-in-browser app.

### Finding N — CSP not documented as a deployment requirement — SHIPPED

- **Severity:** LOW (operational hygiene gap)
- **Status:** SHIPPED. OPERATIONS.md gained two new
  sections:
  - §14 "Deployment topology requirement" — explains
    why the Finding B/E fix depends on an actual
    loopback-proxy deployment, gives a verification
    procedure operators run during setup (curl test
    from another machine to confirm direct-port access
    fails), and documents the `LOOPBACK_PEERS`
    allowlist for off-host-proxy deployments.
  - §15 "Frontend CSP + security headers" — full
    nginx snippet for HSTS, nosniff, referrer-policy,
    DENY frames, and the CSP that mirrors
    `svelte.config.js`. Per-directive explanation of
    what each directive does. HTTPS-only requirement
    with redirect pattern. One-line curl verification.
  - Both sections added to the Contents list at the
    top of OPERATIONS.md.
- **Location:** `docs/OPERATIONS.md` (absent) + frontend
  deployment story
- **Description:** SvelteKit emits CSP as a `<meta http-equiv>`
  tag at build time, which browsers honor. But many
  browsers treat HTTP-header CSP as more authoritative,
  and some contexts (preflight, extensions, SW scope)
  only see HTTP headers. Operators running a node must
  know to serve CSP as an HTTP response header, not rely
  solely on the meta tag.
- **Fix:** add a section to `docs/OPERATIONS.md` under
  "§Frontend deployment" documenting:
  (a) the expected CSP header (copy the values from
  `svelte.config.js`),
  (b) other security headers to set (HSTS, nosniff,
  referrer-policy, DENY frames — the indexer nginx
  config at `ops/nginx/indexer.conf:32-35` is a fine
  reference),
  (c) the serve-over-HTTPS-only requirement.
- **Blast radius:** an operator who stands up a Morphit
  frontend on plain nginx without extra config gets a
  node that's functionally correct but weaker than the
  reference deployment.

### Positive notes (things the audit found done right)

- Parameterized SQL throughout all three apps (with the
  verified-safe SAVEPOINT exceptions noted in Finding C)
- XML escape applied consistently to RSS output
- LIKE-pattern escaping correct with `ESCAPE '\'` clause
- Relay active-key unlock: Argon2id envelope, retry-limited
  passphrase prompt, passphrase scrubbed from memory after
  decrypt, envelope field stripped from Config so no caller
  can re-decrypt
- Create endpoint validation: zod schema, name policy,
  pubkey format, distinctness check, chain-availability
  check, dedupe-before-broadcast, fresh fee fetch
- Drainer failure model: per-row transactions, retry
  ceiling, fail-soft on error-record write, FIFO ordering
- **Frontend key handling is structurally clean.**
  `LiveIdentity` type forbids owner+active privates in
  session memory. `useActiveKey` / `useOwnerKey`
  callback-pattern with `finally`-block scrubbing makes
  it physically impossible for calling code to retain a
  key reference past the signing operation. Memory
  semantics traced end-to-end: `useActiveKey` → `wanted`
  (slice of decrypted priv) → `broadcastOrderWithFee`'s
  `activePriv` (same reference) → signing → `finally`
  scrubs the same buffer. No production call site uses
  the owner key (Phase 5 doesn't need it; the primitive
  exists for future key rotation).
- CSP mode 'hash' correctly covers SvelteKit-emitted
  inline scripts + the pre-paint locale script in
  `app.html`. No `unsafe-inline` or `unsafe-eval`
  anywhere.
- Release-op trust anchor correctly requires BOTH signer
  account match AND on-chain posting pubkey match,
  records rejected releases for audit (key-compromise
  visibility).
- Chat ciphertext handling: indexer stores opaque
  base64, makes no attempt to inspect — E2EE integrity
  preserved at the infrastructure layer.

Three items pulled out during the wrap-up audit that are
not blockers but should be picked up in specific future
sessions.

- **Order-detail CTA — wire to chat when chat ships.**
  `apps/web/src/routes/[x+40][account=account]/[permlink=permlink]/+page.svelte`
  has a paragraph CTA "Interested in this trade? Chat
  with the poster to agree on details and complete the
  trade off-platform. Morphit never holds funds." for
  non-owners on live orders. Today it's just descriptive
  prose — it reads as "contact them however you can"
  rather than promising an in-app chat. When chat ships
  (see `docs/CHAT-UI-DESIGN.md`), this CTA should become

  + scrolls + syncs URL without collapsing the source
  entry. New i18n key `faq.related_label` × 10 locales.
  Relatedness is structural (lives in code, not i18n)
  so translators can't accidentally break the graph.

- **Draft persistence — /post/edit skipped (2026-04-23).**
  The per-order edit flow at `/post/edit/[permlink]` has a
  3-minute edit window enforced by the indexer; after that,
  the order is locked for everything except cancellation.
  A draft-recovery system expiring no sooner than 14 days
  provides negative value there: a stale draft referencing
  an order that's already been locked, cancelled, or
  expired is worse than no draft at all. The compose flow
  at `/post` (minutes of work, no server-side lock) and
  the feedback forms (no time limit) both integrate the
  new draft helper; /post/edit intentionally does not.

- **Draft persistence — chat pickup (pending).**
  When chat UI ships, the compose box should drop in the
  same `$lib/drafts` helper that /post and the feedback
  forms use. Suggested key pattern: `chat.<threadId>` so
  each conversation preserves its own unsent message. The
  private-key redaction-at-write invariant applies for
  free via the helper — no additional work needed at the
  chat-side integration.

- **Draft subsystem shipped this session:**
  - `apps/web/src/lib/drafts/index.ts` — generic helper
    wrapping `safeLocal` with TTL + private-key redaction
    at write + versioned envelope with `savedAt` timestamp
    for "restored from X ago" UI.
  - 33 vitest tests in `apps/web/src/lib/drafts/index.test.ts`
    covering every known failure mode (corrupt JSON, wrong
    version, expired TTL, legacy envelope without savedAt,
    storage unavailable, private-key redaction at every
    string position).
  - `/post` integration with full emerald restore banner.
  - `LeaveFeedbackForm` + `RespondToFeedbackForm` with
    compact one-liner restore indicators (per-order and
    per-feedback keying respectively).
  - i18n keys `post_order.draft.restored_banner` (with
    `{age}` interpolation) and `post_order.draft.discard`
    × 10 locales. Reused by both feedback forms, so the
    two-key footprint covers three integration surfaces.

- **User avatar subsystem shipped (2026-04-23).**
  Users can now replace the default heart identicon with
  an uploaded SVG or raster image, broadcast on-chain in
  the existing profile op's json_metadata bag.

  **What shipped:**
  - `apps/web/src/lib/avatar/index.ts` — sanitizer +
    minifier + raster re-encoder. Sanitization uses a
    strict tag/attribute allowlist with DOMParser, stripping
    `<script>`, `on*=` handlers, `<foreignObject>`,
    `<animate>`, external hrefs, `<image>`, `<filter>`,
    DOCTYPE, comments. SVG output is minified losslessly
    (leading/trailing zero stripping, whitespace collapse,
    prolog strip, empty title/desc removal). Raster path:
    Canvas resize to 96×96 with contain-fit, WebP re-encode
    at quality 0.8, base64 data URI output.
  - `apps/web/src/lib/avatar/index.test.ts` — 40+ tests
    covering every enumerated attack vector in the
    sanitizer plus every minifier rule plus MIME dispatch.
  - Indexer: `MAX_JSONB_BYTES_PROFILE = 8192` (raised from
    4 KB default) on the profile handler only, to match
    the Blurt chain-level custom_json ceiling and make
    room for the avatar alongside other metadata fields.
  - Broadcast path: `ProfilePayload.avatar_svg` and
    `.avatar_data_uri` fields. Empty string is a
    deliberate "clear avatar" signal, so the indexer
    overwrites prior state (omitting the field leaves
    the prior avatar intact, which is the wrong semantic).
  - `IdentityLabel.svelte` renders with priority
    user-SVG → user-raster → heart identicon fallback.
    Profile page hero uses the same priority.
  - Settings page: full upload UI with upfront guidance
    (filetypes, dimensions, SVG tips) shown BEFORE the
    file picker, prominent permanence warning, live
    preview via IdentityLabel, staged state before
    broadcast, byte-size meter with soft warning at 2 KB.
  - 32 new i18n keys under `settings.avatar.*` × 10
    locales = 1203 → 1235 leaves.

  **What's deliberately NOT done:**
  - Orderbook rows + feedback lists continue to show
    identicons, not user-uploaded avatars. They would need
    N+1 profile lookups per render; a batch endpoint is
    a separate design task. For now the profile page is
    the only surface that shows custom avatars. Pattern:
    IdentityLabel callers opt in by passing avatarSvg /
    avatarDataUri props.
  - No path-data compaction in the minifier. Compact
    encoders exist (M10,10L20,20 style) but have subtle
    edge cases around implicit commands; the 5%
    byte-savings isn't worth the risk.
  - No color hex shortening (#aabbcc → #abc).

  **Future work:**
  - Batch profile lookups for avatar rendering on
    orderbook + feedback surfaces. Design question: cache
    ttl, indexer endpoint shape (fetch-many-profiles vs
    push with orderbook response).

  **Verified behaviors (previously listed as future work):**
  - Animated GIF input — already handled correctly. The
    `createImageBitmap` + `drawImage` path extracts the
    first frame and re-encodes as a static 96×96 WebP.
    The uploader copy tells the user the output is
    static, so no expectation mismatch.

- **S14 — local signature verification of chain ops.**
  ~150 lines of crypto + serialization, one extra
  `get_accounts` RPC per verification, multi-sig posting
  authority handling. Defends against single-malicious-RPC
  attack which is already mitigated by endpoint rotation.
  Documented for a future hardening pass. §F.5 details.
- **Local secp256k1 verification of off-chain fee txns
  (BTC/XMR explorer trust).** ⚠️ **RE-SCOPED 2026-05-03
  (Audit Part 26).** Original spec said "secp256k1 verify
  of off-chain fee txns ~150 lines per chain."  Honest
  pushback after investigation: signature verification on
  an explorer-returned tx doesn't actually defend against
  the documented threat (lying explorers).  Anyone can
  produce a perfectly-valid signed BTC or XMR transaction;
  the question is whether it's in the blockchain.
  Verifying inclusion would require SPV merkle proofs
  against a header chain (BTC) or out-of-band view-key
  decryption (XMR) — both substantially bigger than
  ~150 lines, both close to "run your own node" territory
  which the operator-config explorerUrls list already
  permits.

  **What was shipped instead:** txid-echo verification.
  When an explorer returns the right SHAPE but the wrong
  TXID, that's now rejected before the data enters the
  cross-check pool.  Catches buggy explorers, single-route
  errors, and trivial substitution attacks; doesn't catch
  a sophisticated explorer that correctly echoes the
  requested txid but lies about contents (the existing
  two-explorer cross-check is the defense for that).
  Real defensive value, ~30 lines per chain, no operator
  infrastructure burden.  Files: bitcoinExplorerVerifier.ts
  (isExplorerTxResponse takes expectedTxid, lowercases
  for case-insensitive match), moneroExplorerVerifier.ts
  (isOutputsResponse takes expectedTxid, checks data.tx_hash
  if present, accepts absence for compat).  Smoke:
  apps/indexer/scripts/explorer-txid-echo-smoke.ts (6
  scenarios: matching, wrong, upper-case, present, wrong,
  absent).  Documented in AUDIT-2026-05.md Part 26.

  **What's still deferred:** SPV merkle proof for BTC.
  Real defense, but requires header chain storage +
  PoW-validation logic (~500-800 LOC just for the chain),
  and operators willing to allocate disk for headers.
  Worthwhile but firmly post-launch.
- **Featured-bid rate plumbed into post-success upsell.**

  Today a stuck queue entry needs operator manual nullification

  shipped two coordinated changes in `apps/relay/src/queue/drainer.ts`
  + `apps/relay/src/config/index.ts`:

  1. Default `MORPHIT_RELAY_QUEUE_MAX_RETRIES` reduced from 10
     → 3, matching the user spec ("flag for manual review only
     after 3 failures"). Operators can still raise it via env.

  2. Exponential backoff between retries replaces the uniform
     10-minute cooldown. Cooldown grows as
     `INTERVAL '1 minute' * LEAST(POWER(2, error_count), 240)`:
     1m / 2m / 4m / 8m / ... capped at 4h. First attempt
     (error_count=0, broadcast_attempt_at IS NULL) bypasses the
     wait and drains immediately. With max_retries=3, total
     auto-recovery window is ~7 minutes before operator
     escalation; with max_retries=10 (operator-tuned), the cap
     keeps total catch-up time bounded at ~24h.

  Implemented entirely in the SQL `selectPendingLocked` query
  using Postgres native interval arithmetic; no migration
  needed. Failure-and-retry tests are covered by the existing

  new SQL behavior is purely a row-selection filter and the

  Original "~200 lines" estimate was high — Part 117's
  actual fix is ~80 LOC on `/post/edit` + the sentinel
  smoke + REVISIT cleanup; the rest had quietly landed.

- ~~**(Q10 — 2026-05-01) Stranger-fee gate triggers on order
  responses.** When a user posts an order, they are actively

  **✅ CLOSED 2026-05-01 (Q11)** — extended `morphit_chat_v1`

  Stranger-fee gate (layer 2) is bypassed when the field

- ~~**(BATCH14-2 — 2026-05-01) Engagement chip Sybil
  amplification (MEDIUM).** Audit Part 14 §2 found the
  `engagement_24h` chip can be inflated by an attacker
  provisioning sock accounts up to the fan-in rate limit
  (20 distinct senders per recipient per 24h, ~$4 in
  account-creation fees for "+20" on the chip). Mitigation
  options: (a) cap displayed value at "5+" so the absolute
  number isn't a precise signal; (b) only count senders
  with feedback_count ≥ 1 (i.e. senders with at least one
  prior verified trade), reducing sock value because socks
  start with feedback_count = 0; (c) leave as-is and rely
  on Sybil-detection signals (`suspicious_reciprocity`,
  `related_accounts`) to flag the attacker's farm. Option
  (b) is the cleanest — it requires a JOIN we already do
  for the rating chip, so the cost is one extra

  **✅ CLOSED 2026-05-01** — option (b) shipped. Engagement
  aggregate in both `apps/indexer/src/api/orderbook.ts` and
  `apps/indexer/src/api/orderbookStream.ts` now requires
  `EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM feedback fb_eng WHERE fb_eng.subject
  = cm.sender AND fb_eng.order_permlink IS NOT NULL)` for a
  sender to count toward `distinct_senders_24h`. Sock accounts
  with feedback_count = 0 contribute zero. Real counterparties
  with prior trade history pass the filter unchanged. Index
  support: `feedback_subject_idx` covers the EXISTS lookup;
  the partial `chat_messages_order_engagement_idx` still
  drives the outer aggregate. No new migration required.

- **(BATCH14-4 — 2026-05-01) USD-equivalent on benefits
  ladder relies on operator-trust assumption (NOTED).**
  Audit Part 14 §5 — the USD-per-BLURT figure flows from
  `/v1/listing-fee` which is operator-served. A malicious
  operator can lie about the conversion to mislead users
  about how much $1 of BLURT actually costs. This is the
  pre-existing operator-trust boundary; users cross-check
  via federation peers. Documented as a known assumption,
  no code change recommended. Bring back if/when the
  cross-instance price comparison feature lands (which
  would let a frontend automatically flag a wide divergence
  from peer instances).

- **(BATCH14-6 — 2026-05-01) Mint-acts heap-residue
  documentation (LOW).** Audit Part 14 §8 — when the
  unattended timer fires, the active-key passphrase enters
  the V8 heap as a JS string and stays there until garbage
  collection. The mint-acts process is short-lived (~minutes
  per week), but a well-timed memory forensic snapshot
  during a run could expose the passphrase. The relay's
  main service has the same property, so this isn't novel
  — but the mint-acts unit fires more often than a manual
  `systemctl start morphit-relay`, slightly increasing the
  exposure window in absolute terms. **Action**: strengthen
  the OPERATIONS.md "Unattended mode" subsection to call
  out `LoadCredentialEncrypted=` + `systemd-creds` as the
  recommended high-threat-model path. Today the doc
  mentions it as an option; the audit suggests promoting
  it to "recommended for operators handling >$1k weekly
  fee volume" or similar.

- **Finding M — CSP `connect-src` wildcard `https:`.** Decision
