### CLOSED this session stack

- **Finding F — password can't be zeroed in JS.** CLOSED as
  accepted residual risk. See `docs/SECURITY.md` "Known minor
  threat-model items" for the full attacker-model rationale.
  Rejected a Uint8Array refactor because it closes one door in
  a house where every other door is already open at the same
  privilege level — not a meaningful hardening trade. §F
  Finding F.

- **S2 — chat_pub indexer-MITM.** SHIPPED via Option 5
  (chain-anchored TOFU pin). Pin includes `(block_num,
  trx_id, pub)`; rotation paths verify against Blurt RPC,
  not just trust the indexer. Five state-machine branches
  with localized error UX + FAQ deep-link. Active-MITM
  defense covered by vitest test. Full close-out at §F.5.

- **S15 — out-of-window false positive.** SHIPPED. Walking
  10000 history ops (vs. previous 500) so verifications
  reach legitimate-but-old chat-identity ops in active
  accounts. §F.5 details.

- **O18 — replace handler waiver-side bypass.** SHIPPED.
  Replace handler now rejects changes to side / asset /
  fiat_currency.  The 3-min replace window is for editing
  details, not for converting a `waived_first_buy` (buy-only)
  into a free sell listing.  §F.6 details.

- **O19 — fee-reuse across orders via shared external_tx_id.**
  SHIPPED.  Migration v18 adds orders.external_tx_id +
  UNIQUE partial index on (fee_method, external_tx_id).
  Order handler pre-probes for reuse before invoking the
  off-chain verifier and surfaces fee_status='reused' on the
  rejected order.  Closes a real fee-bypass: previously,
  one BTC/XMR payment could be reused across N orders.
  §F.6 details.

- **O27 — featured-bid permlink-collision attack.** SHIPPED.
  Both the featureBid handler's order-existence SELECT and
  the featured-orderbook query were filtering on `permlink`
  alone, but orders are PRIMARY KEY (account, permlink) —
  permlink collisions across accounts could surface the wrong
  account's order in the featured slot.  Both queries now
  constrain on (account, permlink).  §F.6 details.

- **O30 — feature-bid hardcoded rate.** SHIPPED.  The
  FeatureBidForm hardcoded 50 BLURT/hour as a default; if
  an operator configured a different rate, the user
  underpaid.  Added `feature_fee_blurt_per_hour` to the
  /v1/listing-fee API; My Orders page lazy-fetches it on
  feature-bid form open and passes it to the form.  Falls
  back to bundled default if the operator runs an older
  indexer.  §F.6 details.

- **N1 — imported-key users silently denied welcome bonus.**
  SHIPPED.  Feedback handler's UPDATE only matched accounts
  in the `accounts` table, but accounts predating the
  indexer's startBlock or created via channels other than
  the relay (blurt-cli, etc.) had no row.  Switched to an
  INSERT...ON CONFLICT...DO UPDATE pattern matching the
  order handler's waived_first_buy claim.  Honors the FAQ
  promise that every account completing a first trade with
  positive feedback gets the bonus.  §F.7 details.

- **N3 + N6 — dedupe locked legitimate retries.** SHIPPED.
  Original dedupe keyed on key-fingerprint alone, so a user
  who got "name taken in last moment" couldn't retry with a
  different name within 60 sec.  Switched to composite
  (name + keys) and added removeDedupeEntry() called from
  non-already_registered failure paths.  Identical retries
  still blocked; legitimate retries with different name OR
  after broadcast failure now allowed.  §F.7 details.

- **N7 — unsalted IP hash recoverable via rainbow.** SHIPPED.
  Invite token's ip_hash field used bare SHA-256 of an IPv4
  (2^32 input space — trivially recoverable via precomputed
  rainbow table).  Switched to HMAC-SHA256 keyed with the
  relay's per-instance secret.  Off-path observers with
  leaked tokens can no longer recover source IPs.  §F.7
  details.

- **N14 — typo-squat reserved names.** SHIPPED.  Original
  reserved list caught exact-match impersonations only;
  attacker could register `morph1t`, `m0rphit`, `morphlt`,
  `morpit`, `morphit-app`, etc. and impersonate the project.
  Expanded the list with ~20 confusable variants.  §F.7
  details.

- **N19 — Math.random for security-critical PoW target.**
  SHIPPED.  The Altcha PoW service used Math.random
  (xorshift128+) to pick the target number — recoverable
  state from a few outputs would let an attacker predict
  future targets and skip the work.  Switched to
  crypto.randomInt(0, maxnumber).  §F.7 details.

- **N22 — anomaly probe threshold-2 was structurally
  unreachable.** SHIPPED.  The probe's "current ≥ 2× peak"
  check used the relay's peakHourCount, which includes the
  current hour itself — a fresh spike that becomes the new
  peak makes the inequality unreachable.  Real attacker
  scenario: ceiling=100, attacker drives 30 signups in one
  hour against a prior peak of 4; neither threshold-1 nor
  threshold-2 fires.  Added peakHourCountExcludingCurrent
  to the relay ceiling, exposed as peak_other_hours in
  /v1/health, consumed in the probe with backwards-compat
  fallback.  §F.7 details.

- **N23 — drainer double-broadcast on race.** SHIPPED.  The
  relay's queue drainer used a plain SELECT...LIMIT, so two
  drainers in an HA setup would pick up the same rows and
  both broadcast.  Added FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED to the drain
  query (concurrent drainers see disjoint sets), wrapped the
  cycle in a single transaction with savepoint per row.
  Also added schema-v19's broadcast_attempt_at column,
  written BEFORE the chain call, so the residual "broadcast
  succeeded but post-update failed" window doesn't double-
  send either.  §F.7 details.

- **N27 — weak passwords accepted unconditionally.** SHIPPED.
  Onboarding accepted any 8+ char password; user picking
  `password` or `12345678` would proceed and a stolen
  keyfile became trivially brute-forced.  Added a
  lightweight passwordStrength helper (no zxcvbn) that
  catches common passwords, sequential patterns, and
  repeated-character.  Wired non-blocking warnings into the
  UI: red for trivial/common, amber for short, green check
  for 12+.  Did NOT block submission — user's keystore,
  user's choice.  §F.7 details.

- **N28 — Signal A false-positive epidemic.** SHIPPED.  The
  related-accounts detector flagged any pair of accounts
  with same-creator + close-timed first activity.  But the
  Morphit relay creates the vast majority of onboarded
  accounts — every pair of friends signing up back-to-back
  shared creator=@morphit-relay AND had close-timed first
  activity → spuriously flagged.  Their reputation would
  silently weight to zero on each other's profiles.  Added
  excludeCreators option to detectRelatedAccounts; poller
  passes the relay account name.  §F.7 details.

- **R2 — headline `weighted_rating` was unweighted AVG ignoring
  signals tables.** SHIPPED.  SQL field named `weighted_rating`
  but computed `AVG(rating)` with zero filtering.  Sock-puppet
  reviews from `suspicious_reciprocity` and `related_accounts`
  flagged pairs were happily included in the headline
  number users see.  Fixed in BOTH the per-account feedback
  summary endpoint AND the orderbook per-row aggregate via
  CTE excluding flagged pairs (canonical LEAST/GREATEST
  join).  Most consequential fix of this audit — the signals
  tables existed precisely to detect manipulation but were
  being populated and never used in the displayed metric.
  §F.8 details.

- **R5 — multiple feedback responses stacked instead of
  edit-in-place.** SHIPPED.  Handler comment said "we allow
  multiple as edit-in-place"; frontend rendered ALL
  responses in a stacked `<ul>`.  Now renders only
  `fb.responses[0]` (API orders DESC).  §F.8 details.

- **R7 — draft persistence stored unredacted private keys
  in localStorage.**  SHIPPED.  Originally caught in
  LeaveFeedbackForm + RespondToFeedbackForm; widened sweep
  found same bug class in `/post` page (terms + region
  fields) and ChatComposer.  All four now redact at draft-
  save time, not just at broadcast time.  §F.8 details.

- **R8 — display name stored without trim.**  SHIPPED.
  Validation length-checked the trimmed value but stored
  the raw input → `"alice   "` rendered with trailing
  spaces.  Severity: low (UX cosmetic).  Fixed: store
  trimmed.  §F.8 details.

- **R15 — per-feedback list showed all reviews including
  suppressed pairs, but summary excluded them.**  SHIPPED.
  After R2 the headline rating excluded sock-puppet
  reviews — but the per-feedback list still showed them
  with no indication.  User saw "1 review, 5.0★" headline
  next to 4 visible reviews, no explanation.  Now API
  exposes `suppressed: boolean` per item; frontend renders
  flagged items with reduced opacity + an explanatory chip
  linking to the new FAQ explainer.  Indexer-client type
  updated for back-compat.  §F.8 details.

- **R17 — feedback handler didn't verify cited
  `order_permlink` existed or was owned by subject.**
  SHIPPED.  An attacker could spam many feedback rows
  about a target by citing fake permlinks (each unique
  → unique-constraint doesn't dedup → each becomes a
  row).  Handler now verifies an order with
  (account=subject, permlink=order_permlink) exists.
  Generic account-level feedback (NULL permlink) still
  allowed.  §F.8 details.

- **A9 — same-block ordering race breaks first-contact
  admission.**  SHIPPED.  Highest-leverage find of the
  anti-spam audit.  When a user paid a stranger-fee in
  tx_A and broadcast a chat message in tx_B that landed
  in the same Blurt block, the witness could order tx_B
  before tx_A → chat handler ran first, saw no
  `stranger_fees` row yet, rejected with
  `stranger_fee_required`.  The user paid $0.01-$1.28
  for nothing and their first message was silently
  dropped.  Dispatcher pre-pass now stable-sorts
  admission-affecting ops (`block_v1`, `stranger_fee_v1`)
  ahead of admission-consuming ops (`chat_v1`) within
  each block.  Stable sort preserves intra-class order
  so escalation and block/unblock chronology still work.
  §F.9 details.

- **A12 — StrangerFeeModal had no Enter-to-submit on
  password input.**  SHIPPED.  Standard expectation for
  password fields; Enter now triggers onConfirm.
  §F.9 details.

- **A14 — StrangerFeeModal backdrop click + Escape during
  paying phase abandoned the UI mid-broadcast.**  SHIPPED.
  Cancel button was already gated; backdrop click and
  Escape weren't, so the user could click outside or hit
  Escape during the in-flight payment, dismissing the
  modal while the chain transaction still proceeded.
  Both now gated.  §F.9 details.

- **A15 — strangerFeeQuote endpoint had a malformed
  errorBody call.**  SHIPPED.  Passed `'invalid_account'`
  as the code (not in the union) and `400` (number) as
  the message (string expected).  Runtime impact: error
  responses had `message: 400` instead of a human-readable
  string.  Fixed to use `'bad_request'` + proper message
  string.  §F.9 details.

- **A20 — optimistic admission flip immediately undone
  by racing fetchAdmission.**  SHIPPED.  After the user
  paid the stranger-fee, ConversationView optimistically
  flipped admission to `'admitted'` then immediately
  called `fetchAdmission()` which queried the indexer
  before it had ingested the fee block, returning
  `admitted=false` → flipped back to `'needs_fee'` →
  user re-clicked the pay-pill, modal queried fresh
  quote, escalation engaged (just-paid fee was within
  5-min window), saw doubled price ($0.02), confused
  and possibly double-paid.  Removed the racing fetch;
  trust the optimistic flip until next mount of the
  conversation.  §F.9 details.

- **F7 — BTC verifier sumOutputsToFeeAddress didn't
  validate out.value is a finite non-negative number.**
  SHIPPED.  A malicious or buggy explorer returning
  `vout[i].value = NaN` would propagate into observedSats,
  and `NaN < expected` is always false → verifier would
  wrongly return `{ kind: 'verified', observedAmount: NaN }`.
  Defensive validation now skips non-finite/negative
  values.  Both explorers must agree (cross-check), so
  full exploitation requires compromising both Blockstream
  + mempool.space — but the shape guard was leaky and
  worth tightening.  §F.10 details.

- **F11 — price oracle plausibility window too loose.**
  SHIPPED.  PRICE_PLAUSIBLE_MAX_USD was $1.0 (1000× normal
  BLURT trading range).  An attacker compromising an
  oracle to push BLURT/USD = $0.5 would deflate Morphit
  listing fees from ~62.5 BLURT to 0.25 BLURT — Sybil
  orders become almost free.  Tightened to $0.10 (50× normal
  upper range).  Multi-source quorum flagged as future work.
  §F.10 details.

- **S12 — BTC/XMR explorer circuit breakers conflated
  transport failures with data failures.** SHIPPED.  A
  flood of bogus user-supplied txids (404s) would open
  the circuit breaker → legitimate users land as
  `pending_external` even though the explorer is healthy.
  Refactored both `fetchTx` (BTC) and `fetchOutputs` (XMR)
  to return discriminated results.  Only transport_failure
  (5xx, network, timeout, 429) calls recordFailure.  404s
  and malformed bodies don't penalize the explorer's
  reputation.  Defends BTC/XMR fee verification path
  against malicious or accidental DoS.  §F.10 details.

- **F16 — frontend showed raw error text on fee-fetch
  failure.**  SHIPPED.  Replaced with friendly i18n
  message `post_order.fee.error_friendly` × 10 locales.
  Raw error preserved as title attribute for debugging.
  §F.10 details.

- **fees / blurt_benefits FAQ corrections.**  SHIPPED ×
  10 locales.  The FAQ promised a 50% BLURT discount that
  isn't enforced anywhere in code.  Updated to reflect
  actual current behavior (Sybil tier escalation IS
  applied, instant-verification advantage IS real, social-
  capital benefit IS real) and note that the 50% discount
  + loyalty milestones are documented in ADR-0011 as
  roadmap.  Compose screen always shows actual amount.
  §F.10 details.

- **U1.1 — Orderbook didn't filter chain-blocked
  accounts.**  SHIPPED.  The chat conversation list
  AND-merges hidden + blocked sets unconditionally.
  The orderbook was filtering by hidden only, ignoring
  `morphit_block_v1` chain broadcasts.  A user who
  paid the chain fee to broadcast a block against a
  peer would still see that peer's orders in
  `/orderbook` — the strongest moderation signal in
  the system was being ignored on its most-traveled
  surface.  Fixed: orderbook imports `blockedAccounts`
  + `loadBlocks` (only fired when authenticated, anon
  viewers get an empty set), AND-merges both stores
  in `visibleItems` and `hiddenInView`, renders a
  distinct "Blocked" marker (rose vs the gray
  "Hidden"), suppresses the per-row Hide button on
  already-blocked rows (it's redundant with their
  existing block).  New i18n key
  `orderbook.blocked_marker` added across all 10
  locales.  Note: FeaturedOrders.svelte on the
  homepage still doesn't filter — a separate UX-care
  decision because the homepage hero needs deliberate
  empty-state handling.  Documented as residual.
  §F.22 details.

- **U2.1 — Orderbook filter inputs didn't NFC-
  normalize.**  SHIPPED.  Post-§F.21 O3.4 the indexer
  NFC-normalizes stored `location_region`,
  `payment_methods` items, and `terms` at write time.
  The orderbook's read-side filter inputs (
  `apps/indexer/src/api/orderbook.ts`) didn't.  A user
  typing decomposed-form filter input (e.g.,
  `e\u0301` instead of `\u00e9`) wouldn't match
  their own NFC-stored orders — silent UX failure.
  Fix: `.normalize('NFC')` applied to
  `q.location_region` and each token in
  `q.payment_methods.split(',')` before SQL
  composition.  Mirrors the §F.21 write-side
  discipline on the read-side surface.  §F.23
  details.

- **O3.3 — feedback + feedbackResponse comments lacked
  NFC normalization.**  SHIPPED.  Same NFD-codepoint-
  stretch class as O3.1 but applied to the 256-codepoint
  comment-length cap rather than a homograph regex.  A
  chain-direct attacker submitting decomposed-form
  comment text (e.g., 256 NFC-chars expressed as 512
  codepoints with combining diacritics) bypassed the
  visual-length cap as designed.  Low-impact (the
  attacker only stretches their own visible content),
  but matches the unified hardening posture across
  profile, operatorRegister, and now feedback.  Fix
  shipped to both `feedback.ts` and `feedbackResponse.ts`
  with one-line `normalize('NFC')` calls before the
  codepoint-count check; the normalized value is what
  gets stored, so DB queries on comment text collide
  consistently for visually-identical strings.  2 new
  smoke scenarios in feedback-handler-smoke.ts cover
  the NFC-normalize happy path and bidi-override
  rejection.  §F.21 details.

- **O3.4 — order + orderReplace text fields lacked
  control/bidi/ZWJ filtering and NFC normalization.**
  SHIPPED.  `location_region`, `terms`, and
  `payment_methods` items in both order op handlers
  accepted any non-control-char-restricted strings.
  Profile, feedback, operatorRegister all enforce a
  forbidden-char regex against control chars (C0/C1),
  bidi-override marks (U+202A–202E, U+2066–2069), and
  zero-width joiners — order op handlers did not.  A
  chain-direct attacker submitting `\u202E` (RIGHT-TO-
  LEFT OVERRIDE) in any of the three fields could
  visually flip rendering of adjacent order data in
  orderbook UI surfaces — making prices appear
  different, payment methods confused, or the buy/sell
  side of the order misleading.  Each field is rendered
  in multiple surfaces (orderbook rows, my-orders,
  featured orders, order-detail card), all auto-escaped
  by Svelte (XSS-safe) but bidi-permissive.  Fix:
  introduce `FORBIDDEN_TEXT_CHARS` constant in both
  `order.ts` and `orderReplace.ts`, apply NFC
  normalization + forbidden-char filter to all three
  fields.  4 new scenarios in order-handler-smoke
  (covering all three fields' reject paths + NFC
  normalization happy path) and 3 new vitest scenarios
  in orderReplace.test.ts (mirror).  §F.21 details.

- **O3.5 — chatRead `last_read_at` accepted non-strict
  ISO 8601.**  SHIPPED.  `new Date()` is permissive
  and engine-dependent: it accepts US-style `12/31/2099`,
  human formats like `December 15, 2025`, date-only
  strings without time component, and other engine-
  specific edge cases.  Different JS engines (V8 vs
  SpiderMonkey vs JSC) parse ambiguous strings
  differently — not a current consensus risk because
  the indexer is Node-only, but the strict shape
  eliminates the surface for engine-specific parsing
  attacks and protects against accidental future port
  to a different runtime.  Order handler already uses
  a strict regex; chatRead diverged.  Fix: apply the
  same regex to chatRead's `last_read_at` validation.
  New chatRead.test.ts file with 12 scenarios covering
  payload shape, peer validation, self-chat rejection,
  ISO format strict-mode (4 reject paths × 3 accept
  paths), time-bound checks, and happy path.  §F.21
  details.

- **O3.1 — indexer profile handler missing NFC
  normalization → NFD-decomposed homograph escape.**
  SHIPPED.  The frontend `validateDisplayName`
  normalizes input via `s.normalize('NFC')` BEFORE
  running `impersonatesReservedName`.  The indexer's
  profile handler did not — it called `dn.trim()` and
  immediately ran the homograph regex.  The regex
  character classes contain precomposed forms like
  `\u00e9` (é) but NOT the bare `e` + combining-acute
  `\u0301` two-codepoint sequence.  A chain-direct
  attacker (blurt-cli, non-Morphit client) submitting
  `morphit-fe\u0301e\u0301s` — which renders identical
  to "morphit-fées" but is byte-different — slipped
  through the impersonation check.  Fix: NFC-normalize
  at the top of `validate()`, BEFORE all subsequent
  string checks.  Also makes the codepoint-count check
  meaningful (NFC-canonical length = user-perceived
  length).  Symmetrical to operatorRegister.ts which
  was fixed in §F.18 but kept the issue alive on the
  user-profile path.  Test rot fix: existing
  profile.test.ts had a "4KB cap" test that still set
  4100-char payload after the cap was bumped to 8KB —
  test would fail in real vitest; fixed alongside.  21
  vitest scenarios + 18 tsx-smoke scenarios cover the
  fix path including the precise NFD-homograph
  scenario.  §F.20 details.

- **O3.2 — `avatar_data_uri` shape not validated at
  receive time → tracking-pixel exfiltration via
  `<img src>`.**  SHIPPED.  Pre-fix, `profileProps`
  accepted any non-empty string for `avatar_data_uri`
  and passed it to `IdentityLabel` which renders
  `<img src={value}>`.  A chain-direct attacker (or
  malicious indexer) could set this to
  `https://tracker.example/pixel.gif` — when a Morphit
  user views any surface containing the attacker's
  avatar (orderbook row, chat list, profile page),
  the browser issues a GET to the attacker's URL,
  leaking the user's IP and the Morphit page URL via
  Referer.  Fix: `safeValidateDataUri` regex check
  requires `data:image/(webp|png|jpeg|gif);base64,...`
  shape with hard 16KB length cap.  SVG explicitly
  excluded — must come through `avatar_svg` →
  `sanitizeSvg`.  Defense-in-depth alongside G2.2's
  SVG re-sanitization: same trust-boundary logic on a
  parallel field.  10 vitest scenarios cover reject
  paths (https URL, javascript:, data:text/html,
  data:image/svg+xml, oversize, malformed base64) and
  accept paths (each permitted MIME).  §F.20 details.

- **O2.1 — onboarding leaks LiveIdentity private bytes
  on all exit paths.**  SHIPPED.  `generateIdentity()`
  returns `{full: snapshot, live}` where `snapshot` is
  independently allocated via `cloneFullIdentity` but
  `live` references `original.posting/memo` (NOT shared
  with snapshot — the snapshot's clone has its own
  Uint8Array allocations).  When onboarding finishes
  (success path: bootFromEnvelope creates a FRESH
  FullIdentity from envelope decrypt, so the store's
  live is independent of local `live`) or aborts
  (onConfirmLeave navigation guard), `wipeFullIdentity
  (full)` zeros the snapshot but `live = null` only
  drops the reference — the original's posting/memo
  private bytes linger in heap until GC.  Same K1.2
  class of session-long key residue, on a different
  code path.  Same bug in onboarding/import (seed-
  path): `importIdentityFromSeed` returns
  `{full, live}` and the page captured only `full`,
  silently discarding `live` without wiping.  Fix:
  import `wipeLiveIdentity` in both pages, call it
  before nulling `live` on every exit path (success
  + abort + import-success + import-error).
  §F.19 details.

- **O1.1 — operator display_name validation weaker
  than user profile validation.**  SHIPPED.  Pre-fix,
  `operatorRegister` rejected control / bidi / ZWJ
  chars but allowed leading-@ (display_name like
  "@morphit-fees" is a literal account-handle
  impersonation), allowed Cyrillic homographs of
  reserved names, and didn't NFC-normalize before the
  codepoint length check.  User profiles already
  enforce all three.  Operators are higher-trust than
  regular users — making operator names a STRONGER
  anti-impersonation surface, not weaker, is the right
  gradient.  Fix: mirror user-profile validator into
  `apps/indexer/src/indexer/handlers/operatorRegister.ts`.
  NFC normalize, leading-@ rejection (ASCII +
  fullwidth ＠), `impersonatesReservedName` check.
  4 new smoke scenarios in
  `apps/indexer/scripts/operator-register-handler-smoke.ts`
  cover all three new rules.  §F.18 details.

- **O1.2 — operator contact_url permitted http://
  (downgrade) and frontend rendered without
  noreferrer.**  SHIPPED.  Pre-fix, `operatorRegister`
  accepted both `http:` and `https:`, letting an
  operator publish a downgrade link that fingerprints
  the user via plain HTTP when clicked.  Userinfo
  (`https://user:pw@host/`) was also accepted — a known
  phishing pattern.  Frontend rendered with `rel=
  "noopener nofollow"` but not `noreferrer`, leaking
  the morphit operator-page URL to the destination
  via the Referer header.  Fix: indexer rejects
  non-https schemes (new `contact_url_bad_scheme`
  semantics — was bad scheme before, now strictly
  https-only) and rejects userinfo with new
  `contact_url_has_userinfo` reason.  Frontend adds
  a render-time `validateContactUrl` helper (defense
  in depth: re-check https + no-userinfo + length cap
  parallel to G2.2's SVG re-sanitization pattern) and
  upgrades rel attribute to `noopener noreferrer
  nofollow`.  3 new smoke scenarios cover the http,
  javascript:, and userinfo cases.  §F.18 details.

- **K1.2 — BIP-39 mnemonic in JS heap as immutable
  string.**  SHIPPED.  Pre-fix, `FullIdentity` carried
  `seed: string` (the mnemonic).  JS strings can't be
  zeroed; the mnemonic survived in the heap for the full
  session, retrievable by an attacker with memory access
  (browser exploit, malicious extension) and re-derivable
  into all four key roles.  Post-fix: `FullIdentity`
  carries `seedBytes: Uint8Array` (16-byte BIP-39
  entropy for 12-word, 32-byte for 24-word).  The
  mnemonic STRING is reconstructed on demand by
  `mnemonicForBackup(full)` only at the moment of
  display-for-backup; once converted, the user is reading
  it from the screen anyway.  `wipeFullIdentity` zeroes
  seedBytes.  `toLiveIdentity` zeroes the source
  identity's seedBytes (LiveIdentity doesn't carry it).
  `useJitKey` zeroes seedBytes after each unlock.
  Single canonical schema — pre-shipping Morphit means no
  legacy keystore migration burden; old `seed: string`
  format dropped cleanly.  Onboarding's seedWords
  derivation now uses mnemonicForBackup.  3 vitest
  scenarios in `apps/web/src/lib/crypto/crypto.test.ts`:
  mnemonic round-trip via seedBytes (different identity
  factories produce same keys from same entropy);
  wipeFullIdentity zeroes bytes; round-trip preserves
  entropy through encrypt/decrypt.  §F.15 details.

- **K1.3 — no in-app password change.**  SHIPPED.
  Pre-fix, users with a compromised password had to
  Sign Out → re-import seed → choose new password to
  rotate — clunky and error-prone.  Post-fix: a "Change
  password" subsection in Settings (gated by
  `hasPersistedKeystore` — same gate as auto-lock,
  password-mode users only) accepts current + new +
  confirm passwords, JIT-decrypts the envelope with the
  current password, re-encrypts with the new password,
  persists, and updates the in-memory store.  Live
  session preserved — no re-sign-in.  All-or-nothing:
  decryption-with-old must succeed before any state
  changes; persistence and store update happen after
  the new envelope is fully built so a mid-process
  failure leaves the user's old password still
  working.  18 new i18n keys × 10 locales = 180 strings
  added.  Strength scorer surfaces 'common'/'trivial'
  warnings (advisory, doesn't block submission — same
  policy as onboarding).  Discriminated-union error
  classification: password_empty, new_password_too_short,
  same_password, locked, bad_old_password, internal —
  each with a dedicated localized message.  §F.16
  details.

- **Cross-tab unlock state propagation.**  SHIPPED.
  Pre-fix, tab 1 calling `reset()` (sign out) wiped the
  persisted envelope but tab 2's in-memory live identity
  stayed alive — user "signed out" in one place but not
  another.  Worse for password change: tab 1 rotates the
  password, tab 2 still holds the old envelope reference,
  and the next JIT unlock there would fail with a
  confusing "wrong password."  Post-fix: identity store
  registers a `storage` event listener that mirrors
  envelope changes from other tabs.  Three cases handled:
  envelope deleted (other tab signed out) → reset() here
  too; envelope value changed (password change) → swap
  envelope reference, keep live keys intact (subsequent
  JIT unlocks need new password); corrupted JSON in
  payload → ignored, no state change (graceful
  degradation, the OLD envelope remains valid).
  KEYSTORE_ENVELOPE_STORAGE_KEY exported from
  persistentKeystore.ts so the listener can target the
  right key.  5 vitest scenarios in
  `apps/web/src/lib/stores/identity.test.ts` covering
  all three cases plus unrelated-key and already-locked
  edge cases.  §F.17 details.

- **K1.1 — keystore envelope's `kdfParams` field
  unauthenticated, footgun for future regressions.**
  SHIPPED.  Pre-fix, the envelope stored opslimit +
  memlimit in clear, the decrypt path used libsodium's
  INTERACTIVE constants regardless, and the stored
  values were essentially audit aids.  But a future
  refactor that "uses what's in the envelope" instead
  of `argonParams()` would silently accept attacker-
  tampered ops=1 mem=8K, enabling cheap brute force on
  the password.  Fix: `decryptIdentity` now refuses
  envelopes whose claimed kdfParams are below safe
  minimums (1 op, 1 MB memory) — well under any
  legitimate libsodium INTERACTIVE output, well above
  any value an attacker could exploit for speed-up.
  Defensive belt-and-suspenders.  4 vitest scenarios
  added to `apps/web/src/lib/crypto/crypto.test.ts`
  covering low-ops, low-mem, missing-params, and the
  normal-params happy path.  §F.14 details.

- **K1.4 — no size cap on imported keyfile.**  SHIPPED.
  Pre-fix, `blobToEnvelope` would call `blob.text()` on
  whatever the user selected — a 10 GB file would hang
  the browser allocating the buffer before any
  validation kicked in.  Real Morphit envelopes are
  ~1 KB.  Fix: `blobToEnvelope` rejects blobs over 64 KB
  with a clear error, before reading the text.  Cap is
  64x typical envelope size — plenty of headroom for
  format growth, plenty under the pathological-import
  zone.  2 vitest scenarios added covering oversize
  rejection and normal-size happy path.  §F.14 details.

- **G2.1 — orderbook & profile reputation aggregates
  counted no-permlink feedback as completed trades.**
  SHIPPED.  Pre-fix, the orderbook's LEFT JOIN on the
  feedback aggregate counted EVERY feedback row toward
  feedback_count and weighted_rating, regardless of
  whether it cited an order_permlink.  After §F.12's
  G1.1 fix (welcome bonus requires order_permlink), an
  attacker who couldn't extract bonuses anymore could
  still inflate their visible orderbook reputation by
  having confederates sign untethered positive feedback.
  R2's sock-puppet detection catches REPETITIVE pairs
  (suspicious_reciprocity + related_accounts) but not
  "real distinct human writes vague positive feedback
  for stranger they never traded with."  Fix: both
  the orderbook aggregate (`apps/indexer/src/api/
  orderbook.ts`) and the profile feedback summary CTE
  (`apps/indexer/src/api/feedback.ts`) now filter
  `WHERE feedback.order_permlink IS NOT NULL`.  The
  feedback list endpoint still returns no-permlink
  rows so users can see them in the per-row list;
  they just don't drive the summary count or the
  orderbook ranking signal.  Coherent end-to-end:
  untethered feedback exists, doesn't trigger the
  bonus, doesn't pump reputation.  Integration test
  mirror updated; 2 G2.1-targeted scenarios added to
  `apps/indexer/test/integration/orderbook-join.test.ts`.
  §F.13 details.

- **G2.2 — frontend trusted indexer-supplied avatar_svg
  without re-sanitization.**  SHIPPED.  Pre-fix, the
  IdentityLabel component inlined `avatar_svg` from
  indexer profile data via Svelte's `{@html}` directive
  with the trust assumption "the broadcast path
  sanitized it."  Two real attack paths bypassed that
  assumption: (a) a malicious indexer (anyone running
  their own Morphit instance) could return arbitrary
  hostile content, (b) the chain doesn't enforce
  sanitization, so a profile op submitted via a non-
  Morphit client could deliver unsanitized SVG.  Either
  path renders to a live XSS in the user's session,
  with full session-key theft potential.  Fix: the
  `extractLabelPropsFromProfile` helper (the central
  identity-extraction site) now re-sanitizes
  avatar_svg via `$lib/avatar`'s `sanitizeSvg` before
  returning.  All consumers — orderbook rows, profile
  page reviewer/responder labels, the profile-page hero
  itself — go through the same gate.  The profile page
  hero, which previously used hand-rolled
  `$derived.by(...)` blocks bypassing the helper, now
  also routes through `extractLabelPropsFromProfile`.
  Defense in depth — even if the broadcast path's
  sanitization is bypassed somehow, the receive path
  catches it.  7 G2.2-targeted vitest scenarios added
  to `apps/web/src/lib/indexer/profileProps.test.ts`
  covering: <script> stripping, event-handler removal,
  javascript: URL stripping, foreignObject stripping,
  unparseable-SVG → null, non-SVG content → null,
  clean SVG roundtrip preservation.  §F.13 details.

- **G1.1 — welcome bonus triggerable without
  order_permlink proof of trade.**  SHIPPED.  Pre-fix,
  any signed `morphit_feedback_v1` op with no
  `order_permlink` would flip the subject's
  `first_trade_complete_at` and queue 10 BLURT liquid + 10 BLURT Power.
  Sybil pair could sign mutual no-permlink positive
  feedback for a net 14 BLURT + 20 BP per pair while the
  relay also paid each 3-BLURT account_creation_fee.
  Post-fix, the bonus path is gated on `orderPermlink !==
  null` (the permlink is already validated upstream as
  existing AND owned by the subject — that's R17's
  defense, repurposed here).  Feedback without an order
  citation still goes through (legitimate uses: chat-
  only first contact, post-reputation general feedback)
  but doesn't trigger the bonus.  FAQ updated × 10
  locales to clarify "your counterparty signed feedback
  citing the specific order they traded with you."  New
  smoke `apps/indexer/scripts/feedback-handler-smoke.ts`
  with 5 G1.1-targeted scenarios catches the bug if
  ever reverted.  §F.12 details.

- **G1.2 / G1.7 — drainer per-row defenses.**  SHIPPED.
  RelayQueueDrainer.processRow now (a) caps
  `amount_blurt` at 10,000 and `amount_bp` at 10,000
  before broadcasting (legitimate writers max out at 10
  BLURT for welcome bonus and 1260 BP for cumulative
  loyalty milestones; cap catches DB corruption or
  future writer bugs), and (b) validates the `reason`
  field against `^[a-z0-9_:-]{1,64}$` before building
  the broadcast memo (catches control chars, very long
  strings, accidentally-injected weirdness).  Both are
  defense-in-depth — no current writer would trigger
  them.  New smoke
  `apps/relay/scripts/drainer-defense-smoke.ts` with 17
  scenarios covering both caps + reason validator.
  §F.12 details.

- **G1.3 — low-balance scanner counted rejected ops as
  activity.**  SHIPPED.  Pre-fix, the scanner's "active
  Morphit user" filter was `EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ops
  WHERE signer = a.name AND block_time >= $cutoff)`.
  Sybil could sign cheap-RC malformed/rejected ops to
  keep their activity timer alive for repeated 1-BLURT
  dust refills.  Post-fix: filter adds
  `AND o.status = 'applied'`.  Rejected ops still appear
  in the event log for forensics, but no longer count
  toward the activity threshold.  §F.12 details.

- **G1.4 — drainer FIFO ordering non-deterministic for
  same-block events.**  SHIPPED.  ORDER BY clause was
  `created_at ASC`, no tie-breaker; two queue rows
  written in the same op (e.g. welcome_bonus_liquid +
  welcome_bonus_vesting from the same feedback handler
  call) had undefined ordering.  Not a correctness issue
  — both broadcast eventually — but logs and operator
  debugging benefit from determinism.  Post-fix:
  `ORDER BY created_at ASC, id ASC`.  §F.12 details.

- **G1.5 — lowBalanceScanner.queueRefill no concurrency
  guard.**  SHIPPED.  Pre-fix, two indexer processes
  pointed at the same DB (HA setup) could both
  selectCandidates → balance-fetch → queueRefill the
  same recipient before either's INSERT landed.  Result:
  recipient gets 2× refill in one cycle.  Post-fix:
  queueRefill uses `INSERT ... SELECT ... WHERE NOT
  EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM relay_pending_transfers WHERE
  recipient = $1 AND reason = 'dust_refill' AND
  created_at >= $cooldown)` — atomic check-and-insert.
  Concurrent scanners both attempt the INSERT; only the
  first sees an empty NOT EXISTS and inserts; the second
  sees the first's row and gets a no-op rowCount=0.
  No error, no duplicate.  §F.12 details.

- **G1.6 — witness-fee poller doc-comment misleading
  post-§F.11.**  SHIPPED.  Doc said "tracks the chain's
  account_creation_fee so its listing fee can adjust"
  — true under §F.10 dynamic-fee model, false under
  §F.11 BLURT-native model.  Refreshed to describe its
  actual current role: pure operator-telemetry, alerting
  on changes to the witness fee that affect cost-of-
  attack for Sybil defense, no live consumer of the
  cached value beyond /v1/health and operator
  dashboards.  §F.12 details.

- **F6 / F17 — ADR-0011 dynamic-fee architectural gap.**
  CLOSED by deletion.  The unimplemented dynamic-fee
  formula (`computeBaselineListingFee`,
  `computeExpectedFee`, account-creation-fee amortization,
  operational margin) — flagged in §F.10 as architectural
  debt — has been DELETED from the codebase under the
  §F.11 BLURT-native fee refactor.  Listing fees are now
  denominated directly in BLURT (60 BLURT default), and
  the static-vs-dynamic divergence is moot because there
  is no dynamic formula.  The FAQ that previously
  rationalized "50% BLURT discount" as roadmap has been
  rewritten to explain the actual model.  §F.11 details.

- **BLURT-native fee model.**  SHIPPED.  Listing fees
  (60 BLURT default), stranger fees (5 BLURT base, 640
  BLURT cap), and frontend fee verification all now use
  BLURT amounts directly — no live USD conversion in the
  critical path.  Eliminates the price-oracle attack
  surface that S1/S2/S3/F11 mitigated (mitigations stay
  but are now defense-in-depth on an opt-in display
  feature, not the broadcast critical path).  Witness
  fee polling demoted to operator telemetry.
  `MORPHIT_INDEXER_PRICE_FEED_ENABLED` defaults to false;
  fresh deployments make zero outbound HTTP calls for
  pricing.  §F.11 details.

- **Monero-positioning UX shift.**  SHIPPED ×
  10 locales.  User-visible "BLURT" replaced with
  "network fee" where BLURT was just plumbing.  FAQ
  entries `fees`, `blurt_benefits`, `welcome_bonus`,
  `first_order_free`, `order_fee_rejected` rewritten to
  lead with BTC/XMR comfort and frame BLURT as the
  underlying ledger's coordination unit, not a feature.
  Compose-page fee picker now pre-selects XMR/BTC fee
  method when the user picks XMR/BTC as the trade asset.
  §F.11 details.

- **stranger_fees.amount_usd_equivalent column dropped.**
  SHIPPED via schema-v20 migration.  The column was a
  USD-denominated record of what the client quoted at
  send-time using the live price feed.  Under the BLURT-
  native refactor it became redundant — the
  `amount_blurt` column already records the actual
  transferred amount, which is now the protocol unit.
  §F.11 details.

- **Fee tolerance tightened 1% → 0.1%.**  SHIPPED.
  Previously the band absorbed both floating-point
  rounding AND price-drift between quote and broadcast.
  Under the BLURT-native model there is no price drift
  to absorb, so the band is now FP-rounding-only.  This
  closes a small theoretical underpayment window:
  previously a $0.125 USD fee at $0.002 BLURT/USD = 62.5
  BLURT, and the indexer accepted as little as 61.875
  BLURT (~1% short).  Now the indexer accepts as little
  as 59.94 BLURT against a 60 BLURT expected — purely
  for FP rounding from `Math.ceil(amount * 1000) / 1000`
  on the frontend.  §F.11 details.

- **O18 — replace handler waiver-side bypass.** SHIPPED. Replace
  now rejects changes to side / asset / fiat_currency. The
  3-minute window is for editing details, not for converting
  a waived buy into a free sell. §F.6 details.

- **O19 — fee-reuse across orders via shared external_tx_id.**
  SHIPPED. Migration v18 adds external_tx_id column + UNIQUE
  partial index on (fee_method, external_tx_id). Order handler
  pre-probes for reuse and inserts rejected rows with
  fee_status='reused'. One off-chain payment, one listing.
  §F.6 details.

- **O27 — featured-bid permlink-collision attack.** SHIPPED.
  Both the featureBid handler's order-existence SELECT and
  the /v1/orderbook/featured JOIN now constrain on
  (account, permlink) — orders are PRIMARY KEY (account,
  permlink) so a bare permlink isn't unique. §F.6 details.

- **O30 — feature-bid hardcoded rate.** SHIPPED.
  /v1/listing-fee API exposes feature_fee_blurt_per_hour;
  My Orders page lazy-fetches it and passes to FeatureBidForm.
  §F.6 details.

### Future optimization: worker-based libsodium for full RAM release

(Tracked here as a future optimization, not a session blocker.)

Current posture: once a user opens any chat route, the chat
crypto module chunk (~few hundred KB including libsodium WASM)
stays resident in the tab for its lifetime. ES modules are
intentionally not garbage-collected per the JavaScript spec —
navigating away from `/chat` releases Svelte components, the
chat controller's private key material (via explicit `memzero`),
and CPU work (polls stop), but the module code and libsodium
WASM heap remain.

A full-cleanup path exists: move libsodium-backed crypto into
a dedicated Web Worker. When the user navigates away from the
last chat surface, `worker.terminate()` reclaims both the WASM
memory and the chat crypto module. Startup cost would be ~5-10ms
extra on the first encrypt/decrypt after opening a conversation.

Not shipping this now:
- Current baseline cost is small and fixed (doesn't grow over a
  long session of opening many conversations — libsodium is
  already used for auth/keygen regardless of chat).
- Worker-based libsodium is a nontrivial refactor (postMessage
  protocol for every crypto call, async boundary through
  chatService deps, test harness changes).
- Other items in the §G backlog are higher priority.

  LTR-only assumptions could break fa (RTL). The remaining
  review work is a human-with-a-browser pass: open /en, /fa,
  /zh-HK in dark mode at mobile width and confirm the icons
  look right next to their localized labels, and that the
  grayscale→color transition is smooth. Requires manual
  review by a human at a screen. §C.

- **Finding K option (c) — confusable-script detection —
  SHIPPED (2026-04-23).** Hand-curated ~250-entry
  confusables skeleton table covering Cyrillic / Greek /
  fullwidth / small-cap / accented Latin / confusable
  dashes. Duplicated as mirror modules on frontend
  (`apps/web/src/lib/crypto/confusables.ts`) and indexer
  (`apps/indexer/src/indexer/confusables.ts`) because
  `@morphit/indexer-client` is types-only and extracting
  a runtime-shared package isn't worth the build-chain
  cost at this scale. Sync-responsibility comment on
  both sides. `impersonatesReservedName()` check is
  case-insensitive — so `MORPHIT-FEES` in Latin caps and
  `morphit-fеes` with Cyrillic `е` are both rejected,
  with the legitimate operator's canonical-lowercase
  form preserved via a byte-equality escape. Wired into
  `validateDisplayName` on both sides with new reason
  codes `display_name_impersonates_reserved` (indexer)
  and `profile.display_name.errors.impersonation`
  (client). 30+ new tests in `confusables.test.ts`
  covering every substitution class + negative cases
  (byte-equal reserved passes through; partial overlap
  passes through; unrelated names pass through). i18n
  key fanned out across 10 locales (script 48);
  parity 1236 → 1237.

- **Finding K (c) expansion — substring matching, leetspeak,
  agorise/kencode — SHIPPED (2026-04-23).** Per user directive
  "don't let anyone use the words morphit/morphit-relay/
  morphit-fees/agorise/kencode in any part of their display
  name or username, not any form including lookalike characters
  regardless of case, such as using #1 for lowercase l."
  Rewrote `confusables.ts` on both sides:
    - `LETTER_EQUIVS` table — per-letter equivalence classes
      (a-z plus hyphen) each listing every visual equivalent
      (Cyrillic, Greek, fullwidth, small-cap, accented, plus
      leetspeak digits/symbols).
    - `compileReservedRegex(name)` builds a case-insensitive
      regex from the equivalence classes.
    - `impersonatesReservedName(input)` is now SUBSTRING
      semantics — any position in the input that matches any
      reserved regex triggers a reject, with a byte-equality
      escape for canonical-lowercase reserved names.
    - `RESERVED_NAMES_RAW` now includes `agorise` and `kencode`
      alongside the 7 morphit variants (9 total).
    - Leetspeak digits: `0→o, 1→i/l, 3→e, 4→a, 5→s, 7→t, 2→z,
      6→b, 9→g/q`, plus symbol confusables `@→a, !→i, |→l,
      +→t, $→s, _→-`.
  Wired into username registration as a client-side veto in
  `apps/web/src/routes/onboarding/register-name/+page.svelte`
  using the existing `rejected` reason code (i18n copy "That
  name is reserved. Pick another." applies correctly). Note
  that the username veto is BEST-EFFORT — Blurt is an open
  chain and someone using a different client can still
  register an impersonation directly; only the display_name
  check (which flows through our custom_json op and is
  enforced at the indexer) is authoritative.
  Updated display_name impersonation error copy across 10
  locales to widen "a Morphit operator account" →
  "a reserved project account" (accurate given Agorise +
  Kencode now reserved; doesn't enumerate names so attackers
  don't get a target list). Script 49; parity unchanged at
  1237 (update-in-place).
  Test count grew to 40+ in `confusables.test.ts` with
  full attack-class coverage (Cyrillic, Greek, fullwidth,
  small-cap, accented, em-dash, underscore, all case
  variants, every leetspeak digit, symbol substitution,
  mixed combinations, substring embedding for every
  reserved name).

- **SEO route-registry audit + drift fix — SHIPPED (2026-04-23).**
  Discovered via drift-audit session. Three concrete issues found
  and fixed:

  1. **`/onboarding/register-name` had a broken <Head /> component.**
     The page was passing `title={...}` and `description={...}` as
     props to Head, which only accepts `routeKey`. Svelte silently
     dropped the unknown props, and Head tried to resolve
     `seo.undefined.title` — which svelte-i18n renders as the literal
     string "seo.undefined.title". The `<title>` tag on that page was
     literally broken in production. Fix: added `seo.register_name`
     to all 10 locales (moved from the already-translated
     `onboarding.register_name.head_*` keys) and changed the page
     to `<Head routeKey="register_name" />`. Script 50.

  2. **`apps/web/src/lib/seo/routes.ts` was stale.** Registry had 13
     routes; app had 22. Missing: `/operators`, `/privacy-terms`,
     `/run-a-node` (all three legitimate indexable landing pages
     that should have been in the sitemap), plus 6 user-specific /
     dynamic routes (non-indexable but needed for Head tag coverage).
     The three missing public pages were invisible to search engines
     via sitemap discovery. Fix: registry now lists all 23 real route
     entries with appropriate `indexable` / `priority` / `changefreq`
     flags. Docstring updated to reflect reality (Head component
     takes `routeKey` directly; registry's role is to enforce that
     every route HAS a matching `seo.<key>.*` i18n key).

  3. **`scripts/build-sitemap.mjs` duplicated the route list.** The
     script had its own hardcoded array with a comment admitting
     "Duplicated (not imported) from src/lib/seo/routes.ts ... a CI
     check in Phase 3 can diff them." We're past Phase 3; the CI
     check didn't exist; the two lists had silently drifted (script
     missed `/operators`, `/privacy-terms`, `/run-a-node`). Fix:
     script still has its own ROUTES array (Node can't import `.ts`
     without a build step) but now calls `assertRoutesInSync()` at
     build time. It parses `routes.ts` as text, extracts the
     indexable subset via regex, and compares. Drift raises an
     explicit error before `vite build` proceeds. Verified by
     injecting a fake route and confirming the build hard-fails
     with a clear message. The prebuild hook runs this check, so
     CI catches drift automatically on every build.

  4. **Added `apps/web/src/lib/seo/routes.test.ts`** with 13 tests
     covering: non-empty paths/keys, key + path uniqueness, priority
     bounds, allowed changefreq values, every route has
     `seo.<key>.{title,description}` in en.json, reverse-drift check
     (every seo.* i18n key has a matching ROUTES entry), dynamic
     routes never indexable, `routeFor` lookup + trailing-slash
     normalization + undefined for unknowns.

  **Sitemap impact:** was 110 URLs (11 routes × 10 locales); now
  140 URLs (14 routes × 10 locales). Three landing pages that
  existed for weeks are now search-engine-discoverable.

  - Profile map state: plain Record<string, ProfileResponse | null>
    rather than Map, because Svelte 5 $state handles deep-update
    reactivity well on plain objects and the template idiom

- **Chat UI — session 1 of 1-2 SHIPPED (2026-04-23).**
  First session of the chat UI per docs/CHAT-UI-DESIGN.md. Everything
  EXCEPT real crypto — the design-doc says "the polling loop works
  without real crypto (decrypts fail silently, messages show as
  '(encrypted)' placeholders) — which actually gives a useful staging
  story where the UI can ship ahead of the crypto work." That's what
  this session does.

  **Type-drift fix (the chat scaffold):**
  - Removed `orderPermlink` from `ChatSession`, `CiphertextEnvelope`,
    `createSession`, `restoreSession`, `loadConversation`,
    `sendMessage`. The scaffold's types referenced per-order sessions;
    the live `morphit_chat_v1` op + `/v1/chat/:a/:b` endpoint both
    treat conversations as per-pair (between two accounts, independent
    of orders). Per-pair is authoritative — design doc confirms, and
    the on-chain op has no order field. Scaffold still throws
    `NotImplementedError` for every function.
  - `CiphertextEnvelope.header` is now `Record<string, unknown>`
    (was `string`) so the UI can attach `client_tag` directly into
    the header object as the design doc specifies.

  **Conversation controller (`chatService.ts`, ~631 lines):**
  - `createConversationController(deps)` factory returns a
    `ChatController` with `start()`, `destroy()`, `sendMessage(text)`,
    `retryMessage(localSeq)`, `snapshot()` methods.
  - State machine for `LocalMessage`:
    `pending → broadcast → confirmed` (happy path) or
    `pending → broadcast → failed` on broadcast error.
    Retry sends a NEW `client_tag` (previous broadcast may have
    actually landed; a new tag keeps the retry distinct on-chain).
  - `client_tag` generation: 16 random bytes → 32-char hex, placed
    in `header.client_tag`. Reconciliation by tag on each poll merges
    server records into matching local pending/broadcast messages.
  - Poll cadence: 3s visible / 15s hidden via
    `document.visibilityState`, with ±500ms jitter. Immediate re-poll
    on visibility-flip-to-visible.
  - ID-based dedup across repeated polls (endpoint's cursor is
    for pagination backward, not "since" mode; TODO noted for a
    future server "since" mode).
  - `decryptOrPlaceholder()` returns `'(encrypted)'` stub text until
    `chat decrypt API` is implemented. When it lands, one
    one-line change in this module wires the real call.
  - Broadcast payload uses placeholder ciphertext `'c3R1Yg=='`
    (base64 of "stub") so the on-chain write path actually exercises.
    The handler accepts it (it's valid base64 ≥ 1 char); the
    recipient sees "(encrypted)", as designed.
  - `runtimeDeps(me, peer, getLiveIdentity)` factory fills in
    browser/network deps for runtime callers; test harness
    substitutes mocks for every dep.

  **chatService tests (`chatService.test.ts`, 20 cases):**
  send→broadcast transition, send failure→failed, locked identity,
  whitespace trim, client_tag match/mismatch, incoming peer message,
  ID dedup across repeated polls, chronological sort (pending at
  end), retry with new tag, retry on non-failed (no-op), 3s visible
  cadence, 15s hidden cadence, visibility flip-to-visible re-poll,
  destroy cleanup, idempotent start/destroy, onChange emission count.
  Uses `vi.useFakeTimers` + `vi.setSystemTime` for timing assertions;
  mocks fetch + broadcast + visibility; asserts snapshot state at
  each transition.

  **ProtectedTextarea enhancement:**
  - Added `onkeydown?: (event: KeyboardEvent) => void` prop so the
    chat composer can implement Enter-to-send / Shift+Enter-newline
    without bypassing the private-key detection overlay. Existing
    callers unaffected (all omit the prop).

  **UI components (3 new):**
  - `ChatMessage.svelte` — single bubble. Outgoing aligned right
    with brand-emerald tint, incoming left with neutral tint.
    pending/broadcast: full opacity, NO timestamp (by design — don't
    train users to expect a distinct confirmation for normal sends;
    only failures warrant prominence). confirmed: timestamp shown.
    failed: red ring, error text, Retry button. "(encrypted)"
    placeholder shown italic + muted until encrypted-chat decrypt lands.
    Takes `me` prop for outgoing detection; sender comparison is
    explicit + correct.
  - `ChatComposer.svelte` — text input. ProtectedTextarea +
    PrivateKeyWarningModal, exactly matching the feedback-response
    pattern. Enter=send, Shift+Enter=newline. Live codepoint

  - `ConversationView.svelte` — assembles message list + composer.
    Uses `height: 100svh` + flex column for iOS-keyboard safety

    design doc: auto-scroll-to-bottom on load + after own send +
    when new message arrives AND user is already at bottom;
    "N new messages ↓" pill when scrolled up + new message arrives.
    Owns the controller's lifecycle (created onMount, destroyed

  **Routes (2 new):**

  **Design decisions worth recording:**
  - Encrypted-chat type drift resolved by treating design doc + live
    indexer as authoritative (both per-pair). Alternative (update
    design doc to match the chat scaffold's per-order model) would have
    required redesigning the on-chain op. Per-pair wins because
    the op already ships and the design doc is newer.
  - Inbox stub rather than DIY crawl of custom_json history: the
    latter would work but needs Blurt RPC plumbing that's not
    justified when a proper endpoint is planned. The recent-peers
    list is good-enough UX for a user who's actively chatting.
  - Client-side ID dedup rather than pushing for a server-side
    "since" cursor: 50 records × small payload × every 3s is a
    minor bandwidth cost; server change would cost more than it
    saves at v1 scale.
  - Message button uses an anchor `<a href>` rather than a button
    + goto() — SSR-safe and preserves middle-click-to-new-tab.

## H. Signup-drain defense stack — SHIPPED 2026-04-24

User request: "make it essentially impossible for the attacker
to just register thousands of accounts just to hurt us."
Rephrased to an achievable target: bounded, detectable fast,
reversible. Six-layer defense, documented in OPERATIONS.md §18.

### Layers shipped

1. **Kill-switch** — `MORPHIT_RELAY_SIGNUP_ENABLED=false` halts
   both /v1/account/invite and /v1/account/create with 503
   `signups_disabled`. Comment in config labels this the
   "blurt faucet" for new-account registration where we pay
   the blurt fee — per user request 2026-04-24.

2. **Global daily ceiling** — `GlobalDailyCeiling` module
   (`apps/relay/src/policy/globalDailyCeiling.ts`). UTC-midnight
   rollover. One-shot `CEILING_REACHED` alert via AlertSink.
   Default 50/day, env-configurable
   (`MORPHIT_RELAY_SIGNUP_DAILY_CEILING`). Tracks hourly peaks
   for the anomaly detector.

3. **Per-IP spacing** — new `Limiter.allowWithSpacing()` method
   with discriminated result (`{allowed:true}` / `{reason:
   'quota_exhausted'}` / `{reason: 'spacing', retryAfterMs}`).
   Default 60 min gap
   (`MORPHIT_RELAY_CREATE_SPACING_MINUTES=60`). User-facing
   copy: "You recently created an account. Please wait N more
   minute(s) before creating another." (User-edited from
   original "from this connection" 2026-04-24.)

4. **Signed invite tokens** — `InviteTokenService`
   (`apps/relay/src/policy/inviteToken.ts`). HMAC-SHA256
   signed, 10-min TTL, IP-hash bound, single-use via nonce
   Map. Secret ephemeral per-boot unless
   `MORPHIT_RELAY_INVITE_HMAC_SECRET` set. Two-step flow:
   client POSTs /v1/account/invite first, then
   /v1/account/create with invite_token in body.

5. **Altcha PoW** — `AltchaService`
   (`apps/relay/src/policy/altcha.ts`) server-side +
   `apps/web/src/lib/auth/altchaSolver.ts` client. SHA-256
   proof-of-work, self-hosted, NO Cloudflare. Triggered on 3rd
   invite per IP per UTC day
   (`MORPHIT_RELAY_ALTCHA_TRIGGER_COUNT=3`, trigger kept at 3
   after explicit user decision 2026-04-24). Client is
   **lazy-loaded** via `await import('./altchaSolver')` — only
   users who hit the 3rd attempt download ~2KB gzipped of PoW
   code. Runs in a Web Worker with embedded pure-JS SHA-256
   (the FIPS 180-4 implementation is ~60 lines inline in the
   worker source string, spawned via Blob URL for bundler-
   agnostic portability). Main thread stays responsive on old
   Android.

6. **Anomaly-aware LOW_BALANCE alerts** —
   `signupAnomalyProbe.ts` fetches relay `/v1/health?verbose=1`
   when the operator-balance scanner fires `LOW_BALANCE` on
   the relay account. Heuristic: current UTC hour ≥ 1/3 of
   daily ceiling OR current hour ≥ 2× today's peak hour AND
   ≥ 5 signups → recommend kill-switch. Wired into Poller's
   scanner config via
   `MORPHIT_INDEXER_RELAY_HEALTH_URL`. Empty string disables
   the probe (default) for deployments where indexer can't
   reach relay.

### Decisions recorded

- **Altcha trigger count: 3** (not 2). Rationale: scenario C
  (legitimate user retries after a network blip or name typo)
  should not hit PoW on what feels to them like the first
  real signup. Moving from 3 → 2 mostly hurts legitimate
  retry-after-failure users while barely affecting the
  attacker's economics, since attackers use many IPs each
  doing ≤2 invites (below the trigger either way).

- **Altcha self-hosted, NO Cloudflare Turnstile.** User
  requirement: "ABSOLUTELY NO RELIANCE ON (OR CALLS TO)
  CLOUDFLARE, EVER." Self-hosted Altcha gives us PoW without
  phoning home.

- **Altcha widget text localized to all 10 locales.** Three
  leaves added (`onboarding.register_name.altcha.verifying`,
  `.verified`, plus 6 new error codes). i18n parity
  maintained at 10/10 (1196 leaves now).

- **Client-side solver lazy-loaded in a Web Worker.** User
  requirement: "we want the site to be lightning fast, even
  on old devices." Design:
  - `altchaSolver.ts` imported only via `await import()` from
    `signupClient.ts`, so non-PoW users never download it
  - Pure-JS SHA-256 in a Web Worker (not `crypto.subtle.digest`
    — that API is async-per-hash and serial-awaiting 2M times
    is ~10× slower than a tight synchronous loop)
  - Worker spawned via Blob URL, no bundler-specific worker
    configuration required
  - Main thread never blocks during the ~1-2s solve

- **"You recently created an account."** User rewrote this
  from "You recently created an account from this connection."
  — less technical, friendlier. Applied in en.json and all 9
  other locales.

- **Global daily ceiling configurable via env var.** User
  request: "i will need an easy way to edit that, say in a
  config file or something (and a notification that the limit
  has been hit)." `MORPHIT_RELAY_SIGNUP_DAILY_CEILING=50`
  default, one-shot alert on hit.

### Ships-but-tested-gaps to flag

- Relay tests for invite, altcha, ceiling, inviteToken all
  typecheck-clean and their logic is verified by careful
  read. Not vitest-runtime-verified in this sandbox (no
  vitest binary available).
- `apps/relay/test/create.test.ts` was bulk-rewritten for the
  new 9-arg constructor + auto-injected invite tokens in
  `post()`. Typecheck-clean but semantic checks were eyeball-
  verified (dedupe test, malformed_operation test, rate-limit
  tests all still make sense in the new flow).
- The anomaly probe is wired but not yet exercised against a
  live drain. The heuristic (1/3 of ceiling in one hour OR
  2× today's peak + ≥5) is conservative-by-design; false
  positives (nag once on a legitimately busy hour) are
  preferred over false negatives.

### What this buys (honestly)

- **Browser-based attacks**: fully blocked (Origin allowlist,
  no path for a foreign frontend).
- **Server-side Origin forgery**: rate-limited + PoW-gated +
  ceiling-capped. Cost per signup non-trivial.
- **Undetected drain**: anomaly detector catches it within
  one 15-min scan cycle.
- **Unstoppable drain**: kill-switch is one env-var flip.

What it does NOT do: cryptographically prevent a determined
attacker with large residential-proxy pool + PoW-solving
capacity from draining up to the daily ceiling. That's the
stronger form ("shared-secret token baked at build time");
deferred to future work. The current stack gets to "cannot
be catastrophically harmed" — worst-case $10/day loss at
50-ceiling, detectable and reversible.

### Files touched

Server (relay):
- `apps/relay/src/policy/globalDailyCeiling.ts` (new)
- `apps/relay/src/policy/inviteToken.ts` (new)
- `apps/relay/src/policy/altcha.ts` (new)
- `apps/relay/src/api/invite.ts` (new)
- `apps/relay/src/api/create.ts` (refactored — 9-arg ctor,
  invite verification, ceiling bookkeeping, spacing check)
- `apps/relay/src/api/health.ts` (signup_stats in verbose)
- `apps/relay/src/middleware/ratelimit.ts` (allowWithSpacing)
- `apps/relay/src/middleware/origin_enforcement.ts` (extended
  to cover /v1/account/invite)
- `apps/relay/src/config/index.ts` (7 new env vars)
- `apps/relay/src/main.ts` (wiring, shutdown)
- `apps/relay/test/*` — `altcha.test.ts`, `inviteToken.test.ts`,
  `globalDailyCeiling.test.ts`, `invite.test.ts` (all new),
  `create.test.ts` (bulk-updated)

Server (indexer):
- `apps/indexer/src/indexer/operatorAccountBalanceScanner.ts`
  (signupAnomalyProbe integration, SignupAnomaly payload on
  LOW_BALANCE)
- `apps/indexer/src/indexer/signupAnomalyProbe.ts` (new —
  buildSignupAnomalyProbe factory + judgeAnomaly)
- `apps/indexer/src/indexer/poller.ts` (probe wired when
  MORPHIT_INDEXER_RELAY_HEALTH_URL is non-empty)
- `apps/indexer/src/config/index.ts` (relayHealthUrl)

Frontend:
- `apps/web/src/lib/auth/altchaSolver.ts` (new, lazy-loaded
  Web Worker PoW solver)
- `apps/web/src/lib/auth/signupClient.ts` (new, two-step
  orchestration with lazy altcha import)
- `apps/web/src/routes/onboarding/register-name/+page.svelte`
  (refactored to use the two-step flow, phase-aware busy
  label, messageArgs interpolation for spacing_cooldown)
- `apps/web/src/lib/i18n/locales/*.json` (10 locales, +8
  leaves each)

Docs:
- `docs/OPERATIONS.md §18` (full defense stack documentation
  with tuning playbook)
- `docs/REVISIT-LIST.md` (this entry)

## I. Orderbook reputation filters + 4-trade sprout — SHIPPED 2026-04-24

User request in three parts: (1) "can i also filter the orders by
user reputation? i'd like to see what the top traders are
offering," (2) implicit question about whether multiple filters
could be combined ("can i add more than one filter at a time"),
(3) "is_new_trader (green sprout) should show for their first 4
trades imo."

### Decisions recorded

- **Combined sort + filter approach, not just filter.** A naive
  "top traders only" reputation filter punishes new sellers by
  hiding them before they can earn their first review. Instead:
  - A **sort** option (recent / rating / trades) keeps everyone
    visible but surfaces top-traders-first when chosen.
  - An **optional discrete min_trades filter** (Any / ≥5 / ≥20)
    for users who actively want to narrow. Defaults to Any.

- **No "minimum stars" filter.** Too gameable (an account with
  2 five-star reviews looks elite but means almost nothing) and
  unfairly punishes good traders with occasional grumpy
  reviewers. Trade count is a sturdier proxy for "has a track
  record."

- **Sprout semantic shift: feedback_count < 4 instead of
  first_trade_complete_at IS NULL.** The welcome-bonus trigger
  still fires ONCE on the first review (that's what the
  accounts.first_trade_complete_at column is for — unchanged).
  The orderbook sprout chip is now purely a UI signal derived
  from feedback count. A trader sees 🌱 for their first four
  completed-trade reviews, giving newcomers a visible grace
  window instead of having the chip vanish the moment their
  first review lands.

- **Multi-filter combination was already shipped.** All five
  original filters (side, asset, fiat, region, payment methods)
  already AND'd together in `currentQuery()`. The new
  min_trades + sort stack with them — same AND semantics, same
  debounced refetch. Nothing to "unlock."

- **Inline reputation chip next to trader name, not clickthrough.**
  Previously users had to click into each trader's profile to
  see their rating — that's friction on every browsing
  decision. Now each orderbook row shows "★ 4.8 (23)" inline
  on first paint. Zero extra network calls — the data joins in
  the same query as the orders.

- **Sample-size cue on low-count chips.** When
  feedback_count < 3, the rating chip renders in muted grey
  instead of emerald. Same data, weaker visual signal —
  nudges the reader toward "take this rating with a grain of
  salt" without hiding it.

- **Both chips can stack.** A trader with 1-3 reviews shows
  BOTH sprout 🌱 AND the rating chip. This is deliberate:
  "young, but has a track record" is exactly what the reader
  wants to see.

### What shipped

Indexer (`/v1/orderbook`):
- New query params: `min_trades` (integer 0-100, treated as
  "≥N feedback rows") and `sort` (recent / rating / trades).
- LEFT JOIN on aggregated feedback subquery. SELECT projects
  `feedback_count` and `weighted_rating` per row.
- `is_new_trader` derivation moved to `COALESCE(f.c, 0) < 4`.
  The obsolete `accounts` LEFT JOIN removed entirely.
- Sort-aware cursor: encodes the sort mode (`s`) and the
  sort-value fields (`r`, `c`) so cursor-continuation requests
  under the same sort resume correctly. Mismatched sort
  returns 400 (frontend clears cursor on filter/sort change,
  so the mismatch case is cosmetic).
- Three ORDER BY paths depending on sort mode; tiebreakers
  always `updated_at DESC, account ASC, permlink ASC` for
  stable pagination.

Shared types (`packages/indexer-client`):
- `OrderRecord.feedback_count?: number` and
  `weighted_rating?: number | null` added.
- `OrderbookQuery.min_trades?: number` and
  `sort?: 'recent' | 'rating' | 'trades'` added.
- Doc comment on `is_new_trader` updated to describe the
  4-trade window.

Frontend:
- `RatingChip.svelte` — new component. Renders emerald chip
  at count ≥ 3, muted chip at count 1-2, hidden at count 0.
  Format: "★ 4.8 (23)". ICU-pluralized aria label.
- `apps/web/src/routes/orderbook/+page.svelte` —
  - New reactive state: `minTrades: 0 | 5 | 20` and
    `sortMode: 'recent' | 'rating' | 'trades'`.
  - `currentQuery()`, `$effect()` refetch, and `clearFilters()`
    all include the new state.
  - Two-column grid UI for the new controls under the
    payment_methods field.
  - Clear-filters conditional extended.
  - RatingChip wired into the per-row IdentityLabel area,
    next to NewTraderChip. Both can show simultaneously.
- `apps/web/src/lib/indexer/client.ts` — both getOrderbook
  and getOrderbookFromOrigin URL builders extended with
  min_trades (elided at 0) and sort (elided at 'recent').

Integration test rewritten: `apps/indexer/test/integration/
orderbook-join.test.ts`. The old file's ORDERBOOK_SELECT
constant referenced the now-obsolete `accounts` LEFT JOIN —
a silent drift had the integration coverage going stale. The
rewrite mirrors the new SQL shape, adds `seedFeedback()` and
`seedOrder()` helpers, and covers:
- zero feedback → sprout + null rating
- 1-3 feedback → still in sprout window
- exactly 4 feedback → sprout closes
- weighted_rating accuracy (ratings 4,5,5,5 → 4.75 average)
- min_trades=5 filter composition
- sort=trades and sort=rating ordering (rating includes
  NULLS LAST)
- fee_method default back-compat guard
- mixed-population (each row gets its own stats)

i18n × 10 locales: 11 new leaves:
- `orderbook.filters.{min_trades_label, min_trades_any,
  min_trades_5, min_trades_20, min_trades_hint, sort_label,
  sort_recent, sort_rating, sort_trades}`
- `orderbook.order.{rating_aria, rating_tooltip}` (ICU plural
  on `count`, interpolates `{rating}` + `{count}`)

Parity 10/10 at **1207 leaves** (was 1196, +11).

### Ships-but-tested-gaps

- Frontend typecheck clean; visual layout of the 2-column
  filter grid + the inline chip position next to the trader
  name are code-level correct but not browser-verified in
  this sandbox.
- Integration test typechecks clean but isn't vitest-runtime-
  verified (no Postgres in sandbox). When an operator runs
  the integration suite, the sort=rating test uses
  NULLS-LAST ordering which Postgres supports natively —
  should pass on any Postgres ≥ 8.4.
- No schema migration required — feedback table exists since
  ADR-0010 and `feedback_subject_idx` already supports the
  aggregation. The LEFT JOIN subquery aggregates the whole
  feedback table once per orderbook query; at live-order
  scale (thousands) this is fine. If feedback grows into the
  millions, a materialized summary per account becomes
  worthwhile — pre-compute on the feedback ingest path, read
  from a summary table on the orderbook query.

### What this buys the user

- "I'm curious what else we can filter on": the orderbook
  already had 5 filters combining via AND; now 7 (+ sort).
- "See what top traders are offering": sort=rating surfaces
  them without hiding newcomers.
- "Sprout for first 4 trades": newcomers have a visible
  grace window that matches their actual ramp-up.
- Zero extra network calls per orderbook load for the
  reputation data — joined server-side in the same query.

### Files touched

Indexer:
- `apps/indexer/src/api/orderbook.ts` (refactored query,
  schema, row shape, cursor)
- `apps/indexer/test/integration/orderbook-join.test.ts`
  (rewritten)

Shared:
- `packages/indexer-client/src/index.ts` (OrderRecord +
  OrderbookQuery extended)

Frontend:
- `apps/web/src/lib/components/RatingChip.svelte` (new)
- `apps/web/src/routes/orderbook/+page.svelte` (filter UI +
  RatingChip integration + new state)
- `apps/web/src/lib/indexer/client.ts` (URL builders)
- `apps/web/src/lib/i18n/locales/*.json` (10 locales, +11
  leaves each)

Docs:
- `docs/REVISIT-LIST.md` (this entry)

## Finding H triad — chat anti-spam layers 1+3 — SHIPPED 2026-04-24

Closes the block-list and rate-limit halves of the Finding H
belt-and-suspenders design. Layer 2 (stranger-fee + Requests
tab) remains pending as a future session.

### What shipped

**Layer 1 — block list** (indexer + frontend, end-to-end):

- New on-chain op: `morphit_block_v1` with
  `{ v: 1, blocked, action: "block" | "unblock", ts }`.
- Indexer schema v15: `blocks` table with composite PK
  (blocker, blocked), `state` column (blocked/unblocked,
  preserves audit on reverse), since_* anchors to the original
  block decision, last_action_* moving with each op.
- Indexer handler `apps/indexer/src/indexer/handlers/block.ts`:
  state-machine semantics — fresh block inserts, fresh unblock
  rejects with `no_prior_block`, idempotent re-block/re-unblock
  is a no-op with no DB mutation, block-after-unblock rewinds
  since_* (new relationship), unblock-after-block preserves
  since_* (original audit stays valid).
- Chat handler gate: before INSERT, consult `blocks` with a PK
  lookup; reject with `recipient_blocked_sender` if the
  recipient has blocked the sender.
- Public endpoint `/v1/blocks/:account` returning the caller's
  current block list (not audit history; that's available via
  blocks.blurtwallet.com by trx_id).
- Frontend op builders `broadcastBlock` / `broadcastUnblock` in
  `apps/web/src/lib/blurt/ops/block.ts`.
- Client-side session store `apps/web/src/lib/chat/blocks.ts`
  with lazy load, optimistic updates, and `refreshBlocks` hook.
  Not persisted to localStorage — a stale list on session open
  is a worse lie than a one-roundtrip fetch.
- Conversation header Block/Unblock button with phase-aware
  label and red-on-blocked styling. Confirmation via native
  `confirm()` (UX debt — a Morphit-styled ConfirmDialog is a
  later polish).
- Settings → Blocked Accounts section with list + per-row
  unblock, refresh button, empty state, locked-session hint.
- i18n × 10 locales: 8 new leaves under `chat.block.*` and 10
  under `settings.blocked_accounts.*`.

**Layer 3 — rate limits** (indexer-only):

- Two complementary caps evaluated in the chat handler BEFORE
  insert, both gated on "recipient has not replied":
  - `FAN_IN_UNIQUE_SENDERS_24H = 20`: rejects
    `recipient_fan_in_exceeded` when more than 20 unique
    never-replied senders have messaged this recipient in the
    last rolling 24h (including this new sender).
  - `PER_PAIR_NO_REPLY_CAP = 50`: rejects
    `sender_no_reply_cap_exceeded` when the same sender already
    has 50+ never-replied messages to this recipient.
- Both caps lift the moment the recipient sends anything back
  to the sender. A real conversation is never throttled.
- Single SQL round-trip computes both counters against
  existing indexes (`chat_messages_recipient_idx`,
  `chat_messages_sender_idx`).

### Decisions recorded

- **Block UX: we do not notify the blocked user.** The op is
  public on Blurt — anyone scraping the chain can learn of it
  — but Morphit's product surface deliberately doesn't tell
  the blocked party. Raising awareness of the block turns it
  into a provocation vector. Documented in OPERATIONS /
  Settings copy.

- **State column instead of DELETE.** Blocks can be reversed
  by posting an unblock op, and the row stays with
  state='unblocked' as audit trail. Round-trip block→unblock→
  block is idempotent AND preserves history; DELETE-on-unblock
  would lose that.

- **since_* anchor semantics.** On block-after-unblock, since_*
  rewinds to the new op (it IS a new relationship from a UX
  standpoint — the user chose to re-engage the block). On
  unblock-after-block, since_* stays put (the original
  decision's chain anchor is still valid historical audit).

- **Per-recipient rate-limit values chosen permissively.**
  20 unique new senders per 24h is well beyond any normal
  user's inbound first-contact rate; 50 messages from one
  stranger with no reply is far past the point where a
  legitimate user would have replied or blocked. Both values
  catch flood-scale abuse, not routine noise.

- **"Without a reply" is forever, not a window.** Once the
  recipient replies, the caps lift permanently for that pair.
  No window-based re-enablement. Rationale: a reply is the
  strongest possible signal of consent; re-imposing caps later
  would be confusing ("why can't I message Alice anymore?
  We've been talking for years").

- **Rate limit query runs BEFORE block-list check?** No —
  block-list check runs first. A blocked sender's message
  never touches the rate-limit path. That's correct: a
  blocked user who's been spamming shouldn't push legitimate
  senders toward the fan-in cap. Checking `blocks` first
  effectively excludes blocked-sender messages from the
  rate-limit bookkeeping.

- **Per-pair count uses COUNT(*), not DISTINCT.** If one
  sender sends 50 messages and the recipient replies once
  between messages 40 and 41, the NULL branch fires and
  subsequent messages are uncapped. If we used DISTINCT on
  some field we'd be narrowing the semantics arbitrarily;
  raw COUNT is what the decision says.

### Honest gaps

- **Chat handler tests for rate-limit gates not yet
  extended.** The existing `chat.test.ts` covers the pre-gate
  behavior. The new reject paths (fan_in, no_reply_cap)
  need coverage. Typecheck-clean but not runtime-verified for
  the new paths.

- **`confirm()` dialog on block action is UX debt.** Works
  correctly; a custom Morphit dialog would be nicer. Not
  tracked as a finding — just noted so the next UX pass can
  swap it.

- **Layer 2 — stranger-fee — not shipped.** Next session.
  Requires: `morphit_stranger_fee_v1` op, `stranger_fees`
  table, BLURT transfer verification against @morphit-fees,
  price-feed conversion for the $0.01 USD equivalent,
  Requests tab in inbox, first-contact modal. Strictly
  additive to what's shipped here.

- **Migration test for schema-v15 not asserted.** The
  migration is registered and will run; no integration test
  confirms the table shape matches expectations. Low risk —
  the SQL is simple and typecheck-verified — but worth an
  integration test when layer 2 lands (both layers' tables
  can be verified together).

- `apps/indexer/src/db/migrations.ts` (v15 registration)
- `apps/indexer/src/indexer/handlers/block.ts` (new)
