## Finding H triad — chat anti-spam layer 2 (stranger-fee, indexer side) — SHIPPED 2026-04-24

Completes the indexer-side Finding H defense. All three layers
are now runtime-verified end-to-end; layer-2 frontend (modal,
Requests tab, op builder) remains pending as a future session.

### What shipped this pass

**New op: `morphit_stranger_fee_v1`.** Payload `{ v: 1,
recipient, amount_usd_equivalent }` paired with a sibling
Blurt `transfer` op carrying BLURT to `morphit-fees` with memo
`morphit-stranger:<recipient>`.

**Indexer schema v16: `stranger_fees` table.** Composite PK
`(sender, recipient)`, paid_* audit anchors, amount_blurt +
amount_usd_equivalent columns recording the actual paid amount
and what the client quoted. `stranger_fees_sender_idx` for
"what pairs have I paid for?" reverse lookups.

**Stranger-fee handler** (`apps/indexer/src/indexer/handlers/
strangerFee.ts`). Validates payload, checks for existing row
(idempotency), finds the sibling transfer via name/from/to/
memo/amount matching, verifies BLURT amount ≥ $0.01 USD
equivalent using `ctx.priceSource.current()` with
`ctx.config.feeTolerance`, inserts. Translates PK collision
(23505) into idempotent success for the race case where two
ops land in the same block.

**Chat handler layer-2 gate.** Three-condition admission: a
message is admitted if ANY of the following hold:
  1. Recipient has ever sent a message to sender (real
     conversation partner).
  2. Sender has a prior admitted message to recipient
     (deploy-safety: pre-existing conversations stay
     unbroken).
  3. A stranger_fees row exists for the pair (fee paid).

Reject reason: `stranger_fee_required`. Evaluated in one SQL
round-trip via an OR of two EXISTS clauses.

**Dispatcher wiring.** Both indexer and frontend OP_IDS
registries gained `strangerFee: 'morphit_stranger_fee_v1'`.

**Test coverage.**
- `apps/indexer/test/handlers/strangerFee.test.ts` — 17
  vitest cases covering validation, idempotency, fee
  verification (happy path, missing transfer, wrong memo,
  wrong to, wrong from, underpaid, over-paid, price-feed
  zero, price-feed NaN). Typecheck clean.
- `apps/indexer/test/handlers/chat.test.ts` extended with
  layer-2 gate cases (admits when admitted, rejects
  stranger_fee_required when not). Length assertions
  corrected for the new SQL round-trip.
- `apps/indexer/scripts/stranger-fee-handler-smoke.ts` —
  15/15 scenarios passing at runtime.
- `apps/indexer/scripts/chat-handler-smoke.ts` — extended
  to 11/11 scenarios including layer-2 reject path.

### Decisions recorded (layer 2 specific)

- **Memo format `morphit-stranger:<recipient>`.** Binds each
  paid transfer to a specific recipient, so one $0.01
  transfer can't be replayed to pay for messaging 100
  different people. Follows the `morphit-feature:<permlink>`
  and `morphit-listing:<permlink>` memo conventions used
  elsewhere in the indexer.

- **Fee amount fixed in code at $0.01, not configurable.**
  A per-operator env var would let a generous operator
  effectively undercut the anti-spam economics (operators
  compete for users; the one with no anti-spam wins the
  abusers). Hard-coded keeps every Morphit instance honest.

- **Idempotency via composite PK + ON-collision translation.**
  The handler does BOTH: a proactive SELECT EXISTS check
  AND a catch on PK collision. The SELECT covers the
  common case (user retries after network blip); the catch
  covers the race where two signed ops land in the same
  block. Either path resolves to `{ ok: true }`.

- **Layer-2 gate does NOT re-check blocks.** A blocked
  sender's stranger-fee IS accepted and recorded (if they
  want to waste BLURT that way). But their chat messages
  still reject at layer-1 because the chat handler's gate
  order is: block → admit → rate-limit. Layer 2's scope is
  pair-level fee bookkeeping, not admission to the chat.

- **Deploy-safety condition (prior sender→recipient
  message).** Without this, layer 2 deployment would
  retroactively gate every pair whose first message
  happened before the feature landed — including valid
  long-running conversations. Condition 2 preserves those.
  Cost: an attacker who messaged before layer 2 deployed
  retains free contact; acceptable for a feature whose
  threat model is future abusers, not historical ones.

- **Price feed degradation fails closed.** If
  `priceSource.current()` returns `0`, `NaN`, or any
  non-finite value, the handler rejects
  `price_feed_unavailable`. Better to briefly block new
  stranger-fee admissions than to admit someone who paid
  against a bogus price.

- **Tolerance 2% (default).** Client-side fractional-BLURT
  rounding can produce ±0.001 BLURT drift; 2% gives
  comfortable headroom for that plus momentary price-feed
  lag between op assembly and block landing.

### Honest gaps

- **No frontend op builder.** Layer 2 ships indexer-ready —
  the op is acceptable on-chain — but no UI yet constructs
  it. The next session must add `apps/web/src/lib/blurt/ops/
  strangerFee.ts` (custom_json + sibling transfer in one
  transaction, a new pattern not present elsewhere in
  the ops directory).
- **No Requests tab in inbox.** Strangers who've paid
  still land in the regular inbox. UX improvement deferred
  to the frontend session.
- **No first-contact modal.** When a user sends to
  someone they've never exchanged with, the UI today
  would just show "message failed" with the
  `stranger_fee_required` reason; a proper modal
  explaining the fee and offering to pay is the real UX.
- **No integration test for schema-v16 migration against
  live Postgres.** Deferred.

### Honest integrity state at close of this session

- Frontend: 0 typecheck errors
- Indexer: 0 typecheck errors
- Relay: 0 typecheck errors
- Shared: 0 typecheck errors
- i18n parity: 10/10 at 1225 leaves
- Smoke runners: 60 scenarios passing across 4 runners
  (block 11, chat 11, stranger-fee 15, drain-defense 23)

### Files touched (layer 2)

Indexer:
- `apps/indexer/src/db/schema-v16.sql` (new)
- `apps/indexer/src/db/migrations.ts` (v16 registration)
- `apps/indexer/src/indexer/handlers/strangerFee.ts` (new)
- `apps/indexer/src/indexer/handlers/chat.ts` (layer-2 gate
  + docstring update to cover all three layers)
- `apps/indexer/src/indexer/dispatcher.ts` (OP_IDS + HANDLERS)
- `apps/indexer/test/handlers/strangerFee.test.ts` (new, 17
  cases)
- `apps/indexer/test/handlers/chat.test.ts` (extended with
  layer-2 gate; length-assertion corrections)
- `apps/indexer/scripts/stranger-fee-handler-smoke.ts`
  (new, 15/15 passing)
- `apps/indexer/scripts/chat-handler-smoke.ts` (extended,
  11/11 passing)

Frontend:

## Finding H triad — chat anti-spam layer 2 (frontend) — SHIPPED 2026-04-24

Closes out Finding H end-to-end. With this session, users can
now pay the stranger-fee, and the frontend UX guides them
through it instead of surfacing an opaque
`stranger_fee_required` error. The Requests tab in the inbox
remains a nice-to-have for a future UX polish session but is
not blocking.

### What shipped

**Op builder** (`apps/web/src/lib/blurt/ops/strangerFee.ts`):
- `STRANGER_FEE_USD = 0.01` constant mirrored from indexer
- `computeStrangerFeeBlurt()` — quotes the BLURT amount via
  `getPrice('BLURT')`. Ceil-rounds up at 3 decimals so
  modest post-quote price drift can't tip the broadcast into
  `fee_underpaid`.
- `broadcastStrangerFee(live, activePriv, peer, quote)` —
  reuses the existing `broadcastOrderWithFee` helper for the
  dual-signed custom_json + transfer transaction. Memo binds
  to `morphit-stranger:<recipient>` matching the indexer's
  layer-2 verification.

**Admission probe endpoint** (`/v1/chat-admission/:me/:peer`):
- Indexer `apps/indexer/src/api/chatAdmission.ts` returns
  `{ me, peer, admitted, reason }` where `reason` is
  `'prior_exchange'`, `'fee_paid'`, or `'none'`.
- Mirrors the chat handler's layer-2 gate query verbatim so
  the UX is consistent with runtime admission decisions.
- Self-chat short-circuits to `{ admitted: true }` so the
  conversation view doesn't flash a pay-fee pill against your
  own account.
- Shared types `ChatAdmissionResponse` +
  `ChatAdmissionReason` in
  `packages/indexer-client/src/index.ts`.
- Frontend client `getChatAdmission(me, peer)` in
  `apps/web/src/lib/indexer/client.ts`.

**StrangerFeeModal component**
(`apps/web/src/lib/components/StrangerFeeModal.svelte`):
- Four-phase state machine: `loading` → `ready` → `paying` →
  `error`. Each phase renders a distinct body; the
  ready/paying card shows BLURT amount, USD equivalent, and
  the live rate for transparency.
- Active-key JIT unlock via `useActiveKey` from
  `currentEnvelope` + password prompt. Bad password is
  distinguished from broadcast failure and restores the
  input so the user can retry.
- Retry button on the `error` phase for transient price
  feed failures.
- Backdrop click + Escape key dismiss.
- Emits `onPaid()` after successful broadcast so the caller
  can refresh admission state and swap the pill for the
  composer.

**ConversationView integration**
(`apps/web/src/lib/components/ConversationView.svelte`):
- New `AdmissionStatus` state machine: `unknown` (brief blank
  until probe resolves, avoids pill-flash) → `admitted` (show
  composer) / `needs_fee` (show pay-to-message pill) /
  `error` (fail open — show composer so transient probe
  failures don't break chat).
- `fetchAdmission()` kicked off from `onMount` alongside
  existing profile + block-list fetches.
- Pay-to-message pill renders the composer area when
  `needs_fee`, with a locked-session hint when session is
  locked (can't sign the fee op).
- `onFeePaid()` optimistically flips to `admitted` after
  broadcast + refreshes from the indexer to confirm.
- Modal mounts conditionally at the route level when
  `showStrangerFeeModal && $liveIdentity`.

**i18n × 10 locales** — 21 new leaves under
`chat.stranger_fee.*`: heading, explain, one_time_note,
amount_label, usd_label, rate_label, password_label,
password_placeholder, confirm, cancel, retry, paying, quoting,
pill_explain, pill_cta, pill_locked_hint, error.quote_failed,
error.no_active_envelope, error.broadcast_failed,
error.bad_password, error.password_required.

### Decisions recorded (frontend)

- **Preemptive probe, not reactive.** ConversationView
  fetches admission on mount rather than letting the send
  path fail. Rationale: custom_json broadcasts succeed at
  chain level even when the indexer will reject; a reactive
  design would look like a successful send that then
  vanishes. Preemptive probe avoids that confusion entirely
  at the cost of one extra round-trip per conversation
  open.

- **Fail OPEN on admission probe error.** If the probe
  fetch fails (network, indexer down), we show the
  composer, not the pay-pill. Fail-closed would mean
  transient indexer blips make chat feel broken and nudge
  users toward unnecessary fee payments. The worst case is
  a broadcast that gets `stranger_fee_required` at the
  indexer — a clean error, not silent money loss.

- **Quote amount ceil-rounded at 3 decimals.** BLURT has
  3-decimal precision; price-feed drift between the modal's
  display and the broadcast can be ±0.001 BLURT. Ceil-rounding
  means the user slightly over-pays (landing inside the
  indexer's 2% tolerance window) rather than risking an
  `fee_underpaid` reject on a momentary price tick.

- **Active-key prompt inline, not via global dialog.** The
  post page and featureBid flow each have their own active-
  key prompt; we follow that pattern rather than extract a
  shared component. Extraction is a nice-to-have UX polish
  that deserves its own session; copy-paste cost is low and
  the prompts are ~15 lines each.

- **Optimistic flip to `admitted` after onPaid.** The
  stranger-fee op lands on-chain synchronously (broadcast
  returns block_num + trx_id), but the indexer needs 1-2
  blocks to ingest it into the stranger_fees table. Between
  broadcast and ingest, a refreshed admission probe would
  return `admitted=false`. Optimistic flip avoids that
  false-negative window; the indexer's eventual-consistency
  catches up naturally.

- **No Requests tab in inbox yet.** The admission system
  gates sending; a stranger's paid first message lands in
  the normal inbox, not a separate Requests tab. A dedicated
  Requests tab is a UX-polish feature that can ship whenever
  — it doesn't affect security. Explicitly deferred.

### Honest gaps at close

- No integration test for the admission endpoint against a
  live Postgres. The endpoint's logic is trivial (two EXISTS
  queries) so risk is low; an integration test is a next-
  session housekeeping item.
- No Svelte-component test for StrangerFeeModal. Its state
  machine has enough branches to warrant one; deferred.
- `active-key-prompt` extraction opportunity noted — three
  surfaces (post, featureBid, stranger-fee) now duplicate
  ~15 lines of similar prompt UI.

### Integrity state at session close

- Frontend: 0 typecheck errors
- Indexer: 0 typecheck errors
- Relay: 0 typecheck errors
- Shared: 0 typecheck errors
- i18n parity: 10/10 at **1246 leaves** (was 1225 + 21 = 1246 ✓)
- Smoke runners: 60/60 passing unchanged
  (block 11, chat 11, stranger-fee 15, drain-defense 23)

### Files touched (layer 2 frontend)

Indexer:
- `apps/indexer/src/api/chatAdmission.ts` (new)
- `apps/indexer/src/main.ts` (route mounting)

Shared:
- `packages/indexer-client/src/index.ts`
  (ChatAdmissionReason, ChatAdmissionResponse types)

Frontend:
- `apps/web/src/lib/indexer/client.ts` (getChatAdmission)
- `apps/web/src/lib/blurt/ops/strangerFee.ts` (new)
- `apps/web/src/lib/components/StrangerFeeModal.svelte` (new)
- `apps/web/src/lib/components/ConversationView.svelte`
  (admission state machine + modal integration)
- `apps/web/src/lib/i18n/locales/*.json` (10 locales, +21
  leaves each: chat.stranger_fee.*)

Docs:
- `docs/REVISIT-LIST.md` (this entry)

With this, **all three Finding H layers are shipped end-to-
end** — indexer + frontend, typecheck-verified, i18n-complete
across 10 locales, with 60 runtime scenarios passing across
handler smoke runners. The Requests tab remains open but is
UX polish rather than a security feature.

## Finding I — attestor eligibility gate (indexer side) — SHIPPED 2026-04-24

Mitigation for the feeAttest sybil vulnerability. Frontend
integration deferred until the attest UI itself is built;
the defensive indexer gate stands on its own.

### What shipped

**Eligibility helper**
(`apps/indexer/src/indexer/attestorEligibility.ts`):
- `checkAttestorEligibility(account, phase, db, now)` returns
  discriminated union `EligibilityOk | EligibilityFail`.
- Structural `Queryable` interface accepts both `pg.PoolClient`
  (inside handler transactions) and `Database` (for API
  endpoints reading outside transactions).
- Single LEFT JOIN query on `accounts` + `account_loyalty`
  returns both age and loyalty. Missing `account_loyalty`
  row is treated as 0 BLURT (account exists but never paid).
- Fail variants carry `loyaltyBlurt`, `ageDays`,
  `missingLoyaltyBlurt`, `daysUntilEligible` for helpful UX
  messaging.
- Thresholds exported as module constants:
  `ATTESTOR_LOYALTY_THRESHOLD_BLURT = 100`,
  `ATTESTOR_AGE_THRESHOLD_DAYS = 30`.

**Config** (`apps/indexer/src/config/index.ts`):
- New `attestationPhase: 'launch' | 'steady'` field on Config.
- `MORPHIT_INDEXER_ATTESTATION_PHASE` env var, zod enum,
  default `'launch'`.
- Operator flips via env var at the Finding I transition
  trigger; no redeploy required.

**feeAttest handler amendment**
(`apps/indexer/src/indexer/handlers/feeAttest.ts`):
- Eligibility check runs after order-lookup, before INSERT,
  using `ctx.blockTime` for deterministic replay-friendly
  results.
- Four distinct rejection codes routed from
  `EligibilityFail.reason`: `attestor_account_not_found`,
  `attestor_insufficient_loyalty_and_young_account`,
  `attestor_insufficient_loyalty`, `attestor_young_account`.
- Docstring updated to describe the Finding I gate.

**Admission probe endpoint**
(`apps/indexer/src/api/attestorEligibility.ts`):
- `GET /v1/attestor-eligibility/:account` returns
  `{ account, phase, eligible, reason, loyalty_blurt,
    age_days, missing_loyalty_blurt, days_until_eligible }`.
- Optional `?phase=launch|steady` query parameter for UX
  preview ("do I qualify under the post-transition rules?").
- Defaults to the indexer's currently-configured phase.
- Mounted at `/v1/attestor-eligibility` in `main.ts` with
  the standard list-rate-limit.

**Shared types**
(`packages/indexer-client/src/index.ts`):
- `AttestorEligibilityReason` union (7 variants — 3 pass,
  4 fail).
- `AttestorEligibilityResponse` interface.

**Frontend client function**
(`apps/web/src/lib/indexer/client.ts`):
- `getAttestorEligibility(account, signal?)` helper.

**Tests + smoke runners:**
- `apps/indexer/test/handlers/feeAttest.test.ts` — extended
  with 5 new eligibility scenarios; existing tests patched
  to include the eligibility SELECT expectation before
  INSERT, and query-count assertions updated accordingly.
  Typecheck clean.
- `apps/indexer/scripts/attestor-eligibility-smoke.ts` — 13
  scenarios covering the helper in isolation (account not
  found, both-gates-fail, loyalty-only, age-only, both,
  launch OR, steady AND, boundary conditions at 100 / 30 /
  99.999 / 29). **13/13 passing at runtime.**
- `apps/indexer/scripts/fee-attest-handler-smoke.ts` — 11
  scenarios driving the full handler flow through every
  rejection code and admission branch, plus regression
  coverage of the existing promotion logic. **11/11 passing
  at runtime.**

### Decisions recorded

- **Structural Queryable typing.** The helper's `Queryable`
  interface is a minimal structural shape, not
  `Pick<pg.PoolClient, 'query'>`. This lets both `Database`
  (Pool-backed, API endpoints) and `pg.PoolClient`
  (transaction-scoped, handlers) satisfy it without a
  type-system compromise.

- **`ctx.blockTime` for the handler, `new Date()` for the
  endpoint.** Handlers must be deterministic-replayable —
  passing the block time anchors the eligibility check to
  on-chain time, so re-indexing from scratch produces the
  same rejections. The API endpoint is a live probe where
  wall-clock is the correct reference.

- **Loyalty threshold at first milestone (100 BLURT), not
  some new number.** Reuses the existing loyalty infrastructure
  (the first milestone-bonus threshold). Prevents drift
  between "loyal enough to get milestone rewards" and
  "loyal enough to attest."

- **Four rejection codes, not one.** The UI needs to tell
  the user exactly what they're missing; the remedies are
  different ("pay X more BLURT" vs "wait Y more days" vs
  "do either" vs "your account isn't indexed yet").
  Typed as a union in shared types so the frontend gets
  exhaustive-match help.

- **Missing `account_loyalty` row treated as zero, not an
  error.** A valid, existing account that has simply never
  paid a fee should be visible to the system as "0 BLURT
  loyalty, N days age" — not as "malformed." LEFT JOIN with
  NULL coalescing does this naturally.

- **Phase defaults to `'launch'`.** Current deploys running
  this code start permissive. An operator affirmatively
  flips to `'steady'` when the Finding I transition trigger
  is reached; no silent in-place tightening.

- **Optional `?phase=` endpoint override.** Lets the frontend
  preview eligibility under a non-active phase for advanced
  UX ("you qualify now but wouldn't under steady" — useful
  during the transition window if Morphit ever wants to nudge
  users toward meeting both gates proactively). No change to
  the handler path; purely a probe-time concern.

### Honest gaps

- **No frontend attest UI.** The Finding I gate is live on
  the indexer and shared types / client helper are ready,
  but no existing Morphit UI calls the feeAttest op. A new
  attest button + eligibility pre-check UI belongs on
  order-detail pages and is genuinely its own feature
  session. The defensive indexer work does not block
  anything; it's ready when the UI catches up.
- **No frontend i18n for eligibility-reject copy.** Same
  reason — no UI surface yet to need the strings. The four
  reject codes are well-defined so the translations can be
  added in one clean pass when the UI lands.
- **Frontend OP_IDS does not yet have `feeAttest`.** The
  indexer's dispatcher has it; frontend will need the

## runWithActiveKey — active-key unlock helper extraction — SHIPPED 2026-04-24

Consolidates the duplicate try/catch + identity-store gate +
error classification pattern used by every active-auth
broadcast surface. Covers 2 of 3 call sites; the post-page
deliberately keeps its bespoke error handling.

### What shipped

**Helper** (`apps/web/src/lib/crypto/runWithActiveKey.ts`):
- `runWithActiveKey<T>(password, callback)` returns a
  discriminated union `ActiveKeyOk<T> | ActiveKeyErr` so
  callers switch on `r.kind` instead of try/catch +
  string-matching.
- Four error kinds: `password_empty` (caller didn't guard),
  `locked` (identity not unlocked), `bad_password`
  (useActiveKey threw with "password" or "decrypt" in the
  message), `broadcast` (callback itself threw).
- Identity store check happens inside the helper via
  `get(identity)` so callers don't duplicate the unlock gate.
- `useActiveKey` wipes the derived scalar internally; the
  helper does NOT wipe the caller's password string
  (caller-owned state).

**Refactored sites:**
- `apps/web/src/lib/components/StrangerFeeModal.svelte` —
  removed the `get(currentEnvelope)` nil check, try/catch,
  and string-matching heuristic. Now a clean
  `await runWithActiveKey(...)` with a discriminated switch.
- `apps/web/src/lib/components/FeatureBidForm.svelte` — same
  refactor. Bonus: gained a proper `error_bad_password`
  translated message (was previously surfacing raw crypto
  error strings to the user).

**Intentionally NOT refactored:**
- `apps/web/src/routes/post/+page.svelte` — keeps its bespoke
  error handling because it distinguishes three broadcast-
  level error kinds (`BroadcastError.code === 'locked'`,
  insufficient-funds keyword match, generic chain reject)
  that the helper's unified `broadcast` kind flattens.
  Forcing post-page through the helper would regress the
  nuanced UX. The helper's header documents this explicitly
  so future maintainers don't assume post-page should be
  ported.

**Test coverage**
(`apps/web/src/lib/crypto/runWithActiveKey.test.ts`):
- 8 vitest scenarios covering password_empty, locked, ok
  success, bad_password via "password" keyword, bad_password
  via "decrypt" keyword, case-insensitivity, broadcast with
  Error cause, broadcast with non-Error string cause.
- Typecheck-clean. Vitest itself isn't runnable in the
  sandbox; CI will pick it up.

**i18n:** 1 new leaf, `feature_bid.error_bad_password`,
across all 10 locales (1246 → 1247).

### Decisions recorded

- **Scope revision mid-session.** Original plan was to
  unify all three active-auth sites. Survey of post-page
  revealed bespoke error classification that would regress
  under a unified helper. Better to do the 2-of-3
  extraction well than force a 3-of-3 that flattens
  post-page's UX.

- **Heuristic classification, not typed errors.** The
  `useActiveKey` keystore primitive doesn't throw typed
  errors — it surfaces the underlying libsodium/crypto
  failure. Rather than bubble a fragile dependency up into
  the caller, the helper does a lowercase substring match
  on "password" and "decrypt" to classify. False positives
  favor the bad-password message, whose remedy (retry)
  is harmless in the broadcast-failure case too.

- **Caller owns the password string.** The helper can't
  mutate a `let password` in the caller's scope. Contract
  is: caller clears on BOTH branches. Enforced by
  convention, not by the type system — still a risk, but
  no lower-risk alternative without making the helper take
  a setter callback (more boilerplate than it saves).

- **Pass `state.live` explicitly in the callback.** Both
  refactored callers capture `state.live` from a pre-call
  `get(identity)` and pass it into the callback closure.
  The helper does its own `get(identity)` inside
  (duplicated read — cheap), but callers that need the
  LiveIdentity in their broadcast call grab it at
  precheck-time. Keeps the helper's signature minimal
  (just `(activePriv) => ...` rather than
  `(activePriv, live) => ...`).

### Honest gaps

- **Post-page not covered.** As above — by design. A
  future session could extend the helper's error type
  with a "classified broadcast" variant the post-page
  could consume, but the ROI is marginal.
- **Future Finding I attest UI would be the 4th site.**
  When it ships, it'll use this helper too unless it
  needs post-page-level error nuance.

### Integrity state at session close

- Frontend: 0 typecheck errors
- Indexer: 0 typecheck errors
- Relay: 0 typecheck errors
- Shared: 0 typecheck errors
- i18n parity: 10/10 at **1247 leaves**
- Smoke runners: 84 scenarios passing across 6 runners
  (block 11, chat 11, stranger-fee 15, attestor-eligibility
  13, fee-attest-handler 11, drain-defense 23)

  8 vitest cases)

## Block action ConfirmModal swap — SHIPPED 2026-04-24

Replaced the native `confirm()` dialog on the chat block /
unblock action with the existing Morphit-styled ConfirmModal
component. Minor UX polish — the behavior was functionally
correct before, but the UI was a native browser dialog which
is jarring in an otherwise styled app and visually confusing
at mobile breakpoints.

### What shipped

**No new component required.** The ConfirmModal at
`apps/web/src/lib/components/ConfirmModal.svelte` already
existed and is robust: uses native `<dialog>` with
`.showModal()` for focus trap, backdrop, Escape-dismiss, and
proper ARIA for free. Default focus on Cancel to prevent a
stray Enter press triggering the destructive action.
Destructive variant tints the top border red.

**ConversationView refactor**
(`apps/web/src/lib/components/ConversationView.svelte`):
- `onToggleBlock` → now just sets `pendingBlockAction` and
  opens the modal. Doesn't await anything.
- New `onConfirmBlock` handles the actual broadcast when
  the user confirms.
- New `onCancelBlock` clears pending state.
- `blockConfirmOpen` state wired via `bind:open` for the
  modal's escape-to-close write-back. Effect syncs
  `pendingBlockAction → blockConfirmOpen`.
- ConfirmModal rendered alongside StrangerFeeModal at the
  root template level.

**i18n restructure across 10 locales.** The old flat keys
`chat.block.confirm_block` / `confirm_unblock` fused title
and body into one string. Split into nested structure
`chat.block.confirm.{block,unblock}.{title,body,yes}` +
`chat.block.confirm.cancel`. Net change per locale:
−2 (old flat keys removed), +7 (title/body/yes × 2 + cancel).
Total parity: 1247 → 1252 leaves at 10/10.

### Decisions recorded

- **Used existing ConfirmModal, didn't build new.** The
  REVISIT note suggested a "Morphit-styled ConfirmDialog"
  needed to be built; it turns out the component already
  existed at `ConfirmModal.svelte`. Zero-cost finish: just
  wiring. Learned lesson documented here so future
  maintainers searching for confirm-dialog infrastructure
  find it on first grep.

- **Two-step toggle flow** (toggle → confirm → broadcast)
  instead of the old single-step (toggle → confirm inline →
  broadcast). The state-machine with `pendingBlockAction` is
  clearer than inline try/catch and lets the async broadcast
  await cleanly inside the confirm handler — the modal shows
  a busy label while the broadcast runs.

- **Settings page unblock left as no-confirm.** Symmetric
  UX question: should the Settings > Blocked Accounts list's
  unblock buttons also get a ConfirmModal? Decided no.
  Unblock is low-stakes (trivially reversible: just block
  again). Settings is a curated management surface where the
  user is already in "I'm changing things" mode. Adding a
  confirm on every row would be friction without safety
  benefit. The chat-header unblock keeps its confirm because
  mid-conversation toggles deserve an "are you sure" beat.

- **Broadcast failure surfaced via transient StatusLine.**
  Initially kept `alert()` as a known gap (no toast system
  exists). On second pass, realized the existing
  `StatusLine.svelte` component is a perfectly good primitive
  for an inline transient error — attached under the chat
  header, auto-clears after 5 seconds via setTimeout (cleared
  on component unmount so no stale-write after navigation).
  Better UX than a native alert dialog; uses infrastructure
  that already exists. The general "toast system" want
  remains on the backlog for cases that need to survive
  page navigation — the chat header is a closed scope where
  the inline banner is sufficient.

- Indexer: 0 typecheck errors
- Relay: 0 typecheck errors
- Shared: 0 typecheck errors

## Inbox Requests tab — SHIPPED 2026-04-24

Closes out Finding H's UX arc. Before this, a stranger
who'd paid the layer-2 fee landed in the same inbox as the
user's known correspondents — visually indistinguishable
from ongoing conversations. The Requests tab separates them
so the user can see at a glance which threads are new
first-contacts needing a response vs ongoing relationships.

### What shipped

**Indexer** (`apps/indexer/src/api/conversations.ts`):
- Added `has_user_sent` column to the conversations query.
  Uses `BOOL_OR(sender = $1)` aggregated over the same rows
  already being scanned — zero additional query cost.
- Returned in the response item shape.

**Shared types**
(`packages/indexer-client/src/index.ts`):
- `ConversationSummary.has_user_sent: boolean`.

**Frontend inbox** (`apps/web/src/routes/chat/+page.svelte`):
- Tab state `activeTab: 'messages' | 'requests'`, defaults to
  'messages'.
- Conversations partitioned by `has_user_sent`:
  - `messagesList` — user has replied at least once.
  - `requestsList` — inbound-only, strangers awaiting reply.
- Per-tab unread counts drive pill badges on each tab button.
- Tab strip hidden entirely when there are no requests AND
  the user isn't already on the requests tab — avoids
  teaching a UX element most users never encounter.
- Dedicated empty-state for the Requests tab explaining
  what lands there ("when someone you haven't chatted with
  before reaches out…") — different from the whole-inbox
  empty state.
- Smart-default: on first data load, if `messagesList` is
  empty but `requestsList` has content, auto-switches to
  Requests. Fires once; subsequent user tab clicks are
  respected.

**i18n × 10 locales**: 5 new leaves under `chat.inbox.*` —
`tab_messages`, `tab_requests`, `tabs_aria`,
`requests_empty_heading`, `requests_empty_body`. Parity
1252 → **1257 leaves**.

### Decisions recorded

- **`has_user_sent` computed at query time, not stored.**
  The conversations endpoint already aggregates over
  chat_messages rows with GROUP BY; adding one BOOL_OR
  column is free. Storing a derived flag in a separate
  table would mean maintaining consistency with every
  new chat message — more moving parts for no gain.

- **Tab hidden when not relevant.** Users with zero
  requests don't see tabs at all; the inbox renders as
  the simple list it always was. Avoids exposing a piece
  of UX most users never need until a stranger contacts
  them. Lazy-learning: the tabs appear when they matter.

- **Smart default to Requests on first load.** If the
  user's only content is in Requests, opening on Messages
  would show an empty tab they'd have to click away from.
  The one-shot $effect with a guard flag prevents
  fighting the user's explicit choice on later re-renders.

- **Fallback-peers path tied to Messages tab only.** When
  the indexer is unreachable and we render from
  `localStorage` recent-peers, we can't know which
  conversations are requests. Fallback shows on Messages
  tab (activeTab default), Requests shows its own
  empty-state. Consistent with "fallback is for when
  things don't work" — a specialized Requests view isn't
  the right place to surface localStorage fallbacks.

- **Default tab choice: Messages.** Could have defaulted
  to "whichever has unread" but that would mean an
  unread Messages item causes switching even when the
  user was mid-flow on Requests. Simpler rule: default
  Messages, switch only when Messages is completely
  empty.

### Honest gaps

- **No way to "dismiss a request without replying".** If
  a user receives a paid stranger-fee first contact they
  don't want to engage with, the conversation stays in
  Requests forever. Block is the escape hatch (it hides
  the peer from subsequent messages AND removes the row
  via the indexer's layer-1 gate on future sends, though
  existing history stays). An explicit "decline" that
  drops the conversation from the requests list without
  a full block is a UX affordance a future polish session
  could add.

- **No metric for requests-tab usage.** Morphit's "zero
  tracking" guarantee means we can't measure whether this
  tab is being used. Decision is accepted — the UX benefit
  doesn't require the metric.

- **Once the user replies to a request, it moves to
  Messages on next inbox load.** That's correct behavior
  but happens invisibly — the user sends, then refreshes,
  and the request is gone from this tab. A tiny
  "conversation moved to Messages" confirmation could
  close the loop UX-wise, but it adds complexity for
  minor polish. Filed as a possible future improvement.

### Integrity state at session close

- Frontend: 0 typecheck errors
- Indexer: 0 typecheck errors
- Relay: 0 typecheck errors
- Shared: 0 typecheck errors
- i18n parity: 10/10 at **1257 leaves**
- Smoke runners: 84 scenarios passing across 6 runners
  (unchanged — indexer change is additive column; no
  logic changes)

### Files touched

Indexer:
- `apps/indexer/src/api/conversations.ts` (+ has_user_sent
  column)

Shared:
- `packages/indexer-client/src/index.ts`
  (ConversationSummary.has_user_sent)

Frontend:
- `apps/web/src/routes/chat/+page.svelte`
  (tab state, partitioned lists, tab strip UI,
  dedicated empty states, smart default)

  +5 leaves each: chat.inbox tab keys)

With this, **Finding H is fully shipped end-to-end with
complete UX polish**: block list (layer 1), stranger-fee
admission (layer 2) with pay-to-message modal and Requests
tab for incoming first-contacts, and rate limits (layer 3).
Block action uses the Morphit-styled ConfirmModal.
Active-key unlock is unified via `runWithActiveKey`
across two of three surfaces. The three-layer anti-spam
system is now a feature-complete chat experience.

## Inbox dismiss + hide/block filter — SHIPPED 2026-04-24

Closes the "decline a request without blocking" gap flagged
in the prior Requests-tab entry. Also makes the inbox
respect hidden-accounts globally, which it previously did
not — a small but meaningful consistency fix.

### What shipped

**Inbox filter unification**
(`apps/web/src/routes/chat/+page.svelte`):
- `sortedConversations` now filters out peers in either
  `$hiddenAccounts` OR `$blockedAccounts`. Previously the
  inbox ignored both stores, so a user who had hidden @x
  via the orderbook would still see @x in chat.
- `loadBlocks(me)` fires alongside the existing parallel
  fetches in onMount so the filter reflects server-side
  block state from first render.

**Dismiss affordance on Requests tab.**
- Row restructured: outer `<li>` is the card container,
  `<a>` is the tappable nav area (now `flex-1`), dismiss
  button is a sibling with its own click handler. Solves
  the "button inside anchor" invalid-HTML issue the
  straightforward approach would hit.
- Dismiss calls `handleDismiss(peer)` → marks conversation
  read + calls existing `hideAccount(peer)` primitive.
- Button only rendered when `activeTab === 'requests'`;
  Messages tab rows are unchanged visually.
- Visual: vertical divider between nav area and button,
  hover-red on the dismiss button label. Destructive
  affordance styling consistent with Morphit conventions.

**i18n × 10 locales**: 2 new leaves under `chat.inbox.*` —
`dismiss` and `dismiss_aria`. Parity 1257 → **1259 leaves**.

### Decisions recorded

- **Dismiss = hideAccount, not a new primitive.** Morphit
  already has `hiddenAccounts` (ADR-0013 Q1.4 ratified),
  used by the orderbook. Reusing it keeps "this user is
  invisible to me" as a single concept with a single
  management surface (Settings → Hidden Accounts). A
  separate "dismissed requests" store would duplicate the
  concept and fragment the UX ("which list do I unhide from?").

- **Dismiss is softer than Block, intentionally.** Block
  is on-chain and permanent-ish (the indexer's
  `recipient_blocked_sender` gate kicks in on future
  sends). Dismiss is local only: no chain op, no signal to
  the other party, no protocol-level mark. Suits the
  "not interested right now, don't want to make a
  statement" case. Symmetric with hide-via-orderbook.

- **Dismiss also marks read.** A dismissed unread request
  would otherwise leave the top-level unread count
  pointing at a row that's no longer visible. Marking
  read alongside the hide keeps the UI counters honest.

- **Filter applies to both Messages AND Requests tabs.**
  A user who hides/blocks someone they *have* exchanged
  with (via the orderbook "hide" button, say) would
  expect the chat thread to disappear too. The filter
  sits in `sortedConversations` so both derived tab lists
  share it — single point of truth.

- **`loadBlocks` fired non-awaited.** Fire-and-forget
  because $blockedAccounts is a reactive store; when it
  populates, the derivation re-runs and blocked peers
  disappear from the list. Alternatively we'd block first
  paint on the blocks fetch for a correctness window of
  maybe a few hundred ms — not worth it.

- **Row restructured to handle dismiss outside anchor.**
  Could have used `onclick={(e) => e.stopPropagation()}`
  on a button nested inside the anchor, but nested
  button-in-link is invalid HTML (HTML spec prohibits
  interactive content inside <a>). The flex-layout
  restructure is the clean answer.

### Honest gaps

- **No confirmation on dismiss.** Reasoned choice: this
  is fully reversible (Settings > Hidden Accounts shows
  the list with unhide buttons), so the friction of a
  confirm would be noise. Block gets a ConfirmModal
  because it's the harder action; dismiss doesn't need one.

- **Still no way to "reply but don't move to Messages".**
  UX question: if a stranger sends a first contact and
  the user replies with "not interested, please don't
  contact again," the conversation moves to Messages on
  next load (has_user_sent becomes true). That's
  technically correct behavior but arguably the wrong
  UX for that specific flow. Low priority — users
  wanting that can dismiss instead of replying, and
  legitimate replies belong in Messages.

- **Hide-via-orderbook doesn't surface a visible
  confirmation when it clears a chat conversation.** If
  a user hides @x via orderbook and @x was actively
  chatting with them, the chat row silently vanishes
  from inbox on next render. Most users won't notice or
  care; a future toast-system introduction could
  surface a brief "this hide also cleared 1 chat
  conversation" affirmation.

- Indexer: 0 typecheck errors
- Relay: 0 typecheck errors
- Shared: 0 typecheck errors

## Toast system — SHIPPED 2026-04-24

Closes the "no shared toast infrastructure" gap that's been
flagged in three prior REVISIT entries (block-action failure,
hide-also-clears-chat-conversation, conversation-moved-to-
Messages). Builds a small ephemeral-notification primitive
the whole app can use, and migrates one existing `alert()`
call site to it.

### What shipped

**Store** (`apps/web/src/lib/stores/toast.ts`):
- `showToast(message, kind?, {timeout}?)` — the common API.
  Four kinds: `info`, `success`, `warn`, `error`, matching
  the StatusLine kind vocabulary for UX consistency.
- `dismissToast(id)` — manual dismiss, clears auto-dismiss
  timeout. No-op on unknown IDs.
- `toastStore: Readable<readonly Toast[]>` — the live
  stack, components subscribe to render.
- Default timeouts are kind-specific: info/success 4s,
  warn 6s, error 8s. Errors get longer read time.
- Stack capped at 5; excess pushes drop the oldest and
  clear its timeout. Prevents runaway growth in edge cases.
- Zero-tracking by design: pure in-memory, never persists.
  A toast by definition is ephemeral — if a caller needs
  durable feedback, they should use StatusLine or a
  banner, not a toast.

**Component** (`apps/web/src/lib/components/ToastRegion.svelte`):
- Two aria-live regions in the same component: polite
  (info + success) and assertive (warn + error). A single
  region can't mix politeness, so the split is required
  for accessibility. Screen readers interrupt for errors
  but announce politely for info.
- Fixed bottom-right positioning, max-w-sm. `pointer-events:
  none` on the wrapping region so empty overlay doesn't
  block clicks; individual toast cards re-enable them.
- Each toast renders as a card with a kind-colored
  left border (matching StatusLine's semantic color
  vocabulary), an icon (dot for polite, triangle for
  assertive), the message, and a close button.
- Dark-mode aware — all colors use Morphit's existing
  palette tokens.

**Mounted once** at
`apps/web/src/routes/+layout.svelte`, alongside
UpdateBanner. Both are fixed-position overlays that don't
affect document flow.

**Existing alert() migration** (1 site):
- `apps/web/src/routes/settings/+page.svelte` — the
  blocked-accounts unblock-failure path. The inline
  comment anticipated this exact replacement ("same UX
  debt note as the conversation header: a Morphit-styled
  toast would be better, but none exists yet in the
  codebase"). Now uses `showToast(msg, 'error')`.

**Dismiss-flow toast integration**:
- The Requests-tab dismiss from last turn now surfaces a
  confirmation toast: "Hid @peer. Undo in Settings →
  Hidden Accounts." Closes the UX loop — users who
  dismissed their first request now know the row didn't
  just vanish mysteriously and have a clear path to
  reverse the action.

**i18n × 10 locales**: 2 new leaves — `toast.dismiss`
(close-button aria-label) and `chat.inbox.dismiss_toast`
(confirmation message). Parity 1259 → **1261 leaves**.

### Decisions recorded

- **Two aria-live regions, not one.** Mixed politeness in
  a single region has undefined screen-reader behavior;
  some readers pick the most recent setting, some the
  initial. Splitting into polite + assertive regions
  ensures the right urgency signal fires per kind. The
  small cost is rendering two flex columns instead of one.

- **Kind vocabulary matches StatusLine deliberately.**
  An operation that shows a `warn` StatusLine inline
  should use the same kind for a toast about the same
  event. Consistency reduces maintenance noise when
  moving feedback between presentations.

- **Auto-dismiss is the default, manual dismiss always
  available.** Most toasts should self-cleanup; errors
  linger longer but still auto-dismiss. A caller can
  pass `timeout: 0` for a sticky toast if they have a
  specific need, but the default is opinionated toward
  "ephemeral."

- **No "action" buttons inside toasts.** Tempting to add
  an "Undo" button on the dismiss toast — but toasts
  that carry actions need focus management to be
  accessible (tab into the toast, press the action,
  context returns…) and introduce timing issues (the
  toast auto-dismisses in 4s, but the user is reading
  it). Instead: the toast text tells the user *where to
  go* to undo (Settings → Hidden Accounts). Less slick
  but more honest about what the toast is for.

- **Zero persistence.** A page reload clears all toasts.
  Consistent with Morphit's no-tracking principle and
  correct for the "ephemeral feedback" semantic — if
  something needs to survive reload, it belongs in a
  banner or a durable UI element.

- **Stack cap of 5.** Arbitrary but reasonable. A user
  who legitimately triggers 5+ simultaneous toasts is
  seeing a programming bug, not a UX flow — dropping
  oldest is a safe fallback, and the cap prevents any
  code path from leaking memory via toast spam.

- **ConversationView's block-failure StatusLine not
  migrated to toast.** That feedback is scoped to the
  chat header context — it makes sense inline. Toasts
  are for feedback that needs to survive context
  changes. Existing StatusLine usage stays; new UX
  decisions pick the right tool case by case.

### Honest gaps

- **No integration tests.** Vitest is available for
  testing, but mocking timers + store subscribe
  semantics + aria-live announcements is more setup
  than the store's complexity warrants. The store is
  typecheck-clean and the logic is simple enough to
  read through.
- **No visual spec for mobile.** Right now the toast
  region uses a desktop-friendly bottom-right with
  max-w-sm. On very narrow viewports this should
  probably span most of the width. Fine for now;
  responsive polish can follow.
- **Other alert() sites unaudited in this session.**
  `grep '^\s*alert('` caught only one genuine site in
  the codebase (settings blocked-accounts unblock). A
  more thorough audit — including alert-like patterns
  that don't literally use `alert()` — could find more
  migration candidates.
- **No way to dismiss all toasts at once.** Not needed
  yet; can add a "clear all" export if a case emerges.

## Onboarding leave-confirmation — ConfirmModal refactor — SHIPPED 2026-04-24

Last known native-browser-dialog call site in the app:
`window.confirm` in the onboarding flow's beforeNavigate
guard. Swapped for the Morphit-styled ConfirmModal with an
async-navigation pattern that adapts the sync
beforeNavigate hook to modal-driven confirmation.

### What shipped

**onboarding/+page.svelte refactor:**
- Replaced synchronous `window.confirm` with an async
  pattern using ConfirmModal.
- `beforeNavigate` now always calls `nav.cancel()` when
  the user is in a sensitive stage (review/confirm) and
  capture the target URL in `pendingLeaveUrl`. An effect
  syncs `pendingLeaveUrl !== null` → `leaveConfirmOpen`
  for the modal's bindable open prop.
- `onConfirmLeave` handler wipes sensitive state
  (`wipeFullIdentity(full)` + nullify `live`), clears
  `pendingLeaveUrl`, then calls `goto()` with the
  captured target. The guard on `pendingLeaveUrl !== null`
  at the top of `beforeNavigate` ensures that goto()
  doesn't re-trigger the modal (the hook would otherwise
  re-fire).
- Early returns for edge cases: `nav.type === 'leave'`
  (tab close / hard refresh — SvelteKit's cancel is no-op
  there anyway), `nav.to === null` (some refresh types),
  same-pathname navigation.

**i18n restructure across 10 locales:**
- Old flat `onboarding.leave_warning` (single string fused
  title + body + CTA) removed.
- New nested `onboarding.leave_confirm.{title, body, yes,
  stay}` matching ConfirmModal's API.
- Parity 1261 → **1264 leaves** (−1 removed, +4 added × 10
  locales).

### Decisions recorded

- **Async navigation pattern.** ConfirmModal is
  inherently async — the user needs to see and click the
  dialog — but `beforeNavigate`'s contract is
  synchronous: the hook either returns or calls
  nav.cancel() before its stack unwinds. The resolution:
  always cancel synchronously when the modal should
  show, then replay the navigation from the modal's
  confirm handler via `goto()`. A `pendingLeaveUrl`
  state variable bridges the two async boundaries.

- **Guard against re-entry.** The confirm handler's
  `goto()` will re-enter `beforeNavigate`. If that
  handler saw the same sensitive-stage gate, it would
  show the modal again in a loop. The explicit
  `pendingLeaveUrl !== null` check at the top of the
  hook short-circuits the re-entry; the confirm handler
  nulls it before calling goto() so the next invocation
  passes through. Alternative design: use the
  `{ replaceState: true }` option on goto to jump out of
  the sensitive stage's state, but nulling the guard
  flag is clearer and doesn't depend on SvelteKit
  internal state semantics.

- **Passes pathname+search+hash, not the full URL
  object.** `goto()` accepts a string or URL. Using a
  path-relative string keeps the navigation inside the
  app and avoids issues if the URL has a different
  origin than expected (edge case but defensive).

- **`nav.type === 'leave'` skipped entirely.** Tab
  close / hard refresh / typed-URL navigation can't be
  cancelled — the browser's own beforeunload handler
  takes over. Showing our modal for those would be
  jarring (the page is about to vanish whether the user
  confirms or not). We let the browser's native prompt
  handle those cases; SvelteKit's beforeNavigate only
  participates meaningfully for in-app navigations.

- **Confirmation text restructured, not just split.**
  The old flat string was "Leaving this page will
  discard… Leave anyway?" — title and prompt fused
  awkwardly for a native confirm dialog. Restructured
  for a proper modal layout: a clean question as the
  title ("Leave onboarding?"), the explanation as the
  body, and two distinct button labels ("Leave anyway"
  and "Stay") that make the choice explicit. The
  'destructive' variant's red top border adds
  appropriate visual weight to the "you'll lose your
  keys" warning.

### Honest gaps

- **The `window.confirm` sweep found only this one
  genuine site**, because the prior `alert()` sweep had
  already migrated one site last turn, and the rest of
  the codebase uses inline StatusLine or custom forms
  for feedback. Good news — the toast system + this
  ConfirmModal refactor close out the last of the
  native-dialog usage.

- **No unit test for the pendingLeaveUrl re-entry
  guard.** The state-machine transition (cancel → open
  modal → confirm → wipe → goto → fall-through) has
  several moving parts. Manual testing in a browser
  would exercise it; a unit test would need to mock
  beforeNavigate, goto, and the Svelte runtime. Cost
  exceeds value for this size of flow.

- **Post-page / settings potentially have similar
  patterns.** The settings page does session-level
  actions (export keys, sign out) but uses inline
  ConfirmModal already, not native dialogs. The post
  page has draft-discard flows that probably warrant a
  similar leave-confirmation pattern for long-form
  drafts; that's a future enhancement, not a gap
  this turn's change introduced.

### Integrity state at session close

- Frontend: 0 typecheck errors
- Indexer: 0 typecheck errors
- Relay: 0 typecheck errors
- Shared: 0 typecheck errors
- i18n parity: 10/10 at **1264 leaves**
- Smoke runners: 84 scenarios passing across 6 runners
  (unchanged — no backend work this entry)
- `window.alert` / `window.confirm` in the codebase:
  **0 remaining** in application code (test fixtures
  for XSS sanitizer retain literal strings like
  "`<script>alert('xss')</script>`" which are input
  data, not dialog calls)

### Files touched

Frontend:
- `apps/web/src/routes/onboarding/+page.svelte`
  (ConfirmModal integration, async navigation pattern,
  pendingLeaveUrl state, re-entry guard)
- `apps/web/src/lib/i18n/locales/*.json` (10 locales,
  onboarding.leave_warning removed,
  onboarding.leave_confirm.{title,body,yes,stay}
  added — net +3 leaves per locale)

Docs:
- `docs/REVISIT-LIST.md` (this entry)

are now Morphit-styled ConfirmModal or ToastRegion
based**. Consistent look across the app, proper focus
management, dismissable on Escape, dark-mode aware, and
translated in all 10 locales.

## Finding I display layer + latent orderbook-filter bug fix — SHIPPED 2026-04-24

What started as a fee_status display polish on the
order-detail page turned into surfacing a significant latent
bug: Finding I's attestation-verified orders were being
issued `fee_status = 'verified_by_attestation'` by the
indexer, but every public-visibility surface in the app
(orderbook, RSS, featured orders) filtered on
`fee_status = 'verified'` exactly. That meant the entire
Finding I attestation path had no user-visible output —
the indexer gate was shipping correctly and the attested
orders were silently invisible.

### What shipped

**Display polish on order-detail page**
(`apps/web/src/routes/[x+40][account=account]/[permlink=permlink]/+page.svelte`):
- All six `fee_status` values now render with proper
  localized copy and semantic color treatment:
  - `verified` (green ✓): indexer saw the BLURT transfer.
  - `verified_by_attestation` (green ✓): community
    validators attested an external-chain BTC/XMR payment
    (Finding I).
  - `pending_external` (amber ⏳): awaiting attestation.
  - `underpaid` (amber ⚠): fee transfer was below required.
  - `missing` (amber ⚠): fee transfer not seen.
  - `unverified` (gray): not yet processed.
- Previously `pending_external`, `verified_by_attestation`,
  and `unverified` fell through to an unlocalized raw-string
  span — a visible UX gap.
- Added a dedicated `fee_pending_external_hint` paragraph
  (small, non-alarming) explaining what attestation means
  for users encountering it for the first time.

**my/orders page fixes:**
- `feeStatusLabel` extended to cover `pending_external` and
  `verified_by_attestation` (previously returned empty
  string, silently hiding the badge for owner view).
- Badge color partition corrected: `verified` and
  `verified_by_attestation` both show the green "good"
  style; all other present statuses show amber "attention."
  Previously `verified_by_attestation` showed amber,
  treating legitimate attestation-verified orders as
  needing attention.
- Feature-button gate widened — an attestation-verified
  order can now be featured, same as a natively-verified
  one. Same economic semantic: fee is paid, order is
  legitimate.

**Orderbook filter widening (the real find — 3 indexer
endpoints):**
- `apps/indexer/src/api/orderbook.ts` — main orderbook:
  `fee_status = 'verified'` → `fee_status IN ('verified',
  'verified_by_attestation')`.
- `apps/indexer/src/api/rssOrderbook.ts` — RSS feed: same
  widening.
- `apps/indexer/src/api/featuredOrderbook.ts` — featured
  orders: same widening.
- **Impact:** Before this fix, BTC/XMR orders going through
  the Finding I attestation flow would reach
  `verified_by_attestation` status and remain invisible in
  every public surface. Sellers would have paid the
  attestation coordination cost for no visible result.
  Finding I's indexer mitigation would look like it was
  working (rejections on ineligible attestors, etc.) but
  the successful path had no outcome.

**featureBid handler gate widening**
(`apps/indexer/src/indexer/handlers/featureBid.ts`):
- Extended the fee_status acceptance check to include
  `verified_by_attestation`. Previously an attestation-
  verified order owner trying to feature-bid would get
  `referenced_order_fee_not_verified` rejection and lose
  their BLURT transfer (rolled back by the op savepoint,
  but still a broken flow).
- Comment updated to explain the dual acceptance.

**Schema v17 migration**
(`apps/indexer/src/db/schema-v17.sql` +
`apps/indexer/src/db/migrations.ts`):
- Drops the old `orders_verified_live_idx` partial index
  (predicate: `fee_status = 'verified'` only).
- Creates `orders_live_established_idx` with predicate
  `fee_status IN ('verified', 'verified_by_attestation')`.
- Renamed to signal the new scope — the old name would
  mislead anyone inspecting the schema.
- Not using `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` because the
  migration system runs each migration in a transaction
  for atomicity. Brief blocking recreate is acceptable
  at indexer-scale.

**i18n × 10 locales:** +6 leaves covering the three new
`order_detail.fee_*` labels, the `fee_pending_external_hint`
explainer, and the two `my_orders.order.fee_*` missing
variants. Parity 1264 → **1270 leaves**.

### Decisions recorded

- **Both verified kinds treated as fully first-class.**
  The orderbook, RSS feed, featured-orders endpoint, and
  feature-bid handler now all accept `verified` and
  `verified_by_attestation` as equivalent for visibility
  and action eligibility. The rationale matches the
  economic reality: Finding I's attestation path is
  designed so that community-attested external-chain fees
  are equivalent-in-value to native BLURT fees (the
  seller has paid money, whether in BTC/XMR to an
  address or in BLURT via transfer). The verification
  mechanism differs; the economic legitimacy doesn't.

- **Color partition by verification, not by mechanism.**
  Both verified kinds show green; the distinction appears
  only in the label text. Users don't need to care whether
  an order was verified by indexer-native BLURT transfer
  or by community attestation — they just need to know
  the fee is established.

- **Dedicated explainer for pending_external.** The other
  fee statuses are self-explanatory to anyone who
  understands listing fees; pending_external is the one
  that introduces an unfamiliar concept (community
  attestation). A small paragraph under the badge is
  less jarring than tooltip-style help and matches
  existing UX convention for novel concepts.

- **Future-proof default branch.** Added an else-branch
  that renders the raw `fee_status` string if the indexer
  adds a new status the frontend doesn't recognize.
  Previously this was the fallthrough behavior for three
  known values — replacing it with a proper else-clause
  (while explicitly handling all six known values above)
  makes the intent clear and future-proofs against
  server-ahead-of-client deploys.

- **Migration renames the index.** The old
  `orders_verified_live_idx` name implies "only the
  verified ones" — which is no longer accurate. Renaming
  to `orders_live_established_idx` reflects the real
  scope ("live orders with an established fee, by either
  verification path"). Small cost: existing monitoring
  queries looking up the old name by string will need
  updating, but the cost is once and worth the honesty.

### Honest gaps

- **Latent bug was live.** This bug was shipping
  invisibly for however long verified_by_attestation
  has been in the indexer schema. Any real-world
  attestation path would have reached the fee_status flip
  and then gone silent. Since attestation traffic was
  likely ~zero in practice (the attest UI doesn't exist
  and the feature bid gate was rejecting), the bug may
  never have been user-observable. But it would have
  silently defeated the entire Finding I rollout the
  moment anyone tried to use it.

- **No runtime test for orderbook fee_status filtering.**
  The orderbook endpoint doesn't have a dedicated smoke
  runner; correctness is relying on typecheck plus the
  query's simplicity. I attempted a runtime runner this
  session but ran into the sandbox's missing hono
  dependency — the existing handler smokes work because
  they don't import hono; endpoint testing crosses that
  boundary. As a workable mitigation this session I
  landed `fee-status-filter-lint.ts`, a grep-based
  static check that fires if any of the three
  public-visibility SQL sites regress to
  `fee_status = 'verified'` hardcoded. **7/7 scenarios
  passing, adversarial-tested.** Covers the exact bug
  class; a true runtime test is still future work but
  no longer urgent.

- **Feature-bid handler's dual-acceptance not covered by
  existing smoke runners.** The feeBid flow has no
  current smoke runner. Same future-session note.

- **Migration downtime untested.** Schema-v17 is a
  DROP + recreate of a partial index. In production this
  is a few seconds of the orderbook falling back to
  sequential scan (the data itself is fine; only the
  index is briefly unavailable). Fine for Morphit's
  scale, but worth noting for operators.

### Integrity state at session close

- Frontend: 0 typecheck errors
- Indexer: 0 typecheck errors
- Relay: 0 typecheck errors
- Shared: 0 typecheck errors
- i18n parity: 10/10 at **1270 leaves**
- Smoke runners: **91 scenarios passing across 7 runners**
  (block 11, chat 11, stranger-fee 15, attestor-eligibility
  13, fee-attest-handler 11, drain-defense 23,
  fee-status-filter-lint 7 NEW)
- Migrations: v2–v17 registered

### Files touched

Indexer:
- `apps/indexer/src/api/orderbook.ts`
  (fee_status IN clause)
- `apps/indexer/src/api/rssOrderbook.ts`
  (same widening)
- `apps/indexer/src/api/featuredOrderbook.ts`
  (same widening)
- `apps/indexer/src/indexer/handlers/featureBid.ts`
  (dual-acceptance + comment update)
- `apps/indexer/src/db/schema-v17.sql` (new)
- `apps/indexer/src/db/migrations.ts` (registered v17)
- `apps/indexer/scripts/fee-status-filter-lint.ts`
  (new — grep-based regression guard, 7/7 scenarios,
  adversarial-tested)

Frontend:
- `apps/web/src/routes/[x+40][account=account]/[permlink=permlink]/+page.svelte`
  (all 6 fee_status values rendered with copy + color +
  explainer)
- `apps/web/src/routes/my/orders/+page.svelte`
  (feeStatusLabel extension, color partition fix,
  feature-button gate widening)
- `apps/web/src/lib/i18n/locales/*.json` (10 locales,
  +6 leaves each across order_detail and my_orders.order
  paths)

Docs:
- `docs/REVISIT-LIST.md` (this entry)

With this, Finding I's display path is fully connected end-
to-end: a BTC/XMR order that reaches
`verified_by_attestation` status via the indexer's Finding I
gate now appears in the orderbook, RSS feed, and featured-
orders surface, can be feature-bid by its owner, and is
rendered with proper localized copy on the order-detail page
and in my/orders. The orderbook partial index covers the
hot path for both verification types.

## Finding I type-consistency polish + extended lint — SHIPPED 2026-04-24

Followup to the display-layer + orderbook-filter fix. An audit
of indexer endpoints for the same class of bug found a stale
TypeScript union and three stale documentation strings. Fixed
all four and extended the lint to guard against the type-
narrowing regression class.

### What shipped

**Internal type completion**
(`apps/indexer/src/api/orders.ts`):
- `OrderRow.fee_status` was narrowed to
  `'unverified' | 'verified' | 'missing' | 'underpaid'` —
  missing both `'pending_external'` and
  `'verified_by_attestation'`. This means anywhere in the
  codebase that destructures `OrderRow` and switches on
  `fee_status` would silently mis-narrow against actual DB
  values (e.g. exhaustive `never`-checks would be wrong).
  The endpoint's `rowToWire` passes through as-is so the
  wire response was unaffected, but the type itself was a
  latent hazard. Extended to the full six-variant union
  matching the schema.

**Shared-type comment correction**
(`packages/indexer-client/src/index.ts`):
- The comment on the shared-type union said
  "values not yet emitted by the indexer" — outdated since
  Finding I's indexer gate landed. Replaced with an accurate
  description of when each value is emitted + what the
  state transition looks like.

**Documentation cleanup:**
- Shared-type doc: "only ever returns live + verified
  orders" → "live orders with an established fee (either
  natively verified or attested)". The /v1/orderbook
  endpoint no longer returns only native-verified.
- `rssOrderbook.ts` docstring: "live, fee-verified orderbook
  entries" → "live orders with an established listing fee
  (native BLURT transfer OR community-attested external-
  chain payment via Finding I's attestation path)".
- `rssOrderbook.ts` user-facing `<description>`: "live,
  fee-verified orders" → "live orders with an established
  listing fee." This is end-user-visible in RSS readers.

**Lint extended** (`scripts/fee-status-filter-lint.ts`):
- Two new scenarios covering the type-union completeness
  class of bug:
  - `orders.ts OrderRow type includes pending_external +
    verified_by_attestation`
  - `shared types include pending_external +
    verified_by_attestation for fee_status`
- Each uses a quoted-literal regex (`['"]value['"]`) so a
  stale comment that mentions the value in prose doesn't
  trick the assertion — must appear as an actual TS string
  literal.
- Adversarial-tested: deleted the `'pending_external'`
  literal line, lint fired precisely on the orders.ts
  assertion; restored, all 9 green.

**Total lint coverage now:**
- 3 × SQL filter "no hardcoded ='verified'" checks
- 3 × SQL filter "uses IN clause" checks
- 1 × featureBid handler accepts attestation
- 2 × TS union completeness (internal + shared)
- = **9 scenarios guarding against the Finding I
  regression class.**

### Decisions recorded

- **Extended the lint rather than refactor toward
  unit-testable SQL builders.** Refactoring the endpoint
  SQL building into pure helpers would enable true runtime
  tests, but it's a bigger change with its own risk
  profile. The lint catches the regression class at near-
  zero cost with good signal-to-noise; the refactor can
  land later when a genuine reason justifies the design
  change.

- **Quoted-literal regex for type-union checks.** A naive
  `/pending_external/` would match a stale comment that
  mentions the value in prose. Requiring quotes means the
  lint only passes when the value exists as an actual
  string literal — either a TypeScript type value or a
  JavaScript runtime constant. False positives are
  effectively impossible; false negatives are limited to
  the case where someone writes
  `type X = \`pending_external\`` using backticks (which
  is legal TS but nobody does).

- **Kept `fee_status: string` untyped at several indexer
  call sites.** `featureBid.ts`, `feeAttest.ts`, and
  `featuredOrderbook.ts` all declare their local row
  types with `fee_status: string`. This is arguably less
  safe than the full union, but it's also the "don't lie"
  option — narrowing there would introduce the same class
  of bug if anyone forgot to update it on protocol
  extension. The lint covers the declared-union cases;
  leaving `string` alone is defensible.

- **Documentation correction done fully.** The outdated
  "live, fee-verified" phrasing appeared in three places
  — a shared-type doc, an internal docstring, and a
  user-facing RSS description. All three updated in this
  pass rather than leaving one for later — the drift
  would have been confusing for anyone auditing.

### Honest gaps

- **The lint still doesn't cover SQL inside handlers.**
  The feature-bid handler's `fee_status` check is
  JavaScript-level (`order.fee_status === 'verified' ||
  ...`), not SQL. The lint spot-checks that
  `verified_by_attestation` appears somewhere in the
  featureBid file — weaker than the SQL checks since it
  could pass if the value is present but used in a
  different context. True coverage would require a smoke
  runner (blocked on hono).

- **Other handler fee_status checks not audited.** I
  grepped the indexer for `fee_status: string` and found
  three call sites that use the loose type. None of them
  currently have semantic bugs, but they're the places
  where a future regression would hide. Filed as a lower-
  priority future audit.

- **Frontend side unaudited.** The frontend also
  references `fee_status` values in several places; I
  fixed the three I knew about from this turn's UI pass
  (`order_detail`, `my/orders`, the orderbook filter), but
  I didn't do an exhaustive grep. The symptom of a
  frontend regression would be less severe (wrong badge
  color on an order, not missing orders entirely), but
  worth a future look.

### Integrity state at session close

- Frontend: 0 typecheck errors
- Indexer: 0 typecheck errors
- Relay: 0 typecheck errors
- Shared: 0 typecheck errors
- i18n parity: 10/10 at **1270 leaves** (unchanged —
  this turn was TS-only)
- Smoke runners: **93 scenarios passing across 7
  runners** (fee-status-filter-lint 7 → 9)

Indexer:
- `apps/indexer/src/api/orders.ts` (OrderRow.fee_status
  union extended to 6 variants)
- `apps/indexer/src/api/rssOrderbook.ts` (docstring + RSS

## Conversation-moved-to-Messages toast — SHIPPED 2026-04-24

Closes a UX-loop gap flagged in the Requests tab REVISIT
entry: a first reply silently moves a conversation from
Requests → Messages on next inbox load, but until now there
was no signal that happened. A brief toast confirms the
transition.

### What shipped

**ConversationView integration**
(`apps/web/src/lib/components/ConversationView.svelte`):
- `handleSend` now detects first-reply via a snapshot read
  of the controller's current messages.
- Detection conditions (both required):
  1. Snapshot is non-empty — guards against firing when
     history hasn't loaded yet.
  2. No prior 'me' messages exist (failed ones don't count,
     since they never reached the peer).
- Toast fires via `showToast(...)` with `info` kind after
  the send returns.

**i18n × 10 locales**: +1 leaf under `chat.conversation` —
`moved_to_messages`. Parity 1270 → **1271 leaves**.

### Decisions recorded

- **Detection at send-time, not at inbox view-time.** The
  alternative (compare previous vs current Requests peers
  on inbox mount) would catch the transition at its
  natural surface, but it adds state tracking across
  renders and user navigation. Send-time detection is
  simpler and lands where the user is actively engaged —
  they're looking at the conversation, they send, they
  get a toast confirming something changed.

- **Snapshot-non-empty guard prevents false positives.**
  The ConversationController loads history asynchronously;
  an empty snapshot could mean "brand-new conversation" or
  "history hasn't arrived yet." We can't distinguish, so
  we don't toast at all in the empty case. The only
  missed scenario is "stranger messaged me, I open chat
  and immediately type before history loads" — rare and
  the toast is purely a nicety, not load-bearing. Missing
  the toast is strictly better than firing it on a
  re-engagement of an existing conversation.

- **Failed messages don't count toward prior sends.** A
  failed message never reached the peer, so a retry after
  a failure is still effectively a first real send. The
  detection uses `m.sender !== 'me' || m.state ===
  'failed'` — the "every" predicate means "there are no
  successful prior 'me' sends."

- **Info kind, not success.** The toast is an informative
  notice about a UI state change, not an achievement. No
  action is required of the user. `info` with the default
  4-second timeout is the right register.

### Honest gaps

- **The toast fires per-send-instance, but only the first
  reply in a session can legitimately be the
  transition-causing send.** Because the detection is
  "snapshot has no 'me' messages," subsequent sends in
  the same session correctly don't fire. But if the user
  refreshes the page after a first reply, loses that
  session, and sends again before history loads (empty
  snapshot), the toast won't fire on either send —
  they'll miss the signal. Fine since by that point
  they've probably already noticed the conversation is in
  Messages.

- **Toast text doesn't disambiguate "moved from Requests
  to Messages" from "your first conversation with this
  peer just started appearing in the inbox."** A
  genuinely new conversation (user initiated, not a
  reply) would also fire this toast because there are no
  prior 'me' messages. But those conversations start in
  Messages directly (since has_user_sent becomes true the
  moment the user sends), so the text is still accurate —
  the conversation IS in Messages now. Loosely correct.

- **No test.** The snapshot-based detection has enough
  logic to benefit from a runtime test, but the
  conversation controller lives downstream of enough
  async dependencies (WebSocket polls, keystore, etc.)
  that mocking it to a clean test fixture is more
  scaffolding than the toast deserves. Relying on
  typecheck + manual verification for this one.

## Operator-docs catchup + REVISIT status truth-up — SHIPPED 2026-04-24

Operational documentation had fallen behind the last few
feature sessions. Three new sections added to
`OPERATIONS.md` covering:

- **§19 — Chat anti-spam (Finding H) operational reference.**
  What operators need to know to diagnose user support
  tickets about rejected messages. Describes each of the
  three layers, the table layout, and what operators
  CANNOT change (the $0.01 stranger fee is hardcoded to
  prevent cross-operator undercutting).

- **§20 — Attestation phase transition (Finding I).** The
  single most operationally significant item: the
  `MORPHIT_INDEXER_ATTESTATION_PHASE` env var flip from
  `launch` → `steady`. Without this section, an operator
  would leave `launch` permanently and the security
  benefit of the AND gate never activates. Includes the
  SQL to check whether the traffic trigger (≥500 accounts
  meeting both gates) is met, and explicit guidance on
  when NOT to flip early or late.

- **§21 — Schema v17 upgrade note.** Informational: the
  v17 migration does a brief DROP + recreate of the
  orderbook partial index. Explains why CONCURRENTLY
  isn't used (migration-in-transaction constraint) and
  offers an escape hatch for large-deployment operators
  who want to pre-create the index manually.

**Appendix A extended** with five new command-line
recipes: attestor-eligibility probe, the eligible-for-
steady SQL, chat-admission probe, stranger-fees audit
SQL, and the fee-status-filter-lint invocation (for
pre-deploy CI).

**REVISIT list truth-up.** Two entries (Finding H and
Finding I) still had "DECISION LOCKED 2026-04-24
(implementation pending)" headers from the day the design
was decided. Both are now materially shipped:
- Finding H is fully shipped end-to-end.
- Finding I indexer gate + display layer is shipped;
  only the attest UI itself remains, and that's
  explicitly flagged as its own future session.
Updated both headers to reflect actual status — a stale
"implementation pending" on a shipped mitigation would
mislead anyone skim-reading the list to find remaining
security work.

### Decisions recorded

- **OPERATIONS.md is a living reference.** Adding
  sections as features ship is the way to keep it
  useful. A new feature that requires operator action
  (Finding I phase transition especially) needs its
  runbook section at or near ship-time, not "eventually."

- **Explicit don't-do guidance.** §20 includes both
  "don't flip before the trigger fires" and "don't
  refuse to flip after the trigger fires." Either
  failure is its own class of operator mistake; both
  are documented so the next person who picks this up
  is calibrated correctly.

- **REVISIT headers are a liar if left stale.** The
  list is now ~5600 lines; nobody reads it top-to-bottom
  — they skim-search for "pending" to find open work.
  Stale "pending" tags on shipped mitigations waste
  readers' time and obscure the actual open items.

### Honest gaps

- **I didn't audit every REVISIT entry.** I fixed the
  two obvious Finding H/I headers because they're the
  most security-relevant, but line 40 ("3 design-locked,
  implementation pending") and the "Phase 5 backlog
  item 7" mention may also be out of date. Left alone
  this turn — a future session doing a full REVISIT
  audit could catch more.

- **No test for the OPERATIONS.md SQL queries.** The
  "count accounts eligible for steady" query makes an
  assumption about column names that matches schema v3
  (`accounts.created_block_time`) and v6 (`account_loyalty
  .cumulative_blurt_paid`). I verified both exist by
  reading the schema files, but there's no runtime
  check. A future session could add a lint that parses
  the OPERATIONS.md code blocks and typechecks SQL
  against the live schema.
