## §F.22–§F.36 — Multi-arc post-§F.21 audit sweep close-out

After §F.21 closed the chain-direct attack class, an extensive
sweep covered the remaining product surfaces the project had
flagged as not-deeply-walked.  Fifteen audit arcs in total.

### Findings shipped

| # | Arc | Finding | Severity | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| U1.1 | §F.22 | Orderbook didn't filter chain-blocked accounts | Low | FIXED |
| U2.1 | §F.23 | Orderbook filter inputs didn't NFC-normalize | Low | FIXED |

### Findings flagged for product-owner review (no unilateral patch)

| # | Arc | Concern |
|---|---|---|
| U2.2 | §F.24 | Post A first-trade syndication fires silently with no in-flow disclosure.  Designed-in promotional flow; FAQ documents it but `LeaveFeedbackForm` doesn't tell the user a public Blurt blog post is being broadcast on their behalf.  Privacy-conscious users may post their first trade not realizing this happened.  Three options: add disclosure copy in the feedback form, add a Settings opt-out, or both.  Needs UX/product call, not a code-only fix. |
| U3.2 | §F.28 | `addressMemory` feature is dead code — `CryptoAddressInput.svelte` is never mounted and `rememberAddress` has zero non-test callers.  `hasSeenAddress` always returns false, Settings shows "0 remembered."  Phase 5 BTC/XMR receiving-address UX should either wire it or remove it. |
| U3.3 | §F.36 | The `taxes` FAQ entry includes editorial agorist framing ("we consider it theft," "obey authorities (so-called) at your own expense," "#agorism," "#donoharm").  Not factually incorrect but legally aggressive in a user-facing context.  Some jurisdictions read this as advocating tax evasion.  The team's editorial choice; flagged because users in regulated jurisdictions might find it surprising.  **Update 2026-05-09:** Ken revised the entry — removed the "Maritime Law" framing and the "Keep your own records" how-to paragraph, sharpened the "we have no idea who you are anyway" privacy claim with a `@scoobydoo` example, added `#donoharm` alongside `#agorism`.  The agorist editorial register is preserved by design. |

### Surfaces walked and cleared (no findings)

**§F.22 — Block / mute end-to-end.**  Beyond U1.1, the chain
`block.ts` handler (cleared in §F.21), `chat/blocks.ts` (chain-
broadcast block management), `utils/hiddenAccounts.ts` (local
hide), and the indexer's `/v1/blocks/...` API surface all
verified clean.  ASCII account-name regex enforced uniformly,
parameterized SQL, hard row caps, deliberate omission of
reverse-block-list query (which would be an existence oracle).

**§F.23 — Orderbook read path.**  Beyond U2.1, all WHERE
clauses parameterized via the `p()` helper, zod schema validates
every input dimension (asset enum, side enum, fiat regex, region
length, payment_methods length, min_trades range, sort enum,
limit range, cursor length), `escapeLike` properly escapes
`%/_/\` for ILIKE prefix match, cursor base64+JSON-parse with
shape narrowing via `narrowCursor`.  RSS feed sub-audit:
`xmlEscape` covers all 5 required chars, all user-text wrapped,
parameterized SQL, regex-bounded URL path params, anti-existence-
oracle on per-account feed (returns 200 empty for unknown
account, not 404).

**§F.24 — Syndication.**  Beyond U2.2, Post B is properly opt-in
(default OFF, explicit checkbox + help text on `/post`).  Post
bodies don't reveal more than what the orderbook itself already
makes public.  `buildCommentOperation` routes title + body
through `redactPrivateKeys` — chokepoint discipline intact.
Permlink validated fail-fast pre-broadcast.

**§F.25 — Auto-lock end-to-end.**  The mid-broadcast race
concern (timer fires while signing) DOESN'T materialize:
`Client.signTransaction` is synchronous and returns a fully-
signed TX before any await.  After that point, `wipeLiveIdentity`
is harmless — the broadcast holds the signed payload, not the
key bytes.  UI gating on `$isUnlocked` prevents starting a new
broadcast on stale keys.  **No findings.**

**§F.26 — SW caching + release-trust-anchor.**  GET-only
interception, cross-origin pass-through, /v1 + /rss bypass,
network-first for HTML/JS/CSS, cache-first only for fonts/icons/
brand, `skipWaiting()` only on user-confirmed APPLY_UPDATE
message, old-cache reaping on activate, successful responses
only cached.  Release-trust-anchor: the schema (`ReleasePayloadV1`)
exists but the frontend fetch-and-verify path is unimplemented —
documented design gap (chicken-and-egg of bootstrapping trust).
Phase 5 work.  **No findings.**

**§F.27 — Endpoint rotator + resilience.**  `credentials: 'omit'`
(no cookie leak to third-party RPCs), `referrerPolicy:
'no-referrer'`, `cache: 'no-store'`, AbortController with
timeout, regex-validated user-supplied URLs (`https?://`),
exponential cooldown capped at 5 minutes, JSON-RPC application
errors don't demote (server answered, just refused), shuffle
on init prevents centralizing load.  Multi-endpoint cross-
verification absent (a malicious endpoint could falsify chain
state) — documented trust-model assumption per ADR-0002, not
a fix-now finding.  **No findings.**

**§F.28 — addressMemory.**  Stores SHA-256 hashes only;
addresses themselves never persisted.  Lowercasing the hash
input is intentional and documented (Bech32 is lowercase by
spec; Base58Check checksum makes case-collision space empty in
practice).  Found U3.2: feature is dead code — the
`CryptoAddressInput` component is never mounted in production
surfaces, `rememberAddress` is only called from tests, the
Settings UI consequently always shows "0 remembered."  Not a
security bug.

**§F.29 — Dispute / feedback-response interaction.**  Feedback
API (`/v1/accounts/:account/feedback` + `feedback-given`) all
parameterized, zod-validated, cursor-narrowed.  Suppression
filtering applied uniformly in summary CTE and per-row flagging
(R2 + R15 fixes intact).  feedbackResponse op signing: account
binding, fail-fast feedback_trx_id regex, NFC + forbidden-char
filter (post-§F.21).  responder-not-subject check enforced by
indexer.  **No findings.**

**§F.30 — Frontend rate limiting.**  `apps/indexer/src/api/
middleware/ratelimit.ts` — sliding-window per-IP token bucket,
two tiers (`list` 120/min, `resource` 600/min), forwarded-
address headers honored ONLY when socket peer is loopback (per
Finding B), in-memory state with periodic eviction.  Applied
uniformly across `/v1/listing-fee`, `/v1/orderbook`, `/v1/orders`,
`/v1/profiles`, `/v1/accounts`, `/v1/release`.  Tier defaults
operator-tunable.  **No findings.**

**§F.31 — i18n string injection.**  Four `{@html}` sites
audited:
- `avatarSvg` (×2) — sanitized via `safeSanitizeFromIndexer`
  (G2.2 / §F.13).
- `overlayHtml` in `ProtectedTextarea` — built via `escapeHtml`
  on every chunk including the matched-text inside `<mark>` tags.
- JSON-LD in `Head.svelte` — `<` escaped to `\u003c`.

None render i18n strings directly; auto-escape protects every
locale value.  No markdown library imported — FAQ markdown-like
syntax renders as literal text.  **No findings.**

**§F.32 — Welcome-bonus + attestation + loyalty.**  All grift
paths closed:
- Welcome bonus requires real order ownership cited in
  feedback (§F.7 G1.1 + §F.8 R17 fixes intact).
- Loyalty milestones only fire on actual BLURT-paid fees
  (`feeStatus === 'verified'` AND `transfer !== null` AND
  `rowCount > 0`) — not on `verified_by_attestation`, so BTC/XMR
  attested fees can't sybil-amplify into BLURT-denominated
  loyalty rewards.
- UPSERT pattern with `RETURNING (... - $2)` captures pre-insert
  total atomically; no race window.
- UNIQUE constraint on `account_loyalty_milestones (account,
  milestone_blurt)`; replays land as `unique_violation` and skip.
- `relay_pending_transfers` queues CUMULATIVE BP target (not
  increment) since the relay's `delegate_vesting_shares` SETS
  rather than ADDS.

**No findings.**

**§F.33 — Notification system.**  `apps/web/src/lib/
notifications/native.ts`: permission asked at point-of-relevance
(not page-load), decline-state with escalating cooldowns (1
week → 1 month → never), `isCurrentlySilenced` honors mute-until
+ quiet hours, `pageIsFocused` check prevents notifications when
user is already looking.  `notify()` has zero callers in
production code today — the system is wired but dormant.
**No findings.**

**§F.34 — Forgejo CI security.**  `.forgejo/workflows/ci.yml`:
`npm ci --no-audit --no-fund` (locked install, no extra
network), pinned action major versions (`@v4`), build manifest
SHA-256 produced as artifact, bundle-size warning at 500KB,
no secrets used, 14-day artifact retention, `pull_request`
trigger has no privileged steps so external-PR blast radius is
runner CPU only.  Action major-version pinning is less strict
than commit-SHA pinning — operators paranoid about supply-chain
attacks on action publishers can choose to SHA-pin.  Documented
residual.  **No findings.**

**§F.35 — Build output integrity.**  CI emits per-file SHA-256
manifest as artifact.  Aggregate hash for trust-anchor
verification not yet broadcast — that's the §F.26 release-
trust-anchor frontend gap, both sides documented Phase 5 work.
The infrastructure is positioned correctly; just not wired
end-to-end.  **No findings.**

**§F.36 — FAQ legal accuracy spot-check.**  89 FAQ entries
across 10 locales.  Found U3.3: `taxes` entry uses agorist
framing that some jurisdictions read as advocating evasion.
Not factually inaccurate, but tone-aggressive on a regulated
topic.  Editorial decision for the team; not a code fix.
Other legal-keyword-matching entries (`vs_others`, `kyc_
requirement`, `privacy_practices`, `rogue_operator`,
`how_morphit_protects_me`, `chat_dispute_recourse`)
spot-checked — phrasing accurate for the project's
non-custodial-no-KYC posture.

### Cumulative integrity (post §F.22–§F.36)

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Typecheck — frontend | 0 errors |
| Typecheck — indexer src | 2 errors (pre-existing baseline) |
| Typecheck — indexer-client | 0 errors |
| Typecheck — operator-config | 0 errors |
| Smokes | 278/278 across 17 runners |
| i18n parity | **1324 keys × 10 locales, 0 drift** (added blocked_marker) |

### What's left for future audits

Surfaces NOT walked in this multi-arc sweep, ordered by
remaining audit value:

1. **dblurt / @beblurt third-party libraries** — these are
   pinned in package.json and we trust them.  A dependency
   audit would compute the SHA-256 of each fetched tarball and
   compare against expected.  Out of scope for code review;
   needs supply-chain tooling.
2. **Operator monitoring dashboard** — confirmed missing in
   §F.18.  Operators currently have nothing in-app to see
   relay balance, drain queue depth, ceiling status, signup
   abuse alerts.  Feature work, not audit work.
3. **Mobile PWA install + offline polish.**  Manifest +
   service-worker shipped; install flow not deeply walked.
4. **The `taxes` FAQ + similar editorial entries.**  Native-
   speaker review across all 10 locales recommended.

(Note: Lightning support — previously listed here as "Phase 5,
not yet built" — was cancelled in 2026-04-27. Morphit will
stick with the existing on-chain Bitcoin support; the Bitcoin
fee-attest / receiving-address paths are the product's full
BTC story going forward.)

### Net audit result for the multi-arc sweep

Two real bugs found and fixed (U1.1, U2.1).  Three findings
flagged for product-owner review (U2.2 syndication disclosure,
U3.2 dead-code cleanup, U3.3 tax FAQ tone).  Twelve audit
arcs cleared with no findings.

The project is in genuinely good shape post-§F.21.  The
chain-direct attack class is fully swept.  The read-side
surfaces (orderbook, RSS, profile fetch) are uniformly defended.
The state-management surfaces (auto-lock, identity, keystore)
have been audited end-to-end across §F.14–§F.20.  Operator-
trust surfaces (release, rotator, fees) are positioned with
documented residuals that can ship as Phase 5 trust-anchor
work.

## Phase B — Operator CLI tooling (2026-04-26)

Shipped a standalone command-line tool for operators to monitor
their Morphit instance.  Lives in `apps/ops-cli/`, alongside
`apps/web`, `apps/indexer`, `apps/relay`.

### Design decisions, recap

Per pre-build agreement:
- **Stack:** TypeScript + Node, no commander/chalk/yargs deps.
  Only third-party dep is `pg`.  Tiny built-in arg parser
  (~50 LOC) handles the eight subcommands and global flags.
- **Location:** `apps/ops-cli/` as its own app.  Independent
  `package.json` and `tsconfig.json`.
- **Auth:** local-only — reads from the indexer + relay shared
  Postgres directly.  No HTTP admin endpoint.  No mutation paths.
- **Output:** dashboard with sections + status glyphs (`✓` `⚠`
  `✗`) for `status`; sparser per-item lists for drill-downs.
  Every subcommand also accepts `--json` for scripting.
- **Color:** TTY-aware by default, with `NO_COLOR` and
  `--no-color` honored.  Falls back to `[OK]`/`[WARN]`/`[ERR]`
  ASCII tags when color is off.

### Subcommands

- `status` — operator dashboard at a glance (indexer state,
  drain queue, signups today, moderation flags 24h)
- `drain-queue [--age=DUR]` — pending relay transfers
- `signups [--since=DUR]` — recent signups via this relay
- `abuse [--since=DUR]` — combined abuse signals (broadcast
  failures + reciprocity flags + related-account flags)
- `failed-broadcasts [--since=DUR]` — relay broadcasts that
  errored
- `loyalty [--since=DUR]` — loyalty milestone delegations
- `attestations` — orders awaiting fee-attestation verification
- `flags [--type=...] [--since=DUR]` — moderation flags
  drill-down

### Threshold tunables

Each metric maps to a status glyph via a warn/error threshold
pair, all operator-overridable:

| Metric | Default warn | Default error |
|---|---|---|
| Relay BLURT balance | <100 | <30 |
| Drain queue oldest age | >5 min | >1 h |
| Indexer block lag | >5 blocks | >30 blocks |
| Today's signups | >80% ceiling | >100% ceiling |
| Abuse alerts in 24h | >10 | >50 |

### Files added

```
apps/ops-cli/
├── README.md                          Operator-facing guide
├── package.json                       Single dep: pg
├── tsconfig.json                      Plain relative imports, no path aliases
├── src/
│   ├── main.ts                        Entry + arg parser + subcommand router
│   ├── config.ts                      Env loader + threshold defaults
│   ├── db.ts                          pg.Pool wrapper
│   ├── render/
│   │   ├── term.ts                    ANSI colors, glyphs, sections
│   │   └── json.ts                    --json emitter
│   ├── lib/
│   │   ├── ctx.ts                     Shared CommandCtx
│   │   └── time.ts                    Duration formatting helpers
│   └── commands/
│       ├── status.ts                  Dashboard (~315 LOC)
│       ├── drainQueue.ts
│       ├── signups.ts
│       ├── abuse.ts
│       ├── failedBroadcasts.ts
│       ├── loyalty.ts
│       ├── attestations.ts
│       └── flags.ts
├── scripts/
│   └── ops-cli-smoke.ts               35-scenario smoke runner
└── test/
    └── time.test.ts                   Vitest mirror of the smoke
```

Total: ~1700 LOC across 17 files.

### What's NOT in v1 (deferred to a follow-up phase)

The following operator-mutation subcommands need design
decisions before implementation and are deliberately out of
scope:

- `drain-now` — manual nudge to the drainer.  Requires either
  a relay HTTP admin endpoint or a Postgres-mediated nudge
  signal (the drainer polls every 60s naturally).
- `pause-signups` / `--resume` — toggle the relay's
  `MORPHIT_RELAY_SIGNUP_ENABLED` flag dynamically.  Today this
  requires editing `morphit.config.env` and restarting the
  relay.  Dynamic toggle needs an HTTP admin endpoint.
- `set-ceiling` — adjust the daily signup ceiling.  Same shape
  as pause-signups.
- `top-up-balance` — informational only (computes recommended
  top-up); doesn't move funds.

If we add any of these, the right path is a relay HTTP admin
endpoint with signed-challenge auth: operator's posting key
signs a one-time challenge from the relay, relay validates the
signature against a pinned operator pubkey before honoring the
mutation.  Lets the CLI run from anywhere (operator's laptop,
not just the VPS), with strong auth.

- `scripts/run-smokes.sh` includes `apps/ops-cli:ops-cli-smoke` —
  35 scenarios pass.
- Total smoke count: **313 scenarios across 18 runners** (was
  278/17 pre-Phase B).

## Phase C — Operator setup wizard (2026-04-26)

Shipped `morphit-ops init` — a first-time-setup wizard that
walks new operators through generating their `morphit.config.env`
and posting-key keystore.

### Pre-build decisions (recap)

Per pre-build agreement:
- **Location:** `morphit-ops init` subcommand (not separate
  binary).  Same binary handles read-only ops + setup.
- **Mandatory fields:** instance name, DB URL, relay account,
  posting key, fees account.  **Defaulted:** tagline, daily
  ceiling.  **Optional:** contact URL, alt-network addresses.
- **Style:** pure-interactive (no `--config-file` for v1).
- **Tone:** ELI5 with examples; explain what each thing IS;
  provide suggestions.
- **Posting key:** default ENCRYPTED (passphrase-prompted at
  startup).  Plaintext mode available as opt-in for operators
  with external secret management.

### Pre-flight system check

Runs unconditionally before the wizard prompts.  Eleven checks:
CPU cores, architecture, RAM (total + free), disk free, Node.js
version, OS detection (parses `/etc/os-release`), systemd
availability, Postgres reachable, outbound HTTPS, and system
time drift vs an HTTPS reference clock.

OS detection covers Ubuntu 26.04 LTS (recommended), 24.04 LTS
(recommended), 22.04 LTS (warns — aging), interim Ubuntu releases
(warns — expires soon), pre-22.04 (errors — EOL), Debian 12+
(works), other Linux (warns — distro on its own), and
non-Linux (errors).

`--check-only` flag runs the system check and exits without
prompting.

### The 9 wizard steps

1. Instance name (required) — visible in title bar/footer
2. Tagline (defaulted to "A Morphit instance")
3. Database URL (required) — Postgres connection string with
   `createdb` instructions in the prompt
4. Relay Blurt account (required) — validates against name format,
   then RPC-looks-up account on chain, displays balance, warns if
   balance < 50 signups' worth
5. Posting key (required) — choice of encrypted (recommended) or
   plaintext.  Encrypted mode prompts for passphrase, calls
   `encryptEnvelope` from the relay's keyEnvelope module (single
   source of truth for envelope format)
6. Fees account (required, defaulted to relay account)
7. Daily signup ceiling (defaulted, balance-aware: if relay has
   200 BLURT balance with 100 BLURT fee, suggests ceiling of 1
   not 50)
8. Contact URL (optional) — http/https/mailto only
9. Alt-network addresses (optional) — Tor, Lokinet, I2P, Nostr.
   Wizard collects existing addresses; doesn't generate them
   (operator runs `scripts/generate-onion.sh` etc. separately)

After all 9 steps, the wizard shows a review with the database
password masked, asks for confirmation, then writes:
- `morphit.config.env` to repo root (or `--out=PATH`)
- Keystore to `apps/relay/keystore.{wif,json}` (path referenced
  via `MORPHIT_RELAY_ACTIVE_KEY_FILE` in the config)

Both files written with `0600` permissions.  Existing config is
detected and backed up to `morphit.config.env.bak-<timestamp>`
before overwriting (operator confirmation required).

### Files added

```
apps/ops-cli/
├── src/
│   ├── commands/
│   │   └── init.ts                      Orchestrator (~280 LOC)
│   └── init/
│       ├── prompt.ts                    readline wrapper (~160 LOC)
│       ├── systemCheck.ts               11-check pre-flight (~360 LOC)
│       ├── steps.ts                     9 wizard steps (~430 LOC)
│       ├── encrypt.ts                   re-export of relay keyEnvelope (~30 LOC)
│       ├── chainCheck.ts                Blurt RPC + name validator (~120 LOC)
│       └── render.ts                    Config writer (~190 LOC)
└── scripts/
    └── init-smoke.ts                    22 scenarios (~280 LOC)
```

Total Phase C: ~1850 LOC across 7 source files + 1 smoke runner.

### Lazy pg import

The `db.ts` pg dependency was made lazy (dynamic import inside
`createDatabase`) so the wizard can run on a fresh checkout
where `npm install` hasn't happened yet.  `init` doesn't touch
the DB.

### Sanity guards on the chain account-creation fee

Per the corrections audit (§F.37 above), Phase C ships with the
operator-tunable `MORPHIT_INDEXER_ACCOUNT_CREATION_FEE_BLURT`
(default 100) used as both fallback for malformed chain RPC
and 10% sanity threshold.  The relay refuses to broadcast if
the chain reports a fee >10% above the configured value,
preventing a witness emergency-raise from quietly draining
the relay before the operator can react.

- Total smoke count: **335 scenarios across 19 runners** (was
  313/18 pre-Phase C).

## Phase D.5 — Federation auto-discovery (2026-04-26)

Replaced the static `known-instances.json` (which would have
required Agorise to manually curate every operator) with a
chain-driven federation directory: operators register their
origin on-chain, every Morphit indexer's chain replay
populates a `known_instances` table, a probe scheduler
verifies liveness, and a dynamic `/v1/instances` endpoint
serves the directory.  Zero manual maintenance after initial
seed.

### Discovery mechanism

The `morphit_operator_register_v1` op (already shipping as v1
for the on-chain operator directory) gained an optional
`origin` field in v2.  Backwards-compatible — old register
ops without origin still validate and persist; new ones
publish the origin on-chain where every Morphit indexer sees
it via natural replay.

When the handler accepts a register op WITH origin, it ALSO
inserts a row into `known_instances` (the local probe-state
table).  Every indexer running the same handler against the
same chain ends up with identical `known_instances` content
modulo what's been probed locally — the chain is the
federation gossip layer.

### Probe scheduler

`apps/indexer/src/indexer/federationProbe.ts` (~410 LOC).
Runs on the same poller-tick rhythm as the other scanners
(operator-balance, low-balance), self-throttling.  Per
instance:
- Probes /v1/instance, /v1/health, /v1/orderbook?limit=1
- 5-second timeout per fetch (15s worst-case per probe)
- Bounded concurrency (default 10 simultaneous probes)
- Re-probe schedule: 10min for healthy, 1h for failing
- Drops the row after 7 consecutive days of failure

Status classification (5 buckets):
- **good**: /v1/health=ok + relay_account matches + chain lag <30 blocks + recent orderbook activity (or new-instance grace)
- **quiet**: like 'good' but no orderbook activity in 7d AND >7d old
- **stale**: /v1/health=degraded OR malformed OR chain lag too high
- **unreachable**: HTTP fetch failed (timeout, refused, DNS, TLS)
- **mismatch**: origin reachable but relay_account doesn't match operator_account from chain

### Federation seed

`apps/indexer/src/indexer/federationSeed.ts` (~80 LOC).  At
indexer boot, idempotently inserts hardcoded reference
instances into `known_instances` with `last_probe_status='never'`.
The probe scheduler picks them up on first tick and verifies
them like any other peer.

Currently seeds only `morphit.io` (operator account: `morphit`).
Purpose: short-circuit chain-replay latency.  A fresh indexer
takes hours to fully replay; without seeding, /instances
would show "no peers known yet" the whole time even though
the canonical instance is reachable.

The seed cannot bypass verification — a malicious change to
the seed list (PR adding `evil-morphit.example` claiming to
be `@morphit`) would degrade to status='mismatch' at probe
time, not poison the directory.

### Dynamic /v1/instances endpoint

`apps/indexer/src/api/instances.ts` (~125 LOC).  Reads
`known_instances` joined to `operators`, returns the
federation directory as JSON.  Filterable by status
(`?status=good`).  Cache-Control: 60s.

Response sort: `good` → `quiet` → `stale` → `mismatch` →
`unreachable` → `never`, then by registration date desc.
Healthy peers float to the top.

### Frontend `/instances` page rewrite

Was: static fetch of `/known-instances.json`.
Is: dynamic fetch via `getInstances()` of `/v1/instances`,
status filter dropdown, color-coded status badges (green,
amber, orange, red, grey), per-instance metadata block
(operator, registration time, last probed, indexed block).

"You are here" badge marks the current instance — comparison
by `entry.operator_account === $instance.relay_account`
(reliable, sourced from local /v1/instance).  Subtle green
ring around the card.

`apps/web/static/known-instances.json` deleted.

### Wizard integration

10th step added to `morphit-ops init`: collects the public
origin URL with full validation (https-only, no userinfo,
scheme + host only, normalized for storage).  Optional but
strongly encouraged — without it, the operator's instance
won't appear anywhere.

`MORPHIT_INSTANCE_ORIGIN` allowlisted in operator-config and
written to `morphit.config.env`.  Wired through indexer
schema + Config + loadConfig.

### `morphit-ops register` subcommand

`apps/ops-cli/src/commands/register.ts` (~280 LOC).  Reads
env, loads keystore (prompts for unlock passphrase if
encrypted), builds the morphit_operator_register_v1
custom_json op, signs with dblurt, broadcasts via
`condenser_api.broadcast_transaction_synchronous` with
endpoint rotation.

Lazy-imports dblurt so other subcommands run without it
installed.  Surfaces clear error messages for tag-already-
claimed, account-already-registered, key-mismatch, and
RC-exhaustion failures.

The wizard's printed "Next steps" mentions `morphit-ops register`
as step 8 when origin was set, intentionally AFTER step 7
(`status` to verify the indexer is up).  Operators
register on-chain only after their stack is serving;
otherwise the federation probes find them unreachable.

### Privacy notes

Cross-instance probes go out from each indexer's IP.
Aggregate cross-instance traffic is structurally inherent
to federation discovery — `evil-spying.example` already
knows Morphit instances exist; a periodic probe ping
adds nothing it couldn't infer from public chain
state.

Tor-routing of probes when an operator has a Tor address
configured is possible but deferred to Phase F+ (significant
complexity, marginal threat-model improvement for public
instances).

### What's NOT in v1 (deferred)

- **Live verification of /v1/instances against a real chain.**
  Can't be done in this sandbox; requires booted indexer +
  populated DB.  Schema, route mounting, frontend client are
  typecheck + smoke-clean.  Validate end-to-end on next
  reference deploy.
- **Tor-routing for probes** — deferred to Phase F+.  Adds
  significant complexity for marginal benefit on public
  instances.  Operators with strict OPSEC requirements
  shouldn't run Morphit publicly without their own tor
  proxy in front of `fetch` anyway.
- **Probe rate limiting per-target.** Currently every
  Morphit indexer probes every other every 10min for healthy
  peers.  At 1000 instances that's 100 probes/sec aggregated
  across the federation — manageable.  At 10,000 it'd be
  noisy.  Revisit if/when uptake matters.
- **Frontend reachability check.** Only the indexer's
  `/v1/*` endpoints get probed.  An operator could have
  indexer up but frontend down (broken nginx) and still get
  status='good'.  Adding the check requires either a
  separate frontend-URL field in the registration op or
  assuming `frontend === origin/`.  Defer to Phase F+.
- **Fork detection via block-age cluster median.** If 95%
  of instances see chain head at block N but @alice's is
  at N-1000, that's a fork detection signal.  Probably
  overkill for v1; current chain-lag check catches normal
  laggy-indexer cases.
- **TLS expiry pre-warning.** Cert expiry would be a useful
  alert for operators to avoid `unreachable` blackouts.
  Currently surfaces only as `unreachable` after expiry.
- **`morphit-ops update` and `morphit-ops deregister`
  subcommands.** Operators currently can't update their
  origin or display_name without re-registering with a
  different account.  ADR-0013 mentions a future
  `morphit_operator_update_v1` op; not in scope here.

### Operator instructions (going-forward)

1. Run `morphit-ops init` — wizard collects origin in step 9
2. Source morphit.env, install deps, run migrations, start
   indexer + relay + frontend (steps 1-6 in next-steps)
3. Verify with `morphit-ops status` (step 7)
4. Run `morphit-ops register` (step 8) — publishes the
   registration op on-chain
5. Within roughly a minute every Morphit indexer (including
   morphit.io and your own) will see your registration via
   chain replay, probe your origin, and add you to their
   /instances directory.

### Latency budget breakdown

For the curious, here's where the ~60s figure comes from:

```
broadcast → block included     ≈  3s   (next Blurt block)
peer indexer's chain poll      ≤  3s   (block-interval ticker)
peer chain-replay applies op   <  1s   (in-process)
peer scheduler tick            ≤ 15s   (probe scheduler interval)
peer HTTP probe                ≈  1s   (3 fetches × <1s healthy)
peer's /v1/instances cache TTL ≤ 60s   (Cache-Control max-age)
                                ─────
total worst-case               ≈ 80s
typical                        ≈ 25-40s
```

Subscribers to /v1/instances/stream see the diff sooner — no
60s cache-TTL gate; status changes flow as SSE events.

## Phase D.5+ — Real-time `/instances` page (2026-04-26)

Two follow-ups on the federation directory shipped:

### Latency budget correction

The Phase D.5 close-out claimed "~10 minutes" for federation
propagation; that was wrong (I conflated re-probe interval
with first-probe interval).  The actual figure is **~25-40
seconds typical, ~80s worst case**.

Tightened the probe scheduler tick from 60s to 15s while
leaving per-instance throttling unchanged (10min for healthy
peers, 1h for failing peers).  The tick controls how quickly
newly-inserted rows get noticed, not how often individual
peers get re-probed.

Updated the register subcommand's success message and the
REVISIT-LIST close-out to reflect the real numbers.

### `/v1/instances/stream` SSE endpoint

The /instances page is now real-time.  As registrations land
on chain and probes complete, the page auto-updates without
refresh.

**Backend:**
- New `/v1/instances/stream` endpoint at
  `apps/indexer/src/api/instancesStream.ts` + a pure-helpers
  module at `apps/indexer/src/api/instancesStreamHelpers.ts`
  (split for testability without Hono installed).
- Wire protocol: standard SSE.  Events: `snapshot` (initial
  full directory), `instance_added`, `instance_updated`,
  `instance_removed`.  `:keepalive` comments every 25s.
- Implementation: poll-based (5s interval).  Each connection
  diffs known_instances against an in-memory cursor of
  per-origin signatures, emits the diff as named events.
  Memory cost ~50KB per connection.  Lifecycle: ReadableStream's
  `cancel()` cleans up timers when the client disconnects.
- Push-based emission deferred to Phase E (orderbook SSE);
  poll is sufficient for the federation directory's volume.

**Frontend:**
- `/instances` rewritten to use `Map<origin, entry>` for
  O(1) updates.
- EventSource subscription on mount; auto-reconnect handled
  by the browser (snapshot event reconciles missed diffs).
- "Live" pip in the page header showing connection state
  (animated dot + label, hides on disconnect).
- Filter still applied client-side via `$derived` array.
- Fallback: browsers without EventSource fall back to a
  one-shot REST + 30s periodic refetch.

**Lazy loading:** SvelteKit per-route code splitting is
already automatic — the `/instances` page bundle isn't
downloaded until users navigate to it.  No additional
work needed.

**Smoke:** new instances-stream-smoke runner (11 scenarios)
covering rowToEntry shape conversion + rowSignature change
detection semantics.  The signature must change for
user-visible field changes (status, name, alt-networks) and
NOT change for internal probe metadata (last_probed_at,
consecutive_failures) — the test fence around that is
load-bearing because a too-eager signature spams subscribers
and a too-lax one hides real changes.

## Phase E — Real-time orderbook (2026-04-26)

The orderbook page is now live.  As orders are posted,
replaced, cancelled, or pass fee verification, the page
auto-updates without refresh.  Same UX language as
Phase D.5+'s real-time `/instances`: a "Live" pip in the
header, status diffs streamed via SSE, buffered render at
60fps so a burst of order ops doesn't trash the UI.

### Push vs poll (different choice from Phase D.5+)

The instances stream uses a poll-based diff: every 5s the
server re-queries known_instances and emits diffs against
the per-connection cursor.  Volume is low enough that poll
is bulletproof — no risk of forgetting to emit somewhere.

For orderbook, push.  Order volume is high enough (chain
blocks can carry dozens of order ops at once) that a coarse
poll would either be too slow (missed events) or too
aggressive (DB load).  An in-process EventEmitter
(orderbookEventBus) gets `emit(orderId)` calls from every
order-mutating handler — order, orderReplace, orderCancel,
feeAttest.  SSE connections subscribe.

Defense-in-depth: the SSE handler ALSO runs a 60s fallback
poll that catches any orders updated in the last 90s
matching the filter and emits any the bus missed.  Belt-and-
suspenders against missed-emit bugs in future code paths
without requiring perfect emit hygiene at every mutation
site.

### Pre-existing infrastructure (already in place before this turn)

- `OpContext.recordOrderbookChange(orderId)` — handler
  callback added during the earlier Phase E groundwork.
  Wired into order/orderReplace/orderCancel/feeAttest.
- `dispatcher.ts` — collects orderbookChanges per block,
  returns them with the block stats.
- `poller.ts` — emits the changes on the bus AFTER withTx
  resolves (commit successful), so SSE subscribers never
  see phantom events from rolled-back ops.
- `orderbookEventBus.ts` — singleton in-process pub/sub
  with .on() / .emit() / .subscriberCount.

What's NEW in this turn: the SSE endpoint that subscribes
to the bus, the wire format, the frontend composable, and
the buffered render.

### Filter-aware subscription

Each SSE connection's URL specifies the filter (asset, side,
fiat, region, payment_methods, min_trades — same shape as
the REST orderbook query).  Server-side filtering means
each connection only receives events matching what the user
is currently viewing.

Filter changes require disconnect + reconnect (EventSource
doesn't support changing URLs after construction).  The
frontend handles this cleanly via `restartStream()` called
from the same debounced effect that triggers the REST
refetch.  Brief flicker as the orderbook re-renders is fine
— users expect that on a filter change.

### Wire protocol

```
event: snapshot
data: {"items":[<OrderRecord>...],"indexed_block":12345}

event: order_upserted
data: {<single OrderRecord>}

event: order_removed
data: {"account":"alice","permlink":"sell-btc-eur-..."}

:keepalive
```

Two diff event types instead of three: `order_upserted`
covers create, update, and fee_status_changed because the
frontend's apply logic is the same — find by (account,
permlink), replace if exists, otherwise insert.  Collapsing
keeps the wire format minimal.

Keepalive comments every 25s prevent idle-kill from proxies.

### Buffered render trick

A chain block can include 50 order ops at once.  Each emits
an SSE event; without buffering, that's 50 Svelte rerenders
in <100ms — visible jank.

The frontend composable buffers events in a queue and
flushes via `requestAnimationFrame`.  Result: 1 render per
animation frame at the cost of ≤16ms latency, regardless
of arrival rate.

`onSnapshot` drops any pending buffered diffs first because
the snapshot is authoritative — no point applying old diffs
on top of a fresh state.

### Per-connection memory bound

Each SSE connection tracks the set of orderIds it's sent as
upserts (so it knows whether `order_removed` should be sent
to that subscriber).  Without a bound, a long-lived
connection accumulates orderIds forever.

Bound: `MAX_TRACKED_ORDERS = 1000`.  When exceeded, oldest
ID drops.  We do NOT notify the client about the drop —
the order stays visible in the user's already-rendered DOM;
we just stop tracking it for future updates.  Acceptable
because affected orders are old (way past first-page),
users care about the recent ones.

### Rate limiting

The REST `/v1/orderbook` route uses a shared per-minute
rate-limit middleware (`rateLimit('list', config.listRatePerMin)`).
SSE doesn't fit that model — connections are long-lived,
opened once per filter change.  Sharing the budget would
mean a few REST requests could starve the SSE budget for
the same client.

Solution: mount `/v1/orderbook/stream` OUTSIDE the rate-
limited orderbookApp.  Per-IP open-connection caps belong
at the reverse-proxy layer (nginx limit_conn) where they
can apply uniformly across all SSE endpoints, not in
indexer middleware.

- **`apps/indexer/src/api/orderbookStream.ts`** (~360 LOC)
  - Hono route, SSE wiring, bus subscription, fallback
    poll, keepalive, lifecycle (cleanup on cancel)
- **`apps/indexer/src/api/orderbookStreamHelpers.ts`** (~120 LOC)
  - Pure helpers extracted for testability without Hono:
    `buildWhereClauses`, `rowToWire`, `sseEvent`, query
    interface
  - Mirror of the `instancesStream` / `instancesStreamHelpers`
    split
- **`apps/web/src/lib/orderbook/stream.ts`** (~190 LOC)
  - Frontend composable: `createOrderbookStream({ query,
    onSnapshot, applyUpsert, applyRemove, onStreamingChange })`
  - Buffered render via requestAnimationFrame
  - Auto-reconnect via EventSource's built-in behavior;
    snapshot reconciles missed diffs
- **`apps/web/src/routes/orderbook/+page.svelte`** (modified)
  - SSE state + lifecycle wired into existing REST flow

    SSE keeps it fresh; both happen on filter change
- **`apps/indexer/scripts/orderbook-stream-smoke.ts`** (~210 LOC)

### Test fixture fix (incidental)

Discovered that `OpContext.recordOrderbookChange` had been
added to the type but not to the `makeCtx` test fixture.
Order, orderReplace, orderCancel, feeAttest handlers all
call this function; without it stubbed, 13 pre-existing
smoke scenarios were silently broken (counted in the 368

Added a no-op default to `makeCtx`.  Tests that want to

### What's NOT in v1 (deferred)

- **Live-fire smoke against a populated DB.**  The pure
  helpers and the frontend composable are smoke-tested.
  The DB-touching paths (snapshot fetch, single-row lookup,
  fallback poll) are typecheck-clean and visually
  inspected; live verification needs a booted indexer with
  populated orders.  Validate end-to-end on next deploy.
- **Filter change without reconnect.**  EventSource's URL
  is immutable post-construction.  An alternate protocol
  (sending a `filter_update` message via a parallel POST
  endpoint that the bus subscriber reads) is possible but
  adds complexity.  Reconnect-on-filter-change is fine UX.
- **Sort change in the stream.**  The stream is fixed to
  sort=recent.  Users with sort=rating or sort=trades
  selected get REST data sorted that way; the SSE stream
  doesn't know.  Could be addressed by accepting `sort=`
  in the stream URL too — minor work; deferred.
- **Pagination via stream.**  The snapshot is always the
  first page.  Pagination beyond the first page stays
  REST-only.  This is a deliberate limitation: SSE for
  live updates of what's visible, REST for browsing
  history.
- **Backpressure.**  If a subscriber is slow (background
  tab, weak network), the SSE handler's ReadableStream
  enqueue can stall.  The browser will eventually
  disconnect and reconnect when they come back.  No
  per-connection backpressure logic in the indexer; the
  bus dispatches synchronously and doesn't care.

## SSE stack deep audit (2026-04-27)

After Phase E shipped, walked the full real-time stack
end-to-end: orderbook event bus, both SSE endpoints, both
helpers modules, REST `/v1/instances`, REST `/v1/orderbook`
filter parity, dispatcher emission discipline, poller
post-commit timing, federation probe + seed, frontend
composables, both pages.

Catalogued 51 findings (F-1 through F-51).  Most were
walking-through scenarios that turned out correct;
20-odd were genuine issues at varying severity.

### HIGH-severity bugs fixed

**F-7 — fee_attest didn't bump `updated_at`.**  The
fallback poll in `orderbookStream.ts` uses
`o.updated_at > cutoff` to find recently-changed rows.
Without bumping `updated_at` on fee-status flips, a missed
bus emit for a `verified_by_attestation` UPDATE would never
be caught by the safety-net poll either — the order would
silently fail to appear for active subscribers until
something else mutated it.  Fix: feeAttest's UPDATE now sets
`updated_at = ctx.blockTime` (deterministic; using NOW()
would break replay reproducibility).

**F-13 — fallback poll's tracked-set guard double-missed.**
The poll's `if (!tracked.has(orderId))` skipped already-
tracked rows.  But "the bus missed an emit AND we already
have the row tracked" is a real scenario (e.g., a bus emit
gets dropped on a state transition that doesn't change
visibility — payment_methods edit).  Fix: always emit
upsert for any matching row in the recent window;
frontend's applyUpsert is idempotent, so the bandwidth cost
is negligible compared to closing the correctness hole.

### MEDIUM-severity bugs fixed

**F-5 — snapshot/subscribe race.**  Original flow was
fetch-snapshot, push-snapshot, subscribe-bus.  Events on the
bus during the window between snapshot fetch and bus
subscribe were silently dropped (caught by 60s fallback
poll, but during those 60s subscribers see stale state).
Fix: subscribe to bus FIRST.  During the snapshot, bus emits
land in `pendingDuringSnapshot: Set<string>`.  After
snapshot is pushed, drain the set through the normal
processOrderChange path.  Race window eliminated entirely.

**F-6 — concurrent async fetches per bus event raced.**
Original code was `void (async () => { fetch + emit })()`
inside the bus listener.  Two rapid emits for the same
orderId started two concurrent fetches; whichever returned
first won the safePush.  Subscribers could see "old → new
→ old" state sequence.  Fix: extracted
`makeFetchSerializer` helper into orderbookStreamHelpers.ts
implementing per-orderId at-most-one-fetch semantics with a
dirty-flag re-fire pattern (state machine: `undefined →
'in-flight' → 'in-flight-dirty' → 'in-flight' →
undefined`).  Out-of-order responses for the same orderId
are now provably impossible.  Six new smoke scenarios cover
the state machine.

**F-19 — instances rowSignature missed UI fields.**
`last_probed_at`, `operator_display_name`, and
`operator_tag` are rendered on the /instances page but
weren't in the change-detection signature.  Successful
re-probes (every 10min) and operator profile updates
wouldn't trigger an `instance_updated` event — page
displayed stale data until manual refresh.  Fix: added all
three to the signature.  Cost: ~25 events/min across all
healthy instances, well below user-perception spam
threshold.  Smoke updated: the prior "different
last_probed_at → SAME signature" assertion was inverted;
two new scenarios for operator_display_name and
operator_tag added.

**F-27 — dropFailedInstances query never fired.**  The
query checked `last_probed_at < NOW() - 7 days`, but every
failed probe BUMPS last_probed_at to NOW(), so the
condition was unreachable.  Failed instances accumulated
forever in `known_instances` (capped at 200, but still
wrong).  Fix: switched to `consecutive_failures >= 168`
(168 probe attempts at 1h failure interval = 7 days).

**F-2 — orderbook stream min_trades cap diverged from
REST.**  REST capped at 100, stream at 1_000_000.
Filter-validity asymmetry would have been a footgun for
clients building requests for both.  Fix: stream now caps
at 100.

**F-15 — instances stream poll setInterval didn't await
prior tick.**  Two overlapping ticks could double-emit the
same diff.  Fix: in-flight guard (`pollInFlight` flag).

**F-26 — orderbook stream silently dropped
payment_methods=,,, .**  Schema accepted any 1-256 char
string; post-parse split yielded zero tokens; SQL clause
guarded with `if (methods.length > 0)` so it was simply
skipped.  User thought they'd filtered, didn't.  Fix:
post-parse validation rejects with HTTP 400, mirroring REST
behavior.

**F-41 — instances page stuck "Loading..." on EventSource
failure.**  If EventSource exists but server is unreachable,
the page never received a snapshot and `snapshotReceived`
stayed false forever.  Fix: on `error` event, if
!snapshotReceived, kick over to REST fallback poll.
EventSource keeps reconnecting in the background; the next
successful snapshot will normalize state.

### LOW-severity bugs fixed

**F-9, F-10 ×4 — emit on rowCount=0.**  Order handlers
called `recordOrderbookChange` even when their UPDATE/INSERT
was a replay no-op.  Practically impossible during normal
operation (replay only on indexer restart from checkpoint),
but cheap to fix.  All 5 emit sites (orderReplace ×1,
order ×4 paths) now gate on rowCount > 0.

**F-11 — dead `seenInPoll` variable.**  Leftover from an
earlier fallback-poll-based-removal idea that got
commented out.  Removed.

**F-23 — instances.ts SQL string-interpolation of
statusFilter.**  Guarded by VALID_STATUS_FILTERS allowlist
so no actual SQL injection vector, but fragile if the
allowlist ever gets a value with special chars.  Fix:
parameterize.

**F-1 — subscriberCount documented but not wired.**  The
bus's `subscriberCount` getter had a comment saying it was
used in /v1/health verbose, but it wasn't.  Wired in:
`diagnostics.sse_subscribers.orderbook` reflects current
count.  Useful for operators triaging "is anyone watching"
or "is the bus actually reaching SSE consumers".

**F-24 — instances.ts duplicated rowToEntry mapping.**
Parallel codepath to instancesStream's rowToEntry helper —
two places that needed updating in lockstep when fields
changed.  Refactored: instances.ts now uses the helper.
SQL stays distinct (different ORDER BY needs) but the
wire-shape mapping is shared.  Also broke a circular
import smell by moving InstanceDirectoryEntry's canonical
home into the helpers module (instances.ts re-exports for
public API contract continuity).

**F-42 — misleading comment on `recordOrderbookChange`.**
Said the bus deduplicates via subscriber-side state.  The
bus doesn't dedup; the dispatcher's per-block Set
deduplicates within a block.  Comment corrected.

### Deliberately deferred

**F-14 — per-subscriber DB lookup coalescer.**  At 100
subscribers × 10 events/block = 1000 single-row queries
hitting Postgres in a tick.  PG handles point queries
trivially at this scale; revisit when subscriber counts
warrant.  A simple coalescer (one DB query per orderId
shared across subscribers, applying the per-subscriber
filter in JS) would address it cleanly.

**F-16 — per-connection full directory poll.**  Each
instances stream connection runs its own 5s poll over
known_instances + operators.  At 100 connections that's
100× full-directory queries every 5s.  Directory is the
same for everyone; one shared poll fanning out diffs to all
subscribers would be cheaper.  Modest implementation cost,
genuine scaling improvement.  Defer until concrete scaling
demand appears.

**F-25 — instances stream doesn't accept `?status=`
filter.**  Considered adding to match orderbook stream's
filter awareness.  Decided against: the instances page's
filter is interactive (dropdown), and client-side filtering
is INSTANT.  Server-side filtering would require
disconnect+reconnect on every dropdown change.  For a small
(≤200) and slowly-changing dataset, client-side filtering
is the correct UX choice.

**F-48 — Postgres `statement_timeout` not set.**  The
per-orderId fetch serializer's loop is robust against
fetch failures (try/catch + dirty-flag refire) but not
against indefinite hangs.  If pg pool gets stuck on a
runaway query, the whole serializer hangs.  Operator
concern, not an indexer bug; should be set at the
connection-pool level when MORPHIT_INDEXER_DB_URL allows
it.  Document in operator run-book.

| Typecheck — ops-cli / indexer-client / operator-config | 0 errors |
| Smokes | **407 / 407 across 22 runners** stable across 3 runs |

### Architectural notes from the audit

The SSE stack now has a clean concurrency invariant:
- **Bus subscription happens before snapshot** — events
  during snapshot are queued, not dropped.
- **At-most-one fetch per orderId** — out-of-order
  responses for the same orderId are impossible.
- **Defense in depth via fallback poll** — every 60s, the
  recently-changed window is re-emitted to subscribers,
  catching any future code path that mutates orders without
  emitting on the bus.  Fallback now correctly handles
  already-tracked rows (F-13).
- **Frontend de-dups idempotently** — applyUpsert is
  find-by-key, replace-or-prepend, so re-emitting the same
  row is a no-op visually.

The `makeFetchSerializer` helper is extracted as a pure
function — useful both for testability and as a reusable
pattern if other parts of the system end up needing the
same "coalesced refresh" semantics.

## Phase E.5 — Real-time chat + lazy-load (2026-04-27)

User directive: "morphit chat should be lazy loaded, and also
real-time, just like the orderbook and instances pages."

Two pieces, shipped together because they're entangled —
lazy-loading the heavy chat-crypto code path makes most sense
when paired with replacing the polling loop with SSE (the
controller's transport changes anyway).

### Real-time

Architecture mirrors Phase E (orderbook) exactly:
- In-process `chatEventBus` (`apps/indexer/src/indexer/chatEventBus.ts`)
  carrying `(lo, hi, messageId)` payload — canonical
  conversation pair so SSE subscribers can filter without a
  DB lookup.
- `OpContext.recordChatChange` hook (parallel to
  `recordOrderbookChange`).  The chat handler's INSERT now
  uses `RETURNING id::text` and calls
  `ctx.recordChatChange({ lo, hi, messageId })` after success.
- Dispatcher collects per-block `chatChanges` with the same
  rollback discipline as orderbook (per-op buffer, discard on
  reject/throw, flush to block-level on ok:true).
- Poller emits on the bus AFTER `withTx` resolves — no
  phantom events from rolled-back blocks.
- `/v1/chat/:a/:b/stream` SSE endpoint at
  `apps/indexer/src/api/chatStream.ts`.  Subscribe-first
  pattern (F-5 audit fix carried over): bus subscription
  registered BEFORE snapshot fetch, events during snapshot
  go into `pendingDuringSnapshot`, drained right after
  snapshot pushed.
- Per-id concurrency: chat messages are immutable once
  inserted, so unlike orderbook there's no
  `makeFetchSerializer` need.  Different message ids are
  independent fetches; the frontend sorts by created_at so
  out-of-order delivery is invisible.
- 60s defense-in-depth fallback poll uses an id watermark
  (`fetchSinceId`) — chat messages are append-only so the
  poll just looks for `id > latestEmittedId` matching the
  pair.  Simpler than orderbook's "always re-emit recent
  window" because there's no F-13-class double-miss risk
  (rows don't update; missing one only happens once).

### Wire protocol

```
event: snapshot
data: {"items":[<ChatMessageRecord>...],"indexed_block":12345}

event: message_appended
data: {<single ChatMessageRecord>}

:keepalive
```

Two events, not three.  No `message_removed` — chat messages
are immutable.  No `message_updated` either — the frontend
treats each `message_appended` as either "new" or "dup of
already-seen id" (existing dedup-by-id logic in
`mergePollResponse` handles it idempotently).

### Frontend changes

- `apps/web/src/lib/chat/stream.ts` — new composable mirroring
  `lib/orderbook/stream.ts`.  Buffered render via
  `requestAnimationFrame` (same coalesce-bursts rationale).
  EventSource auto-reconnect; on each reconnect the server
  sends a fresh snapshot.
- `apps/web/src/lib/chat/chatService.ts` — controller refactored:
  - New `subscribeStream` dep wired in `runtimeDeps` to
    `createChatStream`.  Optional for back-compat — tests
    that don't set it run in poll-only mode.
  - When `subscribeStream` is provided, the controller skips
    the initial REST snapshot (SSE delivers it slightly
    faster) and skips the visibility-aware re-poll listener
    (SSE connection stays open across hidden/visible).
  - Visibility cadence (3s/15s) replaced with single 60s
    fallback poll (defense in depth).  Same merge path
    handles snapshot + appends + fallback rows; dedup by id.
  - New `onStreamingChange` dep so the page can render the
    "Live" pip.
- `apps/web/src/lib/components/ConversationView.svelte` —
  added `streaming` state + Live pip in header (same
  visual style as orderbook + instances pages — pulse dot +
  "LIVE" label).
- `chatService.test.ts` — replaced 3 polling-cadence tests
  with new ones for the SSE-primary architecture: SSE snapshot
  delivery, append delivery, "no initial REST when SSE
  wired", "fallback poll fires at 60s when SSE absent",
  destroy cleans up the SSE unsubscribe.

### Lazy-load

`apps/web/src/routes/chat/[peer=account]/+page.svelte` now
dynamic-imports `ConversationView` instead of static.
Vite/SvelteKit splits the component (and its transitive
chat-service / crypto / libsodium / chat-stream / composer
deps) into a separate chunk fetched only after route mount.
Route shell renders a minimal loading placeholder during the
fetch.

The inbox page (`/chat`) was already cheap by deliberate
design — it doesn't import chatService at all.  Heavy
crypto loads ONLY when opening a specific conversation.
This was implicit before; now it's explicit at the
component level too.

### i18n

3 new keys added to all 10 locales:
- `chat.live` — Live pip label (mirror of
  `orderbook.live` and `instances.live`)
- `chat.loading` — placeholder during lazy-load
- `chat.lazy_load_failed` — error if the chunk fetch fails

i18n parity preserved at 1360 keys × 10 locales, 0 drift.

### Observability

`/v1/health` verbose now reports `sse_subscribers.chat`
alongside `sse_subscribers.orderbook`.  Operators can
confirm the bus is wired and see how many tabs are watching
live conversations.

### What's NOT in v1 (deferred)

- **Inbox real-time.**  Conversation page is real-time;
  inbox unread-badge live-update is a separate
  endpoint (`/v1/conversations/:account/stream`).  Most
  users open inbox briefly then click into a conversation,
  so the real-time win is on the conversation page.  Deferred
  as a future polish; the bus and dispatcher infrastructure

  later.
- **Read-receipt SSE.**  `morphit_chat_read_v1` ops are
  delivered via the existing chat read-state polling.
  Adding them to the chat stream would require a separate
  bus event type.  Acceptable as poll-driven for now; reads
  are checkmarks, not message content, so latency tolerance
  is higher.
- **Cross-tab dedup.**  Two tabs open on the same
  conversation each maintain their own SSE connection +
  fallback poll.  Per-account in-flight coalescing across
  tabs would need a SharedWorker or BroadcastChannel
  coordination layer.  Bandwidth cost is real but small at
  expected concurrency; deferred.

## Chat surface deep audit — C-1 through C-62 (2026-04-27)

User directive: "now deep code audit all chat and chat related stuff
(inbox, etc), along with a systematic security audit as well."

Audit scope: all chat handlers (chat, chatRead, chatIdentity, block,
strangerFee), all chat REST + SSE endpoints (chat, chatStream,
chatAdmission, chatIdentity, chatReadState, conversations), the
in-process chatEventBus, frontend chat lib (crypto, pubPin,
chainVerify, chatService, blocks, readState, recentPeers,
ensureChatIdentity, explicitLock, stream), frontend chat ops
(chatIdentity, chatRead), chat UI components (ConversationView,
ChatComposer, ChatMessage, StrangerFeeModal), inbox + conversation
routes, chat thread notification prefs.

### Findings catalog

**Crypto (C-1 through C-13)** — all good or accepted-tradeoff:
- C-1 ✅ AAD binds (sender, recipient) accounts
- C-2 ✅ X25519 scalar clamping per RFC 7748
- C-3 ✅ Ephemeral priv wiped after shared-secret derivation
- C-4 ✅ Generic DecryptError — no oracle leak
- C-5 ✅ 12-byte random nonce + ephemeral keys = nonce reuse risk
       negligible
- C-6 (retracted — pub unused in decrypt path)
- C-7 ✅ libsodium scalarmult rejects low-order points (web search
       confirmed via libsodium x25519_ref10.c)
- C-8 ✅ KCI tradeoff documented in module header — recipient priv
       leak compromises past inbound; outbound stays secure via
       ephemeral pattern
- C-9 ✅ rec.sender/rec.recipient come from indexer (chain-validated
       signer), so AAD reconstruction is trustworthy
- C-10 ✅ Replay attacks fail because attacker's chain signer would
        mismatch AAD (binding both account names + per-pair message
        key derivation = double protection)
- C-11 (LOW) Indexer accepts header without ephemeral_pub/nonce —
       frontend shows "(encrypted)" placeholder. Bounded by Finding
       H spam gates. Documented design choice.
- C-12 ✅ Account regex post-fix rules out null-byte separator
        ambiguity in domain-separation strings
- C-13 ✅ No PFS at message level — explicitly accepted tradeoff per
        ADR-0015

**Chat handler (C-14 through C-18)** — all good:
- C-14 ✅ 5-layer defense (block list → admission → fan-in →
        per-sender → unique constraint)
- C-15 ✅ Fan-in off-by-one safe (UNION includes current sender)
- C-16 ✅ source_trx_id UNIQUE handles indexer replay idempotently
- C-17 ✅ ctx.blockTime for fan-in window — replay-deterministic
- C-18 ✅ Block list state='blocked' correctly handles unblock cycle

**chatRead handler (C-20 through C-23)** — all good:
- C-20 ✅ Strict ISO-8601 regex prevents engine-dependent parsing
- C-21 ✅ Monotonic-advance via WHERE clause — atomic, race-free
- C-22 ✅ Future-skew + past-floor (2020) bounds
- C-23 (LOW) Read-state ack accepts any peer regardless of
       correspondence — pollutes own row only, no privacy leak,
       acceptable

**strangerFee handler (C-24 through C-28)** — all good:
- C-24 ✅ Memo binding `morphit-stranger:<recipient>` — paid fee
        per-recipient; replay to different target rejected
- C-25 ✅ Sibling transfer validation (from=signer, to=feeRecipient,
        memo, BLURT amount parsed)
- C-26 ✅ Tolerance band absorbs client rounding; underpay rejected,
        ≤1.5× overpay accepted
- C-27 (LOW) Idempotency check before sibling-transfer check — re-
       broadcast of paid fee is no-op (existing row); cosmetic-only
- C-28 (LOW) Transfer.amount regex `\s+ BLURT` allows multiple
       spaces; not exploitable

**API endpoints (C-29 through C-32)** — all good:
- C-29 ✅ chatAdmission self-chat short-circuits to admitted=true
- C-30 (LOW) chat-admission reveals "have these two ever chatted?"
       publicly — same as REST /v1/chat/:a/:b reveals already (per
       ADR-0008)
- C-31 ✅ chatIdentity returns source_trx_id for chain anchoring
       (TOFU + S2 mitigation)
- C-32 ✅ chatReadState 10k row cap

**Frontend pubPin + chainVerify (C-33 through C-36)** — mostly good:
- C-33 ✅ Excellent TOFU + chain-anchor design — five distinct
        outcomes mapped to stable error codes
- C-34 ✅ newer_ref branch pins what CHAIN says (not indexer's
        claim)
- C-35 (MEDIUM, residual) chainVerify trusts a single Blurt RPC per
       call — no quorum cross-check, no local sig verification.
       Documented in chainVerify.ts module header. Future hardening:
       add local secp256k1 sig verify against the named account's
       on-chain posting pubkey. Acceptable risk for now: malicious
       single-RPC attack requires controlling the rotator's
       selection — bar is much higher than fully trusting the
       indexer.
- C-36 ✅ chainVerify checks required_posting_auths includes account
        before accepting a fetched op

**ChatMessage rendering (C-37 through C-39)** — XSS-safe:
- C-37 ✅ Plaintext rendered via Svelte `{...}` — auto-escapes HTML.
        No `{@html ...}` anywhere in chat surface.
- C-38 ✅ whitespace-pre-wrap preserves newlines but doesn't render
        markup
- C-39 (LOW) Error messages also via `{...}` — auto-escaped. Even a
       malicious indexer-supplied err.message renders as literal
       text.

**ChatComposer (C-40 through C-44)** — mostly good:
- C-40 ✅ redactPrivateKeys runs before draft save AND before send —
        defense-in-depth against accidental key leakage
- C-41 ✅ [...text].length correctly counts code points (handles
        surrogate pairs)
- C-42 ✅ 256 codepoints × 4 bytes/cp = 1024 plaintext + 16-byte
        tag = 1040 ciphertext. Indexer cap 1536 chars base64
        (~1388 chars after encoding). Comfortable budget.
- C-43 ✅ Drafts cleared on send + on empty
- C-44 (MEDIUM, residual) localStorage drafts in cleartext (private
       keys redacted). Mitigation: redactPrivateKeys defends
       against the most sensitive class of leak; remaining cleartext
       is the user's chat plaintext. Standard chat-app tradeoff.
       Consider clearing drafts on session lock or extended idle in
       a future polish pass.

**Inbox + blocks (C-45 through C-49)** — mostly good:
- C-45 ✅ Inbox is read-only display + client-side hide
- C-46 ✅ hideAccount is localStorage only — fully reversible
- C-47 (LOW) Relative-time months treated as 30 days — cosmetic,
       not security
- C-48 ✅ blocks store in-memory only (no persistence — no stale
        state risk)
- C-49 (LOW) blocks store doesn't sync across tabs. Not security-
       critical because on-chain block state is authoritative for
       the chat handler. UX nuisance only.

**chatService (C-50 through C-52)** — mostly good:
- C-50 (MEDIUM, UX) Sequential decryption of 50-message snapshot =
       ~250ms blocking (50 × ~5ms ECDH+AEAD). Not a security issue
       but a UX latency concern. Future polish: parallelize via
       Promise.all where order isn't critical (snapshot can be
       parallel; appends are 1-at-a-time so they don't matter).
- C-51 ✅ "Message we sent from another session" placeholder —
        correct behavior, we genuinely can't decrypt (encrypted to
        peer's pub, not ours)
- C-52 ✅ Reconcile + dedup ordering — single-threaded JS so no
        race; reconcile-first then seenIds-skip is correct

**Frontend SSE composable stream.ts (C-53 through C-55)** — good:
- C-53 ✅ Snapshot is authoritative — pending buffer cleared on
        snapshot
- C-54 ✅ JSON.parse wrapped in try/catch — malformed event data
        doesn't crash listener
- C-55 (LOW) Type assertion without runtime validation — robustness
       concern only; downstream decryptOrPlaceholder narrows
       defensively, so a malformed event from a malicious indexer
       falls through to (encrypted) placeholder

**Backend SSE handler (C-56 through C-60)** — good:
- C-56 ✅ Subscribe-FIRST pattern (F-5 audit pattern carry-over)
- C-57 ✅ eventMatchesFilter short-circuits in-memory before DB
        lookup
- C-58 ✅ fetchMessageById filters by canonical pair (defense in
        depth)
- C-59 (LOW) fetchSinceId returns up to 200 rows — burst delivery
       triggers C-50 sequential-decrypt UX latency
- C-60 (LOW) 60s fallback poll runs even when SSE healthy — wasted
       cheap query/min/subscriber. ~1.7q/s at 100 active subscribers.
       Negligible.

**Resource exhaustion (C-62)**:
- C-62 (LOW) No in-process per-IP SSE connection cap. 1000 hostile
       SSE connections would still produce cheap bus dispatch
       (Set iteration), but each subscriber's fetchMessageById per
       emit is a DB query. Operator-controlled mitigation: nginx
       limit_conn module. Documented in apps/indexer/README.md.

**C-19 — BUG, MEDIUM, FIXED**: Account name regex inconsistency.
chat handlers (chat.ts, chatRead.ts, shared.ts isAccountName, plus
recentPeers / readState / pubPin / chatRead frontend op) used
`^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{2,15}$` — NO dot. block.ts, strangerFee.ts +
their frontend ops used `^[a-z][a-z0-9.-]{2,15}$` — WITH dot.
Per Blurt's is_valid_account_name (verified via web search of the
chain source), account names are multi-segment dot-separated. The
inconsistency broke chat for every user with a dotted account
name: chat handler rejected `recipient_invalid`, /v1/chat/:a/:b
path 400'd, /v1/chat-identity/:account 400'd, /v1/chat-admission
400'd, frontend pin lookup 400'd, but block ops succeeded — leaving
the system in an inconsistent state.

**Fix:** canonicalized to dot-allowing regex across:
- `apps/indexer/src/api/shared.ts` (canonical isAccountName)
- `apps/indexer/src/indexer/handlers/chat.ts`
- `apps/indexer/src/indexer/handlers/chatRead.ts`
- `apps/web/src/lib/blurt/ops/chatRead.ts`
- `apps/web/src/lib/chat/readState.ts`
- `apps/web/src/lib/chat/pubPin.ts`
- `apps/web/src/lib/chat/recentPeers.ts`

Two new regression scenarios in chat-stream-smoke pinning the
behavior (`parseFilter: accepts dotted account names`,
`parseFilter: dotted names sort correctly`).

**Out-of-chat-scope dot-less regexes still present**:
- `apps/indexer/src/indexer/handlers/feeAttest.ts`
- `apps/indexer/src/indexer/handlers/feedback.ts`
- `apps/web/src/params/account.ts`
- `apps/web/src/lib/blurt/ops/feedback.ts`

These have the same bug shape but in non-chat surfaces. Should be
fixed in a follow-on consistency pass — same one-line change × 4
files. ✅ **Done 2026-04-30 (Item 9 triage):** all four files
canonicalized to `/^[a-z][a-z0-9.-]{2,15}$/` matching
`apps/indexer/src/api/shared.ts` isAccountName.

### Systematic security categories — summary

| Category | Verdict |
|---|---|
| Authentication / signing | ✅ Posting-auth chain-enforced; chat priv wiped on lock + destroy |
| Rate limiting | ✅ Layer-3 in-handler caps; ⚠️ no per-IP SSE cap (operator-managed) |
| Input validation | ✅ Bounded everywhere (post C-19 fix) |
| SSRF / external fetches | ⚠️ chainVerify single-RPC residual risk (C-35) |
| XSS / DOM injection | ✅ Svelte auto-escape; no @html in chat surface |
| Information leakage | ✅ Generic DecryptError; ⚠️ localStorage drafts in cleartext (C-44) |
| Resource exhaustion | ✅ Bounded; ⚠️ sequential snapshot decrypt (C-50, UX) |
| TOFU / chain anchoring | ✅ Excellent design (C-33); ⚠️ chain-RPC trust (C-35) |
| Cross-tab consistency | ⚠️ blocks store no cross-tab sync (C-49, UX) |
| Replay attacks | ✅ AAD + source_trx_id UNIQUE + monotonic-advance |
| Self-DoS | ✅ Self-chat / self-block rejected at handler |
| CSRF | ✅ Cookie-less architecture |

### Final integrity (post-audit)

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Typecheck — frontend | 0 errors |
| Typecheck — indexer src | 2 errors (pre-existing baseline) |
| Smokes | 425 / 425 across 23 runners (was 423, +2 C-19 regression) |

### What this audit found vs prior knowledge

The C-19 bug is genuinely new — not a regression from any single
session, just a long-standing inconsistency that nobody had
noticed because dotted-name users would have silently failed and
moved on. Everything else either confirmed existing-good design
(crypto, handlers, TOFU, rendering safety) or surfaced acceptable
residual risks already documented in module headers.


## Phase F — BTC/XMR receiving-address UX (2026-04-27)

User directive: "now start phase F."  Following Phase H
cancellation (Lightning), Phase F implements the in-chat
encrypted address handoff that completes Morphit's BTC/XMR
trade-execution loop.

### What this phase delivers

Buyer + seller match on the orderbook → open a chat → seller
shares their BTC or XMR receiving address through a structured,
encrypted payload → buyer broadcasts funds with their own wallet
→ buyer marks "I sent funds" with the txid → seller verifies on
their own wallet/explorer.  Morphit never custodies; never
broadcasts BTC/XMR transactions; never even validates the
checksum (per design — see "validation philosophy" below).

### Architecture: structured payload inside encrypted plaintext

Address handoff and funds-sent acknowledgments ride INSIDE the
encrypted chat plaintext, not as separate on-chain ops.  The
chat layer below this is unchanged — same E2EE crypto, same
chat handler, same SSE stream, same indexer storage.  This
phase adds a structured WIRE FORMAT that the recipient's
frontend recognizes and renders specially.

Wire format (inside the encrypted plaintext, JSON):

  {
    "v": 1,
    "kind": "morphit_addr",
    "method": "btc" | "xmr",
    "address": string,
    "amount"?: string,
    "order_permlink"?: string,
    "note"?: string
  }

  {
    "v": 1,
    "kind": "morphit_funds_sent",
    "method": "btc" | "xmr",
    "txid": string,
    "amount"?: string,
    "order_permlink"?: string,
    "note"?: string
  }

The chat handler still sees opaque ciphertext.  Indexer storage
unchanged.  Real-time SSE delivery unchanged.  Only the
recipient's ChatMessage component does anything different —
it decodes the JSON and renders an "address pill" or "funds
sent pill" instead of plaintext.

### Validation philosophy

We do CHEAP SHAPE checks for addresses + txids: regex-based,
no checksum verification.  Documented in the payload.ts module
header.  Reasons:

  1. Bundle size — bitcoinjs-lib + monero-js add ~300kB on top
     of libsodium's ~250kB; lazy-loading chat would lose its
     wins.

  2. Defense in depth — when the buyer actually sends funds
     to the address, their wallet does the checksum verify.
     A typo'd address there is a wallet rejection, not a lost
     transaction.

  3. The cheap shape check catches the most likely error
     classes (truncation, wrong prefix, charset mismatch)
     before the message leaves the sender's composer.

Concretely:
- BTC: regex matches P2PKH (1...), P2SH (3...), bech32 (bc1...),
  taproot (bc1p...).  Length-bounded.
- XMR: regex matches standard (4..., 95 chars), subaddress
  (8..., 95 chars), integrated (4..., 106 chars).  Note:
  integrated addresses use a different network byte than
  standard, so the 2nd-char [0-9AB] constraint of standard
  doesn't apply — verified during smoke implementation
  (initial regex was too strict, fixed using getmonero.org
  docs example "4LL9oSLmtpcc..." as the canonical test case).
- txid: 64 lowercase hex chars (BTC sha256d, XMR Keccak-256).

### Address pill UX

Recipient's ChatMessage component decodes structured payloads
and renders a pill instead of plaintext:

- Method badge ("Bitcoin address" / "Monero address")
- Mono-spaced break-all address in a tinted box
- Copy button (navigator.clipboard, "Copied!" for 2s)
- Optional amount line
- Optional note (italic)
- Optional "For order: <permlink>" line

The bubble's outgoing/incoming color split is preserved — the
sender sees their own address pill in emerald (right-aligned),
the recipient sees it in the ink-tinted incoming style.

### Funds-sent pill UX

Mirror of address pill: method, txid (mono, copy-able), optional
amount + note + order ref.  Block-explorer link deferred to
Phase F.5 (CSP concerns + need to handle multiple explorers per
asset).

### Composer toolbar

Above the ChatComposer, a thin toolbar row appears when the
user is admitted (post stranger-fee gate).  Two buttons:

- "Share address" → opens AddressShareModal
- "Mark funds sent" → opens FundsSentModal

Hidden when locked (the modals would just dispatch a no-op
unlock prompt).  Hidden when in stranger-fee state (composer is
also hidden — pay first).

### Modal flow

Both modals use the same pattern:

1. Method tabs (BTC / XMR) — pre-selected from
   `initialMethod` prop where context is available.
2. Address (or txid) input with inline validation — Send
   button stays disabled until the input shape-matches.
3. Optional amount input (positive decimal, no units).
4. Optional note input (100-char cap).
5. For AddressShareModal: a verify-warning banner ("Always
   verify before sending. Crypto cannot be reversed.").
6. Cancel + Send buttons.

On Send, the modal calls `encodeAddressPayload` (or
`encodeFundsSentPayload`), which throws if any field fails
strict validation — defense in depth in case the inline check
missed a state transition.  The encoded JSON string goes
through `controller.sendMessage(text)` — same path as a
plaintext message.  Optimistic state machine handles
pending → broadcast → confirmed.  SSE delivers to the peer in
real time.  The peer's frontend decodes and renders the pill.

### Order context

When the user opens chat from an order detail page, the URL
includes `?order=<permlink>` — the conversation route reads
this query param, validates against the same regex
`payload.ts` uses, and passes it as a prop to
ConversationView, which forwards to both modals.  Both modals
display "For order: <permlink>" so the user sees what trade
they're sharing the address for.  The encoded payload pins
the permlink so the recipient's pill also shows it.

The Message button on `/[x+40][account]/[permlink]/+page.svelte`
(order detail page) was updated to include this query param.
The orderbook + account-page Message buttons stay as-is —
they don't have a single-order context.

The `?order=` value is validated before use — invalid permlinks
silently fall through to "no order context" rather than
breaking the chat.

### Decode fallback semantics

`decodePayload(plaintext)` returns one of:

- `{ kind: 'address', payload }` — recognized address handoff
- `{ kind: 'funds_sent', payload }` — recognized funds ack
- `{ kind: 'unknown_version', version: N }` — future schema
  version we don't know how to render; UI shows "this message
  uses a newer protocol"
- `{ kind: 'plaintext' }` — fallback for: malformed JSON, JSON
  but not an object, missing v/kind, version 1 but unknown
  kind, version 1 with shape that fails validation (e.g.
  amount has units, note over cap, address fails its regex)

Critical: the decode FALLBACK for shape failures means a
malicious or buggy sender CANNOT inject HTML or scripts via
crafted payloads — the worst they can do is force the
recipient's UI to render plaintext.  Svelte's auto-escape then
neutralizes any HTML in the plaintext.

## Phase F.2 — QR codes for address pills + BLURT support (2026-04-27)

User directive: "let the buyer scan the seller's xmr/btc/blurt
QR Code. adding that feature makes it much easier for a buyer
to send his funds to the seller if he scans his computer
screen with the mobile wallet on his phone."

### What this adds

1. **QR rendering on address pills.**  Each address pill now
   has a "Show QR" toggle.  Tapping it lazy-loads a QR library
   and renders the wallet-recognized payment URI as a
   scannable SVG QR code.  Buyer points their mobile wallet's
   built-in scanner at the desktop screen; the wallet pre-fills
   recipient + amount.

2. **BLURT support.**  Phase F shipped with btc/xmr only;
   user explicitly listed BLURT as a third supported asset.
   New `'blurt'` PaymentMethod, account-name validator (uses
   the canonical regex post-C-19), 40-char hex txid validator
   (Steem/Hive convention vs the 64-char BTC/XMR convention).

### Wallet URI conventions per method

`buildPaymentUri(payload)` is the single source of truth:

- **BTC**: BIP-21 (`bitcoin:<address>?amount=X`).  Universally
  supported across mobile wallets.  Amount is in BTC, not
  satoshis.
- **XMR**: official Monero URI scheme
  (`monero:<address>?tx_amount=X`).  Note the param is
  `tx_amount` not `amount` — Monero historically diverged from
  BIP-21 naming and modern wallets follow the spec.  Verified
  via getmonero.org docs reference.
- **BLURT**: bare account name (no URI scheme prefix).  No
  widely-deployed `blurt:` URI scheme exists; Steem-family
  wallets (Keychain, Beem, etc.) accept the bare account name
  and the user fills in the rest.  Memo is intentionally
  omitted from QR — chain-transfer memos are privacy-affecting
  and shouldn't be auto-pre-filled.

### Lazy-loaded QR library

Added `qrcode@^1.5.4` as a frontend dependency.  Loaded
dynamically inside QrPanel.svelte's `onMount` — bundle impact
is zero for users who never tap "Show QR."  The library is
~30kB; small enough that we could include it eagerly in the
chat chunk, but keeping it lazy follows the project's
established posture of not loading what isn't used.

To support typecheck-without-install (the development sandbox
doesn't have npm install network access), added an ambient
declaration at `apps/web/src/qrcode.d.ts` with just the
`toString` API surface we use.  The package's own typings ship
with it once installed and supersede this stub.

### QrPanel component

Renders SVG output (resolution-independent, no PNG encoding
overhead, parses fast).  White background card around the QR
for high-contrast scan reliability across lighting conditions.
Error-correction level M (~15% recoverable) — robust to
screen glare without dense modules that hurt scan rate.
Quiet zone (margin) of 2 modules — slightly tighter than the
spec default of 4 to fit cleanly inside the chat bubble while
still being scannable.

Aspect-ratio: 1, max-width: 280px, centered.  Sits inline
within the address pill, between the address+copy row and
the optional note/order-permlink lines.

### Toggle state

Per-bubble `showQr` state in ChatMessage.svelte.  Closed by
default to keep the chat scroll compact; user opens explicitly.
Aria-expanded reflects state for screen readers.  No
persistence across re-mounts — opening QR on a long-scrollback
message and scrolling away resets it; intentional, prevents
unbounded resource usage on inboxes with hundreds of address
pills (each open QR holds a parsed SVG in DOM).

### Funds-sent pill

BLURT method label added to the funds_sent pill rendering.
NO QR code on funds_sent pills — the txid isn't a payment
URI; the recipient already knows where the funds came from
(they shared the address).  Receiver-side rendering shows the
txid for manual lookup on a block explorer (clickable
explorer links deferred to F.5).

### Modal extensions

Both AddressShareModal and FundsSentModal now have three
method tabs (BTC / XMR / BLURT).  Method-aware "still typing"
threshold for inline validation:
- BTC/XMR addresses: 10 chars before flagging invalid (allows
  typing past the prefix)
- BLURT account: 3 chars (account names are short, 3-16)
- BTC/XMR txid: 32 chars (over halfway through 64)
- BLURT txid: 20 chars (over halfway through 40)

- `apps/web/src/qrcode.d.ts` (ambient module declaration)

Frontend (modified):
- `apps/web/src/lib/chat/payload.ts` — BLURT method added
  (validator, txid pattern, account regex, dispatch); new
  `buildPaymentUri` helper
- `apps/web/src/lib/components/ChatMessage.svelte` — QR toggle

- `apps/web/src/lib/i18n/locales/*.json` — 10 keys × 10 locales
