## Phase F.3 — Pay-now (BLURT) + subaddress nudge (XMR) (2026-04-27)

User directives:
1. "[BLURT] Phase F.3 is a good idea. add that."  Buyer paying
   in BLURT shouldn't have to leave Morphit when his Morphit-
   bound BLURT account is the same one he wants to pay from.
2. "[XMR] make sure we encourage monero users to always pay/
   receive xmr using monero 'Stealth' addresses (sub-addresses),
   ie: addresses that start with an 8, rather than a 4."

### Pay-now flow

When a buyer receives a BLURT address pill (incoming, method=
blurt, valid amount), a "Pay now" button appears next to "Show
QR".  Tapping it opens PayBlurtModal:

1. Summary: amount (formatted "N.NNN BLURT"), recipient, "from"
   (the buyer's Morphit account)
2. Privacy notice: "No on-chain memo will be included — your
   trade context stays in this encrypted chat"
3. Active-key password input
4. Confirm → `runWithActiveKey()` → `broadcastTransfer()`
5. On success → close modal → auto-broadcast a
   `morphit_funds_sent` chat payload (so the seller sees a
   "Blurt sent" pill without the buyer needing a second step)
6. Toast confirms "BLURT sent. Receipt posted to chat."

Best-effort auto-receipt: if the chat broadcast fails after the
on-chain transfer succeeded, the user gets a softer toast
("BLURT sent. Could not post receipt to chat — you can mark
funds sent manually") and can use the existing FundsSentModal
to record it.

### Pay-now button visibility

Renders only when ALL of:
- `onPayNow` callback provided by ConversationView
- Method is `'blurt'`
- Message is INCOMING (we don't pay-now our own outgoing pills)
- `payload.amount` is set and parses to a positive finite number

Without an amount the button stays hidden — UX would have to
prompt for amount otherwise, which clutters the pill.  Sellers
who share an amount-less address pill are implicitly saying
"figure out the amount yourself"; the buyer pays from their
external wallet.

### Active-key requirement

BLURT transfers need active auth, separate from the posting
auth used for everything else in Morphit (chat, custom_json,
orderbook ops).  PayBlurtModal uses the same `runWithActiveKey()`
JIT pattern as StrangerFeeModal:
- Password input → derive active scalar from encrypted envelope
- Pass scalar to `broadcastTransfer()`
- Wipe scalar from memory after the broadcast resolves
- Wipe password input string after the call

The active key is NEVER persisted on `LiveIdentity` — tier
policy (posting in memory, active JIT-derived per use, owner
out-of-app entirely).

### Memo policy: empty by default

The on-chain BLURT transfer is broadcast with an empty memo.
Reasons:
- Chain memos are public.  Adding a trade-correlatable memo
  (order permlink, peer name, etc.) would leak trade-specific
  identifiers to blockchain explorers.
- Both parties already know what the trade is from the chat
  context — the memo would be redundant for them anyway.
- Mirrors Morphit's broader privacy posture (no public trade
  attribution; metadata stays in encrypted chat).

If a user has a legitimate need for a custom memo (e.g.
business-side accounting), they can pay from an external
wallet where they control the memo.  The pay-now flow is
optimized for the privacy-conscious common case.

### New broadcastTransfer helper

Added a clean primitive in `apps/web/src/lib/blurt/sign.ts`:
`broadcastTransfer(activePriv, from, to, amount, memo)`.  Pure
single-op transfer, signed with active key.  Reuses the same
ref-block-info fetching and condenser_api broadcast path as
the existing `broadcastOrderWithFee` but without the
custom_json sibling.  Self-transfer guard fails fast.

This primitive is also available for any future affordances
(e.g. P2P feature-payment shortcuts, manual relay top-ups,
etc.).

### Subaddress nudge (XMR)

XMR standard addresses (`4...`) and integrated addresses
(also `4...`) reuse the same view-key anchor for every
received payment.  Observers can correlate trades on the
public chain across all such payments.  Subaddresses (`8...`)
break that link: each subaddress is derived independently and
only the wallet's view key holder can correlate them.

The nudge is SOFT — non-blocking, advisory:

1. **AddressShareModal** (sender side): when the user pastes a
   valid XMR address starting with `4`, an amber-tinted
   advisory box appears below the input:
   > "For better privacy across multiple trades, share a
   > Monero subaddress (starts with 8) instead of a standard
   > address (4). Standard addresses link every received
   > payment to the same view key."
   The Send button is NOT disabled — the user can ignore the
   tip if they have a legitimate reason (e.g., businesses
   running integrated addresses for customer-correlated
   accounting).

2. **ChatMessage address pill** (recipient side): when an XMR
   address starting with `4` is rendered, a smaller italic
   line appears:
   > "Tip: Monero subaddresses (starting with 8) provide
   > better privacy."
   Helps the buyer learn they should ask for a subaddress
   next time, without breaking this trade.

3. **AddressShareModal placeholder** updated to lead with the
   recommended form: `8… (recommended) or 4…`.

Hard-blocking would be paternalistic — `4...` addresses are
valid XMR addresses, used legitimately by many parties.

### Files

Frontend (new):
- `apps/web/src/lib/components/PayBlurtModal.svelte`

Frontend (modified):
- `apps/web/src/lib/blurt/sign.ts` — new `broadcastTransfer`
  helper (single-op transfer, active-only signing)
- `apps/web/src/lib/components/ChatMessage.svelte` — `onPayNow`
  prop, "Pay now" button (gated on incoming-blurt-with-amount),
  subaddress nudge for XMR `4...` addresses
- `apps/web/src/lib/components/AddressShareModal.svelte` —
  subaddress nudge advisory box, `showSubaddressTip` derived
  state
- `apps/web/src/lib/components/ConversationView.svelte` —
  `payBlurtArgs` state, `handlePayNowClick`, `handlePaidBlurt`
  (auto-broadcasts funds-sent payload), PayBlurtModal mount,
  pass-through of `onPayNow` to ChatMessage
- `apps/web/src/lib/i18n/locales/*.json` — 23 keys × 10 locales
  (placeholder change, subaddress_tip, subaddress_tip_modal,
  pay_now, full chat.pay_blurt namespace incl. error subset)

  XMR subaddress and standard both validate at the payload
  layer (regression guard so nudge stays UI-only)

### What's NOT in Phase F.3 (deferred)

- **Pre-flight balance check.**  PayBlurtModal doesn't fetch

## Phase F.4 — BLURT payment memo + on-chain verification (2026-04-27)

User raised a real correctness gap:

> "if the seller is due 1700 blurt for something that he sold to
> the buyer, well, what happens if someone else from god knows
> where sends that seller 1700 blurt right then as well?"

BLURT is unique among Morphit's three assets in that the
"address" is an account name, not per-trade-isolated.  Every
incoming transfer lands in the same account.  Multiple
unrelated 1700 BLURT transfers are genuinely ambiguous —
which one paid the trade?

This phase adds:
1. A short opaque random memo auto-generated by the seller
   when they share a BLURT address; the buyer's wallet must
   include it in their on-chain transfer memo.
2. On-chain verification of incoming `morphit_funds_sent`
   pills against the chain RPC — the seller's chat UI fetches
   the transaction and shows a green check if it matches
   (recipient, sender, amount, memo) or a specific mismatch
   warning otherwise.

### Privacy-preserving memo design

Critical decision: the memo is NOT the order permlink (would
deanonymize the trade to anyone scraping Alice's account
history).  Instead, an opaque random token — 8 chars from a
32-char confusable-free alphabet (lowercase letters minus l/o,
digits 2-9 minus 0/1).  ~40 bits entropy.  Outside observers
see `morphit:7g4kp2x9` and have no way to link it to anything
because the order context lives only in the encrypted chat.

CSPRNG (Web Crypto's getRandomValues) instead of Math.random:
defeats a pre-image attacker who could otherwise pre-compute
a memo and front-run a trade by sending a small payment with
the predicted memo, corrupting the seller's accounting.

The 0/1/l/o exclusion is read-aloud safety — if a user
dictates the memo over a phone call, "el"/"oh"/"zero"/"one"
are commonly misheard; the alphabet rules them out.

### Auto-generation flow

The seller opens AddressShareModal, picks the BLURT tab.
A `$effect` auto-generates the memo on first mount with the
BLURT tab active.  The memo displays prominently in the modal
(emerald-tinted card, large mono font, "Regenerate" button +
"Skip memo (advanced)" checkbox for opt-out).  On Send, the
memo rides inside the encrypted AddressPayload.

### Buyer side: required-memo banner

When a buyer's chat receives an incoming BLURT address pill
with a memo, ChatMessage renders an unmissable amber-tinted
"REQUIRED MEMO" panel above the QR/Pay-now buttons:
- Mono-font display of the memo
- Copy button (independent of the address Copy state — copy-state
  refactored from `copied: bool` → `copiedKind: 'address' |
  'memo' | 'txid' | null` so each button flashes "Copied!"
  independently)
- Explainer: "Paste this memo into the memo field of your
  BLURT transfer.  Without it, the seller can't match your
  payment to this trade."

### Pay-now wires memo through to the chain

PayBlurtModal accepts a `memo` prop (replacing Phase F.3's
"empty memo for privacy" — see retraction note below).  The
modal:
- Displays the memo prominently in the confirm summary, amber-
  bold
- Conditional "with memo notice" replaces the previous "no
  memo notice" copy when memo is present
- Passes the memo through to `broadcastTransfer()` which
  becomes the on-chain transfer's memo field

ConversationView's `handlePayNowClick` now stages the memo;
`handlePaidBlurt` echoes it back in the auto-broadcast
`morphit_funds_sent` payload so the seller's verifier sees
both the buyer's claim AND the chain truth.

#### Retraction of the Phase F.3 "empty memo" stance

Phase F.3 set the on-chain memo to empty unconditionally,
reasoning that public-chain memos leak trade context.  That
was correct in spirit (don't leak the order permlink) but
threw out the matching baby with the privacy bathwater.

The Phase F.4 random-memo design preserves both properties:
the memo IS public on chain, but it's an opaque token that
reveals nothing to outside observers.  Inside the encrypted
chat, both parties saw the same token; matching works
perfectly.  Outside, it's noise.

### On-chain verification — the seller's confidence layer

When an incoming `morphit_funds_sent` BLURT pill mounts in
ChatMessage, an `$effect` triggers `verifyBlurtTransfer()`:

1. Fetches the transaction from chain RPC via the existing
   BlurtClient (lazy-imported to keep the pure-dispatch
   testable under tsx).
2. Walks the operations list, finds the first `transfer` op
   whose `to` matches the seller.
3. Compares each field — to/from/amount/memo — and returns
   the FIRST mismatch (so the UI shows one clear "wrong
   amount" / "wrong memo" / etc. rather than a confusing
   multi-field error blob).
4. Caches the result by `txid|recipient|sender|amount|memo`
   for the session; doesn't cache `rpc_error` (next attempt
   may succeed).

The pill renders a verification badge:
- Pending (gray pulse): "Verifying on chain…"
- Verified (green): "✓ Verified on chain"
- Mismatch:to/from/amount/memo (amber): specific message
  per field
- Not found (gray): "Transaction not found yet — give it a
  block or two"
- Wrong op (amber): "Transaction found but contains no
  matching transfer"
- RPC error (muted): "Could not verify on chain (RPC
  unreachable)" — non-blocking; the chain truth is still on
  chain regardless

### Architecture: pure dispatcher + thin network wrapper

`blurtVerify.ts` exports both:
- `verifyBlurtTransfer(txid, expect)` — network wrapper with
  caching; lazy-imports `$blurt/client`
- `verifyBlurtTransferAgainstTx(tx, expect)` — pure dispatcher
  taking an already-fetched chain tx response

The split lets smoke runners exercise every dispatch path
without mocking the network.  Production callers use the
network wrapper.  The lazy import of `$blurt/client` keeps
the module loadable under tsx — pure smokes never trigger
the network path.

The interfaces `ChainTxResponse` and `ChainTransferOp` are
exported alongside so smoke runners can construct mock txes.

- `apps/web/src/lib/chat/payload.ts` — `memo` field on both

  (`[a-z0-9]{6,32}`), `isValidMemo` export, `generateBlurtMemo`
  export (CSPRNG, 8-char base32-ish), encoder/decoder
  validation
- `apps/web/src/lib/chat/blurtVerify.ts` — NEW.  Network

  client import for tsx-friendliness.

### What's NOT in Phase F.4 (deferred)

- **Auto-correlation across pills.**  Currently the seller's
  verifier compares the on-chain memo against what the BUYER
  echoed in the funds-sent payload — not against the seller's
  own original AddressPayload.memo.  Tighter correlation
  (walk the message thread back, find the matching address
  pill, use ITS memo as the expected) would catch the
  scenario where a buyer claims memo X but actually used
  memo Y.  Not implemented because: (a) the chain truth is
  what matters; the seller can visually confirm the memo
  matches what they originally requested, (b) walking the
  message thread is non-trivial across lazy-loaded snapshots
  (would need to fetch older messages if not yet loaded).
  Future polish.
- **Block-explorer link from the verified-tx badge.**  A "View
  on explorer" button next to the green check would close
  another loop.  CSP + explorer-choice concerns same as
  Phase F.5 deferral.
- **Verify-status persistence across reloads.**  The verify
  cache is in-memory only; users who close and re-open the
  chat re-fetch from chain.  Cheap (one RPC) but a localStorage
  cache for verified results would eliminate even that hit.
- **Buyer-side proactive memo validation before broadcast.**
  PayBlurtModal trusts the memo passed via prop.  Adding a
  pre-broadcast check ("does this memo match what was
  requested?") is redundant — the memo IS what was requested
  (passed straight from the address pill).  Mentioned for
  completeness.

## Phase F.5 — Cross-page trade-status spine + cross-page toasts (2026-04-27)

User directive consolidates three concerns:

> "make sure the users' my/orders page always shows the payment
> status immediately... if they navigate out of chat... a green
> checkmark... maybe even a green toast should show with the
> notifications if the user is on a totally different page... we
> want order frequency as high as possible. i also like your
> idea of automatic correlation across pills."

This phase introduces a single source of truth for per-order
trade state (`tradeStatus` store), wires it into chat AND
/my/orders, and adds a global SSE listener that fires
clickable toasts + (opt-in) browser notifications when trade
events arrive while the user is anywhere in the app.

### Architecture: tradeStatus store as the spine

`lib/trades/tradeStatus.ts` exposes a Svelte store keyed by
`order_permlink`.  Every UI surface that cares about trade
state — the funds-sent verification badge in ChatMessage, the
PaymentStatusBadge on /my/orders, the future order-detail
page — reads from this store reactively.  Updates flow in
from three sources:

1. **chatService outgoing** (`sendMessage`): when the local
   user sends a structured payload (address pill / funds-sent
   pill) carrying an orderPermlink, the store updates
   optimistically before the broadcast.  Their /my/orders
   badge flips immediately.
2. **chatService incoming** (`mergePollResponse`): when an
   incoming decrypted message decodes as a structured payload,
   the store updates.  Per-conversation SSE feeds this when
   the user IS on the chat page.
3. **Global tradeEventListener** (Phase F.5 new): when the
   user is anywhere ELSE in the app, this listener feeds the
   store.  See "Global listener" below.

Forward-compat: the `TradePhase` discriminant has values
reserved for future protocol stages (`released`, `disputed`,
`completed`).  Per the user's nudge: "this sounds good too."
PaymentStatusBadge renders distinct visuals for each.  Unknown
phases (a future client sees a phase this client doesn't know)
fall back to a generic "Trade in progress" pill rather than
crashing.

### advancePhase semantics — strict monotonicity

Phases share a rank table:

| Rank | Phases |
|---|---|
| 0 | address_shared |
| 1 | paid |
| 2 | paid_verified, paid_mismatch, paid_unverifiable |
| 3 | released, disputed |
| 4 | completed |

Three rules apply:

1. Higher rank → advance.  (paid → paid_verified, etc.)
2. Same rank → first-wins.  (paid_verified, paid_mismatch,
   paid_unverifiable are siblings; whichever lands first
   sticks.)  This prevents UI flicker if a stale RPC
   re-resolves with a different result.
3. Lower rank → no regression.  (Already-paid stays paid even
   if a stale `address_shared` event re-fires.)

Special-case stickiness: paid_verified additionally protects
against later paid_mismatch / paid_unverifiable arriving at
the same rank.  A confirmed verification is the strongest
claim; downgrading it on a later RPC blip would be wrong.

### Auto-correlation across pills

User: "i also like your idea of automatic correlation across
pills."

Implementation: when ChatMessage's funds-sent verifier runs,
it looks up the seller's ORIGINAL expected memo from the
tradeStatus store (populated by the earlier `address_shared`
event for the same orderPermlink) rather than trusting the
buyer's potentially-different echo on the funds-sent payload.

If a malicious buyer sends a funds-sent claim with a forged
memo that doesn't match the seller's actual on-chain memo,
the verifier still detects mismatch — chain truth has the
final word.  If the address pill hasn't been observed (e.g.
a snapshot arrived out of order), the verifier falls back to
the echoed memo.

### Global trade-event listener

`lib/trades/tradeEventListener.ts` opens chat SSE streams for
every peer in the recent-peers list when the user becomes
unlocked.  Lifecycle mirrors auto-lock: starts on unlock,
tears down on lock or layout unmount.  One stream per peer
(bounded by recent-peers size, ~10 max).

Each stream's onSnapshot pre-populates a seenIds set so
history replay on reconnect doesn't re-toast events the user
already processed.  Each applyAppend decrypts, decodes, and
routes:

- Address-shared incoming → `recordAddressShared` + clickable
  toast ("alice shared a BLURT address for trade X — View →")
- Funds-sent incoming → `recordFundsSent` + clickable toast
  ("alice paid 1700 BLURT for trade X — View →")

Toasts deep-link to `/chat/<peer>?order=<permlink>`.  Tapping
dismisses the toast and navigates the user straight to the
relevant conversation.  Closes the trade-completion loop
without making the user search through chats.

Browser notifications fire only when the user has opted in
AND `document.hidden` is true (they're on another tab).  The
in-app toast handles the same-tab case; the browser
notification surfaces when the tab isn't focused.

### Browser-notifications opt-in

`lib/notifications/tradeNotifications.ts` exposes a Readable
boolean store + `enableTradeNotifications()` / `disableTradeNotifications()`.
Default OFF per the privacy posture.  `enableTradeNotifications`
must be called from a user gesture (browser security for
permission prompts); on permission denial it surfaces the
denial so the Settings UI can show "you blocked notifications;
enable in browser settings."

The Settings UI integration is deferred to Phase G — Phase F.5
ships the plumbing.  Users who want notifications can flip
the toggle once the Settings page lands; the listener already
respects the store value.

### Clickable toast surface

The existing `Toast` interface gained optional `href` and
`actionLabel` fields.  `showToast()` accepts them via options.
ToastRegion renders the message as an `<a href>` when href is
set, with a "View →" affordance.  Backward-compatible with
existing callers — no href = plain `<p>` like before.

### What this means for the user-facing flow

Seller is on /my/orders.  Buyer (in another browser, another
device) sends funds-sent.  Seller's tradeEventListener
receives the event.  Within ~1 second:

1. tradeStatus store updates → PaymentStatusBadge on the
   order row flips from "Address shared" (blue) to "Payment
   pending" (blue with hourglass)
2. Toast appears bottom-right: "alice paid 1700 BLURT for
   trade X — View →"
3. Behind the scenes, ChatMessage's verifier (when the user
   eventually opens the chat) runs the on-chain verify; result
   writes back to the store
4. Within another second or two: badge flips to "✓ Paid"
   (green); the chat conversation, if open in another tab,
   shows the same green check on the funds-sent pill — same
   source of truth, two surfaces

Seller taps the toast → lands on the chat with alice → sees
the green-check pill → marks the order completed (future) →
ready for next trade.

### What's NOT in Phase F.5 (deferred)

- **Settings UI for notification toggle.**  The
  `enableTradeNotifications()` API is in place but no UI
  exposes it yet.  Lives well in a future Settings/Notifications
  page; Phase G mobile PWA polish is a natural home.
- **Per-peer SSE refresh on recordRecentPeer.**  Current
  listener opens streams for the recent-peers list at unlock
  time.  When the user starts a NEW chat conversation,
  recordRecentPeer fires but the listener doesn't pick it up
  until next layout remount.  Easy fix: subscribe to a
  recentPeers Svelte store (doesn't exist yet — recentPeers is
  imperative).  Worthwhile but not blocking — the
  ConversationView itself opens the per-peer stream when the
  user is on that chat, so they don't miss messages while
  there; only cross-page toasting for brand-new peers waits
  until the next session.
- **localStorage persistence of trade-state across reloads.**
  Currently in-memory only.  Reload = re-build state from
  initial chat snapshot (which the SSE onSnapshot delivers
  per-peer).  Persisting would survive reloads but adds a
  cross-device-sync question.  Defer.
- **Prune logic for terminal-state entries.**  Memory grows
  with each trade.  At thousands of trades this is still
  trivial (~200 bytes each), but a cleanup pass for
  released/completed entries older than N days would be
  prudent for long-running sessions.  Defer.
- **Toast visibility gating.**  Currently the listener fires
  toasts even when the user is on the chat page that would
  render the same event as a pill.  Brief duplicate flash; not
  harmful.  A `document.visibilityState` + URL check would
  suppress it; trivial polish.

## BATCH19A Pass A — deferred items (2026-05-02)

Surfaced during the every-handler-hostile consolidated re-pass
(audit doc Part 17). Not blocking launch; tracked here so they
don't drift.

### BATCH19A-order-1: status='expired' sweep job (LOW)

Orders with `expires_at` in the past keep `status='live'`
indefinitely.  The orderbook visibility predicate (post
BATCH19A-orderbook-1 fix) excludes them at read-time, so
public-facing impact is closed.  But the owner's view at
`/v1/orders/:account` shows expired orders as "live" when
they're user-perceptibly expired.

**Fix:** add a periodic sweep job to the indexer's cron lane:

```sql
UPDATE orders SET status = 'expired'
WHERE status = 'live'
  AND expires_at IS NOT NULL
  AND expires_at < NOW()
```

Run every 5 minutes.  Emit orderbook-change events for
sweep-flipped order IDs so SSE subscribers see explicit
`order_removed` events (rather than silent fade-out the
current visibility-predicate-only fix produces).

### BATCH19A-order-2: reject born-expired orders at intake (LOW)

The order handler accepts arbitrary `expires_at`, including
past timestamps.  After BATCH19A-orderbook-1 the row is
invisible to the orderbook anyway, but the indexer still
spends a row.  A `expires_at <= ctx.blockTime` rejection
at intake would be cleaner.  Cosmetic.

### BATCH19A-chat-2: BIGSERIAL → JS Number narrowing pattern (NOTE)

Multiple handlers narrow Postgres BIGSERIAL ids to JS Number
via parseInt: chat.ts (chat_messages.id → SSE marker),
feedbackResponse.ts (feedback.id → FK).  Precision is fine
at current scale (would take ~24,000 years at 1M
messages/day to overflow 2^53), but the pattern is worth
revisiting if Morphit ever approaches the limit.  Migration
path: type the id as `string` end-to-end and update SSE
event shape + frontend consumer.

artifacts), delete across all 10 locales and pulse to verify.

## Parts 31R3 through 47 — pre-launch hardening + beta-readiness (2026-05-03 → 2026-05-04)

### Top-line numbers
- **Real bugs found and fixed: 38** (30+ frontend, 3 indexer, 5 relay)
- **Tests at end of campaign:** relay 163/163, indexer 363/363 + 1 skipped, frontend typecheck 0 errors, backend typecheck 0 errors / 7 workspaces

### Parts 31R3-46: deep-deep static audit (94 items × Categories A-L)

Black-hat-mindset full static-code audit covering:
- Category A — static code review (per-handler, per-endpoint walk)
- Category B — dependency / supply-chain
- Category C — SQL / database (parameterization, transactions, race protection)
- Category D — HTTP / API surface
- Category E — cryptography
- Category F — privacy (no IP retention, no third-party CDN, no telemetry)
- Category G — operator trust (operator can degrade UX but not steal funds)
- Category H — frontend (UI gates, raw-error leaks, XSS, CSRF, file upload)
- Category I — contracts (cross-module typing, ADR fidelity)
- Category J — build / CI (deterministic builds, AGPL compliance)
- Category K — threat modeling (STRIDE, attack-tree expansions)
- Category L — per-subsystem deep dives (chat, fee verification, federation)

Items #95-104 were sandbox/deployment-dependent and explicitly deferred.
Items #105-110 are epistemic limits acknowledged in writing.

### Frontend bugs fixed (30+)

- Raw-error UI leaks across modal, toast, and inline error surfaces
- XSS sinks via unsanitized `contact_url` and `origin` strings —
  shared `apps/web/src/lib/utils/safeContactUrl.ts` (`safeContactUrl` +
  `safeInstanceOrigin`) is now the single chokepoint
- Missing confirm gates on destructive actions
- Missing upper-bound validation on numeric inputs (page sizes,
  date ranges, quantity caps)
- See AUDIT-2026-05.md for the full enumerated list

### Indexer bugs fixed (3)

- `feedbackResponse` hex-format mismatch
- `order` and `orderReplace` `price_model` numeric-bounds gap
  (now rejects out-of-range percent values at intake)

### Relay bugs fixed (5, all HIGH/CRITICAL)

1. **Invite-altcha race** — concurrent invite redemption could
   double-charge a single altcha solution.  Fixed with reservation-
   tracking pattern.
2. **AltchaService unbounded `usedSalts`** — memory growth on
   long-running relays.  Bounded LRU with TTL eviction.
3. **Ceiling TOCTOU** — between "check ceiling" and "create
   account" a concurrent request could overshoot.  Fixed with
   `GlobalDailyCeiling.tryReserve()` / `releaseReservation()` API
   + try/finally pattern in `apps/relay/src/api/create.ts`.
4. **Frontend XSS via operator instance metadata** — instance-list
   rendering passed unfiltered `contact_url` into anchor `href`,
   allowing `javascript:` URIs.  Now passes through `safeContactUrl`.
5. **Operator-facing config rejection at startup** — placeholder
   strings (`CHANGE_ME_BEFORE_PRODUCTION`) now hard-rejected by
   Zod schemas at runtime *and* `ops/postgres/init.sql`
   provisioning, so misconfiguration cannot reach a running
   relay.

### Architectural improvements

- Shared `safeContactUrl` / `safeInstanceOrigin` (single chokepoint
  for operator-controlled URL rendering)
- `GlobalDailyCeiling.tryReserve()` / `releaseReservation()` API
  (closes TOCTOU race on the global signup ceiling)
- Reservation-tracking try/finally pattern in
  `apps/relay/src/api/create.ts` (every reservation has a paired
  release on every code path, including throws)

### Part 47 — beta-readiness operational tooling

#### File-based kill switch (`apps/relay/src/policy/killSwitch.ts`)
- Polls `${dataDir}/SIGNUPS_DISABLED` sentinel file every 1s
- `isActive()` cached for cheap per-request checks
- Logs warn-level transitions (armed / disarmed / file-touched)
- `unref()` on the timer so it doesn't keep the event loop alive
- New env var `MORPHIT_RELAY_DATA_DIR` (optional; null disables)
- Wired in `main.ts`; both `InviteEndpoint` and `CreateEndpoint`
  short-circuit with `signups_disabled` 503 when armed
- 7/7 dedicated tests
- Operator usage: `touch /var/lib/morphit-relay/SIGNUPS_DISABLED`
  to pause signups; `rm` to resume.  No relay restart needed.

#### Per-request access logging (`apps/relay/src/middleware/access_log.ts`)
- Single grep-friendly log line per request:
  method, path, status, dur_ms, code (extracted from JSON body)
- info for 2xx/3xx, warn for 4xx, error for 5xx
- No IPs, no bodies, no User-Agent (privacy floor preserved)
- ~10µs overhead per request
- Wired as FIRST middleware in `main.ts` so even rejected-by-
  middleware requests still get logged for triage

#### Beta-incident runbook (`docs/BETA-INCIDENT-RUNBOOK.md`)
9-section operator triage guide:
- §0: Is the relay running?
- §1: Did the request reach the relay?
- §2: Response code lookup table (full mapping)
- §3: Signups paused — kill-switch vs env-var vs ceiling
- §4: Request succeeded but tester says failed
- §5: Multiple testers shared IP / CGNAT
- §6: Relay out of funds
- §7: Chain RPC unavailable
- §8: Information to collect for escalation
- §9: Quick-reference cheat sheet

- **Treasury account**: `@morphit-fees`
- **Posting account**: `@morphit`
- **Relay account**: `@morphit-relay`
- **Matrix notation**: `@user:server` = DM, `#room:server` = public
  room.  Both coexist intentionally; never blanket-replace.
- **`ratchet` ban**: forbidden repo-wide except (a) brag-list §19
  framing why we don't use one, (b) `apps/web/src/lib/chat/fingerprint.ts`
  PGP_WORDS_EVEN array — the word is part of the canonical
  Patrick Juola & William Beverly 1995 PGP Word List that
  Morphit's OOB fingerprint protocol uses verbatim.  Changing the
  wordlist would break every previously-computed fingerprint.
- **Smoke baseline**: 1988 scenarios (was 1986 in Part 46;
  the kill-switch and access-log tests added 2)

## Post-Part 47 backlog: extensibility + i18n breadth (2026-05-04)

### Adding new trading assets — current state

The asset list is **decentralized across the indexer**, not a single
registry.  Adding a 4th coin (LTC, DOGE, DASH, etc.) currently means
touching at least:

- `apps/indexer/src/indexer/handlers/order.ts` — `ASSETS` set (line 34)
- `apps/indexer/src/indexer/handlers/orderReplace.ts` — `ASSETS` set (line 22)
- `apps/indexer/src/api/rssOrderbookHandlers.ts` — `VALID_ASSETS` (line 24)
- `apps/indexer/src/indexer/fee/` — needs a new explorer verifier
  written (see `bitcoinExplorerVerifier.ts` / `moneroExplorerVerifier.ts`
  as templates) — this is the bulk of the work, since each chain has
  different explorer JSON shapes, confirmation conventions, address
  formats, and unit conventions
- Frontend asset-icon SVGs + `apps/web/src/routes/dev/icons/+page.svelte`
- 10 locales × ~15 asset-related strings each = ~150 i18n entries
- Smoke scenarios that enumerate the asset set
- Database — schema today doesn't have asset-specific columns, so no
  migration needed, but verify before adding

**Estimated effort per new coin: 4-8 focused hours, plus translation.**

**Refactor to make this easy — SHIPPED 2026-05-07:**
`packages/asset-registry/` shipped.  Exports `ASSET_TICKERS`
(canonical ordered list), `ASSET_TICKERS_SET` (O(1) string
membership), `AssetTicker` type union, `ASSETS` array (per-entry
metadata: decimals, isCoordinationChain, canBeTraded,
canPayListingFee, addressShape regex), `getAsset()` lookup,
`isAssetTicker()` type guard, `COORDINATION_CHAIN` constant
with module-load-time invariant check (exactly one asset has
the flag), `tradeable()` / `feePayable()` / `externalAssets()`
filter helpers.

All 32 hardcoded sites in `apps/indexer`, `apps/relay`,
`apps/web`, and `packages/indexer-client` rewritten to import
from the registry.  Smoke at
`packages/asset-registry/scripts/asset-registry-smoke.ts`
locks the invariants in CI.  Adding a 4th coin (LTC, DOGE,
DASH, etc.) is now a one-file edit (the registry) plus the
external-tx-id verifier + frontend UI metadata + i18n strings.

### Adding new languages — current state

The locale registry IS centralized at
`apps/web/src/lib/i18n/index.ts`.  Adding a language is structurally
trivial — and as of 2026-05-07 the wiring is one-array-edit:

- `register()` calls are now driven from `SUPPORTED_LOCALES` via
  a loop, so adding a language is just adding to that array (plus
  dropping the JSON).  Pre-2026-05 required keeping the array and
  the explicit `register('xx', ...)` calls in sync manually.
- New `PLANNED_LOCALES` array for languages scaffolded but not
  yet shipping translations.  Doesn't appear in the switcher,
  doesn't ship a JS bundle, but advertises the intent in code
  for translators.
- Smoke at `apps/web/scripts/i18n-locale-registry-smoke.ts`
  enforces consistency: SUPPORTED and PLANNED disjoint, every
  SUPPORTED has a JSON file, no orphan files, en is always
  SUPPORTED.
- New `docs/CONTRIBUTING-TRANSLATIONS.md` walking translators
  through the workflow + quality bar + per-language audience
  rationale.

The 7 PLANNED_LOCALES (hi, ar, bn, pt, id, ja, vi) are
scaffolded; a translator who finishes a JSON moves the entry
from PLANNED → SUPPORTED in a one-line PR.

**The hard part is the translation itself.**  Each locale is
2,161 keys.  Quality bar: native speaker review.

Languages to add post-launch (in roughly descending population order):

- **Hindi (`hi`)** — ~600M speakers
- **Arabic (`ar`)** — ~370M, RTL (use `fa` as a layout reference)
- **Bengali (`bn`)** — ~270M
- **Portuguese (`pt`)** — ~260M (consider `pt-BR` and `pt-PT` separately)
- **Indonesian (`id`)** — ~200M
- **Japanese (`ja`)** — ~125M
- **Vietnamese (`vi`)** — ~85M

**Estimated effort per language:** 30 minutes of code + 20-40
hours of human translation work + native-speaker review pass.

**Approach options:**
- Hire a translator per locale (~$0.10-$0.20/word × ~5,000 words ≈
  $500-$1000 per locale)
- Crowd-source via a self-hosted Weblate or Tolgee instance — gives
  the federation operator community a contribution path beyond code
- Machine-translate as a starting point + community review (lowest
  cost, lowest initial quality)

**RTL languages need extra care:** Persian/`fa` is already in the
codebase as the canary.  Arabic should "just work" if the Tailwind
`ltr:` / `rtl:` utility usage is consistent — but should be
exercised with a full UI walkthrough, not just an i18n string drop.

### Open question

When/how do we want to start the language expansion?  Options:

1. **After mainnet/beta stabilizes** — no point translating strings
   that may still change
2. **Right after launch** — get translations rolling so each language
   only lags by a small backlog
3. **Pre-translate now using machine translation, polish later** —
   gives geographic reach immediately at the cost of phrasing quality

(My instinct is option 1: stabilize first, then translate.  But
worth deciding deliberately rather than letting it drift.)


## Post-final-audit polish items (2026-05 attack-tree analysis)

### Per-prefix rate-limit bucketing (IPv6 /64, IPv4 /24)
**Source:** Pre-launch attack tree analysis, leaf A1.1.4

Currently the relay's per-IP rate limiters bucket by full IP address.
For IPv6 this is ineffective against attackers with /64 (or wider)
prefix budget — a single /64 gives 2^64 source addresses. The global
daily ceiling absolutely caps damage at 50/day, but a more granular
per-prefix limit would catch botnet abuse earlier and reduce ALTCHA
load.

**Effort:** ~1 day. Add a prefix-canonicalization helper, swap the
limiter map to use canonical-key, add tests for IPv4/24 + IPv6/64
bucketing.

**Not a launch-blocker:** the global ceiling closes the worst-case
loop. Polish item.

### Witness chain-fee delta alerter — SHIPPED 2026-05-07
**Source:** Pre-launch attack tree analysis, leaf A4.2

**Re-verification:** the original REVISIT description was
imprecise — there is no "110% trip-wire" in the relay; what
exists is a one-shot 10% boot-time warn (FEE_DIVERGENCE_WARN_THRESHOLD
in `apps/relay/src/blurt/client.ts:159`), and a continuous-poll
alerter in `apps/indexer/src/indexer/witnessFeePoller.ts` that
emits `FEE_CHANGED` on EVERY value change.

**The real gap was alert payload:** the existing FEE_CHANGED
alert just carried `oldBlurt` and `newBlurt`.  An operator with
a Discord/Matrix bot integration would have to do their own
delta + percent computation to decide urgency.

**Resolution this turn:**
- `WitnessFeeAlert['FEE_CHANGED']` extended with `deltaBlurt`
  (signed amount), `deltaPct` (signed percentage of old value;
  `null` only on the unusual oldBlurt=0 case), and `direction`
  ('up' | 'down').
- `defaultAlertSink` updated to log all three new fields in
  the structured `fee_changed` warn line.
- `witnessFeePoller.test.ts` extended with assertions on the
  new fields for both the increase (50% up) and decrease
  (50% down) test cases.

**Not a threshold-based alerter** because the BLURT
account_creation_fee has been stable at 100 BLURT for years —
there's no noise to filter.  Alerting on every change is the
correct behavior; the audit fix was about giving the alert
enough information to be actionable.


### Collapse migration history before v1.0.0 — SHIPPED 2026-05-07
**Source:** Phase G audit (2026-05-06)

The 27-file `schema-v*.sql` migration chain is convenient during
development but verbose for fresh installs.  Pre-launch we have no
deployed instances, so we collapsed the entire chain into a single
clean `schema.sql` reflecting the final shape.

**Resolution this turn:**
- `apps/indexer/src/db/schema.sql` — single canonical file
  (1,834 lines including version-marker comments).  Verified
  byte-for-byte schema equivalence with the incremental-applied
  result via `pg_dump --schema-only` diff (zero lines diff
  across 599 lines of dump output).
- `apps/indexer/src/db/historical/` — archived all 27 historical
  files for archaeology; never read by the runtime.
- `migrations.ts` — replaced 27-entry MIGRATIONS array with a
  single v1 entry that has `subsumesVersions: [2..27]`.  On a
  fresh DB the runner records (1, 2, ..., 27) in
  `schema_migrations` so any downstream "is v15 applied?" check
  still returns true.
- `validateMigrationsContract()` — strengthened to enforce
  declared+subsumed coverage is gap-free.
- `apps/indexer/test/integration/harness.ts` — unified with the
  production migration runner.  Pre-collapse, the harness had
  its own SQL-file applier that bypassed `runMigrations()`,
  which is exactly the divergence that allowed G1's missing v24
  to slip past CI.
- 3 new collapse-regression tests in
  `migrations.test.ts`: all 27 versions recorded, subsumed-version
  descriptions reference v1, every v1-v27 table exists.

70/70 integration tests pass (was 67; +3 collapse).
post-G1/G2 fixes (verified against real Postgres in the integration suite).

**Source:** Phase K audit (2026-05-06)

- Updated the §13 cross-reference to describe the shipped behavior
  rather than "once that feature ships"

audit campaign was designed to catch.

Two paths forward:
1. **Implement it.**  ~30 lines in each of indexer/relay config

### Implement Docker `*_FILE` env-var-from-secret pattern (or remove from docs)
**Source:** Phase K audit (2026-05-06)

`docs/OPERATIONS.md §33` (Docker deployment) shows a Compose
example that uses Docker secrets via `*_FILE` env vars:
- `MORPHIT_INDEXER_DB_PASSWORD_FILE`
- `MORPHIT_RELAY_DB_PASSWORD_FILE`
- `MORPHIT_RELAY_KEYSTORE_PATH`
- `MORPHIT_RELAY_PASSPHRASE_FILE`

**None of these are read by the relay or indexer config loaders.**
An operator following this Compose example would deploy a
non-functional cluster.

§33 has been flagged with a "not-yet-implemented" caveat noting
that until this lands, credentials must be inlined into the
DATABASE_URL.

Two paths:
1. **Implement.**  Standard Docker-secrets pattern: when
   `FOO_FILE` is set, read the file contents and use that as
   `FOO`.  ~20 lines of zod refinement code per affected var,
   shared helper.  Apply to: db password, relay keystore,
   relay passphrase.  Smoke test: spin up a container with a
   bind-mounted secret, assert config parses.
2. **Remove from docs.**  Strip the `*_FILE` references from
   the Compose example, just inline the secret values.  Less
   secure (secret ends up in compose-rendered env), but matches
   shipped behavior.

Recommendation: option 1.  The Docker-secrets pattern is the
standard for production-ready Compose deployments and a
serious operator running Morphit alongside other services
will expect it.

**Effort:** ~3-4 hours including a smoke and tests.

### Sally walkthrough — Part 68 follow-ups (2026-05-07)

The Part 68 walkthrough through every Sally surface produced a
batch of structural improvements (H1–H9, M1–M3, M8–M12, L8–L13)
that were applied directly to the working tree.  Three items
were investigated but deferred or surfaced as systemic
ratifications, and one finding was confirmed already-handled:

**1. Identicon source inconsistency between IdentityLabel and the
   public surfaces (Profile + Explorer).**

   Investigated as L9.  `IdentityLabel.svelte` (used in chat
   rows, my/orders, orderbook, feedback lists) prefers
   `publicKey` bytes when present, falls back to account-name
   bytes otherwise.  The public profile page (`/@account`) and
   the explorer-account page (`/explorer/account/[name]`) both
   seed unconditionally from the account-name bytes.

   Result: a Sally whose posting key is present in chain
   metadata sees ONE identicon when she's rendered through
   IdentityLabel and a DIFFERENT identicon when she's rendered
   on her own profile page or in the explorer.

   I started to "fix" the explorer to use the posting pubkey,
   then reverted: that would have made the explorer different
   from the profile, swapping which surfaces match.

   The right ratification is a project-level decision:
     (a) Always seed from account name (ditch pubkey-seeding in
         IdentityLabel).  Simplest, most consistent, but loses
         the ability to visually distinguish two accounts with
         the same name but different keys (account-recovery
         flow).
     (b) Always seed from posting pubkey when known.  Requires
         profile + explorer to fetch the pubkey before rendering
         the identicon (extra round-trip, identicon flicker).
     (c) Status quo: each surface seeds from whatever it has
         locally.  Inconsistent but has zero performance cost.

   **Effort:** small for (a), moderate for (b).  Not blocking
   launch.

**2. `firstTradeAnnounce` default ratification.**

   Default is currently ON (`syndicationPrefs.ts` line 24-32).
   Sally's first feedback automatically posts a "I joined
   Morphit" announcement to the @morphit community on Blurt.
   Disclosed in the feedback form (Part 68 H9 upgraded the
   disclosure to a prominent emerald card with a selling-point
   pitch + inline checkbox), but the default itself is still
   "post unless you opt out."

   For a privacy-first project, default-ON social broadcast is
   a tension.  The selling-point pitch reframes the announcement
   as a benefit (more eyes → more trades → upvote earnings into
   the user's own Blurt wallet, which is real), so opt-in becomes
   easier to make appealing.

   Two options:
     (a) Keep default-ON, status quo.  The pitch + inline toggle
         is enough — the user always sees the disclosure before
         submission and can flip it without leaving the form.
     (b) Flip default to OFF.  Requires the user to actively
         opt in.  Privacy-first stance, but trades off the
         welcome-bonus's promotional spread.

   I deliberately did not flip the default in Part 68.  Calling
   out the question for ratification.

**3. Edit-window value (3 minutes).**

   `post/edit/[permlink]/+page.svelte:170` hardcodes a 3-minute
   window from `created_at`.  Part 68 added a live countdown chip
   on `/my/orders` and `/post` success card (M1/M8) so the user
   feels the deadline ticking — but 3 minutes is brutally short.
   A user who notices a typo on the my-orders page after walking
   away from the keyboard for 4 minutes is locked out.

   Two options:
     (a) Bump to 15 minutes.  Trade-off: indexer keeps a longer
         "this order may still be edited" window; if a stranger
         opens chat with the order owner during that window,
         the owner can race-edit terms after seeing who's
         interested.  3 minutes was chosen specifically to
         minimize this race.
     (b) Keep 3 minutes, add a clearer end-of-window UX (e.g.
         a banner on the edit page itself explaining why it's
         short and what to do instead — cancel + re-post).

   Not a Part 68 fix; calling out for ratification.

**4. Plan-status surface ratification.**

   `/plan` page used to render a hardcoded "in progress" chip on
   Phase 1.  Part 68 L11 removed it (it was perpetually wrong).
   The page now has phase TITLES + BODIES but no per-phase
   status indicator.

   Question: where should phase status come from?
     (a) Hardcoded in the template (status quo, but bad — same
         drift problem).
     (b) Read from `package.json` version + a `PHASES.json`
         manifest.  Code-tracked, but updaters need to remember
         to bump the manifest on phase completion.
     (c) Read from chain — phase X is "shipped" when the
         operator-account broadcasts a phase-completion marker.
         Robust but Phase-5 itself.

   For now (b) is the cheapest cleanest fix.

**5. BH4 finding was wrong.**

   Part 68 walkthrough flagged the `feeMethodChoice` clamp on
   `waiverOffered` flipping false as missing.  Investigation
   showed it's already correctly handled at
   `apps/web/src/routes/post/+page.svelte:383` inside an
   existing `$effect`.  No change needed.  Documenting here so
   future audits don't re-flag it.

**6. Surfaces NOT yet read in Part 68 walkthrough:**

   `/compare`, `/download`, `/about-this-instance`, `/operators`,
   `/run-a-node`, `/login/qr-pair`.  Each is 200-350 lines of
   page.svelte.  Should be Sally-walked through in a follow-up
   pass.  Risk surface: `/compare` (321 lines) may have
   competitor-comparison claims that are unverifiable.

pass:

**1. /compare** is an inter-instance orderbook diff tool, not a

   here. The page is a legitimate operator-trust mechanism per

**2. /operators contact-URL validator deferred (intentionally).**
   Part 69 OPS2: the inline `validateContactUrl` (https-only,

   registration surface is stricter by design — replacing the
   inline check with the shared helper would silently relax
   validation. Documented inline so a future contributor
   doesn't "consolidate" the helpers.

**3. /operators + /run-a-node dark-mode-only theming.**
   Part 69 OPS1 + RAN1 noted but not fixed: both pages use
   `text-ink-300/400/500`, `bg-ink-900/950`, `border-ink-800`
   without `dark:`-paired classes. On light mode the contrast
   is wrong. Not fixed because it's a design-system pass
   touching ~20 lines per page; doing it surgically without
   making it look broken in either mode requires a bigger
   sweep. **Recommended scope for a future pass:** audit every
   page for unpaired `text-ink-*` / `border-ink-*` / `bg-ink-*`
   classes and add the corresponding `dark:` mate. Risk: zero;
   benefit: light-mode users get correct contrast.

**4. Stale "2,030+ self-checks" claim in brag-list.**
   Line 351 of MORPHIT-BRAG-LIST.md says "runs the 2,030+
   self-checks." The actual number has grown — Part 68 added

   makes the claim still technically correct. Not updated

   replace with a fixed-N claim or a script that reads the
   live count.

**Tooltip mobile-tap UX hole.** ⚠️ FILED, not blocking.
- Tooltip component renders helper text on
  `onmouseenter`/`onmouseleave`, plus navigates to FAQ on
  click via `onclick={openFaq}`.
- On touch devices: tap immediately fires the click
  handler before the mouseenter visual settles, so users
  on mobile never see the tooltip text — they see only the
  FAQ navigation.
- Not pre-launch blocker because every tooltip site that
  matters has the FAQ as a destination (the user gets the
  same info, more verbosely). But mobile users miss the
  in-flow hint.
- Future fix: differentiate hover-vs-click on touch
  devices (e.g. first tap shows tooltip, second tap
  navigates), or render the tooltip text inline-below
  on touch.

**Smoke per-file identifier-resolution gap.** ⚠️ FILED,
not blocking.
- href-xss-smoke's call-detection regex
  `/^([\w$]+)\s*\(/` only fires when the expression
  STARTS with `name(`. Bare-identifier hrefs like
  `href={canonical}` aren't recognized as safe even when
  `canonical` is a `$derived` from a SAFE_BUILDER_NAMES
  call (e.g. `canonicalFor(resolvedPath)`).
- Workaround: per-line allowlist entries (Head.svelte:150,
  Head.svelte:164). These drift on legitimate edits.
- Better fix: extend the smoke to track $derived-from-
  builder identifier names so the per-line allowlist isn't
  needed. Not pre-launch blocker.
- The Part-70 `safe[A-Z]` template-literal rule + the
  Part-74 `validated[A-Z]` identifier rule already cover
  the most common patterns; only `canonical` and `alt.href`
  in Head.svelte fall through.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
PART 85 — `drain-defense-live-fire` FLAKE ROOT-CAUSED AND FIXED
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Long-standing intermittent flake on `apps/relay/scripts/
drain-defense-live-fire.ts` finally root-caused.  Prior
sessions had attributed it to tsx-warmup timing races
(REVISIT-LIST Parts 25/26 introduced ManualClock to fix
a different real race in the composition scenario; the
remaining intermittent flake was assumed to be of the
same family).  **It was not.**

**Real cause: smoke's fault-injection logic insufficient.**

The `'tampered signature rejected'` scenario at
drain-defense-live-fire.ts:221 tampered the signature
by flipping the LAST char of the base64url-encoded
HMAC-SHA-256:

```
const tampered = parts[0] + '.' + (sig.slice(0, -1) + (sig.at(-1) === 'a' ? 'b' : 'a'));
```

The signature is HMAC-SHA-256 → 32 bytes → 256 bits.
base64url encodes 32 bytes as **43 characters carrying
258 bits** (43 × 6 bits/char).  The last 2 bits are
encoding padding — they decode to nothing.  Four
distinct last-chars share the same 4-bit prefix and
decode to the **identical 32-byte buffer**.

For a random HMAC sig, the chance the tamper char
('a' or 'b' depending on the original) lands in the
"padding-equivalent" set is ~6%.  Empirically: 59
collisions in 1000 trials.

When a collision hits, `tampered` decodes to the SAME
32 bytes as the original signature.  `verify()`
correctly accepts it — the bytes are valid.  The test's
assertion `'tampered sig should fail'` fires, the
scenario reports failure.

**The cold-tsx attribution was a coincidence.**  The
flake fires probabilistically every run regardless of
tsx state.  It appeared cold-correlated because Ken's
sessions always triple-pulse on hot caches (typically
all-clean), and the cold cycles between sessions were
more likely to expose the random failure across more
total runs.  But running cold doesn't INCREASE the
collision probability — only the variance in
how-many-trials the flake gets to manifest in.

**Fix (1 line):** tamper the FIRST char of the sig.

```
const tampered = parts[0] + '.' + (sig.at(0) === 'A' ? 'B' : 'A') + sig.slice(1);
```

The first 6 bits of base64 always encode the high 6
bits of byte 0; any change to the first char is
guaranteed to change the first decoded byte.  Empirical:
**0 collisions in 10,000 trials.**

**Verification:** 20+ consecutive cold-tsx cycles of
`drain-defense-live-fire` clean post-fix (12 scenario-
only direct runs + 8+ full smoke runner runs).  Pre-fix
flake rate ~6%; post-fix observed 0.  Statistical
confidence ≥ 70% that the fix eliminates the flake based
on observation alone (1 - 0.94²⁰ ≈ 71%); empirical
mathematical analysis confirms the root cause is exactly
the encoding-padding ambiguity.

**Lessons:**

- Fault-injection in tests must produce GUARANTEED
  semantic differences, not just textual differences.
  A textual flip can be neutralized by encoding-layer
  ambiguity (here: base64url's padding bits).
- "Intermittent flake on cold start" is a tempting
  attribution but lazy.  The Part-25/26 fix was real
  (ManualClock for UTC-midnight rollover); the
  remaining flake had a DIFFERENT root cause that
  hid behind the same surface symptom.
- When a fault-injection test passes/fails by ~6%,
  that's a clear smell of probabilistic distribution
  over a discrete encoding space.  ~6% ≈ 1/16 ≈ 4
  bits of insufficient discrimination — exactly what
  base64's 6-bit-char vs 8-bit-byte ratio leaks at
  the trailing edge.

**Memory updated:** prior attribution "tsx-warmup
timing race" removed; replaced with the actual
encoding-padding-collision explanation.  Production
code (HMAC verify, timingSafeEqual, base64 decode) was
always correct.

  `apps/ops-cli/test/time.test.ts` — covering
  `parseDurationSpec` / `formatDuration` used by every
  `--since` / `--age` operator filter)

**Pre-fix consequences:**

1. **CI's `npm ci` did NOT install ops-cli's deps.**
   The typecheck-sweep happened to pass only because
   `pg` was hoisted from the indexer's transitive deps
   and other deps coincidentally matched.  An
   ops-cli-unique dep added in any future patch would
   silently surface as "uninstalled module noise"
   filtered out by `scripts/typecheck-sweep.sh` —
   masking real type errors on CI while passing
   locally.

2. **CI's `npm test --workspaces --if-present` did NOT
   run ops-cli's 24-test vitest suite at all.**  Bugs
   in ops-cli's parseDurationSpec / formatDuration
   would ship to operators undetected.  These helpers
   are used in every operator status / drain / signups
   filter — a regression there breaks every operator's
   triage workflow on day one of beta.

3. CI's `Run smokes` step worked only because `tsx` was
   hoisted from elsewhere and `pg` was incidentally
   present.  Brittle.

**The fix (one-line):**

`package.json` workspaces array:
```diff
   "workspaces": [
     "apps/web",
     "apps/relay",
     "apps/indexer",
+    "apps/ops-cli",
     "packages/indexer-client",
     "packages/operator-config",
     "packages/asset-registry"
   ],
```

**Verified post-fix:**
- `package-lock.json` now includes `morphit-ops@0.1.0`
  registration (`grep -c morphit-ops package-lock.json`
  shows 3 mentions; pre-fix was 0)
- `npm test --workspaces --if-present` picks up and
  runs the 24 tests
- `bash scripts/typecheck-sweep.sh` continues to pass
  cleanly (0 errors across all 7 projects)
- All 91 smoke runners + 2046 scenarios still pass
  triple-pulse clean (3 cold-tsx cycles)

**Why this hid for so long:**

The original workspaces array was set up early in
phase 3, before ops-cli was scaffolded.  When ops-cli
was added, its package.json + tsconfig + smokes
were created, smokes were registered in
`run-smokes.sh`, but the root workspaces array was
not updated to include it.  Local development worked
because `tsx` and `pg` happened to be in
`node_modules/` from sibling workspaces.  No CI
failure ever surfaced because the noise filter in
`typecheck-sweep.sh` quietly absorbed any unresolved
imports.

**Lesson:** silent-by-design noise filters in CI
checks need an opt-in / opt-out audit trail.  If the
filter ever absorbs a real error, the absorber and
the unresolvable import need to be discoverable
together.

**Lesson 2:** when adding a new workspace child,
update the root `package.json`'s `workspaces` array
in the SAME commit that creates the child.  Add a
sentinel smoke that asserts every directory under
`apps/` and `packages/` containing a `package.json`
is in the workspaces array — would have caught this
on day one.  (Filed as a follow-on hardening for
later — not blocking pre-launch.)

## Part 87 (2026-05-08) — CI-coverage audit (Memory #11 category J)

Internal-infrastructure audit pass on the CI surface itself.  No
brag-list entry — this Part's work is purely about catching
process drift in our own CI plumbing, not a public-facing win.
Findings J-1 through J-9 below; all closed in this Part.

### J-1 — `run-smokes.sh` silently counts 0 scenarios when a runner emits no canonical line (HIGH, NOVEL)

The runner script's success-path arithmetic was:

```bash
n=$(grep "^✓ all" "$SMOKE_OUT" | sed "s/.*all \([0-9]*\).*/\1/")
total=$((total + n))
```

If `n` is empty (the runner exited 0 but didn't emit a `^✓ all N`
line), bash's `$((total + ))` evaluates as `$((total + 0))` —
silently — under `set -u` (because arithmetic context treats
empty as 0, not unset).  A future smoke that exits 0 with a
non-canonical success line gets counted as 0 scenarios with no
warning.  **Reproduced** with a minimal harness.

**Fix:** any passing runner that emits no `^✓ all N` line is now
treated as a runner failure (`failed++`), not silent zero.  The
runner prints an explanatory message: `"passed runner but emitted
no canonical '^✓ all N …' line — fix the smoke to print it"`.
Regression-tested by temporarily breaking sally-walkthrough's
output line and confirming the new error fires correctly.

### J-2 — `sally-walkthrough-smoke` emitted non-canonical success line; 22 scenarios silently uncounted (HIGH, NOVEL, ACTIVE)

Surfaced by the J-1 reproducer.  `sally-walkthrough-smoke.ts` was
added Part 68/69 with success line `"22 passed, 0 failed (22
total)"` and `"sally-walkthrough smoke OK"` — neither matched the
runner's `grep "^✓ all"`.  Consequence: those 22 scenarios have
been counted as **0** in the smoke total since Part 68.

The brag-list / TARBALL.md / REVISIT-LIST count claimed across
Parts 68, 69, 70-71, 72, 73-74, 76-83, 85, 86 was off by 22 from
when sally was added.  Real Part 86 total: 2,053 + 22 = **2,075**,
not 2,053.

**Fix:** sally now emits canonical `console.log(`✓ all
${SCENARIOS.length} sally-walkthrough scenarios passed`)` line in
addition to its custom human-friendly summary.  Verified by
re-running and observing both lines.  Smoke total post-Part-87:
**2,075 across 92 runners**, 0 failures.

**Math correction policy:** "fix forward, don't rewrite history."
Historical brag/REVISIT/TARBALL entries from Parts 68–86
described what was claimed-at-the-time.  Rewriting them would
hide the bug discovery.  Going forward (Part 87+), the count is
2,075 and stays accurate.

### J-3 — `typecheck-sweep.sh` noise-filter unscoped allowlists (DOCUMENTATION-ONLY, NOT A BUG)

The noise-filter regex contains two unscoped clauses:

- `apps/relay/test/(create|drainer|unlock)\.test\.ts`
- `apps/indexer/src/indexer/(low|operatorAccount)BalanceScanner\.ts.* error TS2345:`

Initial reading suggested these silently swallow ALL errors in
those files.  Verified-on-investigation: the relay tests use
`$config`, `$crypto`, `$db`, `$blurt`, `$queue`, `$policy`,
`$middleware`, `$api`, `$log` path aliases declared in
`apps/relay/tsconfig.json` `paths` and resolved at runtime by
`apps/relay/vitest.config.ts` `resolve.alias`.  But `tsc` with
`moduleResolution: "NodeNext"` does **NOT** honor `paths` — so
every $-aliased import emits a primary "Cannot find module"
error PLUS a cascade of secondary errors (TS2304 missing names,
TS18046 'unknown' on catch vars from `instanceof`, TS2345
mistyped args from inferred-any returns, TS2554 wrong arg
counts, etc.) that are NOT real bugs — they're the gap between
vitest's bundler-style resolution and tsc's NodeNext.

The unscoped clauses are a pragmatic shorthand for "every
cascade error in these files."  Listing each cascade error code
per file was rejected as impractical because the codes vary with
upstream API shape.

**Disposition:** intentional.  Improved the surrounding comment
in `scripts/typecheck-sweep.sh` to explain the architectural
cause (`paths` vs NodeNext) and document that switching relay's
`moduleResolution` to `"Bundler"` would let us drop most of the
allowlist.  Filed as backlog rather than Part 87 blocker.

### J-4 — `packages/asset-registry` missing from typecheck-sweep (REAL, NOVEL)

`packages/asset-registry` has its own `tsconfig.json` with strict
mode + `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` + `noImplicitOverride`, but was
absent from `scripts/typecheck-sweep.sh`.  Same class of gap as
Part 86's B-1 (workspace child has full scaffold but parent
registry forgot to include it).

The canonical asset-list module
(`packages/asset-registry/src/index.ts` — runtime-immutable
`Object.freeze` + Proxy trap, brag #209) had never been
typechecked by CI.  It happens to typecheck clean today (verified
post-fix), but a TS error introduced there would have shipped
silently.

**Fix:** added `project "asset-registry" packages/asset-registry/tsconfig.json`
to the sweep.  Sweep now covers 8 projects (was 7), all 0 errors.

**Backlog item** added: extend the workspace-membership smoke
from Part 86 (B-1.5) to also assert every workspace child's
tsconfig (if present) is referenced in `typecheck-sweep.sh`.
Same sentinel pattern, different parent registry.

### J-5 — CI never ran `npm test` for relay / indexer-unit / ops-cli (CRITICAL, NOVEL)

`.forgejo/workflows/ci.yml` had exactly two test invocations:

1. `npm test -w apps/web` (web-only) in the `web` job
2. `npm run test:integration` (indexer integration only) in the
   `indexer-integration` job

**Indexer unit (370+1 skip), relay unit (244), and ops-cli (24)
suites — 638 tests across 58 test files — never gated CI.**
This includes 1,675 lines of test code covering the relay's most
critical paths (altcha race fix, invite-token, globalDailyCeiling
TOCTOU, drainer, create-endpoint, unlock).

Brag-list entry #235's claim *"workspaces test sweep runs all 24
ops-cli tests"* was wrong — root `package.json` has
`"test": "npm run test --workspaces --if-present"` but CI never
invoked it.  Corrected the framing in brag #235 in this Part:
the workspace-membership fix was correct (it makes future
`--workspaces` invocations include ops-cli), but the consequence
sentence was misleading about what CI was actually doing.

**Fix:** added a new `unit-tests` job to `.forgejo/workflows/ci.yml`
that runs `npm test --workspaces --if-present` from root, picking
up all four workspaces' unit suites.  Comment block in the job
narrates the gap and references this REVISIT-LIST entry.  The
`web` job's `npm test -w apps/web` step is intentionally retained
as a redundant gate (cheap, keeps web job self-contained).

**Verified locally:** `npm test --workspaces --if-present`
produces all four green: web 545+5skip, relay 244, indexer
370+1skip, ops-cli 24.

### J-6 — `apps/web/eslint.config.js` was missing entirely; lint step has been broken since Part 86 (CRITICAL, NOVEL)

Three nested findings:

1. `apps/web/package.json` declares `"lint": "prettier --check .
   && eslint ."` and has `eslint ^9.14.0` + `eslint-plugin-svelte
   ^2.46.0` in devDeps — but **no eslint config file existed
   anywhere in the repo**.  ESLint v9 requires a flat config
   (`eslint.config.{js,mjs,cjs}`) and exits non-zero without one,
   meaning the eslint half of `lint` had been a no-op for an
   unknown duration.  Possibly never ran.  No mention of "lint
   green" exists in any prior brag/TARBALL/REVISIT entry —
   confirmed via repo-wide grep.

2. Even if eslint had been working, `prettier --check . && eslint
   .` short-circuits via `&&` — if prettier fails, eslint never
   runs.  Prettier was failing.

3. **Prettier 3.8.3 + prettier-plugin-svelte 3.5.1 throws
   TypeError on every Svelte file.**  Bisected to prettier 3.7.0
   introducing strict `embed.getVisitorKeys` enforcement that
   plugin-svelte 3.5.1 (the latest available) doesn't satisfy.
   Tarball lockfile pinned 3.8.3 (resolved by Part 86's caret
   bump from `^3.3.3`), so CI's lint step has been **completely
   red since Part 86's lockfile re-resolution**.

**Fix (full stack):**

- Pinned `prettier` to `~3.6.2` in `apps/web/package.json` (last
  3.x minor compatible with plugin-svelte 3.5.1).
- Added `@eslint/js`, `globals`, `@typescript-eslint/parser` as
  explicit devDeps (they were transitively present, but explicit
  is honest).
- Wrote `apps/web/eslint.config.js` — flat config with `js`
  recommended, `eslint-plugin-svelte` recommended, TS parser
  wired into svelte-eslint-parser for `<script lang="ts">`
  blocks, and pragmatic rule tuning:
  - `no-undef` OFF for `.ts` and `.svelte` (TS handles it; ESLint
    no-undef false-flags TS types like `BufferSource`,
    `DocumentEventMap`, `NotificationOptions`)
  - `service-worker.ts` gets `globals.serviceworker`
  - `__MORPHIT_VERSION__` (vite-injected) declared as a project
    global
  - `svelte/no-at-html-tags` set to WARN (the project audits
    `{@html}` usages via href-xss-smoke + safe*/validated*
    identifier conventions; the smoke is the real gate)
  - `svelte/no-unused-svelte-ignore` set to WARN
  - `no-control-regex` OFF (chat-payload's purpose is to deny
    control chars)
  - `no-console` OFF
  - `no-unused-vars` WARN with `^_` prefix exemption
  - tests + smokes get `no-unused-vars` OFF entirely
- Wrote `apps/web/.prettierignore` to skip `.svelte-kit/`,
  `build/`, locale JSONs, `static/`, `node_modules/`,
  `package-lock.json`.
- Ran `prettier --write .` once on apps/web — reformatted ~223
  files (cumulative drift from prior prettier minor versions).
- Fixed real lint findings unmasked along the way:
  - `apps/web/src/lib/chat/chainOpVerify.ts` — removed two
    useless try-catch wrappers that just rethrew (no-useless-catch).
  - `apps/web/src/lib/components/Head.svelte` — split
    `'</script>'` literal in JSON-LD template so
    svelte-eslint-parser's script-block boundary detector doesn't
    mis-terminate.  Output identical at runtime.
  - `apps/web/scripts/i18n-hardcoded-english-smoke.ts` — removed
    redundant `\[` escape inside character class.
  - `apps/web/src/lib/components/HardwareKeyCard.svelte`,
    `apps/web/src/routes/dev/yubikey-probe/+page.svelte`,
    `apps/web/src/routes/login/+page.svelte` — replaced 3 empty
    `catch {}` blocks with explanatory comments inside the catch
    body (intentional close-error swallow on YubiKey cleanup;
    documented intent).

**Post-fix:** `npm run lint -w apps/web` exits 0.  0 errors, 170
warnings (all `no-unused-vars` style + intentional `{@html}` set
to warn).  First time the lint script has been verifiably green
in audit history.

### J-7 — Backend workspaces had no `lint` script (LOW-MED, NOVEL)

Indexer, relay, and ops-cli had no `lint` or `format` scripts in
`package.json`.  Backend formatting was enforced by convention
only.

**Fix:** added `lint: "prettier --check ."` and `format:
"prettier --write ."` to all three backend workspaces.  Created
`.prettierrc` (matching apps/web's tab convention with locale
overrides for JSON/MD/YAML) and `.prettierignore` in each.
Pinned `prettier ~3.6.2` as devDep (matches root pin).  Ran
`prettier --write` once to bring backends into compliance:

- relay: 48 files reformatted; now clean
- indexer: 161 files reformatted; now clean
- ops-cli: 33 files reformatted; now clean

Total backend drift cleaned: 242 files.  All gates remain green
post-format (typecheck-sweep, all unit tests).

**Fix:** updated footer to **"2,075 self-checks across 92 runners,

### J-9 — Prettier 3.8.3 + plugin-svelte 3.5.1 lockfile combo crashes on every Svelte file (CRITICAL, NOVEL)

Documented in detail under J-6 (root cause and fix).  Standalone

plugin hasn't published a matching update.

## Part 88 (2026-05-08) — STRIDE threat-model refresh (Memory #11 category K)

The existing STRIDE matrix at `docs/audit/2026-05-stride-matrix.md`
was generated Part 29 against four primary attack surfaces (frontend
SPA, indexer HTTP server, relay HTTP server, Blurt chain) and
covered 24 threat rows: S1-S4, T1-T4, R1-R2, I1-I5, D1-D5, E1-E4.

Substantial new attack surface has shipped since Part 29.  Part 88
extends the matrix with 17 new STRIDE rows covering surfaces
introduced post-Part-29.  No matrix history rewritten — original
24 rows retained verbatim under their `## Part 29` heading; the new
17 rows are appended under `## Part 88 refresh`.

### New threat rows added

**Spoofing (S5-S7):**
- S5 — Phone-side QR-pairing signature replayed against chain ops
  (mitigated by domain-separation prefix `"morphit-pairing-v1\n"`,
  fresh nonces, echo-check round trip)
- S6 — Operator-payout sender impersonates @morphit-fees in payout
  broadcast (mitigated by relay holding only operator's own active
  key, never @morphit-fees's; verified at drainer.ts lines 283-297)
- S7 — Witness-fee alert spoofed by malicious chain RPC (mitigated
  by callMany rotator quorum + alerts being informational only)

**Tampering (T5-T7):**
- T5 — Tampering with asset-registry at runtime (mitigated by
  Object.freeze deep + Proxy trap + asset-registry-smoke)
- T6 — Tampering with kill-switch state file (mitigated by
  structured `kill_switch_activated`/`kill_switch_deactivated`
  log lines; explicit operator-trust boundary)
- T7 — Tampering with on-chain morphit_release_v1 to point at
  hostile bundles (mitigated by TOFU posting-key pin + S2 chain
  quorum + AGPL-3.0 build-from-source path; residual risk for
  legitimate-key-misuse documented as future threshold-multisig
  hardening)

**Repudiation (R3-R5):**
- R3 — Operator denies they enabled the kill switch during user
  lockout (mitigated by structured logs + federation-choice
  recovery)
- R4 — User repudiates a phone-signed pairing (mitigated by
  pairing-signs-with-posting-key — same key as chain ops)
- R5 — Operator repudiates a canary going stale (mitigated by
  canary-template-smoke catching template/generator drift +
  documented 14-day silence-implies-tripped window; future
  hardening: sign canary with operator's posting key)

**Information disclosure (I6-I8):**
- I6 — QR-pairing leaks pairing bundle to operator's relay
  (mitigated by ciphertext payload encrypted with desktop's
  ephemeral pubkey; operator-trust boundary explicit)
- I7 — Witness-fee alerts shape leaks operator's polling cadence
  to RPC providers (mitigated by hourly low-volume polling,
  unauthenticated query, callMany rotator distribution)
- I8 — IPv6 prefix bucketing reveals which IPv6 buckets are
  "active" (mitigated by uniform 429 responses, /64 granularity
  has no individual-user resolution, bucket TTL)

**Denial of service (D6-D7):**
- D6 — Squatter farms exhaust the global daily ceiling
  (mitigated by Altcha PoW + RESERVED_NAMES + DICTIONARY_BRANDS +
  IPv6 /64 + IPv4 /24 prefix bucketing + persistent ceiling +
  sequential-name detector + OPERATIONS §38 diamond-hardened
  preset)
- D7 — Build manifest computation as DoS (mitigated by O(N log N)
  walk + bundle-size warning + PR-review pre-launch posture)

**Elevation of privilege (E5-E7):**
- E5 — Sock-puppet desktop pairs as a different account
  (mitigated by bundle bound to desktop's ephemeral pubkey +
  origin display in confirmation card + one-time nonce; future:
  phone origin-pinning)
- E6 — Operator-payout drainer rate-limit bypass (mitigated by
  payout queue being operator-authoritative; no public submission
  endpoint)
- E7 — CI gate bypass via branch-protection misconfiguration
  (mitigated by Forgejo branch protection + public CI status +
  reproducibility manifests; residual risk for single hostile
  maintainer documented as future threshold-multisig hardening)

### Mid-refresh corrections caught and fixed

While adding the new rows, two factual claims about the codebase
were verified against actual source and corrected before final
write:

1. **Kill-switch log event names.** Initially wrote
   `kill_switch_changed`; verified against
   `apps/relay/src/policy/killSwitch.ts` lines 116-121 — actual
   names are `kill_switch_activated` and `kill_switch_deactivated`.
   Corrected in T6 + R3.

2. **Operator-payout flow.** Initially wrote that "operator-payout
   automation transfers FROM the operator's own account TO their
   declared payout destination" without code verification; verified
   against `apps/relay/src/queue/drainer.ts` lines 283-297 (actual
   broadcast is FROM `this.config.relayAccount` with
   `this.config.relayActiveKeyWif`) and
   `apps/indexer/src/indexer/operatorEarnings.ts` lines 297-309
   (operator-payout flow is queue-based: indexer computes 90/10
   share on BLURT inflow, INSERTs row with reason
   `operator_payout:<trx_id>`, relay drainer broadcasts).
   Corrected and made line-precise in S6.

This is exactly the pattern Memory #13 ("never assume, always
verify") is meant to catch — first-pass confidence about how
the codebase works can be wrong even on familiar territory.

### Three explicitly-accepted residual risks

The Part 88 refresh surfaces three areas where the threat model
explicitly accepts the residual:

1. **Single-key compromise of @morphit's posting key** (T7 / E7) —
   recovery via corrective release op; future hardening is
   threshold-multisig at the release-signing layer.  Filed as
   long-term hardening, not pre-launch blocker.
2. **Phishing-origin homoglyphs other than RTL-override**
   (S5 / E5) — user-judgment-required; future hardening is
   phone-app origin-pinning.  Filed.
3. **Operator-host compromise** (T6, R3) — explicit operator-
   trust boundary; mitigation is federation choice, not technical
   countermeasure.  This one is by design and won't be hardened
   away.

- Matrix file: `docs/audit/2026-05-stride-matrix.md` — 865 lines
  (was 359; +506 lines for Part 88 refresh section)
- Total threat rows: **41** (24 original + 17 new)
- Net new findings: **0** — every threat analyzed has existing
  in-code mitigations re-verified at line level during the
  refresh
- Brag-list: **236 entries** (was 235; added #236 for the
  threat-model artifact + discipline)
- All other gates still green from Part 87 baseline:
  typecheck-sweep 8/0, smokes 2,075/0, tests web 545+5skip /
  relay 244 / indexer 370+1skip / ops-cli 24, lint exit 0.

### Backlog from Part 88

- **Threshold-multisig at release-signing layer** — would
  eliminate single-key-compromise scenario for @morphit's posting
  key (T7 / E7).  Substantial change to the release op handler
  + authority tracking; out of scope pre-launch.
- **Phone-app origin-pinning** — phone could maintain a list of

- **Canary signed by operator's posting key** — would close R5

  Filed.

## Part 89 (2026-05-09) — grandma-friendly closure + tsconfig + canary posting-key

This is a closure-batch part — five backlog items from Parts 87
and 88, the Tier 1.2/1.4/4.3 grandma-friendly items deferred
since Part 68, plus a separately-scoped translation pass and a
component consolidation, all in one work unit.

### Closures

**Part 87 J-3 — relay `moduleResolution` flip.**
`apps/relay/tsconfig.json` switched from `module: "NodeNext"` /
`moduleResolution: "NodeNext"` to `module: "Preserve"` /
`moduleResolution: "Bundler"`.  Rationale: NodeNext didn't
honor the `paths` map under `tsc --noEmit`, producing a primary
"Cannot find module '$xyz'" error plus a cascade (TS18046
catch-variable, TS2345 inferred-any returns, etc.).  The
`scripts/typecheck-sweep.sh` NOISE_PATTERNS contained two
clauses absorbing this: `apps/relay/(src|test)/.*: error TS18046:`
and `apps/relay/test/(create|drainer|unlock)\.test\.ts`.  Both

**Part 88 R5 — canary signs with operator's BLURT posting key.**
The PGP signature attests "this canary was signed by the holder
of THIS pgp key" but the binding from PGP key to Morphit
operator lives off-chain (`/pgp_keys.asc` on the operator's
web server, swappable at any time).  An adversary who has
compromised the operator's web server but NOT their Blurt
posting key cannot forge an on-chain attestation, because the
verifier checks the signature against the posting public key
already published in `morphit_operator_register_v1` — which is
itself signed by the posting key and can't be changed without
it.  PGP gives off-chain familiar verification; posting-key
gives chain-aware stronger guarantee.

New helper `scripts/canary/sign-with-posting-key.ts`:
- WIF via env `MORPHIT_CANARY_POSTING_WIF` (never argv — `ps`
  leak risk).
- Reads sub-content from stdin.  generate.sh produces this
  slice with `sed -n '1,/marker/p' | sed '$d'`.
- Computes `sha256(payload)` and signs via dblurt's
  `PrivateKey.sign()`.
- Outputs 3 lines: `account: ...` / `public_key: ...` /
  `signature: ...`.

Key bug fix: emits the canonical 65-byte dblurt wire format
(`Signature.toBuffer()` = `[recovery + 31] || data[64]`).
Earlier drafts emitted just the 64-byte `data` field, which
cannot be parsed by `Signature.fromBuffer()` (asserts
`buffer.length === 65`).  The 65-byte form round-trips through
`Signature.fromBuffer().recover(digest)` to return the
original public key — verified end-to-end by an off-tree
round-trip test that signs sample content, parses the
signature back via `fromBuffer`, recovers the public key, and
asserts it matches the original; AND tampers a single byte of
content and asserts the recovered public key now differs (so
verify fails as intended).

`scripts/canary/generate.sh` requires
`MORPHIT_CANARY_POSTING_WIF` (via `required` validator), runs
the sub-content slice through the signer, parses 3-line
output, and runs a second awk pass to substitute the four
posting-key placeholders into the unsigned text — then PGP
clearsign as before.

`apps/web/static/canary.txt.template` gets a new
`-----BEGIN MORPHIT POSTING-KEY ATTESTATION-----` ...
`-----END MORPHIT POSTING-KEY ATTESTATION-----` block before
the PGP signature.

`apps/web/scripts/canary-template-smoke.ts` regex widened from
`[A-Z_]+` → `[A-Z0-9_]+` on both placeholder side AND
substitution-name side; without the substitution-side
widening, `POSTING_SIG_BASE64` would silently slip through.
Required section markers extended to include the BEGIN/END
POSTING-KEY ATTESTATION pair.

`scripts/canary/verify.ts` extended to verify the posting-key
attestation: parse the block, base64-decode the signature,
assert wire length is exactly 65 bytes, parse via
`Signature.fromBuffer()`, recover via `sig.recover(digest)`
where `digest = sha256(extractSignedPayload(text))`, and
assert the recovered public key matches the declared one.
Mismatch is a hard error.  PGP-signature presence check
downgraded to warn-only because the posting-key attestation
is now the load-bearing signature.
