### `RelativeTime` component consolidation

Built `apps/web/src/lib/components/RelativeTime.svelte` to
replace four inline `formatRelativeTime` impls (three terse:
`/my/orders`, `/orderbook`, `/@account` profile; one
descriptive: `/chat`).  Two formats: `terse` (`<1m`, `5m`,
`2h`, `3d`, `4mo`, `2y`) and `descriptive` (`just now`,
`5 min ago`, `2h ago`, etc.).  60-second auto-tick via
`setInterval` + `onDestroy` so a long-mounted page stays
current rather than freezing on "just now."  NaN-safe via
`Number.isFinite(then)` — malformed ISO renders the localized
"earlier" fallback rather than "NaN months ago."  Native
`<time datetime>` for free a11y and machine-readability.
Native `title` with `toLocaleString()` absolute time, so
hovering "2h" shows the exact instant.

Locale namespace migration: `chat.inbox.relative_*` (7 keys
that lived under `chat.inbox` because the descriptive form was
originally introduced for chat) moved to
`relative_time.descriptive.*` (still 7 keys), and a parallel
`relative_time.terse.*` set added (7 keys: `lt1m`, `minutes`,
`hours`, `days`, `months`, `years`, `unknown`).  Net +7 keys
per locale: 2,243 → 2,250.  Then +48 from glossary brings the
final count to 2,298.

### Backlog filed during Part 89

- **Tier 1.4 in-context `<term>` tooltips.**  The original
  Tier 1.4 sketch envisioned a `<term>` component that
  rendered a glossary-linked term with a dotted underline and
  hover/tap tooltip surfacing the definition inline.  Part 89
  shipped the pure-page glossary first because that's the
  load-bearing piece (the page itself works as a destination
  even without inline tooltips).  The tooltip component is a
  good follow-up but not a launch blocker.

- **Posting-key signing key rotation flow.**  The Part 89
  posting-key attestation assumes the operator's posting key
  is stable.  In practice operators may rotate posting keys.
  When that happens, the previous canary will fail to verify
  against the new key.  Operators should re-broadcast
  `morphit_operator_register_v1` with the new key before
  rotating, and verifiers should consult the most recent
  register op.  This is documented behavior already, but
  worth a follow-up FAQ entry covering the rotation
  ceremony explicitly.

- **Pre-launch corner-case: empty BLURT-paid invite.**  Not
  related to Part 89 work but spotted during the dead-code
  sweep.  No action needed pre-launch — the
  invite-with-zero-cost path is intentional for first-buy
  waivers — but worth a pass at first-real-launch metrics
  review to confirm the structured logs distinguish
  zero-cost-by-design from zero-cost-by-accident.

### B — In-context glossary tooltips

**New component: `apps/web/src/lib/components/Term.svelte`**

`<Term key="fiat">word</Term>` renders the wrapped word with a
dotted-underline cue.  Hover/focus/tap surfaces a small popover
showing the glossary entry's title + body + a deep-link to
`/glossary#<key>`.  Escape-to-close + click-outside dismissal +
native `aria-describedby` for screen readers.

**Key UX call: first appearance per route only.**  Subsequent
`<Term key="fiat">` instances on the same route render as plain
text — a long page peppered with dotted underlines on every
"fiat" trains the user to ignore them.  Tracking lives in
`apps/web/src/lib/stores/glossarySeen.ts` (writable store keyed
by pathname; `markSeen` returns true on first call, false on
subsequent calls), reset on navigation by the top-level layout's
`$effect`.

**Svelte 5 quirk:** the `key` prop is captured non-reactively
via `untrack` because props don't change for a given `<Term>`
instance — each call site like `<Term key="fiat">` makes a
stable instance, and re-evaluating on key changes would be
nonsensical (different glossary term entirely).  Without
`untrack`, svelte-check trips
`state_referenced_locally` warning.

**Two real placements:**

- `<Term key="listing_fee">` wraps the "Listing fee" `<h2>`
  heading on `/post`'s fee-display section.
- Key-terms `<aside>` callout on `/run-a-node` introduces
  operator / indexer / relay / federation as inline-wrapped
  terms with prose around them.

**Restraint by design:** call sites explicitly opt-in by wrapping
individual words.  Auto-detection over rendered text was
considered and rejected — false positives on user-generated
content, locale-specific wording (the same glossary key may map
to different inflected forms per locale), and tests that would
have to mock the glossary DOM walker.

**i18n:** +1 `glossary.tooltip.open_full` key, +11
`run_a_node.key_terms.*` keys, all translated into 10 locales.

was 2,298 at Part 89 close).

### D — Category I ADR-fidelity audit

**Methodology:** read every ADR under `docs/adr/` (21 files,
~6,500 lines), identify load-bearing claims (file paths,
constants, type names, op-id strings, code locations), grep for
each claim in code, flag drift.  Spot-check rather than
exhaustive line-by-line reading — the goal is "would a developer
reading this ADR get a wrong impression about what's in code?"

**Findings:**

**I-1 — ADR-0016 phantom reference.**  ADR-0016 was the planned
slot for desktop QR pairing but was never authored; the work
shipped as ADR-0022.  Three references found:

- `docs/audit/2026-04-28-batch-i-and-adjacent-surfaces.md` line 50
- `docs/audit/2026-04-28-batch-i-and-adjacent-surfaces.md` line 444
- `docs/AUDIT-2026-05.md` line 323

The first two are historical audit artifacts, intentionally
left untouched (rewriting historical audit narratives is not
generally a good idea — they capture what the team was
thinking at audit time).  The `AUDIT-2026-05.md` reference
was active context, fixed inline:

> ...Surface NOT audited (deferred): the QR-pair desktop/mobile
> pages (landed later as ADR-0022; ADR-0016 was the planned slot
> at audit time and was never authored under that number),
> the YubiKey-enrollment UI orchestrator...

**I-2 — ADR-0003 stale "8 languages" claim.**  Section 3 of
ADR-0003 said "for all 8 languages" but the codebase supports
10 (zh-CN and zh-HK were added later).  Sitemap and locale
JSONs already at 10; only the ADR was stale.  Fixed inline:

> 3. A static `robots.txt` that allows all crawlers, and a
>    static `sitemap.xml` generated at build time with
>    `hreflang` alternates for all 10 languages (the ADR was
>    originally written when the supported set was 8; zh-CN
>    and zh-HK were added later).

**I-3 — ADR-0004 substantial body/header drift.**  Status
header: "Accepted (implemented in
`apps/indexer/src/indexer/price/`)".  Body: "Phase 3 plan (NOT
YET DECIDED; candidate)" — describing three client-side
providers (`BlurtOracleProvider`, `ApiRelayProvider`,
`DirectClientProvider`).  Actual implementation (verified in
`apps/indexer/src/indexer/price/{compositeSource,coingeckoFetcher,klingexFetcher,factory,source}.ts`
+ `apps/web/src/lib/prices/{index,types}.ts` +
`apps/web/src/lib/prices/providers/{fallback,coingecko,composite}.ts`):
indexer-side `CompositeCachedPriceSource` with
Coingecko + Klingex fetchers; frontend-side `$lib/prices/`
registry with fallback / coingecko / composite providers
(no `BlurtOracleProvider`).  The architecture is functionally
what the ADR proposed (multi-provider, swappable, privacy-first
default) but split across indexer/frontend rather than
all-frontend.  Appended Part-90 amendment to
`docs/adr/0004-price-feeds.md` reconciling shipped state.

**I-4 — ADR-0011 USD-denominated fee model superseded by
BLURT-native.**  Body described "Flat $0.25 base listing fee"
+ "$0.125 BLURT-discounted" with USD anchor at verification
time.  Actual implementation
(`apps/indexer/src/config/index.ts` line 332):
`MORPHIT_INDEXER_FEE_BASE_BLURT.default(60)`.  Indexer
`apps/indexer/src/indexer/fee.ts` doc comment explicitly says
"BLURT-native: fees are denominated directly in BLURT, not
derived from a USD anchor at verification time."  Canonical
`docs/FEES-AND-REWARDS.md` is current; ADR-0011 was stale.
Sybil multiplier table, BLURT incentive, loyalty rewards,
first-buy waiver are all preserved exactly as the ADR
specified.  Appended Part-90 amendment to
`docs/adr/0011-dynamic-fee-model.md` explaining the
simplification.

### Tier 2.1 — chat-composer account-number proofread reminder

Highest-value tier in the queue: a grandma typos her bank
account number into chat, hits Enter, and the wrong digits are
permanently encrypted on the Blurt chain.  A correction message
goes through but the wrong one is there forever — and if the
recipient ever screenshots or leaks the message, the typo is
unrecoverable.

**Why the fix is informational, not prescriptive:**

  - **Redaction is wrong** — account numbers in chat are
    LEGITIMATE.  They're how trade partners share where to
    send fiat.  Redacting would break the core trade flow.
  - **Blocking is wrong** — would punish the common case
    (most users sending account numbers WANT them through)
    to defend against an edge case (typo'd numbers).
  - **Soft reminder is right** — surface "Permanent.
    Account numbers in chat go on the Blurt chain forever.
    Proofread carefully before sending." once per session
    when the user is about to send a message containing
    account-number-shaped text.  Dismissable.  Never
    blocks.

**New module:**
`apps/web/src/lib/security/accountNumberDetector.ts`
(212 lines including doc comments).  Mirrors the
`privateKeyDetector.ts` pattern with three regex sets:

  1. **IBAN** — `/\b[A-Z]{2}[0-9]{2}[A-Z0-9]{11,30}\b/gi`.
     Country code + check digits + BBAN.  Case-insensitive
     to tolerate paste-ins.
  2. **Connected 9+-digit run** —
     `/\b[0-9]+(?:[ -][0-9]+)*\b/g` with post-processing
     filter for `digitCount >= 9`.  Tolerates space and
     hyphen separators (no backslash needed; the hyphen is
     last in the character class which is the canonical
     literal-hyphen form).  Initially I had `[ \-]` and
     ESLint flagged `no-useless-escape`; fixed to `[ -]`.
  3. **SWIFT/BIC** — `/\b[A-Z]{4}[A-Z]{2}[A-Z0-9]{2}(?:[A-Z0-9]{3})?\b/g`.
     Case-sensitive — real BICs are uppercase, lowercase
     8-char alphanumeric runs in regular prose are common
     and would false-positive otherwise.

`hasAccountNumberShape(input)` is a presence-check
convenience function with an early-exit hot path that walks
the string char-by-char counting digits-in-run.  Cheaper
than allocating the full match array when the caller only
cares about presence/absence.

**Wire into ChatComposer.svelte:**

  - New imports: `hasAccountNumberShape` from the detector,
    `browser` from `$app/environment`.
  - `ACCT_REMINDER_KEY = 'morphit.chatComposer.acctReminderSeen'`
    sessionStorage key.
  - `readAcctReminderSeen() / markAcctReminderSeen()` helpers
    with try/catch around the storage access (incognito
    quota errors).
  - `acctReminderDismissed` $state for the in-page dismissal
    + the persistent sessionStorage flag — both must be
    false for the reminder to show.
  - Derived `showAcctReminder` =
    `!acctReminderDismissed && !readAcctReminderSeen() &&
    hasAccountNumberShape(text)`.
  - `dismissAcctReminder()` writes the sessionStorage flag
    AND the in-page state simultaneously, so the reminder
    disappears immediately and stays gone the rest of the
    session.

**Inline banner UI:** amber-tinted div above the textarea
with bold heading + body + ✕ dismiss button.  Uses
`role="status"` + `aria-live="polite"` so screen readers
announce on first appearance without interrupting whatever
the user is doing.

**i18n:** 3 new keys (`chat.composer.acct_reminder.heading,
body, dismiss_aria`) × 10 locales.  Heading is short
(English: "Permanent.", German: "Endgültig.", Russian:
"Навсегда.", Chinese: "无法撤回。" / "無法撤回。"), body is
the actionable reminder.

**Permanent regression smoke** at
`apps/web/scripts/account-number-detector-smoke.ts` —
21 scenarios:

  Positive (warn fires): German IBAN, French IBAN, lowercase
  IBAN, 10-digit US bank account, 16-digit card with spaces,
  16-digit card with hyphens, SWIFT 8-char, SWIFT 11-char,
  routing+account combo, mixed IBAN+BIC, phone number with
  hyphens (intentional warn).

  Negative (warn doesn't fire): plain greeting, price
  discussion, 8-digit YYYYMMDD date, short 4-digit order
  ID, 3-word phrase that looks BIP-39-ish, lowercase 8-char
  alphanumeric (not BIC), BTC bech32 address (out of scope
  here — handled by other defenses), empty string,
  whitespace only.

Registered in `scripts/run-smokes.sh` between
`active-owner-key-invariants-smoke` and `sally-walkthrough-smoke`.
Smoke runner now 89 runners (was 88), 2,108 scenarios (was
2,086).

**Phone-numbers-trigger is intentional design:**

A 10-digit phone number with hyphens reads as a digit run
under our detector.  It would be possible to filter phone
shapes via more specific patterns (country codes, 3-3-4
grouping, etc.) but the design leans "warn more" because
the cost asymmetry is severe:

  - false positive (warn on phone number): user dismisses
    once per session.  Annoyance.
  - false negative (don't warn on account number): user
    sends typo'd account number, money lost forever.
    Catastrophe.

Documented in the module's doc comment so future
contributors don't try to "fix" this as a bug.

### Lint quirk (Part 91)

ESLint's `no-useless-escape` rule flagged my initial regex
`/\b[0-9]+(?:[ \-][0-9]+)*\b/g` because `\-` inside a
character class doesn't need the backslash — `-` only has
special meaning when between two other characters, and at
the end of a class it's a literal hyphen.  Fixed to
`/\b[0-9]+(?:[ -][0-9]+)*\b/g`.  Smoke 21/21 still passes
with the cleaner regex.

Memory: when writing regexes that include literal hyphens
inside `[]`, put the hyphen at the end of the class (or
the beginning) — no backslash needed, and ESLint won't
complain.

## Part 92 (2026-05-09) — Tier 1.3 fully closed (printable seed-backup card)

User said "everything in order" — first up: Tier 1.3 of the
grandma-friendly investigation, which had three sub-items:
copy softening (Part 90, done), printable backup card (this
part), "show me the seed again mid-quiz" (already shipped).

### Architectural decision: native browser print, no PDF library

Three candidate approaches considered for the printable card:

1. **Server-side PDF generation** (Python/reportlab via the
   pdf skill).  Rejected — the seed phrase MUST NEVER leave
   the device.  Sending it to a server, even Morphit's own
   server, breaks the core privacy invariant.  Even if the
   server immediately discarded the data after rendering,
   the network transit alone is unacceptable.

2. **Client-side PDF library** (pdf-lib, jspdf, etc.).
   Rejected — adds ~330KB to the bundle, a new audit surface
   for crypto-adjacent code (any code path that touches the
   seed needs careful review), and more cross-browser
   inconsistency than native CSS print.  PDF libraries
   often produce output that prints worse than HTML+print-CSS
   in real-world testing.

3. **Native browser print with `@media print` CSS.**  Chosen.
   Zero new dependencies, the browser handles paper-vs-PDF
   choice via its native dialog, print-to-PDF is universally
   trusted, and the user can preview before committing.

The cost of #3 is one extra click for the user (the print
dialog) — acceptable, and it doubles as a confirmation step
("the layout looks right before I commit to printing").

### Component architecture

`apps/web/src/lib/components/SeedBackupPrint.svelte`:

  - Always in the DOM.
  - Hidden on screen via `display: none` on the
    `.morphit-seed-print-card` class.
  - During print: every element on the page becomes
    `visibility: hidden`, then the seed card and its
    descendants are forced `visibility: visible`.  Hidden
    elements still occupy layout space (irrelevant — only
    at print time) but don't paint pixels.  Standard
    print-isolation idiom.
  - Triggered via an html-level class flag
    `morphit-printing-seed`, added by `triggerPrint()`
    before calling `window.print()` and removed by the
    `afterprint` event handler.
  - The `afterprint` listener is a one-shot — registered
    via `addEventListener` and immediately
    `removeEventListener`'d inside the handler, so
    repeated print clicks don't accumulate listeners.

### Why CSS visibility, not display

The standard `display: none` / `display: block` toggle
doesn't work cleanly because Svelte renders the page
content inside `<div id="svelte" style="display: contents">`
(see `apps/web/src/app.html:143`).  The `display: contents`
only affects layout, not the actual DOM tree, so a CSS
selector like `body > *:not(.morphit-seed-print-card)`
matches `<div id="svelte">` and `<noscript>` and any
siblings — without descending into the SvelteKit-rendered
tree.  The seed card itself is nested inside the
onboarding page, multiple levels deep from `<body>`.

The visibility-based pattern works regardless of nesting
depth: `* { visibility: hidden }` applies to every element
(direct or nested), and `.morphit-seed-print-card *`
overrides for descendants.  No DOM tree assumptions.

### Page format

  - 0.75-inch padding on all sides — safe for both US
    Letter and A4.
  - 11pt base text, 18pt title, 14pt monospace seed words
    with 0.5pt letter-spacing for legibility.
  - Light grey + black + amber palette (no color-printer
    dependency; the amber warning box renders fine in B&W
    via its border).
  - 12 words in a 3-column grid.  Each word numbered
    (1.-12.).  Hairline-dashed bottom border under each
    word for visual separation.  2pt solid black border
    around the grid.
  - Footer: amber-tinted warning box ("This paper IS
    your account...") plus recovery instructions.

### No QR code by design

Considered: print the seed as a QR for fast re-import.

Rejected: scanner-attack surface.  Anyone who photographs
the paper can decode the QR programmatically; paper-OCR of
hand-written words is also possible but has higher friction
than QR scanning.  Hand-written or hand-typed seed entry is
the recommended Morphit recovery flow, and matching the
printout format to that flow (numbered words in legible
text) is the right shape.

### Wiring into onboarding

`apps/web/src/routes/onboarding/+page.svelte`:

  - Import `SeedBackupPrint`.
  - Inside the seed-display block (line ~436), gated on
    `{#if showSeed}`, render the component + a small
    helper hint ("Opens your browser's print dialog. You
    can print to paper or save as PDF.").
  - Why `{#if showSeed}`: a hidden seed shouldn't be
    accidentally printable.  If the user has clicked
    "Show recovery seed" to reveal the words on screen,
    they're already in the trust posture where printing
    them is appropriate.

### Show-seed-again-mid-quiz (verified shipped)

The third Tier 1.3 sub-item.  Discovered already shipped at
`apps/web/src/routes/onboarding/+page.svelte:669-679`:

```svelte
<BusyButton
    variant="ghost"
    disabled={quizSubmitting}
    onclick={() => {
        stage = 'review';
        showSeed = true;
    }}
>
    ← {$_('onboarding.confirm.show_again')}
</BusyButton>
```

When clicked, returns to the review stage and forces
showSeed to true.  Translated across 10 locales.  Note: the
quiz indices re-randomize on the next attempt — that's the
right behavior (prevents shoulder-surfing risk on the same
positions across multiple visibility cycles).

### i18n

11 new keys × 10 locales = 110 strings.  Translations
matched register per locale:

  - **Spanish** — "Imprimir tarjeta de respaldo" /
    "Este papel ES tu cuenta."
  - **German** — "Backup-Karte drucken" / "Dieses Papier
    IST Ihr Konto."
  - **Persian** — "چاپ کارت پشتیبان" / "این کاغذ همان حساب
    شماست."
  - **Chinese (Simplified)** — "打印备份卡" / "这张纸就是您
    的账户。"

Strong language deliberately preserved across all locales:
the user is being warned that the paper IS the account,
not just a copy of it.  Softening "this paper IS your
account" to something like "this is your backup" loses the
weight of the warning.

## Part 93 (2026-05-09) — Tier 2.5 first-post starter pack

User said "everything in order" — second up: Tier 2.5 of the
grandma-friendly investigation.  The post-order form treats
every user identically, with the same defaults (90-day expiry,
blank payment-methods list, no inline guidance).  A grandma
posting her first listing has the same blank canvas as a
seasoned trader who's posted hundreds.  This part adds a
detection-and-education layer.

### Architecture decision: separate component, not in-form integration

Considered two approaches:

1. **Bake first-time detection into the post-order form
   itself.**  Conditional rendering at form-field level:
   show inline tips next to each field for first-time
   posters, hide for experienced ones.

2. **Standalone component at the top of the form.**
   Single starter-pack card with three tips, callback to
   pre-fill safer defaults.

Chose #2.  Reasons:

  - Field-level inline tips would clutter the form for
    experienced users (or require duplicated "tip-mode"
    branches throughout).
  - A standalone component is a single dismissable unit —
    the user sees it once, dismisses it, doesn't see it
    again that session, and the form below it works the
    same as always.
  - The detection logic (`getOrdersByAccount` query) lives
    in one place, not threaded through the form.
  - Easier to remove or modify later without touching the
    form's internals.

### Component architecture

`apps/web/src/lib/components/FirstPostStarterPack.svelte`:

  - Single optional callback prop:
    `onFirstTimeStatus?: (_isFirstTime: boolean) => void`.
    Fired once when status is determined.  Caller decides
    what to do with it (pre-fill defaults, log, etc.).
  - Detection: `getOrdersByAccount(viewerAccount, { limit:
    1 }).items.length === 0`.  Counts ALL orders for the
    account regardless of status — open, cancelled,
    expired, completed.  A user who previously posted and
    cancelled doesn't see the helper.
  - Per-session sessionStorage dismissal via key
    `morphit.firstPostStarterPack.dismissedThisSession`.
  - Self-hides on next mount once any historical order
    exists.  No "remind me again" path — once you've
    posted, you're past the first-impression moment.

### Why guard on form-default before pre-filling

The `onFirstTimeStatus` callback at the call site:

```svelte
<FirstPostStarterPack
    onFirstTimeStatus={(isFirstTime) => {
        if (isFirstTime && expiresDays === 90) {
            expiresDays = 7;
        }
    }}
/>
```

The `expiresDays === 90` guard is critical.  Without it:

  - A user with a saved draft that has `expiresDays = 30`
    explicitly chose 30; we'd override their intent on
    every page mount.
  - A user who manually picked 14 days, navigated away,
    and came back would see their value reset to 7.

The narrow guard means the pre-fill only fires for users
who haven't customized.  Other defaults (payment methods,
region, etc.) aren't auto-pre-filled because they require
user input — the tips card educates, doesn't decide.

This is a reusable pattern worth memorizing (Memory fact
#27): when a helper pre-fills a form value, guard on the
form's default before overriding.

### Distinct from FirstTradeHelper

A subtle but important architectural distinction.
`FirstTradeHelper` (Item 16 phase 4, Part 91-verified)
renders inside chat for users with no completed TRADES
(zero outgoing feedback).  `FirstPostStarterPack` renders
on `/post` for users with no posted ORDERS.

A user can be:

  - First-time poster + already-completed-trade: matched
    on someone else's order (chat with seller, swap
    payment+crypto, leave feedback) before ever posting
    their own.  Sees `FirstPostStarterPack` on /post but
    NOT `FirstTradeHelper` in chat.
  - First-time trader + already-posted: broadcast orders
    that nobody matched, never engaged in chat.  Sees
    `FirstTradeHelper` in chat (when they finally do
    chat) but NOT `FirstPostStarterPack` on /post.

The two helpers cover the two distinct moments without
overlap.  Don't conflate them.  Memory fact #26.

### Lint quirk (Part 93)

The new component initially had a one-warning regression
on the type-signature parameter `isFirstTime` —
ESLint's `no-unused-vars` rule complained because the
parameter is part of a function-type signature, not
actually used in the component body.  Fixed by renaming
to `_isFirstTime` per the project convention for unused
type-only parameters (same pattern used in
`Term.svelte` from Part 90).  Caller still uses the
parameter at the actual call site with whatever name they
prefer.  Back to 153 warnings.

### Tips content design

Three tips chosen for "highest-leverage advice for a
first-time poster":

  1. **Start small** — ($50 cap suggested) loss
     mitigation if anything goes wrong.  This is the
     single most important piece of advice.

  2. **7-day expiry** — pre-flipped from 90.  Stale
     offers that linger when the user has changed their
     mind are a UX papercut, not a financial risk per se,
     but they erode trust over time.

     blank-canvas confusion ("what do I put here?").
     Starter examples (PayPal, Wise, bank transfer, cash
     in person) cover ~80% of common cases without
     deciding for the user.

Plus a deep link to the full first-trade walkthrough FAQ.

The card uses 🌱 (sprout) emoji for the heading — light
visual marker that this is friendly orientation, not a
warning.  Green tint reinforces the same.  Different from
the amber tint of `accountNumberDetector`'s reminder
banner (which IS a warning).

## Part 94 (2026-05-09) — Tier 3.3 number/date format consistency

User said "everything in order" — third up: Tier 3.3 of the
grandma-friendly investigation.  The codebase had 35+ call
sites mixing `.toFixed()`, `.toLocaleString()`, and ad-hoc
`Intl.NumberFormat` invocations with no central pattern.  A
grandma in Germany sees inconsistent number formats across
the same UI session.

### What changed

New module `apps/web/src/lib/i18n/formatters.ts` (~210 lines)
exports seven helpers: `formatUsd`, `formatPercent`,
`formatBlurt`, `formatCount`, `formatDateLong`,
`formatDateMedium`, `formatDateTime`.  Reads the active locale
from svelte-i18n's `locale` store at call time; falls back to
`'en'` in SSR / smoke contexts where the store isn't
initialized.

`Intl.NumberFormat` and `Intl.DateTimeFormat` instances cached
per `(locale, options)` tuple via a small `Map`.  Bounded —
one entry per locale × format kind, so memory stays tiny on
long-running pages.

### Migrated call sites (4)

  - `StrangerFeeModal.svelte` — chat-stranger-fee USD
    preview.
  - `/post` — listing-fee USD preview.
  - `apr.ts:formatApr` — BLURT vesting APR display.
  - `balanceMath.ts:formatPercentage` — MANA-percentage
    display.

### Deliberately NOT migrated (3)

  - `priceModelDisplay.ts`'s local `formatPercent` — bespoke
    trailing-zero stripping for orderbook line density.
  - Rating displays (`weighted_rating.toFixed(1)`) — single-
    decimal star ratings are conventional cross-locale.
  - File-size displays (`(n / 1024).toFixed(1)} KB`) — out
    of normal user surface.

### Two architectural learnings

**Cross-workspace imports avoid `$lib` aliases.**  My first
attempt routed `apr.ts` through `import { formatPercent }
from '$lib/i18n/formatters'`.  Worked in SvelteKit but broke
3 backend smokes (`apps/indexer/scripts/apr-smoke.ts`,
`balance-math-smoke.ts`, `pnl-smoke.ts`) which import
`apr.ts` and `balanceMath.ts` for unit coverage.  Pure tsx
in `apps/indexer` can't resolve the `$lib` alias of
`apps/web`.  Fixed by switching to relative paths
(`../i18n/formatters`).  Memory fact #28.

**Centralization must preserve historical behavior exactly.**
My first `formatPercent` set `minimumFractionDigits: 0,
maximumFractionDigits: 2` — produced `'7.5%'` where the
shipped behavior was `'7.50%'` (via `.toFixed(2)`).  Three
smokes broke on the regression.  Fixed by setting
`min=max=fractionDigits` to preserve the 2-decimal padding.
If we want non-padded output later, that's a separate
deliberate change with the smokes updated in the same commit.
Memory fact #29.

### Why direct svelte-i18n locale store

`apps/web/src/lib/i18n/index.ts` imports `$app/environment`
for `browser` detection (line 1).  Smoke contexts (and any
pure-Node tooling) can't resolve `$app/...` aliases, so
importing `currentLocale` from `./index` would lock the
formatters out of test environments.  Reading `locale`
directly from `svelte-i18n` keeps the formatters portable.
`DEFAULT_LOCALE = 'en'` is duplicated locally — narrow,
intentional duplication for portability across SSR,
SvelteKit-bundled, and pure-Node smoke contexts.  Memory
fact #30.

### New regression smoke

`apps/web/scripts/i18n-formatters-smoke.ts` — 16 scenarios:

  - `formatUsd` — "1234.5 contains 1234", zero, NaN,
    Infinity (graceful degradation).
  - `formatPercent` — "1.5 contains digit and %", APR-
    style 7.6 with fractionDigits=1, NaN.
  - `formatBlurt` — 60 with 3 decimals, 0.001 precision,
    60 with zero decimals.
  - `formatCount` — 1234 has digits no decimal.  (Initial
    test had a regex bug — `/[.,]\d{1,3}$/` on "1,234"
    matches the thousands separator; fixed by stripping
    non-digit chars and equality-comparing the digit
    string.)
  - `formatDateLong` / `formatDateMedium` / `formatDateTime`
    — non-empty output, year/time presence, invalid input
    returns "—".
  - Sanity: works without an initialized locale store.

Registered in `scripts/run-smokes.sh`.  Smoke runner now
2,128 scenarios across 90 runners (was 2,111 / 89).

## Part 95 (2026-05-09) — Tier 3.5 printable cheat-sheet

User said "everything in order" — fourth up: Tier 3.5 of the
grandma-friendly investigation.  A grandma using Morphit
needs a paper reference for the four concept-pairs she keeps
mixing up.  Now shipped at `/cheat-sheet`.

### Architecture: reuse, don't reinvent

The cheat-sheet is print-bound static content.  Same problem
shape as the seed-backup card from Part 92.  Solution: reuse
the visibility-based print-isolation pattern verbatim.

The Part 92 pattern is:

  1. Component renders TWO things: an on-screen UI (button,
     intro text) and a hidden printable element (always in
     DOM, `display: none` on screen).
  2. Click handler adds a specific html-class flag to
     `<html>` (e.g. `morphit-printing-seed`,
     `morphit-printing-cheatsheet`).
  3. `@media print` block scoped under that flag: every
     element becomes `visibility: hidden`, then the
     printable element and its descendants are forced
     `visibility: visible`.
  4. The printable element is `position: absolute; inset: 0`
     to fill the print page.
  5. `requestAnimationFrame` defers the `window.print()`
     call so the class application paints first.
  6. `afterprint` event handler removes the class — fires
     whether the user printed or canceled.

This is a robust, generic pattern.  Memory fact #31:
specific html-class flag per printable artifact so multiple
printable surfaces can coexist on the same page without
interfering.  E.g., a future "print this transaction
receipt" feature would use `morphit-printing-receipt`,
not pollute `morphit-printing-seed`.

### What's on the cheat-sheet

Four sections, deliberately chosen to cover the highest-
confusion concept-pairs from the grandma investigation:

**Section 1 — Account name vs seed phrase vs password.**
The single most-confused triplet.  A grandma will say "my
password is twelve words" or "I lost my account name."
Three paired explanations make the distinction visible:

  - Account name: public, others see it, costs ~3 BLURT
    once-and-permanent.
  - Seed phrase: 12 words, the recovery secret, paper
    only.
  - Password: per-device, encrypts the seed in this
    browser, forgettable because the seed is the
    recovery path.

**Section 2 — Listing fee vs network fee vs trade
payment.**  Equally confused.  Users blame Morphit for
miner fees they paid directly to the chain, or expect
Morphit to refund a trade payment they sent off-platform.
Three paired explanations clarify the boundary:

  - Listing fee: ~60 BLURT, what Morphit charges to
    publish.  First buy free.
  - Network fee: BTC/XMR miner fees, NOT Morphit's,
    varies, comes from the user's own wallet.
  - Trade payment: the actual money, buyer to seller,
    off-platform — Morphit never touches it.

**Section 3 — BTC vs XMR vs BLURT.**  Three explanations
covering the three asset roles: Bitcoin (most known,
public ledger), Monero (privacy choice), BLURT (the chain
Morphit runs on, the protocol fee asset).

**Section 4 — If something goes wrong.**  Four numbered
scenarios with actionable steps.  Deliberately blunt
register — "Lost the seed phrase? There is no recovery
path. Morphit has no copy."  Memory fact #32: do NOT
soften this section.  A grandma reaching for the sheet in
a panic needs the truth fast.

### What's NOT on the cheat-sheet

  - **No QR code.**  Same logic as `SeedBackupPrint`:
    the cheat-sheet doesn't contain user-keyed data, so
    a QR would just encode the URL — pointless.  And QR
    codes on paper invite scanner workflows that grandmas
    don't have.
  - **No version stamp / no provenance.**  This is
    reference material that ages well.  If a copy is 6
    months old, it's still correct (none of the concept
    distinctions change).  Adding a version stamp would
    invite "is this still current?" panic for no
    benefit.
  - **No user data.**  Anyone can print the cheat-sheet,
    signed in or not.  No account name, no balance, no
    seed.  Just the reference content.

### Layout (US Letter / A4)

Tighter than the seed-backup card because there's more
content:

  - 0.5-inch padding (vs 0.75-inch for `SeedBackupPrint`).
  - 9pt base text; 16pt title; 11pt section headers with
    light-grey background bars.
  - Two-column rows for paired definitions (1.4-inch label
    column + flex body column).
  - Hairline-dashed bottom border under each row.
  - 4-section vertical layout fits one page in all 10
    locales.

### i18n breakdown

37 new keys × 10 locales = 370 strings.  Persian and
Chinese translations match the same blunt register as
English in section 4: "Morphit کپی ندارد" (Persian:
"Morphit has no copy"), "Morphit 没有副本" (Simplified
Chinese: "Morphit has no copy"), preserving truth-fast
posture in every language.

Persian uses LRM-flipped grouping where the bullet symbols
flow correctly in RTL context.  Chinese-Simplified and
Chinese-Traditional differ in 8 character pairs (e.g.
打印/列印 for "print", 助记词/助記詞 for "seed phrase") —
both translations done by hand, not auto-converted.

### Footer wiring

`apps/web/src/routes/+layout.svelte` lines 519-524: added
`/cheat-sheet` link in the footer next to `/glossary`.
The two routes form a natural pair (glossary = word
definitions, cheat-sheet = concept distinctions).

## Part 96 (2026-05-09) — Memory #11 Category M operator-facing docs fidelity

User said "everything in order" — fifth and final scheduled
item: Memory #11 audit campaign Category M.  Walked the four
operator-facing docs (API.md, OPERATIONS.md, RUN-A-MORPHIT-
NODE.md, SECURITY.md) end-to-end against code.  ~8,800 lines
of doc against ~120 v1 endpoints + ~108 documented env vars
+ port references + crypto primitives.

This part is **audit-class internal/process work** — no brag
list entry per Memory #15.  Precedent: Part 90 Category I
(ADR fidelity) closed the same way.  The fixes themselves
are user-meaningful (operators reading the docs get correct
information) but the audit-class wrap-up isn't a public
selling point.

### 8 fixes applied

**M-1 — API.md `/v1/featured` URL drift.**  Documented at
`/v1/featured`, actually mounted at `/v1/orderbook/featured`
(`apps/indexer/src/main.ts:178`).  Real public-API drift —
documented URL returns 404.  Fixed inline.

**M-2 — API.md `/v1/listing-fee` response shape.**  Listed
`fee_recipient` (actually on `/v1/instance`) and
`fee_tolerance` (config-only, not surfaced on any HTTP
response).  Missing `quote_ttl_seconds: 300`.  Fixed inline
with explanatory note about the misplaced `fee_recipient`.

**M-3 — API.md `/v1/instance` response shape (significant).**
Listed `operator_account` (doesn't exist), missing
`fee_recipient`, `operator_tag`, `seo`.  `alt_networks.i2p`
was the old single-field shape; code now has
`i2p_b32`/`i2p_name` split.  Rewrote response example with
explanatory paragraphs.

**M-4 — API.md `/v1/health` response shape.**  Listed
`lag_sec` (not in code), missing `uptime_sec`,
`chain_head_block`, `stale`.  Status enum documented as
`{ok, degraded, down}` but `down` returns 503 instead of
a body.  Fixed inline.

**M-5 — OPERATIONS.md USD-anchored fee model.**  Three
doc-only env vars reflected the pre-ADR-0011-amendment model
that was simplified out (Part 90):
`MORPHIT_INDEXER_FEE_BASE_USD`,
`_LISTING_FEE_AMORTIZATION_FACTOR`,
`_LISTING_FEE_OPERATIONAL_MARGIN_BLURT`.  Fixed in two
places: the fee runbook section + the FEE_BASE_USD config
section, both now describing the BLURT-native model
(`MORPHIT_INDEXER_FEE_BASE_BLURT`, default 60).

**Port placeholder clarification (OPERATIONS.md).**  The
verification-procedure curl used `:8080/v1/health` —
technically not wrong since the surrounding text says
"replacing 8080 with the indexer or relay listen port", but
8080 is the relay default and `/v1/health` is on the
indexer.  Replaced with a `<PORT>` placeholder + clarifying
sentence about which default is which.

**M-6 — RUN-A-MORPHIT-NODE.md wrong port for /v1/operators.**
Earnings curl pointed at `localhost:8080/v1/operators/yourtag`,
but `/v1/operators` is on the indexer (default 8081), not
relay (default 8080).  An operator running it literally
gets connection refused or hits the wrong app.  Fixed to
`8081` + parenthetical naming both defaults.

**M-7 — SECURITY.md crypto-primitives table missing keystore
AEAD row.**  Table listed chat AEAD (ChaCha20-Poly1305) and
password KDF (Argon2id) but had no row for the keystore's
storage encryption.  Keystore actually uses BOTH Argon2id
(KDF) AND `crypto_secretbox_easy` (XSalsa20-Poly1305 AEAD)
— two distinct primitives.  Added the keystore AEAD row +
explanatory paragraph distinguishing chat AEAD
(`crypto_aead_chacha20poly1305_ietf_*`) from keystore AEAD
(`crypto_secretbox_*`).

**M-8 — SECURITY.md display-name spoofing mitigation named
the wrong mechanism.**  Doc said the UI "renders the
truncated posting public key next to the name (e.g. `Sally
Doe (BLT7gHu8mn…A9bb)`)".  Actual mitigation is the
project's `IdentityLabel` component, which renders an
**identicon** (deterministic visual hash from identity
bytes) next to every username — verified at
`apps/web/src/lib/components/IdentityLabel.svelte` lines
1-43.  The pubkey-truncation approach was either earlier
intent or never shipped.  Fixed to describe identicons +
cite the IdentityLabel component policy ("no render site
ever writes raw `@{account}`").

### Findings considered but NOT real drift

- 4 `*_FILE` env vars in OPERATIONS.md — explicitly flagged
  as "not yet implemented" in a 2026-05-06 caveat block.
  Doc honest about the gap.
- 11 indexer endpoints undocumented in API.md
  (login-pairing, profiles, chat-identity, conversations,
  chat-read-state, blocks, chat-admission,
  stranger-fee-quote, activity, instance/payment-methods,
  operator-blocks).  All internal Morphit-client surface,
  not public third-party API.  API.md is explicitly
  public-API scoped; this is intentional.
- `MORPHIT_OPERATOR_CONFIG_FILE` — lives in
  `packages/operator-config`, not `apps/`.  My initial
  scan was scoped too narrowly.
- `MORPHIT_RELAY_ORIGIN` — frontend-build constant in
  `apps/web/src/lib/net/config.ts`, not a runtime env var.
  Doc context correctly notes "in your frontend build
  environment".
- `MORPHIT_INDEXER_DB_PASSWORD` — used by
  `ops/postgres/init.sql` as a one-shot DB-init env var.
  Doc accurately scoped.
- `MORPHIT_RELAY_WEEKLY_ACT_COUNT` — exists in
  `apps/relay/scripts/mint-acts.ts`, not the main relay
  src dir.  Initial scan missed; no drift.

### Workflow lessons codified

The audit produced three new memory facts:

**#33 — Cross-workspace env-var audit must scan ALL
workspaces.**  `apps/*/`, `packages/*`, `ops/`, `scripts/` —
not just the obvious src dirs.  In Part 96 I initially
flagged 11 doc-only env vars as drift; after broadening the
scan, only 3 were real drift.  The other 8 were legitimately
elsewhere or honestly disclosed as not-yet-implemented.

**#34 — ADR amendments need an operator-docs checklist.**
ADR-0011's BLURT-native amendment (Part 90) propagated to
OPERATIONS.md only in this part — six parts later.  Future
ADR amendments should include a checklist of operator-facing
docs to update at the same time, so amendments don't leave
operator docs stale for months.  In retrospect, Part 90's
amendment should have flagged OPERATIONS.md sections
referencing the USD-anchored model as needing update.

**#35 — SECURITY.md identity-related claims must grep
component names.**  The display-name spoofing description
named the wrong mechanism (truncated pubkey instead of
identicon).  Future SECURITY.md edits touching identity-
related claims should grep `apps/web/src/lib/components`
for the actual component name before describing the
mechanism.

## Part 97 (2026-05-09) — Tier 2.6 identity-label policy enforced

The pre-planned "everything in order" sequence finished at
Part 96.  User said "keep goin'" so I picked the next-
highest-value open item from the Part 96 TARBALL backlog
list — Tier 2.6, the avatar-identicon concern — because it
is the natural follow-on to Part 96's M-8 fix that
established the identity-label policy authoritatively in
SECURITY.md.

### Re-framed scope

The original Tier 2.6 spec proposed that "the avatar
identicon is intimidating" to grandmas and suggested making
the "edit display name" affordance more discoverable.

Part 96's M-8 fix clarified that identicons are
non-negotiable per project policy.  The IdentityLabel
docstring at `apps/web/src/lib/components/IdentityLabel.svelte`
lines 1-43 documents the rationale: identicons are the
cheapest accessibility win Morphit ships (zero user effort,
zero bandwidth, zero privacy cost), and they're the
spoofing counter-measure for typosquats like `@morphit` vs
`@morph1t` (those collide textually but identicons cannot).
Replacing identicons with photos or initials would cost
privacy, cost bandwidth, or cost the spoofing protection.

So the actionable Tier 2.6 fix splits into:

  1. Audit that the project's "no raw `@{account}` without
     an identicon" policy is consistently applied across
     the codebase (closes the audit-compliance side of the
     M-8 finding).

  2. Make the user's own identicon prominently visible to
     the user themselves, so grandma can associate "the
     abstract pattern" with "me."  Solves the original
     grandma concern indirectly: once she sees her own
     identicon attached to her own account name in
     settings, she understands what the patterns mean.

### The audit (1)

Regex sweep over `apps/web/src/routes` and
`apps/web/src/lib/components` for the pattern
`@\{[a-zA-Z]+\}` (raw `@{account}` interpolations).  5
findings.

**3 in code-rendered context, all in
`apps/web/src/routes/settings/+page.svelte`.  All three
fixed:**

- Line 886 — user's OWN account name in settings.  No
  spoofing surface (user viewing self), but the fix is
  the own-identicon Tier 2.6 grandma payoff.

- Line 1581 — hidden-accounts list.  Real spoofing
  protection gap.  "I hid `@morphit`, but I might unhide
  `@morph1t` thinking it's the same user."

- Line 1669 — blocked-accounts list.  Same problem, more
  critical for safety.  "Did I block the right person?
  Or did I block the spoof and the real attacker is
  unblocked?"

All three replaced with `<IdentityLabel>` (already
imported by the file).  Settings line 886 uses
`weight="bold" avatarSize={40} showCopy={false}` for the
own-account hero card; lines 1581 and 1669 use
`weight="semibold" showCopy={false}` for the list rows.

**2 in acceptable-exception context, documented in the
smoke's allow-list:**

- `SeedBackupPrint.svelte:138` — print-only output of
  the user's OWN seed backup.  User viewing self (no
  spoofing surface), identicons add no value on paper,
  the card is intentionally minimal.  Documented in the
  smoke's `ACCEPTED_FILES` set with comment.

- `explorer/account/[name=account]/+page.svelte:304` —
  profile-page hero `<h1>@{account}</h1>`.  Already
  renders a 64px identicon adjacent (lines 298-302).
  This is exactly the case the IdentityLabel docstring
  describes as warranting `hideAvatar` if used —
  wrapping in IdentityLabel would either duplicate the
  avatar or require the larger version to be discarded.

**Comment-context references** (not real renders, ignored
by the smoke's `lineIsCodeRender` heuristic):

- `IdentityLabel.svelte` itself — quotes the rule.
- `publish.ts` — JSDoc reference to a syndication
  template expanded server-side.
- Various JSDoc URL pattern descriptions like
  `/@{account}/{permlink}` explaining route arg shapes.

### Memory facts codified

**#36 — IdentityLabel policy has 2 documented acceptable
exceptions.**  Print-only user-self contexts (no
spoofing surface, paper output) and profile-page heroes
(adjacent larger identicon already rendered).  Future
exceptions must be added to the smoke's allow-list with
a comment justifying why.

**#37 — Render the user's own identicon even when no
spoofing surface.**  Grandma-recognition payoff: the
visual association ("the abstract pattern is me") is
established at the surface where she's already looking
at her own identity.  Tier 2.6 grandma concern resolved
indirectly via familiarity rather than mechanism
replacement.

**#38 — apps/web/scripts smokes are ESM, use
fileURLToPath(import.meta.url).**  My initial smoke crashed
with "ReferenceError: __dirname is not defined in ES module
scope."  Pattern fixed inline; future smokes should follow
the ESM pattern from the start.

### New regression smoke

`apps/web/scripts/identity-label-policy-smoke.ts` walks all
`.svelte` and `.ts` files in the route + component dirs,
scans for raw `@{...}` patterns, ignores comment-context
matches, and ignores the documented allow-list.  6
scenarios:

  1. No raw `@{...}` renders outside accepted-exception
     files.
  2. IdentityLabel imported in settings.
  3. IdentityLabel renders in hidden-accounts list (regex
     anchored to the `{#each hiddenList...}` loop).
  4. IdentityLabel renders in blocked-accounts list.
  5. IdentityLabel renders for the user's own account in
     settings.
  6. Allow-list non-empty (sanity).

Smoke runner now 2,135 scenarios across 91 runners (was
2,129 / 90).  Triple-pulse 3-for-3 stable.

## Part 98 (2026-05-09) — Tier 2.3 onboarding review-stage back button

User said "keep goin'" so I picked the next-highest-value
open item from the Part 97 TARBALL backlog list — Tier 2.3,
the missing back button on `/onboarding`'s multi-step flow.

### Stage analysis identified one real gap

`/onboarding` has stages `choose → generating → review →
confirm → done`.  Auditing each transition for a
back-button gap:

- `confirm → review` — already shipped (Part 92's "Show
  again" button).  Re-show the seed for additional
  write-down attempts.
- `generating → choose` — implicit via the error fallback;
  stage runs <600ms (per Tier 4.3 minimum-visibility
  floor) so a back button would flash.
- `done → anywhere` — forbidden (chain state already
  written, keystore on disk, identity bootstrapped).
- `review → choose` — **the gap.**  User has just seen
  the seed, path-picker explanations are no longer in
  view, switching path mid-flow requires the browser back
  button.

So the actionable fix is one back button, in the review
stage, that returns to `choose`.

### Key-handling contract drove the implementation

Going back from `review` MUST wipe the in-memory key
material per the project's contract (SECURITY.md "Key
handling contract" section, finding K1.2, finding O2.1).
Specifically:

- `full: FullIdentity | null` carries `seedBytes` (16-byte
  BIP-39 entropy as a `Uint8Array`) and four keypair
  private keys.
- `live: LiveIdentity | null` carries `posting.privateKey`
  and (when present) `memo.privateKey` — independent
  allocations from `full`'s keypairs.

The codebase already exposes `wipeFullIdentity` and
`wipeLiveIdentity` helpers
(`apps/web/src/lib/crypto/keygen.ts:519-537`), and
onboarding already imported both.  Two existing call sites
already used them (post-keystore-write cleanup near line
221, abandon-on-leave cleanup at `onConfirmLeave` ~line
310).  Part 98 added the third: the new
`confirmRestartFromReview()` handler with the same
wipe-both-then-null-both shape.

### Why a confirmation modal

The user just generated 12 random words they were asked
to write down.  A misclick on the back button that
silently discards them would feel like data loss, and
regenerating costs ~600ms minimum (the Tier 4.3 spinner-
visibility floor).  A confirmation modal is justified.

The codebase already has `ConfirmModal` (used by
`onConfirmLeave` for the abandon-on-leave flow).  Part 98
adds a second `ConfirmModal` block at the bottom of the
page bound to a new `pendingRestartFromReview` boolean
state.

### Confirmation copy is deliberately blunt

```
Discard this seed and start over?

Going back will discard the seed phrase you just
generated.  The 12 words will be wiped from this device.
If you've already written them down somewhere, you'll
want to destroy that copy too — it won't unlock anything
anymore.

[Yes, discard and start over]    [Stay here]
```

Three things the copy does that softer copy wouldn't:

- **Names the operation:** "Discard this seed and start
  over."  Not "Are you sure?", not "Going back will lose
  your progress."  Memory fact #40: confirmation-modal
  copy on destructive identity-loss flows must explicitly
  remind the user about their paper backup.  A grandma
  who already wrote the seed down might think "discard"
  here is harmless because she has a copy.  She doesn't —
  the discarded seed is the only one that ever unlocked
  anything.

- **Cancel button is a noun:** "Stay here," not "Cancel."
  Memory fact #41: easier to scan when adrenaline is
  elevated and the modal text was a surprise.

- **Confirm button names the action:** "Yes, discard and
  start over."  Confirms the request rather than just
  "Yes" or "OK."

### UI restructure

The previous review-stage actions row was a single line
with status text on the left and the primary continue on
the right.  Restructured to a two-row layout: status text
on top, both buttons (back left, continue right) on the
bottom — matching the visual register of Part 92's "Show
again" button in the confirm stage.

### Memory facts codified

**#39 — onboarding review→choose wipes both `full` and
`live` and nulls both refs.**  Same K1.2/O2.1 pattern as
the abandon-on-leave cleanup and the post-keystore-write
cleanup.  Future state-machine changes that add new
"discard the unsaved identity" transitions must use the
same pattern.

**#40 — destructive identity-loss confirmation must
remind about paper backup.**  Naming the consequence
("destroy that copy too — it won't unlock anything
anymore") is load-bearing because grandma-mental-model
("I have a copy on paper") doesn't apply to chain
identity.

**#41 — confirmation-modal cancel labels are nouns, not
verbs.**  "Stay here", not "Cancel."

### New regression smoke

`apps/web/scripts/onboarding-back-button-smoke.ts` parses
the onboarding source and asserts 15 structural
invariants.  Catches the regression class where someone
refactors the back-button flow and forgets the wipe.

The smoke uses a small `functionBody(source, name)` helper
that finds a function declaration by name and returns its
brace-balanced body, so per-call assertions don't deal
with whitespace fragility.

ESM-compatible per Memory fact #38:
`fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)` for `__dirname`.

Smoke runner now 2,150 scenarios across 92 runners (was
2,135 / 91).  Triple-pulse 3-for-3 stable.

## Part 99 (2026-05-09) — Tier 3.2 user preferences store

User said "keep goin'" after Part 98 closed Tier 2.3.  I
picked Tier 3.2 — the last open Tier 3 grandma-friendly
item — because it's a real-feature addition (new state
surface, persistence, multi-page integration) rather than
another audit category.  After Part 99, all Tier 1, Tier 2,
and Tier 3 items in the grandma-friendly investigation are
either shipped or closed-by-audit.

### Scoping decision: which preferences

The Tier 3.2 spec named three candidates: fiat, region,
and language.

- **Language** — already handled.  The locale switcher
  exists at the layout level, persists to
  `morphit.locale` in localStorage, and svelte-i18n loads
  the right dictionary on next page render.  Not part of
  this Part.

- **Region** — used by `/post` for filtering trade
  visibility ("Global", "US", "EU", etc.).  Defaults to
  empty string per the form's initial state.  Reasonable
  to remember.

- **Fiat currency** — used by `/post` for the price-in-
  fiat field.  Defaults to empty string.  Same logic.

So Part 99 ships fiat + region.  Future preferences can
be added to the same store without schema bump as long as
they're optional with empty-default semantics; an
incompatible schema change would bump the localStorage key
suffix (`v1` → `v2`).

### Privacy is the load-bearing property

Stored preferences MUST stay local.  Specifically:

- Never broadcast in any chain op (so the on-chain
  history can't be data-mined for "who buys USD" patterns
  cross-account).
- Never sent to indexer or relay (so an operator can't
  build a per-user fiat-preference index).
- Never logged or telemetry-tracked (Morphit doesn't have
  telemetry in the first place, but the constraint is
  documented for future contributors).

The store's docstring restates this commitment so a
future maintainer adding a new preference doesn't
accidentally start syncing them.  Memory fact #42:
network-syncable values don't belong in this store —
open a different mechanism.

### Empty-state cleanliness matters

A subtle but real concern: localStorage entries are
visible in the browser DevTools, persist across sessions
in non-private browsing, and are part of the user's
visible surface area.  An entry like
`morphit.userPreferences.v1 → {"fiat":"","region":""}`
is noise to a user who's never set any preference but is
peeking at their site data.

The fix: when both keys are empty,
`writeToStorage(EMPTY)` calls `localStorage.removeItem`
instead of `setItem(JSON.stringify(EMPTY))`.  Same
end-state at read time (both yield empty), but the
former leaves localStorage tidy.

### Graceful failure modes

Every reader and writer is wrapped in `try {} catch {}`.
The catch arms are deliberately empty — no logging, no
toast, no fallback retry — because preferences are
best-effort UX polish, not user-data integrity.  A
broken localStorage shouldn't surface as an error to the
user; it should silently fall back to "no preferences
saved" and let the form work.

Failure modes covered (all in the regression smoke):

- localStorage unavailable (private browsing, certain
  embedded contexts).
- Quota exceeded.
- Malformed JSON in storage.
- Parsed value is not an object.
- Object with wrong field types.
- Object with unknown extra fields (forward-compat for
  v2 fields read by v1 code).

### Wiring layers

`/post` integration uses three precedence tiers for form
field initialization, ordered from most-specific to
most-general:

1. **Saved draft restore.**  If a half-composed draft
   exists at `localStorage.morphit.compose.v2`, restore
   it.  Wins over everything.

2. **Session-storage prefill.**  If the user clicked
   "Re-list this order" on `/my/orders` or "Top up BLURT"
   on a profile page, those flows write to sessionStorage
   under `PREFILL_KEY`.  This part fills any field the
   draft didn't.

3. **Persisted preferences.** (NEW Part 99.)  Reads from
   `localStorage.morphit.userPreferences.v1` and fills
   any STILL-empty field.  Doesn't override anything the
   first two tiers set.

Memory fact #44: pre-fill from a persisted store runs
LAST and ONLY fills empty fields.  This is the same
"guard on form default before overriding" pattern as
Part 93's `FirstPostStarterPack` (Memory #27), generalized
to localStorage-backed stores.

The post-success persist step uses a small helper
`persistPreferencesAfterSuccess()` called at both the
waived/BTC/XMR success path (~line 1015) and the BLURT-paid
success path (~line 1110), right after `clearDraft()`.
Only persists non-empty values so an order with empty
fiat (which the form's submit gate disallows, but
defense in depth) doesn't overwrite a previously-set
preference.

### `/settings` integration

A new "Preferences" section between the existing
blocked-accounts section and the session-control section.
Two-state UI:

- **Empty state** — when neither field is set: a single
  paragraph explaining "No preferences saved yet. Post
  an order and your fiat currency and region will be
  remembered for next time."
- **Populated state** — a `<dl>` showing each non-empty
  field as a label + value row, plus a destructive
  "Clear preferences" button below.

The clear button uses the same two-step inline-confirm
pattern as the existing "Unhide all" / "Sign out"
confirms — toggle to an amber `role="alertdialog"` block
with body text and "Yes, clear" / "Keep them" buttons.
No modal; matches the rest of settings.

Cancel button is a noun ("Keep them") not a verb
("Cancel") per Memory fact #41 from Part 98.

### Memory facts codified

**#42 — preferences store is local-first; never syncs.**
Future preferences added must preserve that property.

**#43 — localStorage-backed stores must use versioned
keys + try/catch reads/writes.**  `v1` suffix lets future
schema changes bump without collision; try/catch yields
empty state silently rather than crashing.

**#44 — form pre-fill from a persisted store runs AFTER
more-specific sources and ONLY fills empty fields.**
Generalization of Memory #27.

### New regression smoke

`apps/web/scripts/user-preferences-smoke.ts` covers 12
scenarios across the localStorage contract.  Uses an
in-memory `MemoryStorage` shim and inline-replicates the
read/write helpers — testing the stored format, not the
Svelte-store-subscription layer (which is covered by
svelte-check + locale-parity smoke).

Smoke runner now 2,163 scenarios across 93 runners (was
2,150 / 92).  Triple-pulse 3-for-3 stable.

**All Tier 1, Tier 2, Tier 3 grandma-friendly items

grandma-friendly item.  All Tier 1 / 2 / 3 of the grandma-
friendly investigation is now shipped or closed.  I picked
Memory #11 Category N — accessibility audit — because (a)
it's the natural follow-on to finishing the grandma campaign
(a11y is the structural extension of "make this work for
grandmas"), and (b) Parts 98 and 99 just added two new
ConfirmModal call sites, so it's a good moment to verify
that the modal pattern is a11y-correct across the codebase.

This part is **audit-class internal/process work** — same
treatment as Parts 90 (Category I — ADR fidelity) and 96
(Category M — operator-docs fidelity).  Mixed character:
includes real runtime changes that help screen-reader users
hear validation errors and broadcast success that they
previously didn't, but framed as a structural audit and the
sighted-user-visible behavior is unchanged.  No brag-list
entry per Memory #15.

### Methodology

The project baseline is already a11y-clean for svelte-
check's standard rules (0 a11y warnings, 205 existing
aria-* references in components — that's not a low bar).
So this audit focused on patterns svelte-check doesn't
catch:

- Structural focus management on dialogs.
- Screen-reader announcements on state transitions
  (route-level phase changes that aren't navigation).
- Form-field error-association wiring (aria-invalid +
  aria-describedby).

### 4 fixes applied

**N-1 — ConfirmModal title not exposed via aria-labelledby.**
Native `<dialog>` doesn't auto-associate child headings.
Without explicit wiring, screen readers may announce the
dialog as just "dialog."  Fixed by generating a per-instance
`titleId` (crypto.randomUUID with fallback), wiring
`aria-labelledby={titleId}` on `<dialog>`, and adding
`id={titleId}` to the `<h2>` heading.  Memory fact #45.

**N-2 — `/post` success phase missing aria-live.**  The
post-order form has phases composing → review →
broadcasting → success / error.  Broadcasting and error
phases were correctly wired; success was not.  A
screen-reader user who broadcast an order would hear the
broadcasting message, then silence.  Fixed by adding
`aria-live="polite" role="status"` to the success-phase
section.  Memory fact #47.

**N-3 — `/post` form-field errors not associated with
inputs.**  Of the 6 warn-level StatusLines, only one input
(txid) had aria-invalid + aria-describedby wiring.  The
other 5 — fiat, amount min, amount max, spread price, fixed
price, payment methods — had visible-only error indication.
Fixed by adding `aria-invalid={!!fieldError}` and
`aria-describedby={fieldError ? 'field-id' : undefined}` to
the inputs, plus matching `id` on the StatusLines.  The
`aria-describedby` is conditional so the input doesn't
reference a non-existent element when there's no error —
pointing to a missing ID is itself an a11y bug.  Memory
fact #46.

**N-4 — `/post/edit` form-field errors not associated.**
Same pattern as N-3, applied to the edit page.  Used
`edit-` prefix on IDs to distinguish from the `/post`
page (defense against future routes ever rendering both
in the same DOM).

### Findings considered but NOT real drift

- Skip-link in layout (already wired, `<a href="#main">` +
  `<main id="main">`).
- ToastRegion (already has `role="status"` + `aria-live`).
- /post broadcasting + error phases (already correctly
  wired).
- All 51 form inputs (svelte-check rule already enforces
  label association — that's why baseline is 0 warnings).
- All 17 `<img>` tags (all have alt attributes).

### Findings deferred to follow-up parts

Each substantive enough to be its own work unit:

- **Route-transition focus management.**  SvelteKit's
  default doesn't move focus on client-side navigation —
  documented SPA a11y issue.  Skip-link mitigates (Tab
  reveals it) but full fix needs an `afterNavigate` hook
  moving focus to the page heading.
- **Full heading-hierarchy audit.**  Spot-checked several
  pages, no obvious skipped levels.  Full audit would
  walk every route.
- **Color-contrast audit.**  Needs runtime tooling
  (axe-core or similar).  Out of scope for static-source
  smoke.
- **PaymentMethodsPicker custom-component aria props.**
  The picker doesn't yet accept aria-invalid /
  aria-describedby props.  Workaround: the StatusLine got
  `id="payment-methods-error"` so the live-region
  announcement still fires when the error appears.  Full
  picker integration is a separate enhancement.

### Memory facts codified

**#45 — native `<dialog>` does NOT auto-associate
headings.**  Every dialog component must explicitly wire
`aria-labelledby={titleId}` + `<h2 id={titleId}>`.

**#46 — `aria-describedby` on form inputs must be
CONDITIONAL.**  Only set when the referenced ID exists in
the DOM, otherwise it points at a missing reference (which
some screen readers verbalize as "described by [missing]").
Pattern: `aria-describedby={error ? 'fiat-error' :
undefined}`.

**#47 — state-transition surfaces must have aria-live
regions.**  Success/error phase changes that aren't
navigation need explicit announcement.  `aria-live="polite"
+ role="status"` for success; `aria-live="assertive" +
role="alert"` for errors.

### New regression smoke

`apps/web/scripts/a11y-patterns-smoke.ts` — 25 scenarios
asserting:

- ConfirmModal titleId + aria-labelledby + matching h2 id
- ConfirmModal default-focuses Cancel button
- Layout has skip-link to #main + matching `<main id="main">`
- /post success phase has aria-live + role="status"
- /post broadcasting + error phases correctly wired
- /post + /post/edit field-level aria-invalid +
  aria-describedby + StatusLine id linkage (10 input/
  StatusLine combinations across both pages)
- StatusLine accepts id prop + emits aria-live correctly

Smoke runner now 2,188 scenarios across 94 runners (was
2,163 / 93).  Triple-pulse 3-for-3 stable.

### Why no brag entry

Per Memory #15: brag list is public-facing launch
marketing.  Part 100 is mixed-character — runtime changes
that help screen-reader users (real users), but framed as
a structural audit and sighted-user-visible behavior is
unchanged.  Same precedent as Parts 90 (ADR-fidelity) and
96 (operator-docs-fidelity): audit campaigns get a
TARBALL + REVISIT-LIST closure, not a brag entry.  If a
specific deferred item ships later as a substantive
feature (e.g. afterNavigate focus management), that one
can have its own brag entry.

## Part 101 (2026-05-09) — Memory #11 Category O chain-op drift sweep

User said "ok, go" after Part 100 closed Category N
(a11y).  All Tier 1/2/3 grandma-friendly items shipped or
closed; Memory #11 categories A-N walked.  Picked
Category O — chain-op handler vs spec drift — as the last
unworked Memory #11 category and the highest-value pre-
launch audit class: drift between handler-accepted payload
and documented payload could mean operators silently
mis-process orders, attribute fees wrong, or worse.

This part is **audit-class internal/process work** plus
public-docs corrections.  Same treatment as Parts 90
(Category I — ADR fidelity), 96 (Category M — operator-
docs fidelity), 100 (Category N — a11y).  No brag-list
entry per Memory #15.  Most fixes are doc corrections;
one is a code-internal SQL alignment.

### Methodology

Walked every shipped op in the indexer's HANDLERS map (17
of them):

  profile, order, orderReplace, orderCancel, feedback,
  feedbackResponse, chatMessage (chatHandler), chatIdentity,
  chatRead, releaseDiscovery, feeAttest, featureBid,
  operatorRegister, operatorBlock, operatorPaymentMethod,
  block, strangerFee.

For each:

  1. Op ID consistency (dispatcher OP_IDS vs frontend
     OP_IDS at apps/web/src/lib/net/config.ts).
  2. Payload field accesses in the handler (every
     `payload.*` field read).
  3. Spec docs (ADRs, API.md, OPERATIONS.md, PLAN.md,
     design docs).
  4. Doc-only ops triaged into: drift / discarded
     alternative / future work / historical planning.

**Code-internal inconsistency closed (1):**

- O-11 `is_new_trader` had two competing SQL

  - orderbook.ts: `(COALESCE(f.c, 0) < 4)` (sock-

- `morphit_featurebid_v1` no-underscore: stale historical

  frontend sends it, handler ignores it.  Correct by

  operator-supplied `ts` is "not authoritative" per

### Memory facts codified

**#48 — three-step new-route registration.**  Adding a
user-routable page requires (1) ROUTES entry, (2) seo.*
locale keys, (3) `<Head routeKey="..."/>`.  The first
step is the easy-to-miss one because steps 2-3 don't
trigger immediate breakage.  `routes.test.ts` catches
the reverse-drift; read the test failure carefully.

**#49 — `is_new_trader` semantics canonical.**  The
field means "sock-puppet-filtered feedback_count < 4"
across `/v1/orderbook` AND `/v1/orders/:account`.  This
is DIFFERENT from `accounts.first_trade_complete_at IS
NULL` (welcome-bonus trigger, ADR-0011 §8) — those
serve different purposes ("low rep" vs "no
counterparty feedback yet").

**#50 — drift-sweep triage rubric.**  Sort each
doc-only chain-op reference into: (a) genuine drift,
(b) explicitly-discarded alternative, (c) future-work-
not-yet-shipped, (d) historical planning artifact.
Ratio in this codebase: 14 drift fixes / 9 not-drift
findings / 17 handlers walked.  ~60% of doc-only refs
are drift; ~40% are intentional historical or
discarded alternatives.

Per Memory #15: brag list is public-facing launch
marketing.  Part 101 is mostly internal/process
(handler-vs-spec consistency) plus public-docs
corrections; sighted-user-visible behavior unchanged

audience not user-facing.  Same precedent as Parts 90,

  - New `mainEl = $state<HTMLElement | null>(null)`

  - `<main>` got `tabindex="-1"` +
    `focus:outline-none`.
  - `afterNavigate(nav => {...mainEl?.focus()})` —
    skips first load (`!nav.from`) and same-path nav
    (`from.url.pathname === to.url.pathname`).
    `queueMicrotask` for DOM settle.

Behavioral effect: screen-reader users hear "main,
region" announced on every real route change.
Previous default kept focus on whatever activated
the nav, leaving SR users with no audible signal.

Why focus `<main>` not the `<h1>`: focusing the
heading is the textbook ideal but requires every
route to expose a stable id on its h1, invasive
across 39 routes.  The `<main>` approach gives ~90%
of the value at near-zero cost.

#### Heading-hierarchy regression smoke

`apps/web/scripts/heading-hierarchy-smoke.ts` walks
every `+page.svelte` (39 files), parses heading tags
in render order with awareness of Svelte
`{#if}/{:else if}/{:else}/{/if}` blocks so
conditional renders aren't false-flagged.

Two rules:

  1. No multiple `<h1>`s in the same render branch
     (mutually-exclusive branches tolerated).
  2. No level jumps > +1 (h2 → h4 with no h3 is
     flagged).

3 documented allow-list exceptions:

  - `/onboarding/import` — funnel title inherited
    from parent `/onboarding` route.
  - `/onboarding/register-name` — same pattern.
  - `/cheat-sheet` — Memory #29 visibility-isolation
    pattern.  One `<h1>` in a `screen-only` div, one
    in `morphit-cheat-sheet` div with `display:
    none` in screen mode.  Screen readers honor
    `display: none` so they see exactly one `<h1>`
    at runtime; static-source scan can't see CSS so
    counts both.

Smoke audits 39 routes, 0 issues outside allow-list,
4/4 scenarios pass.

#### PaymentMethodsPicker aria props

`apps/web/src/lib/components/PaymentMethodsPicker.svelte`
gained `invalid?: boolean` and `describedById?: string`
props.  Wired onto the search `<input>` (NOT the root
— `aria-invalid` is not supported on `role="group"`,
which svelte-check correctly flagged during
authoring):

```svelte
aria-invalid={invalid || undefined}
aria-describedby={invalid && describedById
                 ? describedById : undefined}
```

The `|| undefined` pattern omits the attribute
entirely when `invalid` is false (rather than
emitting `aria-invalid="false"`, which some SRs
verbalize as "valid" — almost never desired).
`aria-describedby` is conditional on BOTH `invalid`
true AND a referenced id supplied (Memory fact #46).

Picker root retains `role="group"` + `aria-label`
landmark semantics.

Call sites:

  - `apps/web/src/routes/post/+page.svelte`:
    `invalid={!!paymentMethodsError}
    describedById="payment-methods-error"`.
  - `apps/web/src/routes/post/edit/[permlink]/+page.svelte`:
    `invalid={!!pmError}
    describedById="edit-pm-error"`.

The StatusLine `id` props at both call sites already
existed from Part 100; this part connects them into
the picker.

`a11y-patterns-smoke.ts` extended 25 → 35 scenarios.
10 new assertions covering afterNavigate hook,
`<main>` tabindex + bind, picker prop interface,
picker root role, picker input aria-invalid +
aria-describedby pattern, both call sites.

### Memory facts codified

**#51 — Forgejo NEVER Gitea.**  Repo at git.agorise.net
runs Forgejo.  Memory edit #16 codifies the policy.
Repo-wide regression smoke catches future drift.

**#52 — SvelteKit doesn't move focus on client-side
nav by default.**  Layout `afterNavigate` + `<main>`
`tabindex="-1"` + `focus:outline-none` is the
canonical pattern.  Skip first-load + same-path
hash navs.

**#53 — `aria-invalid` not supported on
`role="group"`.**  Wire invalidity on the inner
form-widget (input/select/textarea), not the wrapping
landmark.  svelte-check's
`a11y_role_supports_aria_props` rule catches this.

**#54 — `aria-invalid={invalid || undefined}`
pattern.**  Omits the attribute entirely when invalid
is false; doesn't render the misleading
`aria-invalid="false"` string.

#### Item C — `feeStatusLabel` missing branches (REAL BUG)

The May-6 Phase J audit had concluded the indexer
never wrote `'missing'`, `'underpaid'`, or
`'unverified'` and removed all three case arms
from `feeStatusLabel` plus the i18n keys.  Part 70
later re-extended `OrderRecord.fee_status` to all
7 states (because `order_detail`'s rendering
depends on them and svelte-check was failing
without the type coverage), but `feeStatusLabel`
was not re-extended.

Part 103 re-verified the indexer's runtime-emitted
set by reading
`apps/indexer/src/indexer/handlers/order.ts:649,714`
plus the explicit assertions in
`apps/indexer/scripts/order-handler-smoke.ts`.
Result: the indexer writes 6 of the 7 typed
values: `verified`, `pending_external`,
`verified_by_attestation`, `reused`, **`missing`**,
**`underpaid`**.  Only `'unverified'` is unwritten
by current handlers (it's the DB column DEFAULT,
defended by `order_detail`'s explicit branch but
never produced at runtime).

So orders in `fee_status='missing'` or
`fee_status='underpaid'` had been rendering an
empty amber pill in My Orders — visibly broken.

**Fix shipped:**
- `apps/web/src/routes/my/orders/+page.svelte:275-298`
  — added `case 'missing'` and `case 'underpaid'`
  arms; upgraded `default:` from `return ''` to
  `return o.fee_status ?? ''` so future indexer
  drift surfaces visibly rather than silently.
- `my_orders.order.fee_missing` and
  `my_orders.order.fee_underpaid` added to all 10
  locales (voice matches existing `fee_reused`
  pattern).

**Fix shipped:**

  with amber-pill styling matching the other
  rejection states.
- `order_detail.fee_reused` added to all 10
  locales (voice matches existing
  `fee_underpaid` / `fee_missing` register).

`apps/web/scripts/fee-status-label-coverage-smoke.ts`
(10 scenarios) — permanent regression smoke that
asserts:

  1. The set of fee_status values the indexer
     emits (parsed structurally from `order.ts` +
     `feeAttest.ts` via union of literal-string
     assignment regex + SQL-block VALUES regex +
     UPDATE-statement regex) is a SUBSET of the

The static check is exhaustive by construction —

#### Item 1a — Color-contrast smoke (LAST Part-100 a11y deferral)

`apps/web/scripts/color-contrast-smoke.ts` (5
scenarios) — the original Part-100 framing was
that color-contrast verification needed runtime
tooling like axe-core, but the project's Tailwind
usage is structured enough that a static-source
check covers the dominant class of failure.

**Methodology:**
1. Parse the custom `ink-*` palette from
   `apps/web/tailwind.config.js` (regex
   extraction; sanity-checked against the declared
   `ink-900 = #0F141C`).
2. Hard-code Tailwind v3.4's standard palette for
   the 7 families used in the codebase (`amber`,
   `blue`, `emerald`, `green`, `orange`, `red`,
   `rose`).
3. Walk every `.svelte` file under
   `apps/web/src`, extract class lists from
   `class="..."` attributes, expand template-
   literal ternary branches into separate virtual
   class lists.
4. Extract `text-X-N` and `bg-Y-N` classes,
   light/dark mode separated.  Reject opacity
   modifiers (`bg-amber-500/10` — alpha-blended,
   no single hex).  Reject state variants
   (`hover:`, `focus:`, `active:`, etc. — only
   `dark:` is accepted).
5. Compute WCAG 2.1 contrast ratios.  Self-test
   the math against 5 known-good pairs before
   trusting it.
6. Flag pairs below AA (4.5:1 uniform; can't
   reliably detect large-text statically).

**Result on the current tree:** 96 svelte files
scanned, 161 text/bg pairs checked, **0 below
AA**.  Allow-list empty.

**Acknowledged limits** (documented in the smoke
header): parent-inherited backgrounds, gradients,
SVG fill/stroke vs ancestor bg, inline
`style="color:..."`.  A future build-time
axe-core pass would close those — filed as
backlog, not pre-launch-blocking.
