### Part 104 — translation completeness audit + permanent regression smoke

**Source:** Ken's question after the Part 103
tarball: "have all of the glossary term
definitions and cheat sheet wording been
translated as well? if not, make sure they are.
please make sure all of the 9 translations are as
complete as possible so that i do not have to
hire so many humans to translate them, correct
them, etc."

**Verification methodology:**

1. **Glossary structure check** — 21 term entries
   in EN (active_key, blurt, blurt_power,
   broadcast, counterparty, custom_json,
   delegation, federation, feedback, fiat,
   indexer, listing_fee, network_fee, operator,
   password, permlink, posting_key, relay,
   release_op, seed_phrase, sign), each with
   {title, body}.  Verified each non-EN locale has
   all 21 entries with non-empty title + non-empty
   body — **189/189 (title, body) pairs complete
   across the 9 non-EN locales**.

2. **Cheat-sheet structure check** — 18
   substantive content entries in EN.  Verified
   each non-EN locale has all 18 with non-empty
   localized values — **162/162 entries complete**.

3. **Body-content translation quality** — for
   non-Latin-script locales (fa, zh-CN, zh-HK,
   ru), confirmed the locale's bodies actually use
   the target script.  Two cheat-sheet `footer`
   entries flagged as "suspiciously Latin" turned
   out to be legitimate brand info ("Morphit ·
   morphit.io · 开源 · AGPL-3.0") with proper
   Chinese translation of "open source" — the
   Latin parts are domain + license code.

4. **Comprehensive byte-identical-to-EN scan** —
   walked all 2,389 keys × 9 non-EN locales =
   21,501 (key, locale) cells; flagged any cell
   whose value is byte-identical to EN.  This
   surfaced ~110 candidates after filtering out
   pure format strings, brand names, and trivial
   strings (length < 3, no alpha chars, etc.).

5. **Triage into 3 buckets:**
   - **(a) same-word**: locale's word for the
     concept happens to be spelled identically
     (e.g. "Region" in German, "Transaction" in
     French, "Conversation" in French, "Plan" in
     ES/PL/DE).  ~25 cases.
   - **(b) loanword**: the locale's tech vocabulary
     has adopted the English term as standard
     (e.g. "Live" / "Filter" in German tech UI;
     "Privacy" / "Password" / "Account" in Italian
     tech context; "Avatar" / "Chat" / "Memo" /
     "Hardware" universal across all 5 Romance/
     Germanic locales).  ~120 cases.
   - **(c) invariant**: brand names, technical
     identifiers, chain-asset symbols, protocol
     names, placeholder examples, pure format
     strings.  ~65 cases.

   This produces the project's formalized
   translation policy.  Until Part 104 it was
   oral tradition.  Now it's an enforceable
   allow-list with documented (a)/(b)/(c) reason
   per entry.

**9 GENUINE translation gaps surfaced + closed:**

1. `fa.profile.pnl.csv_header.memo` —
   Persian had `'Memo'` (Latin script) while every
   other Persian CSV header was already
   Persian-script (`'یادداشت'` etc.).  Fixed →
   `'یادداشت'`.

2. `fa.onboarding.register_name.field_placeholder`
   — Persian had `'your-new-name'` (Latin) for the
   register-name placeholder; Persian-script users
   couldn't read the URL-format example.  Fixed →
   `'نام-جدیدتان'`.

3. `zh-CN.settings.blurt_media_url.label` — was
   `'Blurt.media URL'`; Simplified Chinese
   convention is to translate "URL" to "网址".
   Fixed → `'Blurt.media 网址'`.

4. `zh-CN.onboarding.register_name.field_placeholder`
   — was `'your-new-name'`.  Fixed → `'你的新名字'`.

5. `zh-HK.settings.session.heading` — was
   `'Session'`; sibling zh-CN had `'会话'`.  Fixed
   → `'工作階段'` (Traditional Chinese form).

6. `zh-HK.settings.session.sign_out` — was
   `'Sign out'`; sibling zh-CN had `'退出登录'` and
   zh-HK's sibling `confirm_yes` already used
   `'登出'`.  Fixed → `'登出'`.

7. `zh-HK.settings.blurt_media_url.label` — was
   `'Blurt.media URL'`.  Fixed →
   `'Blurt.media 網址'` (Traditional form).

8. `zh-HK.onboarding.register_name.field_placeholder`
   — was `'your-new-name'`.  Fixed → `'你的新名字'`.

9. `de.download.iphone_heading` — was `'iPhone &
   iPad'`; German conventionally uses "und"
   instead of `&` in headings (other locales
   render the locale-appropriate conjunction:
   ES "y", FR "et", IT "e").  Fixed → `'iPhone und
   iPad'`.

**Permanent regression smoke (the value-add):**

`apps/web/scripts/i18n-translation-completeness-smoke.ts`
(4 scenarios, registered in `scripts/run-smokes.sh`):

  1. all 10 locale files load successfully
  2. EN source-of-truth has ≥2,000 string keys
  3. allow-list has documented justifications for
     every entry (each entry must cite (a)/(b)/(c)
     reason)
  4. no string is byte-identical to English in a
     locale outside the allow-list

The allow-list contains ~210 (key, locale) pairs.
Future translator drift is now caught at smoke
time: if someone adds a new key but forgets to
translate a locale, the smoke flags it.  If the
flagged value is genuinely a same-word /
loanword / invariant, the fix is to add it to
the allow-list with a one-line rationale.  No
more relying on "we'll catch it in human
review."

**Important nuance on what's NOT a translation gap:**

Many byte-identical-to-EN entries are
**legitimately the correct rendering**:

  - "Region" in German is also "Region"
  - "Transaction" in French is also "Transaction"
  - "Live" in German tech UI is the convention
    even though "direkt" exists
  - "Privacy" in Italian privacy-policy contexts
    is the established loanword
  - "Avatar" / "Chat" / "Memo" / "Slot" / "Hardware"
    are universal tech loanwords across multiple
    Romance/Germanic locales
  - "Witness" is the universal Blurt-chain
    technical term in all 9 non-EN locales (just
    like Bitcoin "miners" stays as the technical
    term in non-EN docs)
  - "BLURT Power", "permlink", "custom_json" are
    universal Blurt-chain proper-name technical
    terms
  - "Bitcoin" / "Monero" stay as universal English
    in Latin-script locales (fa/zh have script
    versions)

These are NOT bugs.  Forcing translation of
loanwords would produce stilted, unnatural copy
that locale-native users would find weird (e.g.
forcing German "Reputation" → "Ansehen" when
"Reputation" IS the German word in tech UI).
The allow-list documents each such case.

#### `RUN-A-MORPHIT-NODE.md §3a` — home-hosting walkthrough (~280 lines)

Seven sub-sections, each with copy-paste commands
and ELI5 explanations:

- **§3a.1 CGNAT check** — visit `whatismyip.com`,
  compare to router's WAN IP; if mismatched (or
  in `100.64.0.0/10`), three options: switch to
  VPS, call ISP, or use Cloudflare Tunnel /

  sign-in, 12+ years uptime).  Dynu listed as
  alternative.  No-IP explicitly NOT recommended
  due to the 30-day-confirmation pestering that
  causes silent outages.  Step-by-step with the
  token-copy and verification.
- **§3a.3 DHCP reservation** — `ip link show eth0`
  to get MAC address, then router admin walkthrough

- **§3a.5 DDNS auto-update** — DuckDNS update

  for Dynu, log-tail verification.
- **§3a.6 Power blips and lid-closing** — UPS
  recommendation ($50, 600VA, plug modem +

  (the three `HandleLidSwitch*` directives), BIOS
  AC-Power-Recovery setting, Pi `boot_delay=1`
  config, end-to-end power-cycle test.
- **§3a.7 Outside-the-house verification** — three
  tests via phone-on-cellular: nslookup the DDNS
  hostname, `nc -vz` port 80, `nc -vz` port 443.
  Each test includes a "if this fails, here's
  what to fix" branch.

## Part 106 (2026-05-10) — Treasury chain-pin closes BTC/XMR fork-attack vector + deep-deep audit

**Trigger.**  Operator question, not the structured audit:
"where are our wallet addresses defined? if I want to change
those 2 addresses then I will need somewhere for me to do
that. Also, are other instances easily able to change our
btc/xmr wallet addresses? I hope not."

That question revealed a real fork-attack vector that
survived the 110-item audit campaign because nothing in
Memory #11 specifically tested the BTC/XMR fee-address
authority chain.

**Pre-Part-106 vulnerability:**

ADR-0011's 2026-05-09 amendment said "BTC and XMR fees:
100% to treasury (`@morphit-fees`)" — the policy — but
**no code enforced the addresses themselves**.  Each
operator's indexer trusted its own
`MORPHIT_INDEXER_BTC_FEE_ADDRESS` and
`MORPHIT_INDEXER_XMR_FEE_ADDRESS` env vars as gospel.  A
hostile fork could silently divert all BTC/XMR fees by
changing those env vars, and the frontend never displayed
the actual address — the locale strings just said "send
the fee to **our** Bitcoin/Monero address, then paste the
transaction ID below" — so the operator was free to
social-engineer alternative addresses into the user's
flow.  Verification flow on the user's hostile instance
returned `verified` against the hostile address; the
federated `morphit.io` indexer checking the same txid
against its own configured address marked the order
`underpaid`/`missing` and the order never appeared on
canonical's orderbook — but the user paid, the hostile
indexer showed the listing, and the treasury got nothing.

**Fix architecture:**

Extend the existing signed `morphit_release_v1` op
(already authenticated by the `@morphit` posting key via
the trust anchor pinned in `apps/web/src/lib/net/config.ts`)
with an optional `treasury` block carrying canonical
BTC/XMR addresses, amounts, and the XMR private view key
(publish-safe per Monero design — reveals incoming
amounts only, never spends or balances).

  - **Schema migration v28** adds `treasury JSONB`
    column to `releases` (nullable for back-compat).
  - **`TreasurySource`** abstraction at
    `apps/indexer/src/indexer/treasurySource.ts`
    resolves with chain-pin > env precedence,
    30s cache, request-coalescing, DB-error fallback.
  - **Indexer poller** queries TreasurySource each
    cycle and rebuilds verifiers when canonical
    address changes.  No restart needed.
  - **Frontend validator** at
    `apps/web/src/lib/net/releaseValidate.ts` mirrors
    the indexer's regex byte-for-byte (proven with 16
    parity test cases in the new
    `release.test.ts:describe('release validator
    parity — frontend ↔ indexer', ...)` block).
  - **`ListingFeeAddressPanel.svelte`** new component
    renders address with copy-button (clipboard API),
    QR code (BIP-21 / Monero URI), XMR view-key
    disclosure, "✓ Chain-pinned by @morphit" badge.
  - **Wired** into post-order page above the txid
    input.
  - **All 14 new locale strings × 10 locales** = 140
    string additions; locale parity 2,389 → 2,403.
  - **Operator runbook `OPERATIONS.md §40`** ~250
    lines, 9 sub-sections walking through release-op
    ceremony.
  - **ADR-0011 amendment** documenting the fork-attack
    vector, the fix, validation rules, hostile-fork
    containment, view-key publication rationale.
  - **`apps/indexer/scripts/release-build-payload.ts`**
    operator helper builds + validates payload before
    broadcast; tested both happy-path and rejection.
  - **`apps/indexer/scripts/release-validator-smoke.ts`**
    extended +24 Part 106 scenarios (46 → 70).
  - **`apps/indexer/scripts/treasury-source-smoke.ts`**
    new 10-scenario regression smoke.

**Validation rules (mirrored on indexer + frontend):**

- BTC: mainnet only — `bc1q.../1.../3...`; testnet
  (`tb1`/`m`/`n`) rejected; satoshis bounded to ≤ 100B
  (1000 BTC).
- XMR: mainnet primary (95 chars, starts `4`) or
  subaddress (95 chars, starts `8`); testnet (`9`/`B`)
  and stagenet (`5`/`7`) rejected; viewkey 64 lowercase
  hex chars no `0x`; piconero positive decimal-string
  ≤ 16 digits.

**Deep-deep audit (per Memory #11 conventions: STRIDE +
attack-tree + red-team):**

Conducted full systematic audit on five axes — indexer
code path, frontend code path, API endpoints, defense
bypass / edge cases, deployment / operator process —
with red-team adversarial exploration of 14+ attack
branches.  Full audit summary table in
`docs/AUDIT-2026-05.md` Part 106 deep-deep audit
appendix.

**Real defense bug found and fixed during the deep
audit:**

Branch 2.1 — bypass chain-pinned AMOUNT.  The order
handler at `apps/indexer/src/indexer/handlers/order.ts:551`
was reading `ctx.config.btcFeeSatoshis` /
`ctx.config.xmrFeePiconero` directly, completely bypassing
the chain-pin.  A hostile fork could set their env
satoshis to `1` (effectively free) while inheriting the
chain-pinned address from canonical, and accept any
payment as `verified` on their own instance.

**Fix:**
  - Extended `OpContext` with
    `feeAmounts: { btcSatoshis?: number; xmrPiconero?: bigint }`.
  - Threaded through `applyBlock(...feeAmounts)`
    signature.
  - Poller tracks alongside `feeVerifierAddresses` and
    syncs from TreasurySource snapshots in both
    bootstrap and refresh.  Amount syncs every refresh
    (handles rotation case where address stays but
    amount changes due to price moves).
  - Order handler now reads `ctx.feeAmounts.btcSatoshis`
    / `ctx.feeAmounts.xmrPiconero` instead of
    `ctx.config.*`; treats `undefined` same as `0` for
    not-configured rejection branch.

**Defensive hardening also added during the audit:**

Branch 12 — XMR `BigInt(snapshot.xmr.piconero)` could
throw if the DB row had a hand-crafted malformed value
(should never happen because validateTreasury rejects
at write time, but defense-in-depth).  Wrapped in
try/catch with log + fallback to `undefined` (treated
the same as not-configured, rejecting the order
cleanly).

**Test coverage:**

`apps/indexer/test/handlers/release.test.ts` extended
with 22 new test scenarios:
  - 6 handler tests for valid-and-stored, missing
    treasury back-compat, testnet BTC rejection,
    testnet XMR rejection, upper-case viewkey
    rejection, 0-satoshi BTC rejection.
  - 16 frontend ↔ indexer validator-parity test cases
    proving the two validators accept/reject every
    payload identically with matching reason names.

Indexer test count: 370 → **392 passing**.

**Bonus finding (out-of-scope for Part 106 — REVISIT):**

The frontend's `validateReleasePayload` is stricter on
`hash_manifest` entries than the indexer's handler.
Frontend rejects entries that don't match SHA-256 SRI
format (`sha256-<43 base64 chars>=`); indexer accepts
any string.  Means a release the indexer stores as
valid could fail the frontend's chain-direct fetch with
`hash_manifest_entry_invalid`.  Not exploitable
(operators control both validators' inputs at
broadcast time), but the asymmetry is a tech-debt /
audit-fidelity gap.  Future part should add a parity
check on hash_manifest entries OR loosen the frontend
to match the indexer's permissiveness.

**Numbers:**

  - Smoke baseline: 2,224 / 99 → **2,262 / 100**
    triple-pulse stable.
  - Locale parity: 2,389 → **2,403** keys × 10
    locales.
  - Brag list: 254 → **255** (entry #255).
  - Indexer tests: 370/371 → **392/393**.
  - Relay tests: 244 unchanged.

**What's left for the operator (you, when ready to
broadcast):**

     `--generate-new-wallet=morphit-treasury.wallet`.
     Get primary address (95 chars, starts `4`) and
     secret view key (64 hex chars).
  2. Get/generate dedicated BTC address (native
     segwit `bc1q...` recommended).
  3. Run
     `tsx apps/indexer/scripts/verify-xmr-viewkey.ts

  4. Edit `/etc/morphit/indexer.env` on morphit.io —

  5. Build payload with

  6. Broadcast as a `custom_json` op signed by the

## Part 107 (2026-05-10) — Privacy correction: XMR view key removed from chain-pin

**Trigger.**  Operator pushback on Part 106 design.

After Part 106 shipped (treasury chain-pin including XMR
private view key broadcast on chain), the operator
cross-checked the "publish-safe by Monero design" framing
with another LLM (Grok) which correctly identified that
publishing the private view key reveals every incoming
payment to the treasury wallet forever, including future
inflows.  The operator pushed back:

> "you mentioned that i should put the monero secret/private
> viewkey into that .env file. i think that is a horrible
> idea."

(The operator's specific concern was about keeping the
viewkey OUT of the env file, which inverted the flow:
viewkey actually NEEDS to live in env — that's its safe
home — but it MUST NOT live on chain or anywhere public.)

**The privacy harm Part 106 would have caused.**

Publishing the private view key on chain via the
chain-pinned `treasury` block means:

  - Every analyst with the chain history sees every
    incoming XMR payment to the treasury wallet, forever.
  - Amounts, timings, subaddress patterns become public
    record.
  - Combined with Morphit's order ops (which name the
    user's Blurt account at roughly the same time as the
    XMR payment lands), users can be deanonymized at scale.
  - Irreversible.  Once on chain, the key is public
    forever — even after a wallet rotation, all the
    pre-rotation history remains analyzable.

For Morphit's positioning ("absolutely private/anonymous
for Monero users"), this is unacceptable.  "Publish-safe"
in Monero docs means "no theft risk"; it does NOT mean
"safe for privacy."  Part 106's framing conflated the two.

**Fix scope.**  Remove the viewkey from every layer of the
chain-pinned path while keeping it in env-only on the
operator's box.  Files touched:

  - **`apps/web/src/lib/net/release.ts`** — drop `viewkey`
    field from `ReleaseTreasuryBlock`; doc comment rewritten.
  - **`apps/web/src/lib/net/releaseValidate.ts`** — drop
    `treasury_xmr_viewkey_missing` and
    `treasury_xmr_viewkey_not_hex64` reasons; drop
    `XMR_VIEWKEY_RE` constant; validator silently strips
    any `viewkey` field present in input.
  - **`apps/indexer/src/indexer/handlers/release.ts`** —
    handler `validateTreasury()` mirrors the frontend; drops
    viewkey-validation branches; silently strips any
    `viewkey` field; doc comments rewritten with Part 107
    privacy invariant.
  - **`apps/indexer/src/indexer/treasurySource.ts`** —
    fully rewritten:
      - `XmrTreasury` shape: `{address, piconero, viewkey:
        string|undefined, addressSource: 'chain'|'env'}`.
      - `ChainTreasuryRow.xmr` no longer expects viewkey.
      - `resolveXmr` uses composite source — address+piconero
        from chain (when available) or env (fallback);
        viewkey ALWAYS from env, `undefined` when env empty.
      - Header doc rewritten with full Part 107 privacy
        invariant explanation, three options for community
        operators.
  - **`apps/indexer/src/indexer/poller.ts`** — refresh logic
    adapted to new `XmrTreasury` shape; rebuild trigger
    refined; `xmr_verifier_disabled` log distinguishes
    `no_address_available` vs `no_local_viewkey`.
  - **`apps/indexer/src/api/release.ts`** — added
    `stripViewkey()` defense-in-depth on `/v1/release`
    response (belt-and-suspenders against hand-crafted
    DB writes, regression bugs, future feature creep).
  - **`apps/indexer/scripts/release-build-payload.ts`** —
    drops viewkey prompt + `xmrViewkey` from `Inputs`;
    new defense-in-depth gate refuses to emit any payload
    containing a 64-hex string (catches future regression).
  - **`apps/indexer/scripts/release-validator-smoke.ts`** —
    drops 4 viewkey-reject scenarios; adds 3 Part 107
    invariant scenarios (silent-strip on input, garbage
    viewkey field still ignored, both-pinned output has no
    viewkey).  70 → 69 scenarios.
  - **`apps/indexer/scripts/treasury-source-smoke.ts`** —
    full rewrite for new shape; adds Case 4b (legacy/hostile
    chain row with viewkey IGNORED, env value used) and
    Case 4c (community-operator state: chain address +
    no env viewkey → viewkey undefined).  10 → 12 scenarios.
  - **`apps/indexer/test/handlers/release.test.ts`** —
    handler tests rewritten for new shape; new test:
    "Part 107: payload with viewkey present → silently
    stripped, NOT persisted"; viewkey-reject parity tests
    dropped; new parity test: "xmr WITH viewkey field
    (legacy/hostile) → ok, silently stripped".  Renamed
    `VALID_XMR_VK` → `VALID_XMR_VK_LOOKING` with comment
    explaining it's for testing strip behavior, not a real
    key.  392 → 391 indexer tests passing.
  - **`apps/indexer/src/db/schema.sql`** v28 migration
    comment rewritten — JSON shape doc no longer mentions
    viewkey; new "Privacy invariant (Part 107)" paragraph;
    `COMMENT ON COLUMN` updated.
  - **`apps/web/src/lib/components/ListingFeeAddressPanel.svelte`** —
    `viewkey` field dropped from `resolved` derived store;
    `copyVkFlash` state dropped; `copyViewKey` function
    dropped; XMR view-key disclosure UI block removed
    entirely; header doc rewritten to mention Part 107

  - **All 10 locale files** — drop
    `fee_address_xmr_viewkey_label` and
    `fee_address_xmr_viewkey_copy` keys.  Locale parity
    2,403 → 2,401.
  - **`ops/env/indexer.env.example`** — XMR section
    rewritten with explicit "🔒 PRIVACY-CRITICAL: NEVER
    PUBLISH THIS KEY" block; mode 0600 reminder; explicit
    list of "never check it into git, never paste it into
    chat or a Forgejo issue, never broadcast it on chain,
    never put it in any API response or log line, never
    share it with a community operator who asks."
  - **`docs/OPERATIONS.md §40`** — full rewrite (~470
    lines, 10 sub-sections including new §40.2 "Privacy
    invariant: the XMR view key NEVER leaves your box").
    Three options for community operators in §40.8.
    Key reference table in §40.10 explicitly shows XMR
    private view key as `/etc/morphit/indexer.env on
    morphit.io ONLY`, mode 0600.
  - **`docs/RUN-A-MORPHIT-NODE.md §8`** — community-
    operator callout rewritten with three honest options
    (disable, run own, trust canonical [Part 108+]).
  - **`docs/adr/0011-dynamic-fee-model.md`** — Part 107
    amendment appended documenting the privacy harm, fix,
    federation change, and operational discipline.
  - **`docs/AUDIT-2026-05.md`** — Part 107 entry
    documenting trigger, harm, fix scope, multi-layer
    defense, federation change, lessons learned (3
    lessons including "publish-safe framings need
    cross-check against the SPECIFIC privacy goal").

**Multi-layer defense for the privacy invariant.**  Part
107's design uses defense-in-depth across multiple layers
so a regression at any one layer doesn't republish the key:

  1. Frontend `validateTreasury` silently strips viewkey
     from input.
  2. Indexer handler `validateTreasury` silently strips
     viewkey before DB persist.
  3. `TreasurySource.ChainTreasuryRow` shape doesn't
     include viewkey field; `resolveXmr` never reads
     viewkey from chain.
  4. `/v1/release` endpoint `stripViewkey()` on output
     (defense-in-depth — catches DB-write bypass).
  5. `release-build-payload.ts` refuses to emit any
     payload containing a 64-hex regex match.
  6. `ListingFeeAddressPanel.svelte` has no UI surface
     for view key.
  7. Locale strings have no view-key-related entries.
  8. Smoke + tests verify each layer.

A regression at layer 1 alone wouldn't leak (handler at
layer 2 still strips).  A regression at layer 1+2 wouldn't
leak (API at layer 4 still strips).  And so on.

**Federation behavior change for XMR.**  Pre-Part-107,
community operators inheriting canonical's chain-pinned
XMR address would automatically also inherit the view
key (because it was on chain).  Post-Part-107, they
inherit the address but NOT the view key.  Three options
documented in OPERATIONS.md §40.8:

  (a) **Trust canonical's federated XMR verdict** —
      requires a federation-trust path that doesn't
      exist yet.  Tracked as Part 108+ work below.

  (b) **Run their own XMR treasury wallet** with their
      own env address + view key.  Deviates from
      canonical (their XMR-fee orders won't appear on
      canonical's orderbook), but they keep 100% of the
      XMR that flows in.

  (c) **Disable XMR fee acceptance** on their instance.
      Cleanest option today.

**Numbers.**

  - Smoke baseline: 2,262 / 100 → **2,263 / 100**
    triple-pulse stable.
  - Indexer tests: 392/393 → **391/392** (+3 Part 107
    silent-strip tests, -4 viewkey-reject tests).
  - Locale parity: 2,403 → **2,401** keys × 10.
  - Brag list: 255 unchanged (Part 107 amends Part
    106's entry rather than adding new — see brag-list
    Part 106 entry).
  - Web tsc: 0 errors.
  - Indexer tsc: 0 errors.
  - svelte-check: 0/0.

**Part 108+ TODO: federation-trust path for XMR.**

Today, community operators inheriting canonical's
chain-pinned XMR address have no way to independently
verify XMR payments without canonical's view key (which
is rightly not published).  The right long-term answer
is a federation-trust path: community indexers query
canonical's `/v1/orders/<id>/fee_status` and adopt the
verdict (verified/underpaid/missing) instead of doing
local verification.  This needs:

  - Authenticated cross-instance queries (signed by the
    target instance's own key) so a hostile operator
    can't forge "canonical says verified" responses.
  - A federation-quorum mode (don't trust just one
    instance — require N-of-M agreement) for resilience.
  - Fall-back behavior when canonical is unreachable
    (orders show as `pending` not `failed`).
  - Visible "verification path" badge on each order so
    users can see whether their XMR fee was verified
    locally or trusted from canonical.

Until that ships, community operators who want to accept
XMR fees should run their own treasury wallet (option b).
Most should disable XMR (option c) and recommend their
users transact in BTC or BLURT.

**Per-payment tx-proof path (Part 108++).**

A separate-but-related Monero-specific design that Grok
correctly highlighted: instead of relying on the view
key for verification at all, users could attach a
per-payment `tx_proof` (tx_key + recipient_address +
tx_hash) to their order op, and any indexer could verify
the proof without holding the view key.  This is
Monero's standard "selective transparency" mechanism for
proof-of-payment without exposing wallet history.

Cost: requires the user's wallet to support generating
the proof (Monero CLI/GUI does; some lightweight
wallets don't), and adds a UX step ("paste your tx_proof
along with your txid").

Benefit: completely eliminates the need for any indexer
to hold a view key for any treasury wallet.  Even
canonical wouldn't need one.  This is the "proper" answer
to the chain-pin-of-treasury-secrets problem.

Tracked as Part 108++ in this list.

**Lessons learned (also in AUDIT-2026-05.md Part 107).**

  1. "Publish-safe by design" framings need to be
     cross-checked against the SPECIFIC privacy goal of
     the system using the data.  Monero's "view key is
     fine to publish for selective transparency" guidance
     is right for charity wallets that WANT transparency.
     It's wrong for treasury wallets that want privacy.

  2. The Part 106 deep-deep audit followed the standard
     STRIDE + attack-tree + red-team methodology and
     found one real defense bug (order-handler amount
     bypass).  But it did NOT catch the view-key privacy
     harm because the harm is a passive-disclosure
     issue, not an active-exploit issue.  Future audits
     should explicitly include a "privacy / passive
     disclosure" axis alongside the attacker-centric
     STRIDE categories — "what does this design publish?
     to whom? for how long? combined with what other
     public data?"

  3. Multi-layer defense is worth the complexity.

  4. Operator pushback caught a design error that made
     it past two LLMs (Claude initially, then me on
     audit) and only surfaced when the operator brought
     in a third opinion.  Cross-checking with another
     LLM is a useful sanity check on design choices,
     especially privacy/security framings.

## Part 108++ (2026-05-10) — XMR per-payment tx_proof verification (no view key required by any indexer)

**Trigger.**  Operator priority confirmation post-Part-107.

The operator confirmed three priorities for Morphit, in
order: (1) privacy & anonymity, (2) decentralization /
fully distributed / unstoppable, (3) UI/UX grandma-
friendliness.  Memory entries #19, #20, #21 committed.

The Part 108+ federation-trust path (deferred from Part
107) was reviewed under the priority lens and **rejected**
— would have created a centralized chokepoint
contradicting priority #2.  Plowing it would have built
the wrong thing.  Skipped; went straight to Part 108++.

**The change in one sentence.**  XMR fee verification no
longer requires the indexer to hold the treasury wallet's
view key; instead, the user generates a per-payment
tx_proof from their own wallet, and any indexer verifies
the proof against the txid + treasury address using a
public Monero block explorer (or local monerod for
maximum independence).

**Why this is the right answer under all three priorities.**

- **Priority #1 (privacy).**  The proof reveals only
  "this txid paid this address this amount" — exactly
  the public information needed for verification, no
  more.  Strictly less leaky than the view-key approach
  (which would let any explorer with the key see every
  past, present, and future incoming payment, forever).
  Indexers hold NOTHING.

- **Priority #2 (decentralization).**  Every Morphit
  indexer can verify every XMR payment independently
  using public information.  No shared secret.  No
  central instance.  Canonical morphit.io is one
  indexer among many.  Federation tolerates any single
  instance disappearing — including canonical — without
  breaking XMR for anyone else.  Operators can self-host
  `monero-block-explorer` + `monerod` for zero
  third-party dependency.

- **Priority #3 (grandma-friendly).**  Trade-off: the
  user must generate a proof from their wallet (one
  extra step vs. just pasting a txid).  Mitigated by:
  inline per-wallet instructions on the post-order
  page (Monero CLI, GUI, Cake, Feather), expandable
  details block in 10 locales; privacy-reassurance
  banner above the textarea; client-side validation
  feedback mirroring the indexer's structural validator;
  new FAQ entry `xmr_tx_proof` with full Q&A in 10
  locales.

- This REVISIT-LIST closure.
- `MORPHIT-BRAG-LIST.md` new entry on per-payment
  proofs.

Ops:
- `ops/env/indexer.env.example` — XMR section
  rewritten for Part 108++.

**Numbers.**

- Smoke baseline: see triple-pulse result below.
- Indexer tests: 391/392 → **406/407** (+15 net: +25
  proof verifier + breaker tests, +5 handler tests,
  -15 deleted explorer tests).
- Frontend tests: 545 → **550** (+5).
- Locale parity: 2,401 → **2,422** keys × 10.
- TypeScript: all 8 projects clean.
- svelte-check: 0/0.

**Federation behavior change (positive).**  Pre-Part-
108++, only canonical morphit.io could verify XMR
fees.  Post-Part-108++, every Morphit instance can.
The "three options for community operators" dilemma
from Part 107 is obsolete; the canonical default flow
now works for everyone.

**Lessons learned.**

  1. **Priority lens before plowing.**  The Part 108+
     federation-trust path was a follow-up item from
     Part 107.  Reviewing it under the priority lens
     before writing code caught that it would create
     a centralized chokepoint.  Going forward, every
     REVISIT-LIST item gets a priority-lens review
     before plowing — not after.

  2. **"Smallest correct change" can be wrong.**  The
     federation-trust path was the smallest change
     from Part 107 status quo.  But "smallest change"
     is only a virtue when the status quo is the right
     design.  When a structural change better realizes
     the priorities, the bigger change is the right
     one.

  3. **Pre-launch is a feature.**  Memory #6 says
     Morphit is pre-launch with zero live instances,
     so breaking changes have no migration cost.
     Part 108++ takes full advantage: clean break from
     the view-key path, no two-mode complexity.  This
     is one of the few times in a project's life when
     fundamental verification mechanisms can be
     replaced wholesale without coordination overhead.

  4. **Cross-checking with another LLM still
     valuable.**  The original tx_proof option was
     surfaced by Grok during the Part 107 review.
     Bringing in a third opinion on privacy/security
     framings continues to pay off.

**Architectural debt for future parts.**

- `MORPHIT_INDEXER_XMR_FEE_VIEWKEY` env var should be
  removed (currently a deprecated stub).  Tracked in
  pending operator items below.
- `apps/indexer/scripts/verify-xmr-viewkey.ts` is now
  diagnostic-only (one-time wallet-creation sanity
  check).  Could be retired or repurposed.  Not
  urgent.
- Self-hosting `monero-block-explorer` for priority
  #2 maximum independence is documented but not
  shipped-as-default.  A future part could ship a
  one-line setup script.

### Part 109 follow-ups added

- [ ] (Part 109 follow-up) Per-user explorer preference.

      configurability; per-USER is the natural next

      strings.  Filed as defer because the per-OPERATOR
      half is the architecturally clean part; per-USER
      can come later without re-doing any plumbing.
- [ ] (Part 109 follow-up) Auto-default the quorum
      threshold based on configured URL count.  Part
      109 ships default 1 (back-compat) and surfaces
      the knob in the env example with explicit
      guidance.  A future part could ship
      `Math.max(1, ceil(N/2))` as the default and let

      routine explorer outages (more "is XMR broken?"

      cross-source guarantees.  Defer until we have
